matches.note: After the timekeeper's bell sounded and the match was briefly ruled a time-limit draw, Commissioner Craig Miles approved five more minutes at the crowd's request. Dones then caught Dread's leg and locked in a Figure Four leglock for the submission. Wildstar and his manager Calvin Carlton appeared at ringside mid-match and distracted Dones, though no direct interference occurred; Dread nearly connected with a top-rope dive on Dones during the distraction. Billed in-ring as 'Devils' Advocate' Javid Dones.

New Movement's Rocky Wellington rolled up Quiksilver with a La Magistral Cradle for the pin after Andersen Scott accidentally clotheslined his own partner. New Movement (Yin & Yang's opponents) is managed by Carlton Chambers, who was at ringside; New Movement repeatedly used hair-pulls and an illegal double-team choke while the referee's back was turned.

Erickson and Koltrane landed a combination chokeslam/powerbomb (called 'Da Bomb') on Jonathan for the pin while Powermaster was kept occupied outside the ring. This was Erickson and Koltrane's (Sex & Violence's) NFW debut. Referee missed an earlier legal tag by Jonathan to Powermaster.

Comelightly appeared to injure his leg on a botched moonsault landing; Wildstar capitalized with a Somersault Legdrop and pinned him while hooking the tights. Wildstar's manager Calvin Carlton ambushed Comelightly with a tennis racket before the bell and interfered again mid-match, including using the racket as a weapon. Commentary treats Comelightly's leg injury as a real mishap rather than a planned finish.

Dubov speared Morrison at the opening bell and finished him with a top-rope X-Factor (called 'Genesis') for the pin. Post-match, Raul proposed to Dubov on the mic and was rebuffed and beaten down; his cousin Cojones Mercado (debuting) then ran in and chairshotted both Dubov and her manager Kevin LeBrock, and Raul poured wine over the unconscious Dubov.

matches.stipulation: Contenders Match
matches.note: After Southern reversed a figure-four and nearly won with several near-falls, Powell struck Southern's already-injured knee with his baseball bat, then hooked a grapevine cradle for the pin when a German suplex attempt buckled Southern's knee. Southern had been attacked from behind earlier in the night by an unidentified man with a golf club; commentary speculated it was champion Bloodhunt. Bloodhunt's valet Miss America watched the match from the ramp. The winner earns the #1 contendership for the NFW World Championship.

matches.stipulation: NFW Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Bracket One Semifinal
matches.note: After Montezuma's Team Cuba entourage beat down Radder at ringside to swing momentum back to Montezuma, Montezuma grabbed a handful of tights on a rollup for the pin. Montezuma's Team Cuba entourage interfered at ringside during the match (a staged-announced result, which stands).

matches.stipulation: NFW Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Bracket Two Semifinal
matches.note: With Ryconik frozen watching his kidnapped daughter Vivian being dragged off by Raul and Cojones Mercado, Wylde rolled him up with a handful of tights for the pin. Raul and Cojones Mercado abducted Ryconik's daughter Vivian at ringside mid-match to distract him; commentary was unsure whether Ryconik allowed himself to be pinned.

matches.stipulation: Pentagram Match (Last Man Standing rules - no pinfalls, submissions, or count-outs; a wrestler is eliminated only by failing a referee's ten count)

eliminations.note: Eliminated after Pat Black's barbed-wire-wrapped 450 splash left him unable to answer the ten count.
Eliminated after a Diamond Cutter through a thumbtack-covered ironing board on the outside.
Action moved backstage to the boiler room; Manson drove a wrench into Neuromancer and slammed him through a table, then Pat Black pulled a shelving unit down on him, and he failed the ten count.
Manson stuffed Black into a rolling hamper and shoved it off a loading dock into an ambulance windshield; Black failed to answer the ten count, leaving Manson the winner.

matches.note: Mike Manson was the sole survivor after eliminating Pat Black with a rolling-hamper shove off a loading dock into a parked ambulance's windshield. The entrant billed in the segment title as 'Cancer' is introduced in-ring as 'the man formerly known as Cancer... the Nihilist Pat Black,' bandaged since being powerbombed into a flaming dumpster by Torch weeks earlier; treated here as Pat Black. Large portions of the match took place backstage (boiler room, loading dock) - treated as fresh live content, not archival replay, per the brief.

matches.stipulation: NFW Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament Final
matches.note: With Montezuma reeling from a ringside spear by Nakita Dubov, Wylde hit a top-rope Frog Splash and pinned him at 13:43 to become the first-ever NFW Mid-Atlantic Champion. Dubov's ringside spear on Montezuma was payback for Raul's earlier ambush; Dubov had also powerbombed Raul through a trainer's table backstage minutes before. A large brawl involving Ryconik, Team Cuba, and security followed the finish.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: Both teams caught each other in simultaneous pin attempts after Lincoln McKinley leapt roughly 20 feet from atop a ladder for a Showstopper (Buff Blockbuster) on Calamity. The referee conferred with an official and ruled Calamity's shoulder was up before the three count, awarding the match and titles to Hellmachine. Earlier in the show, an outside pair calling themselves the Original ShowStoppers (Franky Fargo and Bradley Mueller), brought in by Calvin Carlton, attacked champions Ryan Connors and Lincoln McKinley during their interview segment over rights to the ShowStoppers name, leaving them bandaged going into this match. Hellmachine is managed by Doc Martina Martens.

matches.stipulation: Three-Way Dance (elimination-tag rules: two men in the ring at a time, tag to switch, first pinfall wins)
matches.note: Ares revealed a secret alliance with champion Bloodhunt mid-match, tagging him in and helping set up a pin attempt on Zane. Commissioner Craig Miles broke up the count, had security eject and handcuff Ares for the interference, and restarted the bout as Zane versus Bloodhunt alone; Zane then won with a sunset flip off the top rope. Referee Greg Herpin was thrown out of the ring by Ares mid-match and was briefly incapacitated. Before the bout, Roger Powell attacked Commissioner Craig Miles backstage with a bat over being denied a guest-referee spot in this match; security dragged Powell away. Miles had pre-announced a strict no-interference rule for this match.

matches.note: The Man in Black hit a top-rope powerbomb for the pin without even hooking the leg. Man in Black attacked Duk during ring introductions before the bell. He left the ring immediately after the pin without waiting for his hand to be raised, jogging straight up the ramp.

Poe delivered a top-rope 'Seventh Seal' Tombstone Piledriver to Benjamin for the pin. Castor Strife never appeared for his own match; 'Nevermore' was revealed as 'The Apocalypse' Gabriel Poe, accompanied by 'The Dark Lotus' Miso. With no Strife present, Poe instead attacked and pinned Strife's servant/valet Benjamin, who had come to the ring to introduce his boss.

Matthews trapped Wildstar's already-injured knee in a figure-four leglock hooked around the ring post until Wildstar tapped out. Matthews kept stomping Wildstar's injured knee after the bell had already rung, ignoring the referee's calls to stop.

matches.stipulation: Dog Collar Match
matches.note: DC Stratton ran in and hit McMillan with a steel chair, allowing a recovering Payne to touch the fourth and final ring post before McMillan could, winning the dog-collar match on the turnbuckle-touch rule. Billed on commentary as a special 'Dogs of War' dog collar match. Referee Chris Fusco was knocked out mid-match by an accidental Irish-whip collision and had to be revived before the finish could be counted. Both men bled heavily; the match featured chairs, a chain, tables, and a ladder.

matches.stipulation: Bar-Room Brawl
matches.note: Two unidentified masked men attacked a fading Knowles with a sledgehammer until Shawn Matthews ran them off; Knowles never got back up, so RAZE was declared the winner for being the one able to walk out. Staged as a remote/satellite segment at a Boston pub, not at the arena. Explicitly billed by commentary as having no pinfalls and no referee (Knowles turned one down); the rule stated on air was that the match ends when one man walks out the front door while the other is down. An unnamed, diminutive ally of RAZE's, nicknamed 'Mini-Knowles' by commentary, also interfered by kicking Knowles in the face.

matches.stipulation: Bunkhouse Brawl (qualifier for the 'Splinter Cell' Tag Team Championship final)
matches.note: After a top-rope German suplex sent Tornado and Calamity crashing through the ring canvas, the referee found Tornado's hand raised inside the wreckage and awarded the fall to Storm (Hurricane and Tornado). The card header lists the champions as 'HELLMACHINE (c)', but on air the ring announcer and commentary never use that name, introducing the team only as 'the Champions' and naming its members, Calamity and Sean Toombs, individually. Doc Martena Martens managed/accompanied Calamity and Toombs, carrying a velvet case referred to as 'The Girl.' No titles change hands in this qualifier; the winner advances to the Splinter Cell final later on the card.

matches.stipulation: Street Fight (qualifier for the NFW World Tag Team Championship)
matches.note: Frankie Fargo broke a baseball bat over Lincoln McKinley's head for the pin, immediately after Calvin Carlton's sister Shaniqua Carlton was low-blowed and kicked in the head and Roger Powell tried to run over her and Ryan Connors with the Powell Brothers' Jeep before security intervened. OSS (billed here as 'OSS', self-identified moments later in the broadcast as 'The Original Showstoppers') is managed by Calvin Carlton; the similarly named 'Showstoppers' (Connors and McKinley) are managed by Calvin's sister, Shaniqua Carlton. Calvin threw powder in Shaniqua's eyes and stomped her mid-match. OSS's win earns them a shot at Storm for the NFW World Tag Team Championship.

matches.stipulation: I Quit Match
matches.note: Stratton passed out during a headbutt-into-a-steel-chair exchange after Manson broke free of his own handcuffs (which Stratton had used against him); the referee called for the bell with Manson declared the winner. Manson then also locked Stratton's manager Neil Riddick in a modified tourniquet hold until Riddick verbally submitted. Neil Riddick interfered heavily throughout, including cuffing Manson with Manson's own handcuffs and attacking the referee, ring announcer, and timekeeper with a chair.

The masked 'Team Viper' interloper chair-shotted Adrenaline and the other ringside brawlers; Steel Viper then hit a Viper Bomb on Adrenaline for the pin and left with the belt and his masked ally before the referee could raise his hand. Shawn Matthews and a debuting Lethal Lex Taylor ran in mid-match and brawled with Tempesta's ringside entourage (Mister Redd, Dieter, Kata). Viper struck Matthews with the newly won title belt on his way out.

Ryconik reversed a Cuban Suplex attempt into a release Polish Suplex, then hit the Polish Hammer into a jackknife cradle for the pin. Billed throughout the show as Rick Ryconik's last-ever NFW match. Ryconik nearly missed the contract deadline; his daughter Vivian Ryconik signed the contract herself without reading it, which (per Quentin Sullivan) staked her own hair against the match. The winner's announcement additionally declares Armando Montezuma suspended from NFW as a result of the loss. Montezuma's entourage Raul and Cojones interfered (leg trip, powerbomb assist) before being ejected; referee Greg Herpin was briefly knocked out during the finishing sequence.

matches.stipulation: Splinter Cell (bamboo cage, barbed wire, hardcore weapons; win by both partners escaping through the cage door)
matches.note: After a tug-of-war at the cage door over a fleeing Brandon Mueller's legs, Frankie Fargo pulled Mueller back to safety; both members of the Original Showstoppers then escaped through the cage door together to win the titles. The Splinter Cell structure was a bamboo cage topped with barbed wire, containing sandpits (one filled with thumbtacks, one with mousetraps) and hardcore weapons. Manager Calvin Carlton was trapped inside the cage and repeatedly injured (foam-blinded into a mousetrap pit, later put through a table); Windy managed Storm at ringside throughout.

matches.stipulation: Two out of Three Falls
matches.note: Fall 1 went to Bloodhunt by pinfall, his feet illegally hooked on the ropes unseen by referee Greg Herpin. Fall 2 went to Southern by submission, via a double chicken-wing Cattle Mutilation. Fall 3 went to Bloodhunt by pinfall, reversing a Southern small package and grabbing a fistful of tights for the three count. Extensive interference throughout the final fall: Armando Montezuma attacked both wrestlers and referee Herpin with a golf club. An unidentified masked man (shown earlier in the broadcast blackmailing Bloodhunt over the safety of his valet Emily) then knocked out Herpin with a towel, hit Southern with a Halliburton briefcase, and afterward turned on the injured Bloodhunt with an armbreaker DDT and a legdrop onto the same briefcase before fleeing -- an apparent double-turn angle left unresolved by the end of the show. matches.finish: Atken hit a low blow before the bell, worked the leg, then delivered a brass-knuckle punch (with the knucks hidden in his tights) followed by a DDT for the pin.
matches.note: Phil Atken's manager, billed "Dick Dirkwood," accompanied him to ringside.

matches.stipulation: non-title
matches.finish: Joe pinned Lovemuscle after striking him with a concealed foreign object, but Cameron Cruise ran down waving the object for the referee to see; the referee reversed the decision and raised Lovemuscle's hand by disqualification.
matches.note: The post-match angle revealed Joe the Plumber and Cameron Cruise's exchange as a work: Kooter Michaels-Cruise and The Sailor Man both ran in during the ensuing brawl.

matches.finish: Red hit his "Ecstasy of the Agony" finisher for the pin after Tui, distracted by an argument with a ringside Kin Hiroshi, was caught off guard.
matches.note: Kin Hiroshi appeared ringside waving the NFW World Heavyweight Championship at Red throughout, to no effect; Red never acknowledged him.

matches.stipulation: ChickenWire Cage
matches.finish: Both men attacked the referee, who called for the bell with no winner declared; security separated them after the referee was knocked down trying to intervene.
matches.note: Miles opened Fargo's forehead using the chicken-wire cage itself before the no-contest was called.

matches.finish: Sean Stevens pinned DC Stark with the X-Factor after Dan Ryan powerbombed Stark on the outside.
matches.note: DC Stark appeared to injure his shoulder taking the finish; the recap frames it as the two teams' first meeting in NFW.

appearances.note: Interferes to reverse the Joe the Plumber/Lovemuscle decision, then cuts a promo turning down Joe's title-shot demand.
Runs in during the post-match brawl and chokeslams The Sailor Man.
Runs in swinging an oar during the post-match brawl; chokeslammed by Kooter Michaels-Cruise.
Appears ringside waving the NFW World Heavyweight Championship at Felix Red throughout the Tui match, ignored.

matches.note: Breaker charged and was caught with Dusk's Lights Out Superkick for the pin. Dusk's debut win; Jack Breaker is noted as returning to the ring after time away.

Both men tumbled to the outside and continued brawling, ignoring the referee's ten count; neither returned to the ring in time, so no winner was declared. Debut match for both men in NFW; text notes a 15-minute time limit is standard for NFW matches, though this finish was a double count-out rather than a time-limit expiry.

Tui escaped a dragon sleeper, hit a side kick, then a springboard 'Fiji Asai Moonsault' for the pin. David Tui's first NFW win. Immediately after, Powermaster charged the ring and began attacking Tui, but Felix Red made a surprise run-in save with a top-rope 'Van Daminator' before leaving without acknowledging the crowd.

After a series of double-team moves, Yori's '9-7-6' finisher on Joe the Plumber sealed the win. Debut of the tag team billed as Honey I Fucked Your Mom (Yori Yakamo Junior & Mittens T. Cat). Joe the Plumber's tag 'partner' is his plunger, credited only as 'Mystery Partner' in the segment title. Joe is referenced as the reigning Television Champion, but the title belt is stated as 'not on display' and not defended here. Segment ends with a debuting character, The Sailor Man, revealed as Joe the Plumber's former tag partner and rival, forcing Joe to sign a Television Title defense against Cameron Cruise for the next Crash TV.

NFW World Champion Kin Hiroshi ran in and swung his title belt at Felix Red, who ducked; the belt instead struck Billy Lovemuscle. A second referee slid in as Teresa Q covered the knocked-out Lovemuscle for the three count. Kin Hiroshi's interference misfired, accidentally costing his own intended target's team the match. Maggot chased Teresa Q from the ring afterward with a liquor bottle handed to him by a fan.

With Cruise laid out after Joe the Plumber broke a toilet-tank lid over his head at ringside, Rocko Daymon hit a top-rope frog splash for the pin. Rocko Daymon's NFW debut, in his first meeting with Cameron Cruise; both men were accompanied by their wives (Caitlyn Daymon and Mercedes Cruise). Referee for the match is named as Bruce Phillips, working his first match since (per commentary) 'the Ultratitle Championship match between Nova and YYJ.'

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Jul 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After a distraction from manager Dick Dirkwood, Atken hit a low blow with brass knuckles hidden in his tights followed by a DDT for the pin. Short, cheating-heavy debut win for Phil Atken, accompanied by manager Dick Dirkwood.

Joe the Plumber won the pin after striking Lovemuscle with a hidden foreign object, but Cameron Cruise ran in afterward holding the weapon, and the referee reversed the decision, awarding the match to Lovemuscle by disqualification. Explicitly a non-title match despite Joe the Plumber holding the Television Championship. Cameron Cruise's interference and subsequent taunting of Joe sets up their upcoming Television Title match.

After a bloody brawl using the chicken-wire cage as a weapon, the referee called for the bell as security separated the two men; no winner was declared. Stipulation: Chicken Wire Cage. Fight opened before the bell as Miles threw a beer at Fargo; match stopped due to escalating violence and heavy blading, not a stated draw or no-contest.

With Nova on the outside, Dan Ryan set up Stark and hit an 'X-Factor'; Sean Stevens then made the cover for the pin. Stark and Nova's first time teaming together. DC Stark is reported holding his shoulder after the match, possibly injured by Dan Ryan; Nova protested that he was the legal man when the pin was counted.

With Tui distracted arguing with the interfering Kin Hiroshi, Felix Red snuck up behind him and hit his 'Ecstasy of the Agony' finisher for the pin. Kin Hiroshi repeatedly tried and failed to get Felix Red's attention at ringside throughout the match, ultimately costing Tui the win.

date.source: the document's own dateline (5 Aug 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Kooter Cruise hit a double-clutch neckhang Chokebomb on the Sailor Man for the pin. Segment title names only Cameron Cruise, but the actual match is a tag bout with Kooter Cruise as his partner, billed together as 'the Original Cameron Cruise Project.' Felix Red served as a distracted, lazily-counting special referee.

After an extended hardcore weapons brawl, Yori Yakamo Junior and Mittens T. Cat collapsed on Suicide Kings member DC Stratton for the pin. An extreme, heavily weapon-laden match; only one Suicide Kings member (DC Stratton) is individually named in the text.

The bell sounded on the 15-minute time limit while all three men were still trading offense; all three were credited with a draw. Stipulation: Triple Threat, Extreme Rules, No Disqualifications, No Countouts. Commentary attributes a sloppy start to jet lag and a tight travel schedule for Daymon and McKail.

Rook Black had Hunchblack locked in a chokehold ('Gauntlet Throwdown') but refused to release it when the referee began a count; the referee awarded Hunchblack the match by disqualification. Rook Black is described as noticeably colder and more clinical than usual, and appears genuinely confused when asked about the decision afterward -- flagged as a possible character shift.

Kin Hiroshi refused to tag into the match at all, eventually leaving the ring and departing the arena by limo, abandoning his partners; the match is left unresolved in the text. Six-man tag debuting both the Southern Baptist Coalition (Abraham & Jacobs, managed by Jimmy Davis) and The New VD (Johnny Styles & Johnny Rage). Hiroshi's walkout draws heavy crowd heat.

date.source: the document's own dateline (26 Aug 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Powermaster and Manpower accidentally clotheslined each other unconscious; Johnny Styles then hit a standing twisting moonsault across both men for the pin. MET-RX Express is the billed team name for Powermaster and Manpower. NFW staff are described handing out unidentified capsules and sugar cubes to the crowd during the match.

After a prolonged neck-targeted beatdown, Rook Black locked in his 'Crossbow' submission for the tap-out win. Billed as a mystery-opponent match revealed to be Clifford Hugo. 'Legion' is shown watching intently from the front row throughout -- his first appearance in the held record; he later references this Vancouver match directly in a Crash TV 41 promo.

Teresa Q ran in against Lovemuscle (out of personal dislike for him) with a leg lariat and chairshot to his knee; Atken -- annoyed by the unwanted help -- then locked in his 'Humiliation' Figure Four, and Lovemuscle passed out from the pain without tapping. Managed by Dirk Dickwood, who is chair-shot by an interfering Cameron Cruise-adjacent... actually attacked by Teresa Q's Northern Lights suplex through the broadcast table. Both Atken and Teresa Q are noted as also entered in the upcoming National Championship tournament.

The Sailor Man swung his oar at the injured Billy Lovemuscle (who had hobbled in on crutches) but hit him instead of Teresa Q; Teresa capitalized with her 'Process of Illumination' finisher for the pin. Billy Lovemuscle's injury from the Sailor Man's oar shot is reported as an ACL injury expected to sideline him for months.

Caitlyn Daymon slid a chair to Rocko, who used it for a double conchairto on Dan Ryan's head; the referee called for the bell over the illegal weapon shot, and Rocko, Caitlyn, and a revived David Tui then continued beating down Ryan until Sean Stevens ran in for the save. No winner is stated. Caitlyn Daymon (Rocko's wife) provided the weapon; her involvement functions as ringside manager-style interference.

Kooter Cruise and Felix Red both ran in during the match's closing stages; the groggy referee explicitly signaled a no contest. Cameron Cruise is left laid out after the interference; Felix Red hit a top-rope Diamond Cutter.

As Hunchblack charged for a running senton, Rook Black ran in and chair-shotted him; despite the interference targeting Hunchblack, the referee still raised Hunchblack's hand as the winner. Rook Black appears to have intended to help Coral Avalon but the decision favored Hunchblack anyway, leaving Rook visibly confused; an angry Avalon then shoved Rook and stormed off.

Felix Red threw an undisclosed powder into both opponents' faces, knocking Mittens T. Cat out cold; he then hit his 'Ecstasy of the Agony' finisher on Yori Yakamo Junior for the pin. Main event; Felix Red and Kooter were on edge with each other after the earlier Cruise/Maggot no-contest involving Kooter.

date.source: the document's own dateline (12 Sep 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: With the referee distracted, the Sailor Man's own oar was used against him by Atken, who then pinned him for the win. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.
After locking in the Pottstown Crab to wear Tui down, Maggot finished with his 'Trash Compactor' for the win. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.

After trading finishing sequences, Teresa Q slipped out of Hunchblack's Jackknife Powerbomb attempt and hit her 'Process of Illumination' for the win. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round. Hunchblack is noted as having had to miss a separate 'PTC Unification Match' to compete here.
Randalls reversed Avalon's 'Ratings Spike' attempt into 'The Devastator'; Avalon passed out from the move before he could tap. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.
Rook Black swatted away a Stevens dropkick attempt and connected with his 'Crossbow' submission for the win. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.

Dusk ducked a McKail clothesline and connected with a superkick for the pin. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round. Dusk is noted as wrestling his third match in three evenings, having been attacked by McKail from backstage before the bell.

Red escaped Daymon's Texas Cloverleaf attempt, blocked the Brain Rocker with a Spinning Heel Kick, then hit 'Shattered Horizon' for the win. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.
After a brawl through the crowd and outside the ring, Payne hit a Full Nelson Slam for the win. Main event; stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- First Round.

name: NFW Brawl 06: ROAD TO WRESTLESTOCK

date.source: the document's own dateline (7 Feb 2008), on the fed's own results archive

no_appearances_reason: Served mechanically from the fed's own archive; no per-show extraction has been done for this document.

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Mar 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Legion battered Bret Kelly around the ring and finished with a Curbstomp; the referee stopped the match rather than let it continue. Won via referee stoppage rather than a pinfall or submission, per the referee's own decision to halt the match out of apparent concern for Kelly's safety.

With Atken's manager Dirk having fled ringside after a recurring loud horn sound effect, Nova capitalized and rolled Atken up (with a slight, possibly accidental tights pull) for the pin. Manager Dirk seconded Phil Atken at ringside for most of the match before running off startled by the horn sound; the announcers debated whether the horn/Dirk business connects to a larger 'Mayfield' angle.
Impulse missed a 450 splash and was caught coming up by a Vertical Drop Exploder from Brock Alyas for the three-count. NFW debut match for both Brock Alyas and Impulse.

Rook won by countout after Legion, panicked by Rook hooking his fingers in Legion's nostrils and going for what looked like a tongue-rip, fled ringside and did not return before the count. Rook Black's attack referenced his past history with a character named Steve Christ, unnerving Legion enough to abandon the match. Teresa Q was in Rook's corner for this match.

After Nova ran in and chairshotted the Hyperspace Kid, Teresa Q hit her Cross-Arm Diamond Cutter for the pinfall. Announced same-day as the main event by Teresa Q herself over a backstage video segment ('Teaseresa Title Queue'), which passed over Legion (originally slated for a title shot) in favor of the Hyperspace Kid. Referee allowed the finish following Nova's interference/chairshot ('This is NFW, we don't brake for chairshots').

date.source: the document's own dateline (17 Mar 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After Alyas put Pollard through a ringside table loaded with sacks of potatoes with a Wrist Clutch Exploder, Alyas beat the count back into the ring at 13 while Pollard did not. Pollard was accompanied to ringside by his butler Jeeves; potato sacks were used as ringside 'weapons' throughout, tying into the show's 'Potato War' theme.

Cruise reached up, grabbed two handfuls of Atken's tights, and rolled him up for the three-count. Atken was seconded by manager Dirk, who fled ringside partway through after being startled by a recurring loud horn sound effect.

Ryan Oracle smashed a full-length mirror he had brought to ringside over Mike Gordey's head, allowing the Dream Team to win. Oracle had used the mirror as a ringside prop throughout his entrance and the match; the finish left broken glass on the mat.

Tremendous offered Impulse a $40,000 briefcase, which exploded with blinding powder when opened; Tremendous then hit a kick to the gut followed by a Spinning Fisherman's Buster for the pin. Tremendous cut a pre-match promo claiming 'the new regime' had approached him with a financial offer questioning Impulse's integrity. The announcers nicknamed the finishing sequence 'The Tremendous Plex.'

Ryan sidestepped a Rook charge, drove a shoulder into his gut, then finished with a long chokeslam followed by the Humility Bomb for the pin. A cautious, drawn-out match with both competitors receiving a standing ovation afterward; the announcers noted this was Ryan's title 'breathing' after a tense first defense against a game challenger.

date.source: the document's own dateline (17 Apr 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: A.D.D. finishes Justin Rose with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker for the pinfall, capping a one-sided dark-match squash. Billed as a 'dark match' with on-site bookies taking last-minute bets before it began; Justin Rose received no entrance music and unusual ring attire ('covered in eggs, tomatoes and small infants' per the recap).

Alyas has Felix Red pinned after a Double Underhook Sitout Bomb, but Madonna Wayne Grossard leaps in with a top-rope elbow to Alyas's head, drawing a disqualification win for Felix Red. Madonna Wayne Grossard (billed manager/valet figure) works the crowd and ringside throughout and costs Alyas the match via interference; Alyas is left enraged outside the ring afterward, pointing and making threats at Red.

matches.stipulation: Non-Title, 20-Minute Time Limit
matches.note: With seconds left on the 20-minute clock, Impulse misses a Shooting Star Press off the top rope; Teresa Q rolls him up for the pinfall at 19:45. Called a 'GREAT match' on-air; Impulse again falls short of his first NFW win despite a competitive showing.

After three consecutive turnbuckle powerbombs (including a top-rope 'Humility Bomb'), Dan Ryan re-applies the Texas Cloverleaf; Nova passes out, and referee Greg Herpin calls for the bell after raising Nova's arm three times and watching it drop each time — a referee stoppage rather than a verbal submission. Commentary frames this repeatedly as a 'career on the line' match for Ryan, though the text elsewhere states that stipulation belongs to the still-upcoming Wrestlestock 2 rematch — left the stipulation field blank rather than guess which contest it truly attaches to (see lane_notes). Dan Ryan retains the title. Immediately post-match, Craig Miles assaults the unconscious Nova at ringside and then backstage, ultimately leading him onto the official Wrestlestock tour bus.

date.source: the document's own dateline (3 May 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Steve Knox hit P. King Duk with the Gold Rush and pinned him. Steve Knox's NFW debut in this document's continuity; described as having new entrance music.

Legion hit Duane Skynyrd with a Package Piledriver for the pin. Charlie Crowe and Duane Skynyrd were billed together as 'Southern Remedy.' Skynyrd was helped to the back afterward but left under his own power.

Legion and Luci4 ran in and hit both competitors with repeated chairshots. When the referee tried to award Impulse the win, Impulse pulled the referee's arm down and refused the decision, insisting on 'NO CONTEST'; the referee ruled it a no-contest. Impulse and the Uber Judge then jointly fought off Legion and Luci4 after the decision was announced. Fans and other wrestlers speculate openly about the Uber Judge's identity (one guess offered is Kin Hiroshi) without resolution.

After Legion and Luci4 positioned themselves at ringside to distract him, James von Doom mistimed a top-rope leap; Brock Alyas caught him with the Wrist-Clutch Exploder and pinned him. Craig Miles offered Brock Alyas $10,000 to face von Doom via a Frontiertron promo; earlier in the match both men traded a simultaneous double-pin attempt that produced no winner. The cash envelope Alyas was given backstage afterward exploded into orange paint when opened.

date.source: the document's own dateline (10 May 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Mike Gordey pinned Legion with a Tiger Driver to win the three-way tag opener for the Dream Team, after Felix Red abandoned von Doom and the masked 'Uber Judge' ran in to attack Legion and Felix. A recurring masked interference character called 'The Uber Judge' ran in unannounced, beat down Legion and Felix Red with his gavel, then vanished into the crowd before the finish; the referee ('the zebra') is unnamed in the text.
Steve Knox hit the Gold Rush lariat on a diving Impulse for the pin after a long back-and-forth singles match.

The referee waved off the match after Felix Red ran in, attacked both men, and locked Marcus Price in the Felix Stretch, leaving Price convulsing; no official result is stated in the text. Felix Red's interference and Price's resulting injury stopped the bout before a clean finish; treated as unresolved per the brief since no draw/no-contest is explicitly declared.

After hitting Pollard with a fameasser (the 'Dying Star Drop'), Nova began repeatedly bludgeoning him with the title belt; the bell rang repeatedly and security had to separate both men without a clean decision being announced. Nova is shown clutching/cleaning the belt as the show closes and Pollard is carried out bleeding, but the text never states a winner, a draw, or a disqualification, so both fields are left null per the brief; Nova retains the title by default since no change is stated.

date.source: the document's own dateline (17 May 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Impulse hit a missile dropkick off the top rope on Cameron Cruise and covered him for the pin to score his first NFW singles win, while James von Doom had rolled to the outside after a flurry of near-falls. Luci4 ran in to attack James von Doom mid-match; von Doom eye-poked her in retaliation before being pinned in the closing stretch.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Elimination

eliminations.note: Pinned with an Exploder Suplex after James von Doom and Luci4 ran in and were both cleared out by Alyas.

matches.note: After eliminating Legion, Brock Alyas dominated Steve Knox until Knox rolled him up for a surprise pinfall win. James von Doom and Luci4 interfered mid-match and were both dispatched by Brock Alyas; Alyas argued with the referee after the loss and Insurgent Security intervened.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: Rayne climbed to the top of the steel cage and hit a Fiji Splash on Calvin Carlton for the deciding pinfall in this six-person cage match. Billed in the segment heading as 'HWC w/ Calvin Carlton vs. Suicide Kings w/ Rayne' (implying Carlton and Rayne were valets), both ultimately competed as full in-ring participants. Blaine Hollywood and Malik Anderson are shown wearing four title belts and are threatened by Craig Miles with being stripped if they don't enter the cage promptly, but the text never states this match itself was a title defense, so title/title_change are left null; Crash TV 45 (aired 2008-06-15) later confirms via recap montage that Hollywood/Anderson remained tag champions afterward, consistent with no title change occurring here.

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Jun 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Pinned with the Tremendous Plex (Spinning Fisherman's Buster) after special guest referee Jason Payne hit Hart with a Paynekiller.

matches.note: Professor Tremendous pinned Shawn Hart with the Tremendous Plex to score the first qualifying elimination of the nine-man gauntlet. Jason Payne served as special guest referee for the entire gauntlet and knocked out a 'Colonel Sanders' cameo with a Paynekiller before the bout began.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Rossi stole the pin after Doctor Curiosity hit Tremendous with a Shining Wizard.

matches.note: Rossi covered a Shining Wizard-downed Professor Tremendous for the pin, denying Doctor Curiosity the elimination credit he had set up. A masked man in a 'Tricky Dick' Nixon mask emerged from under the ring twice to attack Doctor Curiosity from the apron; referee Jason Payne did not see it.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Rossi held Phoenix's legs down to assist the pin; referee Jason Payne controversially ruled the credit split as a 'half elimination' each for Curiosity and Rossi rather than a clean elimination for Curiosity alone.

matches.note: Doctor Curiosity pinned a groggy Jay Phoenix with Rossi's assistance holding him down, though referee Jason Payne split the elimination credit between the two of them. Masked interferers struck repeatedly: a 'Tricky Dick' Nixon mask attacked Jay Phoenix with a chair, and a Ronald Reagan-masked man shoved Rossi into the ringpost; Phoenix appeared to suffer a possible concussion after being rolled up for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Pinned with the Locomotive Yakuza Kick; Rossi finishes his gauntlet run with a stated total of 1.5 eliminations, the most of anyone eliminated so far.

matches.note: High Flyer knocked out Andrew Rossi with the Locomotive Yakuza Kick for the pin, eliminating him and qualifying for the Grand Prix. A man in a Ronald Reagan mask interfered from under the ring again, later hitting High Flyer with a low blow-assisted 'Ronninator' (Van Daminator) before diving back under the ring; referee Jason Payne chased him unsuccessfully both times.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Pinned with a Shining Wizard while Flyer had Doctor Curiosity trapped in the Peaceful Slumber submission; Flyer had already qualified in the prior bout and remains qualified despite this elimination.

matches.note: Digital Mortality capitalized on the chaos to pin High Flyer, earning his own Grand Prix qualification. A masked interferer disguised as Bill Clinton (unmasked mid-scene to reveal a JFK mask underneath) attacked ringside again during this segment before being chased off by referee Jason Payne.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Pinned under a triple pileup after Curiosity hit an illegal Shooting Star Press using metal plating smuggled inside a vest handed to him by a masked 'Dick Cheney' interferer. Referee Jason Payne discovered the cheating afterward and ruled the elimination credit split between Curiosity and Sars rather than awarded outright to Curiosity.

matches.note: Doctor Curiosity pinned Digital Mortality under a triple pile using an illegal weighted vest; Jason Payne caught the cheating afterward and split the elimination credit between Curiosity and Sars. A masked man in a Dick Cheney mask handed Curiosity the loaded vest from under the ring; Payne tore the vest apart after the pin and then big-booted Sars in the head out of apparent personal dislike.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet
matches.note: No fall occurred in this segment. The masked 'G-Dubya' entrant attacked referee Jason Payne, who unmasked him in stages (revealing a John McCain mask underneath, then the wrestler's own face) before the man declared himself and was knocked down by Payne. The masked man revealed here is gauntlet entrant 'The Illustrious' FaceEater in disguise, unmasked on-camera as 'Adam Dick.' The next Credits segment picks up as a standard three-way with him now openly in the match; this entry is kept separate since it carries its own Credits heading despite containing no clean fall.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet

eliminations.note: Pinned after roughly 90 minutes in the gauntlet without ever scoring a clean elimination of his own; despite this, the text states Curiosity ultimately does qualify for the Grand Prix on the strength of his two prior half-elimination credits.

matches.note: 'The Illustrious' FaceEater broke up Sars' loaded-fist attack on Doctor Curiosity, tossed the weapon aside, and pinned Curiosity himself to eliminate him from the gauntlet. A masked man in a black trenchcoat (later revealed as Big Bill Judo) interfered repeatedly, tripping Curiosity off the top rope; Sars used a loaded fist ('Sars Knucks') in the closing stretch.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier Gauntlet
matches.note: Sars hit the Killing Joke on FaceEater for the pin to win the final gauntlet bout and qualify for the Grand Prix. Big Bill Judo, unmasked here as the trenchcoat man who had been aiding Sars all night, was clotheslined by referee Jason Payne with a Paynekiller after the bell; Sars pretended not to know Judo, laughing at ringside.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Jul 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The recap gives no specific finishing move; it is played entirely as a one-sided squash with Noble dominant throughout against the winless journeyman Kelly. Comedic recap deliberately withholds match detail; no discrete finishing sequence is described.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: Professor Tremendous's ringside appearance distracted Digital Mortality, letting Doc Curiosity hit a reverse DDT followed by the Schrodinger's Smack for the pin. Professor Tremendous is credited as Curiosity's 'partner in academia' for the distraction.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: SARS hit his 'Killing Joke' front-face-lock DDT and followed with a 360 Shooting Star Press off the top rope for the pinfall.

A group of decoy wrestlers dressed as the Uber Judge lured Legion into a brawl outside the ring while the real Uber Judge slid back inside before the referee's twenty count, giving him the win by countout. After the decision, Legion attacked the decoy Judges and the real Uber Judge with ringside chairs as security intervened.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: Pollard was awarded the win by disqualification after Illustrious Face Eater ignored a referee warning and struck him with a steel chair. Face Eater was restrained and dragged off by Cojones Mercado and security afterward, shouting that he was 'not supposed to stay here.' Segment header billed him as 'I.F.E.'; body text calls him 'Illustrious Face Eater' and 'Facey' throughout.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series, 30-minute time limit
matches.note: Both men were exhausted after nearly 30 minutes of action; when Simply Beautiful missed a late legdrop, the time limit expired before either man could capitalize, and the match was ruled a draw.

Kin Hiroshi interfered at ringside with a megaphone shot to Alyas; Cameron Cruise then hit his 'Reality Check' reverse flatliner for the pin. Cruise saw the replay of Hiroshi's megaphone shot on the Startron after the bell and reacted with disgust rather than celebrating.
Teresa Quaranta reversed a Frankensteiner attempt into a falling powerbomb, then hit her 'Process of Illumination' finisher for the pin to retain.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: Impulse ducked High Flyer's 'Locomotive' running yakuza kick and rolled him up for a surprise pinfall. Doctor Curiosity interfered at ringside with a steel chair mid-match but both men dropkicked him simultaneously before returning to the ring.

matches.stipulation: NON TITLE
matches.note: The match spiraled into ringside interference from Brock Alyas and Cameron Cruise; Hiroshi retrieved the actual World Heavyweight Championship belt from under the ring and fled the arena in a cab, resulting in a countout win for Nova. Brock Alyas ran in seeking his own confrontation with Hiroshi; Nova press-slammed him and drove him through a table with a back body drop. Cameron Cruise watched the aftermath from the exit without intervening. The belt itself was not defended since the match was billed non-title.

date.source: the document's own dateline (27 Jul 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: SARS connected with the Killing Joke DDT for the pinfall after Face-Eater had earlier kicked out of an Exploder wristlock counter.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: Doctor Curiosity distracted Digital Mortality from the entrance ramp, allowing Professor Tremendous to hit the Tremendous Plex for the pin. The distraction set up a post-match brawl between Doctor Curiosity and Impulse, and between Curiosity and High Flyer backstage.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series
matches.note: High Flyer hotshotted Simply Beautiful throat-first on the top rope off a charging lariat attempt, then hit a kick to the gut and an underhook brainbuster for the pin.

Zan Diego and Nakita Dahaka (F.A.T.E.) hit a double chokeslam on both members of Southern Remedy for the win. F.A.T.E. remained in the ring afterward and refused to leave, prompting the following Legion/Luci4/James von Doom segment.

A man in a Koopa Troopa costume interfered, smashing James von Doom with his shell; Steve Knox capitalized with a suplex, then tagged in a surprise partner, Kooter Michaels-Cruise, who hit a Vader Bomb on von Doom for the pin. Craig Miles swapped Steve Knox's expected partner, The Codemaster, for Kooter Michaels-Cruise at the last moment. The interfering Koopa Troopa was later chased down and knocked out by The Codemaster, then handcuffed by Insurgent Security on Miles's orders, tying into the show's 'Kill the Koopa' theme.

Helga interfered, shoving and attacking Teresa Quaranta from behind after Quaranta fought off Phil Atken; the match was awarded to Quaranta by disqualification. Cameron Cruise walked out of the match in disgust before the finish. Dirk Dickwood and Helga were at ringside as Phil Atken's manager/valet.

With the referee knocked unconscious, Cameron Cruise ran in and hit Kin Hiroshi with the stolen World Heavyweight Championship belt; Alyas then made an unofficial three-count on Hiroshi with no referee present, so no decision was rendered. Alyas immediately attacked Cruise and the brawl spilled backstage, where Hiroshi chairshotted Alyas and fled with the title belt. Craig Miles subsequently added Hiroshi, Cruise, and the Devil's Rejects to the Frontier Stampede match; Alyas was left out.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series; Pollard's 'Diplomatic Immunity' status in effect
matches.note: Felix Red intentionally struck himself with a steel chair, then tossed the chair to Lord Coyner Pollard, who was caught holding it by the recovering referee and disqualified. Pollard's butler Jeeves interfered throughout (holding ropes, striking with a chair). Afterward, El Presidente Eddie Mayfield ruled on the Startron that Felix Red's Grand Prix points would stand for exposing the loophole in Pollard's Diplomatic Immunity, while awarding Pollard a consolation point for Felix's underhanded tactics.

matches.stipulation: Frontier Stampede: Koopa hung on a hook inside a chicken-wire cage; elimination by leaving the cage, pinfall, submission, or failing a standing ten-count; B.Y.O.B. (Bring Your Own Blank) weapons rules in effect

eliminations.note: An outside participant brought in specifically for this spot by Craig Miles; hit a splash that 'popped' Koopa's shell for the elimination.
Exited the cage voluntarily alongside Codemaster after helping eliminate the Koopa, described as 'their job done.'
Exited the cage voluntarily alongside Craig Miles after helping eliminate the Koopa.
Eliminated via a Demolition Derby Elbow Drop after being cut up by Legion.
Eliminated together with Legion, Luci4, and Helga when Knox and Kin Hiroshi pushed a pile of grappling wrestlers off the top of the cage, crashing through two tables outside.
Eliminated in the same six-person pileup off the top of the cage as Steve Knox, Luci4, and Helga.
Eliminated in the same pileup off the top of the cage as Steve Knox, Legion, and Helga.
Kicked open the cage door mid-match and chokeslammed several wrestlers before being eliminated in the same pileup off the top of the cage; not one of the nine originally announced participants.
Knocked unconscious with a chloroform-soaked rag ('Cruise Chloroform') after the two faked a handshake.

matches.note: Cameron Cruise faked a handshake with the final opponent, Kin Hiroshi, then knocked him out with a chloroform rag, winning via standing ten-count as the last man able to answer. Cruise left without acknowledging the crowd. The source's elimination numbering is internally inconsistent (it labels the four-way simultaneous elimination of Knox, Legion, Luci4, and Helga with only three numbers, '#5, #4/#3'), reproduced here as best interpreted; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Series, 30-minute time limit
matches.note: The match reached its 30-minute time limit while Impulse had Doctor Curiosity locked in a deepened Ankle Lock in the center of the ring; the bell sounded before a submission could be forced. High Flyer interfered heavily on Impulse's behalf throughout (rope shakes, an eye poke, distracting the referee). Craig Miles announced afterward that this result, combined with the Grand Prix standings, sets up a 5-on-5 Grand Prix elimination tag match at Crash 46: Group A (High Flyer, Impulse, Felix Red, Lord Coyner Pollard, with Diplomatic Immunity) vs. Group B (SARS, Professor Tremendous, Digital Mortality, Illustrious Face-Eater, Doctor Curiosity).

date.source: the document's own dateline (12 Oct 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: James von Doom ran in from the crowd and chair-shotted Tsunami, then fled; the referee, believing Legion had swung the chair, called for the bell and awarded the match to Tsunami by disqualification. Heavy pre-match and in-match interference: Blaine Hollywood attacked DC Stratton with a dragonboat paddle, Rayne broke up the ensuing chaos with a fire extinguisher, and Malik Anderson/Calvin Carlton also ran in. Von Doom's late chair shot on Tsunami is what actually drew the DQ call against Legion.

matches.stipulation: No Holds Barred
matches.note: Von Doom wrapped his fist in duct tape over broken glass and street debris and battered Koopa until the referee stopped the contest. Match was arranged on the spot after Koopa challenged von Doom following a taunting video package; Koopa briefly got stuck trying to exit the ring through the ropes.

Pollard baited a distracted Bojangles into hitting the referee, then hoisted him for the Boleyn Driver for the pin. Bell rang before either man was ready, and the match played out as an impromptu street fight; the referee warned Bojangles about using a closed fist.

After Doc Curiosity's run-in backfired into a low blow on Flyer via Impulse's drop-toehold counter, Impulse followed Flyer through the ropes and hit a Superkick for the three count. Doc Curiosity ran in mid-match, apparently targeting Impulse ahead of an expected SUPERCRASH meeting; an incensed Flyer chased Curiosity backstage after the match.

Cruise reversed a second Shipwreck (Cradle Piledriver) attempt into a bridge, but Knox escaped and connected with the Gold Rush Lariat for the pin. Impromptu title defense granted after Cruise demanded a shot in Nova's absence. 'Voodoo' von Doom and Legion both ran in mid-match; Cruise tore apart the ringside area afterward in frustration at the finish.

name: NFW Brawl 17: Road to SUPERCRASH 2

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 Oct 2008), on the fed's own results archive

no_appearances_reason: Served mechanically from the fed's own archive; no per-show extraction has been done for this document.

matches.stipulation: Battle Royal for National Championship
matches.note: The card's only match, a battle royal of "a little more than a baker's dozen" for a shot at Steve Knox's National Championship, over the top rope to the floor with weapons allowed. Ivan von Doom, the Horny Mathematician and "a couple others that we're not going to mention" also entered and are not in the sides. Late in the match Jeeves hit Alexandria Malone with a serving tray; Lord Coyner Pollard, flanked by Insurgent Patrol, entered late, hit her with the Boleyn Sisters Driver and threw her out to win the title shot. Steve Knox then ran in and hit him with the two titles.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Feb 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: McGee hit the Union Buster (Go 2 Sleep) on the imposter billed as 'Impulse' for the three count. The real Impulse watched ringside during the match without wrestling; after the bell, yet another masked 'Impulse' attacked the loser backstage-adjacent with a shovel. McGee had opened the segment picketing new NFW president Eddie Mayfield before his microphone was cut off.
Dos Equis finished La Estrella with a double stomp off the apron (the 'Bulimia Nervosa Bomb') followed by a double underhook brainbuster (the 'Hangover') for the pin.

Tarano dominated from the bell and planted Duk with the Bull Rush for an academic three count. Tarano continued attacking Duk after the bell; the referee threatened a reversal/disqualification before he stopped.

After his parents/managers interfered to daze Kooter, Atken rolled him up while grabbing a handful of tights for the three count. Atken's parents/managers Dirk and Helga Dickwood interfered at ringside — Dirk was warned by the referee for goading the crowd, then Helga lawn-darted him into Kooter on the middle rope and later hit Kooter with a steel chair, setting up Atken's rollup pin.

After Legion and Turkington brawled and Cosmo Kid took high-flying shots at both, Turkington landed a right hand with something concealed in his fist on Cosmo Kid and pinned him with a handful of tights.

Doc Curiosity's ringside run-in with the Curious Hammer distracted Flyer as he went for his finish, letting Rook duck the Yakuza Kick and land the Gauntlet Backhand for the pin. After the bell, Curiosity attacked champion Rook Black with the Curious Hammer until Flyer pulled him off with a DDT, leaving Flyer and Curiosity in a tense standoff.

Cojones Mercado and the Insurgents ran in and chairshotted Impulse and Felix Red; Quaranta then hit a Shooting Star Press on Impulse and the referee counted the pin under Mercado's demand. Quaranta appeared uneasy about how the finish came together.

After Brock Alyas ran in and took Cruise out with a fireman's carry into a running DVD (the 'Ninth Mile Exploder'), JTP capitalized on a staggering Cruise with the Shit River Plunge for the pin. The physical World Heavyweight Championship belt itself was not present ringside, described as 'still in the new regime's possession'; the bout is nonetheless framed by the show as JTP's first title defense. Brock Alyas' run-in follows a cold-open vignette depicting his release from prison.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Feb 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The Cosmo Kid caught Dos Equis in a forward rolling cradle for the three count. Dos Equis' claimed tag partner never existed (he mimed high-fiving thin air); the referee ruled it a handicap match against Chambers and Cosmo Kid. First round of the 8-team tournament to earn a shot at Legion & von Doom.

Brock Alyas tossed Tornado out early and hit Hurricane with an Exploder suplex for the pin, without Kooter ever tagging in. Second first-round tournament match; Alyas left the ring without acknowledging his own partner Kooter.

Impulse locked in an ankle submission on IROC, forcing an immediate tap out. Manager Leroy Brown (billed as 'the Brotha from Anotha Motha') accompanied The SST ringside; third first-round tournament match.

Helga smashed P. King Duk's own kendo stick over his head at ringside while the referee's attention was on a tag-legality dispute; Teresa Quaranta then pinned the incapacitated Duk. Fourth first-round tournament match. Dirk Dickwood and Helga (Phil Atken's family) worked the outside interference.
Brock Alyas hit the Ninth Mile Exploder Suplex on The Cosmo Kid for the pin just as Chris Chambers dove in a split-second too late to break it up. Tournament semifinal.

Rook Black hit a Gauntlet Backhand on Phil Atken for the pin while Impulse simultaneously dropkicked Teresa Quaranta outside the ring. Tournament semifinal. Legion and Luci4 (unbooked) surrounded the ring and interfered; Legion swung a barbed-wire 2x4 at Teresa Quaranta but Phil Atken took the shot for her. Legion fled when confronted by Helga.

Impulse hit a superkick on Kooter Michaels-Cruise for the pin after Brock Alyas abandoned his partner mid-match in frustration. Tournament final; Rook Black and Impulse win the 8-team tournament, earning the right to face Legion & von Doom plus a tag title shot at the EMT Champions.

Before a formal bout could develop, Legion viciously attacked his own partner von Doom with a chair and a curbstomp, badly injuring him; Rook Black and Impulse then arrived, and Impulse superkicked Legion out of the ring as the bell rang for the win. Stipulation from the show's framing: if Legion or von Doom were pinned, that man would be out of NFW. The finish is chaotic and non-traditional -- it is not fully clear from the text whether the pin was recorded on von Doom; the document does not spell it out explicitly. Insurgent Patrol then swarmed the ring; Impulse superkicked Cojones Mercado through a broken chair seat. Afterward Teresa Quaranta chairs Legion and hangs him with barbed wire, revealing Luci4's 'burial in Canadian cement' and her own on-camera 'Grudge' tape were both faked.

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Feb 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Dos Equis hit a Beersteiner followed by a Springboard Bulimia Nervosa Bomb for the pin. Dos Equis again wrestled as though accompanied by an invisible tag partner.
Felix Red hit the Ecstasy of the Agony for the pin. Cary Turkington wrestled visibly, heavily intoxicated throughout.
Rook Black hit the Gauntlet Throwdown for the pin. Eddie Mayfield appeared via video to thank Rook Black for 'erasing the New Frontier of Wrestling from all things von Doom.'

The match was thrown out (Teresa Quaranta awarded the win by disqualification) after Legion and Luci4 stormed the ring and attacked her. Devil's Rejects (Legion & Luci4) interfered on Teresa Quaranta, then a masked 'Impulse' impersonator attacked her with a chair; the real Impulse fought off the impersonator and the Rejects. Cojones Mercado then appeared on the video screen to announce a same-night Legion vs. Impulse match.

matches.stipulation: Insurgent Bootcamp match
matches.note: Impulse hit the Sudden Impact Superkick for the pin after Teresa Quaranta cut Legion's forehead open with a scalpel at ringside. Cojones Mercado, citing a 'Presidential Decree,' announced this match on Legion's behalf and sent an enforcer named Raul to referee-adjacent ringside duty. The Insurgent Patrol, Teresa Quaranta, Luci4, and the fake 'Impulse' all interfered at various points.

Joe the Plumber hit the Tiger Driver ('Shit River Plunge') for the pin. Cameron Cruise appeared mid-match to reveal he was the one who had Brock Alyas arrested (called the police on him), distracting Alyas at the critical moment.

date.source: the document's own dateline (5 Apr 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Brock Alyas ran in from the crowd and cracked a chair over Cameron Cruise's head while the referee's back was turned; Dos Equis crawled over to make the pin. Dos Equis' 'Futurequis' (billed as a future version of himself) accompanied him to ringside but did not wrestle.

High Flyer busted Steve Knox open with a chair shot, drawing an immediate disqualification. High Flyer unilaterally declared this a 'Triangle Match for the NFW Television Championship,' using a chair with a 'Fakepulse' mask duct-taped to it as a stand-in third combatant ('Chairpulse'); this was not a sanctioned stipulation, so no title is recorded. Post-match, High Flyer struck himself with the chair repeatedly and stared at the mask -- foreshadowing the later Crash 47 reveal that he is the Fakepulse impersonator.

Joe the Plumber forced Shawn Coppola to submit. Handicap match, one on two. Cojones Mercado had earlier threatened to strip the title unless Joe 'relinquished his claim.' Manager Michael Heenan was taken out at ringside by Joe using a toilet-bowl prop.

Impulse hit the Sudden Impact Superkick for the pin. Match arose spontaneously after Legion incited a crowd disturbance (feeding fellow crowd-worker Calamity liquor); Impulse challenged him on the spot for his newly won Television Championship.

date.source: the document's own dateline (19 Apr 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: During a ring-lights blackout, Futurequis was revealed to physically exist; Dos Equis collapsed onto the bloodied Shawn Coppola for the pin, with the intimidated referee making the count. Dos Equis was originally billed alone; Futurequis' physical existence had previously been ambiguous (implied hallucination). David Jericho was left in a wrecked table at ringside.
Teresa Quaranta hit the Process of Illumination (Cross-Armed Diamond Cutter) for the pin. Captain Conga's NFW debut.

Impulse hit an assisted spinning legsweep clothesline on Kooter Michaels-Cruise, and Rook Black followed with the Gauntlet Throwdown for the pin. Builds toward a scheduled National Championship match between Rook Black and Felix Red at a future event.

With Brock Alyas trapped in High Flyer's Boston Crab, the referee performed the three-arm-drop test and stopped the match; Cameron Cruise had struck Alyas' jaw with a steel-plated 'Coal Miner's Glove' just beforehand. Cameron Cruise's interference (revealed post-match to be a loaded, steel-plated glove disguised as a coal miner's glove) was the deciding factor.
Joe the Plumber hit the Shit River Plunge for the pin. A hard-fought main event; Legion came close to winning on multiple near-falls.

date.source: the document's own dateline (24 May 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Stratton finished P. King Duk with a package piledriver, billed as the 'Credit Crunch,' for an easy three count. Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld accompanied Stratton and berated the fans on the microphone before the match; Duk interrupted her promo, prompting the attack.

Atken hit a top-rope DDT and pinned Conga while illegally hooking his tights, aided by manager interference that had crotched Conga on the top turnbuckle beforehand. Atken was accompanied by managers Dirk and Helga; Dirk held down the middle rope to trip Conga and later tried following him up the turnbuckles, while Helga kicked and headbutted (with a Viking helmet) a dazed Conga at ringside. Multiple near-falls traded both ways before the finish.

Impulse (Randall Knox) hit a 'Sudden Impact Superkick' for the three count to retain the Television Championship. A scripted film sketch ('Bill Killed,' starring Problem Child and directed in-story by Castor V. Strife) was aired on the Frontiertron partway through, distracting Impulse and giving Turkington a brief flurry of near-falls before Impulse regained control and finished the match.

Vic Tarano hit a running knee strike ('Bull Rush Shining Wizard') on Dos Equis, and High Flyer immediately hooked a backslide for the three count. Suspended wrestler Luci4 ran in from the crowd mid-match to aid Cuatro-X and Legion, attacking the referee and diving onto Cameron Cruise, before the finish went the other way. Immediately after winning, High Flyer turned on his own pinfall victim Dos Equis, bludgeoning him with his bat and going for his mask until FutureQuis drove him off, suggesting friction within the winning trio.

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Jul 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: NFW Debut Showcase
matches.note: American Panda overpowered Duk with forearms, a big boot and a Gorilla/"Panda" Press, then finished with a top-rope-style neck move for the pin. Debut match for both American Panda and P. King Duk.

matches.stipulation: NFW Debut Showcase
matches.note: After a low blow, Mahogany hit the "Sex-Plex" (a bridging Fisherman's Suplex) for the pin. Debut match for both men; Scissors was jokingly dubbed "winner of Worst Haircut in NFW History."

matches.stipulation: Chaos Rules (no disqualification, no countout)
matches.note: As Legion's valet Luci4 climbed the top rope to attack Knox, Felix Red pulled her leg out from under her, crotching her; Legion turned into a rebounding Knox and was hit with the "Gold Rush Axe Bomber" for the pin. Felix Red and Steve Knox are both slated to face each other (and others) at Crash 50's Pentagram Match, making Felix's assist here notable ringside interference from a future rival.

Masters locked in a body-vice guillotine choke with a body scissors; Alyas never tapped but was knocked unconscious (his arm dropped three times), awarding Masters the win. Kelly Masters' debut match, filling in after Felix Red failed to answer Brock Alyas's open challenge.

Flyer planted a screwdriver in Dos Equis' tights and then deliberately allowed himself to be pinned by a Beersteiner. The referee discovered the screwdriver on Dos Equis afterward and reversed the decision, awarding High Flyer the win. This was a rematch/grudge continuation from Crash 49, where Dos Equis had pinned Flyer and driven his tag partner BatPulse through a table.

Problem Child went for his "A.D.D." finisher, but Impulse slid down his back and hooked him into "The Message" neckbreaker submission for the tap-out. Match was made spontaneously mid-promo after Problem Child insulted Impulse. Starshooter ran in and was hit with a Sudden Impact for his trouble; after Impulse won, Castor V. Strife ran in and brained him with the Television Title belt, prompting a surprise run-in save from a large security group ("National Guard") led by Rook Black.

date.source: the document's own dateline (8 Aug 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Captain Justice hit the "Holy Justice!" Powerslam on Skynyrd, setting up Ultrajira's top-rope "U-Crusher" splash for the pin. NFW debut for Monsters of the Pacific. Charlie Crowe was legitimately knocked unconscious with a broken nose in the first two minutes (via a clothesline/kick combo) and taken out by EMTs, leaving Skynyrd to absorb the finish alone.

Alyas hit the "EXPLODAH" exploder suplex twice, then pinned Kelly by standing on his chest after referee Greg Herpin warned him to make the cover. One-sided squash; Alyas mockingly offered Kelly free shots before finishing him.
Quaranta reversed Problem Child's "A.D.D." Spinning Tombstone attempt into a Victory Roll for the pin. Problem Child had to be forcibly escorted from the ring by security after the loss.

Von Doom finished Duk quickly with his "Commercial Break" finisher after roughly four minutes of one-sided offense. Squash match; von Doom cut a taunting promo afterward, which led into his impromptu match with Impulse.

Impulse reversed a submission attempt onto von Doom, who fled ringside and was counted out. Spontaneous match set up mid-promo after von Doom insulted the roster as drug addicts. Impulse is billed as NFW Television Champion and the segment header marks him "(c)," but the commentary itself is explicitly unsure whether the belt was actually on the line ("I don't know if the title is on the line or not"); title recorded as null per that ambiguity rather than assumed.

Panda hit a double-clutch Neck-Hang into a mist to the eyes, then a sitout Chokebomb, for the pin. Dominant squash win; commentary teases Panda as a wild-card entrant for the upcoming Crash 50 Bunkhouse Stampede.

The match dissolved into a mass brawl after Legion's valet Luci4 chairshotted the referee unconscious; her interference on Legion's behalf resulted in a disqualification win being awarded to Cuatro-X. Billed as a preview for the Crash 50 War Games match. Kooter Johnson and Cameron Cruise ran in for High Flyer's side; Unicorn Mask made a surprise save with a Singapore cane before being chair-beaten by Legion. The brawl continued backstage, causing enough property damage that the venue billed President Mayfield directly.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Aug 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The text never resolves this six-person match with a pinfall or submission; it ends mid-brawl (a beer bottle headbutt, a chokeslam block, a springboard dropkick exchange) and fades into a staredown between American Panda and Captain Justice, with security separating Ultrajira and FutureQuis outside the ring. Recorded per the brief's instruction to leave winner and result null when a match is simply never resolved in the text.

A chaotic no-rules brawl using chairs, a table and a timekeeper's bell; it ends when Kooter Johnson and Cameron Cruise run in, with Cruise attacking Alyas and Johnson choking Luci4 and boot-stomping Legion, apparently chokeslamming him through the table von Doom had been set up on. No pinfall, submission, countout or disqualification is ever declared in the text; recorded per the brief's instruction to leave winner and result null.

After a series of near-falls between all three, High Flyer accidentally kicked Problem Child, then turned into a Sudden Impact Superkick from Impulse for the pin. Immediately after the bell, Castor V. Strife ran in and attacked Impulse with the title belt, locking in a Camel Clutch; Unicorn Mask made the save with a DDT-style move on Strife, then was chairshotted from behind by Legion, sparking a mass roster brawl (Dos Equis, Captain Justice, La Estrella 100%, P. King Duk, FutureQuis and American Panda all ran out) that closed the show.

name: NFW Brawl 27: 2010 Opening Night in Philadelphia

date.source: the document's own dateline (27 Apr 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Castor hits a Director's Cut snap swinging neckbreaker and pins Saxon after a hard-fought debut showing from the rookie. Blanche Barnett interfered by holding the ropes during a cloverleaf; Kid Lifto tripped Saxon; Reno Stone distracted with darts on The Human Trashcan.

matches.stipulation: Special Exhibition
matches.note: Black works a full comedic 'match' against an unseen/imaginary opponent only he claims to see, ending when the referee rings the bell on what the text calls a count-out. The document's own result line reads 'RESULT: Double (or Single) Count-out'; mapped to a draw per the brief's double-count-out rule, though it is unclear whether a genuine second competitor existed to be counted out.

Not shown blow-by-blow; commentary recaps Flyer's arm being raised after brutalizing the Green Man, part of his ongoing crusade against masked wrestlers. Match itself is only summarized after the fact by Natrone Rice; Flyer delivers a post-match beatdown that draws out American Panda.

Flyer swings a chair he yanked from the referee, misses, and ricochets it off his own head, staggering into Impulse's Sudden Impact Superkick for the pin. Post-match Flyer attacks Impulse with the chair; American Panda runs in to brawl with Flyer; Dan Ryan then appears, big-boots Panda, and chokeslams Impulse through the mat (angle, not a match).

Stevens lands an X-Factor for the pin after a competitive main event. Post-match, Bloodhunt's wife Emily produces a newly-created 'PURE World Heavyweight Championship' belt, which Bloodhunt presents to Stevens and declares him the 'drug free' champion, demanding Olympic-style drug testing of any future challenger -- explicitly aimed at World Champion Joe the Plumber.

date.source: the document's own dateline (29 Apr 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Flyer hits a trio of piledrivers, a Brainbuster, and a Frog Splash for the pin. Opponent is a fan in a Cleveland Browns Dawg Pound mask heckling Impulse; effectively a squash the crowd could not bring itself to cheer.

After the original fifteen-minute time limit expired and Impulse demanded (and got) five more minutes, he ducks a green mist attempt and lands the Sudden Impact Superkick for the pin. An unscheduled, spur-of-the-moment title defense; afterward Castor V. Strife appears on the Frontiertron laughing maniacally, teasing unfinished business with Impulse.

Panda is counted out after Dan Ryan, blinded by Panda's own mist attack, accidentally chokeslams him outside the ring; High Flyer's interference (bagging Panda's head, then a Yakuza Kick) compounds the finish. Ryan is awarded the win but reacts with confusion and anger after seeing a Frontiertron replay of High Flyer's interference; fans turn on Flyer with 'FLYER SUCKS' chants.

matches.stipulation: British Rules (best of two falls/submissions/knockout/DQ, five three-minute rounds)
matches.note: In round five, Pollard's butler Jeeves smuggles him a loaded icepack after a ringside scuffle; Pollard knocks Legion out with it and pins him for the deciding fall, winning two falls to one. Legion won round two by submission (double-arm suplex); Pollard won round three by sunset flip/leg nelson; round four ended by the round bell with no fall; Jeeves interfered repeatedly throughout. Per the brief's 'staged-announced results stand' rule the cheap win counts.

Dos Equis and FuturEquis hit a tandem 'ace crusher from the ropes' (called the XXtreme XXecution) on Ultrajira for the pin after a long back-and-forth main event. XXXX is billed elsewhere in the held record as 'Cuatro-X'; no title was at stake.

name: NFW Brawl 29: Run for the Border!

date.source: the document's own dateline (10 Jun 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After a submission attempt and a top-rope '420 Splash,' Black covers and gets the three count. Comedic gimmick match against an inanimate steel ladder personified as a former Japanese indy champion; genuinely staged and officiated with a real referee, bell, and pinfall, so logged as a match per the brief.

matches.stipulation: 10-Man Battle Royal (entrants restricted to wrestlers under exclusive NFW contract)

eliminations.note: assisted by Bret Kelly; narrated as the match's first elimination despite appearing later in the recap's summary order
skin-the-cat elimination
both men went over together in a brawl; McGee held on

matches.note: Rich Mahogany hits an 'Iceman buttbump' on Mike McGee, the last man standing, to win the battle royal. Winner earns a Television Championship match against Castor V. Strife; per Mayfield's decree, entries were restricted to wrestlers under exclusive NFW contract, explicitly excluding Castor Strife and Impulse (both known for outside bookings) from competing. Castor sits ringside under Presidential order and golf-claps the finish.

Cuatro-X wins via disqualification after Brandon Mueller chairs FuturEquis and the referee, and Frankie Fargo crushes Dos Equis with a 'Double Chair Rocket Launcher Splash.' Dos Equis reportedly suffers cracked ribs and possible sternum damage from the finish, threatening to sideline the team.

name: NFW Brawl 30: A Left Turn at Albuquerque

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Jun 2010), on the fed's own results archive

city: University of New Mexico), Albuquerque, New Mexico

matches.note: McGee wins with a victory roll out of nowhere. DROIDARMY recap describes an unremarkable match, undersold by the crowd.

matches.stipulation: Diplomatic Immunity Rules
matches.note: Impala hits a Michinoku Driver, then locks in the 'Diplomacy in Action' Cross-Arm Chickenwing for the submission win. The referee allows Impala's servants to interfere/cheat without penalty under the 'Diplomatic Immunity' stipulation; the winner replaces the injured Tsunami in the National Championship 'Around the USA in 80 Days' tour field, and the loser (per Mayfield's earlier decree) also loses his NFW contract.

Stevens hits an X-Terminator for the pin after Alyas' early comeback burst fades under his ongoing drug-withdrawal struggles. Alyas' performance is framed around his real-time addiction/rehab storyline; manager Bloodhunt coaches ringside throughout.

matches.stipulation: Icepack on a Pole Match (six-man tag)
matches.note: After The Mighty Impala runs in from the crowd to lock a crossface chickenwing on FutureEquis, giving Pollard time to recover, Pollard hits a Dragon Suplex on FutureEquis for the pin. Originally announced as a singles Icepack-on-a-Pole match between Legion and Pollard, changed by the Executive Office to a six-man tag. Pollard's team also wins the right to determine initial seeding for the National Championship tour finale.

date.source: the document's own dateline (7 Jul 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Before a proper bell, Malik Anderson spinebusters the blind Joe the Plumber on the entrance ramp; Rich Mahogany joins the beatdown instead of helping; Castor V. Strife then runs in and piledrives Mahogany on the ramp; security intervenes and the bout is called off. Billed as a PURE Championship contender's match for JTP, still blind from being splashed with lye by Dorchester Stratton at NFW Reloaded 02; Stratton directs the beatdown from a luxury box via the Frontiertron. The text explicitly declares this 'a NO CONTEST.'

Bryant hits the 'Birmingham Breaker' backbreaker for the pin after Alyas re-aggravates an injury attempting a third snap suplex. Alyas shows signs of physical decline post-rehab (lost weight and strength); his first in-ring showing since Albuquerque.

matches.stipulation: Diplomatic Immunity Rules
matches.note: Ryan Humility Bombs Pollard through a ringside table, which is ruled a 'Diplomatic Immunity Infraction,' awarding Pollard the win by disqualification. Pollard's butler Jeeves recites absurd 'diplomatic' rules (no closed fists, mandatory time-outs, forcing Ryan to turn around on request) that heavily favor Pollard throughout; Ryan chokeslams Jeeves onto the concrete mid-match. Commentary calls it a 'hosejob perpetrated by the Executive Office' aimed at keeping Ryan from both the PURE and NFW World titles.

date.source: the document's own dateline (10 Jul 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Elite Championship Interfed Tournament, 1st Round
matches.note: Tchu hits a Dragon Suplex with a bridge for the pin after FuturEquis catches Flyer with a necksnap over the top rope. American Panda also attempted to interfere but was stopped by the referee. Post-match Tchu, from the PRIME promotion, criticizes NFW for allowing outside interference in a 'prestigious and global' title tournament.

matches.stipulation: PURE Title Contendership
