matches.note: Alyas rolls out of the way of Black's 450 Splash attempt, and covers Black for the pin. Both men passed PURE-mandated drug tests; a roughly 22-minute match with Alyas wrestling through a re-injured muscle from the Jack Bryant match in Cleveland.

Castor hits the Cult Classic (fireman's carry knee strike) for the pin. Fulfills Mahogany's title shot earned by winning the Boise battle royal; Blanche Barnett interferes for Castor during the match.

date.source: the document's own dateline (31 Oct 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat, Barbed Wire Steel Cage
matches.note: A surprise appearance by Dos Equis saw him climb the cage and hit a double-axehandle intended for Rook Black that instead landed on FutureQuis; Legion then hit Dos Equis with a Reverse DDT, and Rook Black capitalized by rolling up FutureQuis for the pin. Originally planned as a four-way National Championship match including Doctor Curiosity, but Curiosity was attacked and removed from the card beforehand by 'Thirteen', disguised as a cameraman, reducing it to this triple threat. Rook Black retains the title.

date.source: the document's own dateline (26 Nov 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: FutureQuis, increasingly unstable throughout the match, turned on his own tag partner Dos Equis: rather than complete a planned Doomsday Device on an opponent, he violently drove Frankie Fargo down in a splash across Dos Equis' body, allowing referee Greg Herpin to count the pin on Dos Equis. Post-match, FutureQuis continued the assault on Dos Equis, hitting a chair-assisted inverted brainbuster ('Chaos Theory') described as potentially having broken his ex-partner's neck.

Bryant attacked McGee before McGee could finish a pro-union speech/handshake offer, then finished him with the Birmingham Breaker for the pin. McGee had brought a pro-union picket sign to the ring and attempted to recruit Bryant to his cause.

The 15-minute time limit expired moments after Castor dumped Brock to the outside rather than completing a Cult Classic; Castor retains the title via time-limit draw, with Brock remaining the #1 contender. Heavy interference throughout from Blanche Barnett and the Triumvirate (Reno Stone, Kid Lifto, The Human Trashcan), including multiple chairshots to Brock's head. Brawling between Brock and the Triumvirate continued after the bell.

name: NFW Brawl 35: ROCKY MOUNTAIN MASSACRE TOUR!

date.source: the document's own dateline (2 Jan 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Atken tapped out to Bryant's Southern Cross Sharpshooter and referee Greg Herpin called for the bell, but Bryant refused to release the hold afterward; officials reversed the decision to a disqualification win for Atken due to Bryant's continued post-match assault. An unusual swerve finish -- the man who submitted (Atken) was ultimately awarded the match.

Impulse escaped a double wristlock exchange with Dan Ryan, floated behind Castor Strife, and hit Sudden Impact for the pinfall win. Both teams showed visible internal dysfunction (repeated blind tags on both sides); tension between Impulse's valet Calico Rose and Castor's valet Blanche also flared at ringside.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet (downgraded mid-broadcast to Triple Threat, then overrun by run-ins)
matches.note: The match ended with Legion arranging Rook Black, Doctor Curiosity, and Lord Coyner Pollard to simultaneously pin a fourth man, High Flyer, for a three-count; the referee declined to render this decisive and left the outcome/championship status to the NFW Executive Branch. Originally a six-man Gauntlet (Rook Black (c), Lord Coyner Pollard, Legion, High Flyer, Doctor Curiosity, The Mighty Impala); Impala was announced as a late scratch. Doctor Curiosity and his brother Eegor interfered disguised as nuns, prompting the ring announcer to declare it a one-fall Triple Threat (Rook/Pollard/Curiosity) mid-broadcast; Legion (with a chair) and a returning High Flyer then entered via unscheduled run-ins, further disintegrating the match's structure. Rook Black wrestled without the physical National Championship belt, which he had surrendered to a North Korean soldier during the 'A Black December'

name: NFW Brawl 36: ROCKY MOUNTAIN MASSACRE TOUR!

date.source: the document's own dateline (12 Feb 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: A mysterious figure known as '13' ran in and struck Doc Curiosity with a blackjack; the referee rang the bell for a disqualification, awarding the match to Doc Curiosity/Legion. High Flyer was ambushed and knocked unconscious backstage by Legion (with a fire hydrant) before the bell, so Rook Black wrestled the entire match alone against a 2-on-1 disadvantage. After the DQ, '13' also attacked Rook Black, suggesting he is aligned with neither team; the source text itself renders the winner declaration uncertainly ('Doc and Legion .. win?').

Castor Strife hit a Stun Gun (called the 'Cliche-Killer') off a superkick setup and pinned Cameron Cruise cleanly to retain the title. After the bell, Bobby Jack Windham and August De La Rossi attacked the fallen Cruise but were run off by the debuting Magnus (billed as NLW World Openweight Champion), revealed by commentary to be protection hired by Castor Strife.

matches.stipulation: Britannia Rules
matches.note: Shown as an encore. Pollard took the first fall with a roll-up in round 3, his feet on the ropes; in round 4 Bobby Jack Windham flipped off the referee and threw a low blow, and was disqualified: "The winner of the match, by disqualification... LORD COYNER POLLARD!" The Windham family stomped Pollard after the bell.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Apr 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Legion attacked Kelly before the bell and dominated throughout, aided by valet Luci4's ringside interference, finishing with a Super Brainbuster (the 'Ninth Gate to Hell') for the pin. The referee reportedly warned he might stop the match via knockout given the beating Kelly was taking; Kelly was stretchered out afterward.

Dan Ryan blitzed La Estrella 100% in well under two minutes with a big boot and a running Axe Bomber, then finished with a Humility Bomb for the pin. Billed by commentary as a severe size/experience mismatch; a very short squash match, not accompanied by the Windham Clan despite Ryan's new alliance with them.

Legion ran in and shoved High Flyer off the top rope to the floor; the referee disqualified Rook Black for the interference, giving High Flyer the win. The match was even for roughly twenty minutes before Legion's interference; Rook Black continued attacking Legion in the ring after the DQ. Rook Black retained the National Championship, as a title does not change hands on a disqualification.

matches.stipulation: Presidential addendum: Lord Coyner Pollard's Diplomatic Immunity privileges at stake
matches.note: After Lord Coyner Pollard used illegal 'Crown Jewels' brass knuckles that knocked out both men, and after Windham Clan interference (Troy Windham blinding Pollard with a spray, August De La Rossi and Problem Child attacking Jeeves), Impulse recovered first and hit a desperation Sudden Impact Superkick for the pin. Because Pollard lost, he loses the right to compete under Diplomatic Immunity rules or dictate match stipulations going forward, per the Presidential decree announced before the match. The finish triggered a mass all-champions brawl between the Windham Clan and the NFW roster that was broken up by security and the National Guard, leading into President Mayfield's address.

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 May 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Eric Dane dominated enhancement talent Barry Lawler and finished him with his signature Stardriver (a stalling brainbuster DDT). '(j.)' marks Lawler as designated enhancement/jobber talent brought in by the Windham Clan.

Deacon overpowered The Warbarian and finished him with a Crucifix Powerbomb he calls The Altar Call. Deacon was accompanied to the ring by Chris Shepherd. Bobby Jack Windham cut a post-match promo at Deacon on the Frontiertron.

Malik Anderson locked Bandit, whose arm was already injured, in the Anderson Armlock (a step-over armlock) for the submission win. The Everette Memorial Tag Team Titles, held by Hollywood and Anderson, were explicitly not on the line. Dorchester Stratton refused to tag in for most of the match and briefly left the ringside area before returning to throw punches. Calvin Carlton led Dynasty to the ring carrying their title belts; Jeeves accompanied Lord Coyner Pollard; Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld confronted Dorchester Stratton mid-aisle when he tried to walk out.

With Impulse dominating, Deville rolled out of the ring and screamed for referee Pee Wee Troutman to call it; Troutman waved for the bell and ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims declared the match a five-minute draw. Troutman, a referee hand-picked by the Windham Clan, gave Deville fast counts and Impulse slow counts throughout. After the bell, the Windham Clan (Peter Windham, Bobby Jack Windham, Bandit, plus local mercenaries) tried to jump Impulse until Castor Strife and Alex Austin ran in with chairs for the save; security then ejected Impulse from the arena and banned Strife and Austin.

Legion hit his finisher, the Six Million Dollar Drive to Hell; despite a Stalker boot to the head breaking up part of the count, referee Speranza's three-count stood and Legion was awarded the win. Stalker issued the open challenge himself but substituted Mr. Myers as his opponent without announcing the switch. After the bell, Stalker and Myers beat down Legion together; when Legion's valet LUCI4 tried to help, Stalker hit her with his Evenflow finisher.

date.source: the document's own dateline (10 Jun 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The match went the full twenty-minute time limit with no fall; commentary explicitly called the outcome 'an interesting draw.' Billed as 'Rook Black/???,' Rook's intended tag partner slot went unfilled after Peter Windham, the lone Windham Clan member present, was comedically knocked unconscious by a Mike Randalls chop feint before the bell; Rook then wrestled the match alone, 2-on-1, against Mike Randalls and Tsunami (billed together as The Dark Storm, managed by Rayne). Because no partner/challenger materialized, the National Championship was explicitly not defended in this match.

Eric Dane countered a Discus Clothesline attempt with a snap DDT, then pinned Hart while grabbing a handful of his tights for leverage, unseen by the referee. Hart protested loudly after the match, including trying to show the referee the tights Dane had grabbed.

With the referee dazed after being kicked in the jaw during the chaos, Stalker knocked Legion out with a chain-wrapped punch and hit a double-arm DDT; Mr. Myers then rolled Legion over for the pin as the recovering referee counted three. Stalker announced at the bell that he would not compete and Mr. Myers would take his place. After the match, Stalker's stable 'The Fallen' swarmed ringside, attacking Legion's valet LUCI4 and dragging the beaten Legion to the back; Deacon then chokeslammed Mr. Myers and stared down Stalker, who retreated. Deacon and High Flyer appeared to reconcile with a handshake, but Flyer immediately turned on him with a sneak locomotive-kick attempt that Deacon countered with a discus punch.

date.source: the document's own dateline (3 Jul 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The Dirty Rotten Scoundrels overwhelmed the challengers from the opening bell, hitting 'Murder One' on Bret Kelly and then on Mike McGee, landing McGee on top of Kelly for the pin. A hastily-arranged title defense (Mayfield 'scrambled' to find challengers) after DRS demanded a defense following their win over the Hollywood Wrecking Crew at Reloaded. Shaniqua Carlton entered post-match to berate Bret Kelly.

Dane hit the Stardriver (a stalling brainbuster DDT) on Peter Windham for the pin while August De La Rossi, seconding Windham, was distracted arguing with a ringside fan. Preceded by a promo in which Dane and, jointly, August De La Rossi and Peter Windham criticize the newly announced Grand Prix tournament's 235lb weight limit. Post-match, Dane also hit the Stardriver on August De La Rossi when he entered the ring, then fled through the crowd (kicking Bandit on the way) as JJ Deville, Bandit, Bobby Jack Windham and Christian Cruise ran in for a beatdown. Commentary notes Dane moves to 4-0 in NFW.

After several minutes of Bryant dominating and Deville stalling/fleeing, Deville grabbed his belt and retreated to the locker room rather than continue; referee counted him out. Preceded by an on-air apology promo from JJ Deville for his actions around Reloaded, in which he invites Bryant to an immediate rematch. Text states Bryant 'scored the win' by countout but does not explicitly declare a new champion; per standard wrestling convention a title normally does not change hands on a countout, and no new champion is announced in the text, so title_change is left null rather than inferred.

Legion appeared to have Mr. Myers pinned after a chair-assisted cover, but Stalker struck Legion with a barbed-wire chair before referee Scott Speranza's three-count landed; Speranza then jumped up 'frantically calling for the bell' as Stalker beat Legion down further. The text never explicitly declares a winner, a no-contest, or a disqualification despite the referee calling for the bell after the weapon interference, so winner and result are left null per lane rules. Luci4 attempted to run in for Stalker's side but was intercepted and driven into the ringpost by an unnamed man in ragged clothing, seemingly a Legion ally ('the FALLEN MEMBER'); his identity is not given verbatim so no appearance row was created for him.

matches.stipulation: National Championship Defense
matches.note: Rook Black hit the Gauntlet Throwdown for the pin. Tsunami, managed by Rayne (holding a kendo stick), reportedly grew rattled as the crowd chanted his name; commentary notes he seemed uncharacteristically drained of energy afterward.

matches.stipulation: #1 Contender's Match
matches.note: Christian Cruise delivered a 'Doomsday That's Entertainment Backcracker' with Blaine Hollywood and Malik Anderson to Bobby Jack Windham for the pin, credited to referee Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips despite him being 'wounded, weary and non-sliding' after earlier taking an accidental Windham Clan hit. Main event, contesting the #1 contendership to the NFW Everette Memorial Team Championship held by the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels. Preceded by an extended prayer-themed promo from the newly formed Chosen People (Bobby Jack Windham and Christian Cruise) targeting a young fan in the crowd. The decisive turn: Dorchester Stratton appeared at ringside and bribed Windham Clan enforcer Bandit with a briefcase described as being 'worth its weight in gold' (implied gold bricks); Bandit immediately turned on Christian Cruise and Bobby Jack Windham, blasting both with the briefcase and enabling the Hollywo

date.source: the document's own dateline (24 Jul 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: 'Wild Heat' Bracket Match (NFW Grand Prix)
matches.note: Legion hit his curbstomp finisher (the 'Six Million Dollar Drive to Hell') on Dr. Curiosity for the pin. Advances Legion to the Wild Heat tournament final. Commentary notes Dr. Curiosity is a former National Champion.

matches.stipulation: 'Wild Heat' Bracket Match (NFW Grand Prix)
matches.note: After Devine had eliminated P. King Duk from contention with a piledriver and nearly pinned Stalker, Stalker hit a snap DDT on Devine for the pin. James Devine's debut match for NFW, billed 'The Southern Psychopath.' Stalker's ringside allies interfered against Devine during the match. Advances Stalker to the Wild Heat tournament final against Legion.

matches.stipulation: Non-Title Four Corners Match
matches.note: Nova hit a jackknife pin on Bandit for a three count that the text describes as a 'somewhat suspicious quick' count from a referee who then rolled out of the ring looking frightened. Billed by commentary as a 'single elimination' format but the match resolves via a single pinfall with no in-match eliminations tracked. Rook Black's National Championship was explicitly not at stake. Adrian Willard, pursuing a bounty on Bandit, attempted to interfere late in the match (throwing a blinding powder at Mr. Myers) but was suplexed and knocked from the ring by Rook Black, inadvertently costing Bandit the match rather than helping collect the bounty. Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld, at ringside with Bandit, distracted the referee at a key moment. A large brawl involving Stalker's minions and the National Guard (Rook Black's ringside faction) also broke out during the match.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match (NFW Grand Prix 'Wild Heat' Tournament Final)
matches.note: Legion climbed the ladder and, after fighting off Stalker on top, drove Stalker's face into the top rung with a boot (his 'Six Million Dollar Drive to Hell') before retrieving the prize hanging above the ring, winning the match. Winner becomes the #1 contender to the PURE Heavyweight Championship, held by Bobby Jack Windham. Stalker attempted to substitute Mr. Myers for himself pre-match, but NFW officials disqualified Myers from competing after weighing him over an unspecified legal limit; Myers nonetheless interfered throughout as Stalker's second, at one point choking Legion. Luci4 (seconding Legion) and Myers were both ordered backstage under threat of a no-contest ruling, but Myers pursued her. Late in the match, a swarm of Stalker's minions overran the ring and trapped Legion in the ropes; Mike McGee and Bret Kelly ran in to free him, and a returning Nova chairshotted Stalker and c

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Jul 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Malik Anderson reversed a 187 chokeslam attempt into an Armbreaker and then the Anderson Stepover Armbar, forcing 187 to tap out. Billed as an 'enforcer vs. enforcer' grudge match between the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels' and Hollywood Wrecking Crew's respective seconds. Managers Calvin Carlton and Shaniqua Carlton interfered repeatedly for their sides, including a tennis-racket shot and a distraction that nearly cost Malik the match. Immediately after the pin, Blaine Hollywood ran in and handcuffed the injured 187 to the ringpost, setting up the next match.

Saafir Muhammed caught Blaine Hollywood in a fireman's carry cutter and pinned him. 187 remained handcuffed to the ringpost throughout, tended by medics. Malik Anderson and Calvin Carlton distracted the referee to help Hollywood during the match. Post-match, Malik Anderson blindsided Muhammed and Hollywood hit him with the 'That's Entertainment' backcracker; the Hollywood Wrecking Crew left with Muhammed laid out, and Malik tossed the handcuff key to Shaniqua Carlton.

matches.stipulation: 'Southern Heat' Bracket Match, Grand Prix Opening Round
matches.note: Levond Daniels hit a reverse tornado kick on Shawn Hart for the pin. Levond Daniels' first-ever NFW match, described as an 'unknown quantity' with a martial-arts background. Advances Daniels to the Southern Heat bracket final.

matches.stipulation: 'Southern Heat' Bracket Match, Grand Prix Opening Round
matches.note: Harmen powerbombed La Estrella 100% and locked in the Liontamer (an elevated Boston crab); Estrella tapped out several seconds after the hold was applied. Billed as Lowell's NFW debut. Lowell nearly stole a pin on Harmen mid-match via a double-team botch. Advances Harmen to the Southern Heat bracket final.

matches.stipulation: 'Southern Heat' Bracket Final, Two-Out-of-Three-Falls Three-Way (NFW Grand Prix)
matches.note: After the fall count reached 1-1-1 (Harmen submitted Lowell with the Flyerboard for fall one; Daniels pinned Lowell with a reverse tornado kick for fall two; Lowell rolled up Harmen off a Daniels dropkick for fall three), Harmen hit a frog splash on Daniels and covered him, but Lowell collapsed on top of the pile as the referee counted three; referee Greg Herpin then raised both Harmen's and Lowell's arms in victory. A genuinely confused, dual-winner finish: the text explicitly describes Greg Herpin declaring both Jack Harmen and Lowell winners simultaneously ('stood between LOWELL and JACK HARMEN and raised BOTH arms in victory'), with Levond Daniels the man actually pinned. The document itself calls this a 'decent sized ovation/WTF-ness' moment and leaves whether Harmen or Lowell actually advances in the Grand Prix unresolved, alongside 'Wild Heat' winner Legion.

date.source: the document's own dateline (21 Aug 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage Match
matches.note: Deville eye-raked Bryant atop the cage and leapt off, crashing through the ringside announce table; Pee Wee Troutman, who had been rejected as the match's official referee, then ruled from outside that escaping the cage -- under a claimed 'Windham Clan rule' -- won the match, and Deville was declared the winner despite no pinfall or submission. Commentary explicitly states that under normal NFW cage-match rules only a pinfall or submission should end the match, making Troutman's ruling a fabricated/crooked decision. The actual in-cage referee was Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips. Post-match, Impulse ran in and attacked Bobby Jack Windham and Christian Cruise for helping Deville and the Windham Clan escape.

matches.stipulation: Single Elimination, First Pinfall/Submission/DQ/Tapout/Countout/Thrown Towel (2011 Grand Prix Final)
matches.note: Legion caught Jack Harmen with a boot to the gut followed by a Brainbustah for the pinfall win. Post-match, Stalker and the Fallen (Mr. Myers, Frederick Krueger III, and 'Hockey Dude' Jason Voorhees Jr.) ran in and beat down Legion with multiple finishers until Deacon ran in for a surprising save.

date.source: the document's own dateline (16 Oct 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After a mule kick to the groin, Eric Dane hit the Shining Star (a running high knee) on Adrian Willard for the pinfall win. Calvin Carlton and Bandit (Dynasty) watched from ringside, and Troy Windham and Bobby Jack Windham (Windham Clan) watched from the entrance ramp, both apparently sizing up Dane as a possible recruit.

After extensive interference left the referee down and both men nearly counted out, Deacon got back into the ring, hit a second Chokeslam on Nova, and pinned him for the three count. Heavy interference throughout: Christian Cruise and Peter Windham attacked Deacon's manager Chris Shepherd and Deacon; Bobby Jack Windham choked Shepherd with an Inverted DDT; Bandit and Adrian Willard attacked Nova; Eric Dane clotheslined Nova from behind. The referee was bumped and briefly incapacitated, and commentary explicitly notes the match nearly ended in a no-contest before Deacon and Nova fought through to a finish. Post-match, Nova accused Deacon of being part of a 'set up' and cut a promo suggesting Eddie Mayfield ('Shadow Boss') was orchestrating manipulation within NFW.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Tag Team match; Freebird Rules invoked by Stalker to forcibly enter Luci4 as a third member of The Fallen
matches.note: 187 and Saafir Muhammed hit Murder One on Mr. Myers for the pinfall, retaining the EMT Championship. The Chosen People (Bobby Jack Windham and Christian Cruise) began the match against The Fallen, with champions D-R-S entering 'midway through' per commentary. Extensive run-in interference: Peter Windham piledrove the coerced/kidnapped Luci4 with the A.D.D. on the arena floor; Legion attacked Peter Windham with a steel chair in apparent retaliation; Deacon chokeslammed Bobby Jack Windham and bodyslammed Peter Windham on the concrete, apparently retaliating for the earlier Deacon/Nova match interference; Blaine Hollywood and Malik Anderson watched from the entrance without engaging. Luci4 had been kidnapped from Legion backstage earlier in the show and forced into this match by Stalker on a leash.

Jack Bryant ran in and swung a chair at JJ Deville, who ducked, and the shot struck Impulse instead; the match was awarded to Castor Strife and Impulse by disqualification. Two referees officiated in conflict throughout: Joe the Plumber (the NFW-assigned official, working off his final reinstatement condition) and Pee Wee Troutman (Windham-aligned), who repeatedly interfered with each other's counts. Moments before the official DQ was announced, Pee Wee Troutman appeared to count a full three-count for JJ Deville pinning Impulse, but Impulse's foot was on the bottom rope, making the count moot. A mass brawl and security intervention followed the decision. Post-match, Impulse and his ringside companion Calico Rose pranked JJ Deville with an asparagus-scented sports drink (aided by a planted ringside fan) before hitting a Sudden Impact into a trash bucket.

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Dec 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Six-Man Tag Team Match
matches.note: Nova abandoned his partners and walked to the back before the match got going. Randalls and Tsunami were overwhelmed by numbers, aided by a new masked Windham Clan enforcer ('Devastator') who chokeslammed Randalls through a table at ringside; the referee counted Dark Storm out, awarding the match to The Fallen. 'Hockey Dude' Jason Voorhees and Zombie Shamon also walked out with Stalker's group but are not clearly credited with in-ring action, so are treated as entourage rather than legal competitors; the actual wrestling is attributed to Stalker, Myers and Krueger III. Troy Windham and JJ Deville personally joined the beatdown of Randalls alongside the masked 'Devastator,' who was introduced this show as a new Windham Clan security hire.
Deacon dominated the bout and finished Christian Cruise with the Altar Call for the pinfall. Bobby Jack Windham was at ringside for his ally Cruise but could not prevent the loss.

Harmen left the ring to taunt/confront Emilio Ruiz (the former National Guardsman '#13,' fired at the previous show), triggering a brawl outside the ring; Harmen was counted out while Rook Black recovered inside the ring, and Rook Black was declared the winner by count-out and retained the title. Post-match, an enraged Ruiz accidentally clocked Rook Black with a blind right hand before escaping into the crowd.

Troy Windham ambushed Bandit before the bell with a top-rope dive, a DDT onto the concrete, and the Slacknife neckbreaker onto the steel steps; neither man ever entered the ring, and referee Greg Herpin called for the bell, ruling the contest a no contest. Afterward, Troy called out Mike Randalls by name on the microphone; Randalls appeared briefly via a spotlight/video effect, teasing a future confrontation.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Match with the pinning wrestler's side winning the Television Championship
matches.note: Jack Bryant hit the Birmingham Breaker (Uranage Backbreaker) on JJ Deville for the pinfall; Bryant/Dane's side won and Bryant retained the Television Championship. JJ Deville forced Impulse to absorb the bulk of the offense and repeatedly denied him tags. Immediately post-match, the Windham Clan (Bobby Jack Windham, Christian Cruise, August De La Rossi, P. King, plus the masked 'Devastator') swarmed the ring; JJ fired Impulse from the Clan on the spot, and Calico Rose was brutally beaten (struck by August De La Rossi, choked by Devastator, and put through a table with Bobby Jack Windham's Running Razor's Edge) and stretchered out. August De La Rossi suffered a broken arm from an Impulse armbar during the melee. Deacon was the only wrestler to attempt a rescue run but arrived too late to stop the beatdown.

After twice declining to finish Legion with the Director's Cut neckbreaker, Castor Strife hit the Cult Classic (fireman's carry into a high knee) for the pinfall to retain. Heavy ringside interference from Stalker, Mr. Myers, and Peter Windham against Castor's entourage (Lana Dremire, Magnus, Alex Austin) failed to change the outcome. Post-match, Castor Strife extended an alliance offer to Legion, who accepted, joining Castor's faction 'The Guild' and apparently ending Stalker's control over Peter Windham's presence alongside him.

matches.stipulation: Southeast DC Street Fight (Falls Count Anywhere)
matches.note: Saafir Muhammed and 187 combined (kick to the gut, then a Jackknife Powerbomb) to pin Malik Anderson for the win after a brawl that spilled from the ring through the arena's ramp and concession areas. Tsunami (revealed mid-segment under the name 'Akita Hoshi') and an ally called Rayne ran in to attack Dorchester Stratton on Joe The Plumber's behalf, including green-misting Dorchester's manager Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld. Joe The Plumber was legitimately hospitalized for a head injury after the match, per the broadcast's closing report. Team alignment for Shaniqua Carlton and Malik Anderson is inferred from who they are shown attacking/being attacked by rather than an explicit roster announcement; see lane_notes.

date.source: the document's own dateline (18 Dec 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Open Challenge
matches.note: Emilio Ruiz sprinted to ringside with a chair and struck Jack Harmen with it during the match, causing referee Greg Herpin to immediately call for the bell; Rook Black was declared the loser by disqualification. Ruiz then also struck Rook Black with the chair, before pulling out and donning a green replica of Impulse's mask and fleeing through the crowd to avoid security. Title-on-a-disqualification convention assumed for the retain; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Six-Man Tag Team Match (Fallen-requested, JJ Deville-approved)
matches.note: Peter Windham botched a Moonsault attempt on Legion during a pin attempt on Stalker; Eric Dane hit Peter with the Stardriver but was then pulled from ringside by Castor Strife and Magnus. Stalker capitalized by crawling onto the dazed Peter Windham for the pinfall. Eric Dane initially tried to flee the assignment and was forced to compete by JJ Deville under threat of suspension, lost pay, and a mandatory physical exam. Heavy ringside interference throughout from both factions' entourages, including Lana Dremire spitting on and clawing Eric Dane, and Magnus press-slamming him on the concrete outside.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: Calvin Carlton threw powder into 187's eyes at ringside, blinding him; Blaine Hollywood then hit the 'That's Entertainment' Backcracker for the pin. Match wager stakes: a Blaine win earns the Hollywood Wrecking Crew another shot at the EMT Tag Team Championship held by Saafir Muhammed and 187; a 187 win would have meant Shaniqua Carlton got Calvin Carlton alone, handcuffed, in the cage for ten minutes. Post-match brawl between DRS and Dynasty/Hollywood Wrecking Crew required both Windham Clan and NFW security to break up; Blaine received stitches and 187 needed prolonged medical eye treatment.

The match never reached a real contest: Bryant took an early advantage, but Dorchester Stratton rolled out of the ring, refused to continue, disparaged the Television Championship on the microphone, and called for Dynasty backup (Calvin Carlton, Bandit, Hollywood Wrecking Crew). Eric Dane ran in with a chair to clear the area, and Akita Hoshi (formerly Tsunami) chased off Dorchester and the Hollywood Wrecking Crew with a kendo stick, ending the segment without a decision. Included as a match per the show's own Credits titling, though no wrestling contest actually took place.

date.source: the document's own dateline (4 Feb 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Nova hit a Bourbon For Breakfast (modified Scorpion Death Drop) for the pin. Ryan Oracle is presented as a returning wrestler, recently out on loan to UWA in Philadelphia and trained by Avery Prosser; described as Powermaster's long-time partner. Match presented as a condensed highlight package, not full commentary.

Harmen hit a Locomotive on a seated Lone Wolf to win. Presented as Lone Wolf's debut for this broadcast (established as an Ultratitle Season 1-era wrestler unfamiliar to newer fans). Referee Scott Speranza warned Harmen against wearing Lone Wolf's headdress to alter his appearance mid-match, threatening disqualification.

matches.stipulation: Open Challenge
matches.note: Bryant hit a Birmingham Breaker for the pin, despite Calvin Carlton breaking up an earlier pin attempt. Immediately after the match, Dorchester Stratton attacked Bryant with a Release Spider German Suplex and the Stepping Stone (step-up soccer kick), then threw the Television Championship belt out of the ring -- no title change, but establishes a new program between the two.

matches.stipulation: Freebird Rules (any two of the Fallen's four members could compete)
matches.note: Rook Black set up Mr. Myers with a Stun-Gun that instead dropped him into Impulse's Sudden Impact for the pin. Wild post-match brawl: Stalker chair-shots Impulse; Legion runs in and fights Stalker; Rook Black hits Impulse with a discus lariat in the chaos (shrugging it off as 'not me, it's you'); Jack Harmen is pulled off the apron by Nova to avoid the fray; Deacon runs down and restores order, tossing Rook Black over the top rope.

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification
matches.note: After Hoshi kicked out of an earlier SlackKnife, Windham hit a second SlackKnife, hooking both legs for the pin. Extremely bloody weapons brawl (kendo stick, chair, a table broken via SlackKnife) covered live by Kerry O'Connor and Lamont Hollywood after starting as a taped highlight package. Immediately after the bell, the returning Mike Randalls ran in and hit Windham with a Backdrop Driver, then menaced him with a broken kendo stick before spitting on him and walking away without further violence.

matches.stipulation: Open Challenge
matches.note: After Mueller and Fargo hit a Rocket Launcher Splash that would have won the match, manager Shaniqua Carlton broke up the pin with a tennis racket shot, drawing a disqualification -- the champions' second consecutive title defense won this way. The returning Original Showstoppers (Frankie Fargo and Brandon Mueller) answered Saafir Muhammed's open challenge. Referee identity is inconsistent in the source: Scott Speranza is credited ringing the opening bell, but Bruce Phillips is shown signaling the disqualification-ending bell. After the match, Calvin Carlton had Bandit chokeslam his own sister Shaniqua Carlton for costing the Showstoppers the titles via DQ.

date.source: the document's own dateline (19 Feb 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Fargo hits a top-rope Veg-a-Matic on Kelly and Fargo hooks the leg for the pin, referee Bruce Phillips making the count. Post-match, the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (187 and Saafir Muhammed) ran in and brawled with the Original Showstoppers after the bell; no result change.

Harmen hits the Locomotive (Yakuza kick) on Krueger for the three count, despite interference attempts from Mr. Myers and the Fallen. Stalker attempted to attack a celebrating Harmen afterward but backed off when Nova ran in with a steel chair; no result change from this post-match stare-down.

Dane hits the Stardriver on Bandit for the three count. Calvin Carlton forced Bandit into this match as punishment for a prank targeting Dane's stolen money; Carlton watched ringside in disgust throughout.

Blaine Hollywood interfered with a steel chair shot to Nova's face, and the referee immediately called for the bell, awarding Nova the match by disqualification. Calvin Carlton repeatedly pressured a reluctant Blaine Hollywood to help his tag partner Malik Anderson; Jack Harmen made a surprise run-in afterward via a pyro diversion to clear the ring and stand with Nova.

The match ended in chaos: JJ Deville put Dorchester Stratton under a suspension countdown to force him to wrestle, then Dorchester turned on his own partner Jack Bryant, chairshotting him from behind while he was set up in a Tree of Woe, after which the referee rang the bell immediately given the escalating attack; no winner is declared in the text. JJ Deville acted as the match's on-screen overseer per a deal with the Board of Directors, ostensibly punishing Rook Black for the earlier Kelly Evans incident by forcing this match; Dorchester Stratton's chairshot on his own partner Jack Bryant is a heel-turn beat rather than a clean finish, and no clear winner or result type is stated.

matches.stipulation: Triple Crown of Thorns (razorwire halo must be retrieved and used on an opponent to win; the Fallen and Windham Clan serve as ringside "Apostles"/lumberjacks)
matches.note: Legion charged at Deacon while holding the razorwire halo; Deacon caught him with a big boot that crushed the halo into Legion's face, satisfying the stipulation, and referee Bruce Phillips called for the bell awarding Deacon the win. JJ Deville immediately sentenced winner Deacon to "five minutes of mercy" alone with the Windham Clan and the Fallen, turning his win into a prolonged beatdown. Multiple run-ins followed: Castor Strife pulled the injured Legion to safety and briefly fought alongside Impulse; Troy Windham was revealed to have been disguised as a cameraman and ambushed President Eddie Mayfield with a camera shot; Dan Ryan then ran in with a steel chair, attacked Fallen/Windham Clan members and Mike Randalls, stopped himself from hitting JJ Deville with the chair (hitting him with a Humility Bomb instead), and cut a season-defining promo severing ties with the Windham Clan and

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Mar 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: Strife hits an STO Backbreaker followed by the Director's Cut on Magnus for the three count. Magnus was booked by new Strife-production owner Eric Dane rather than Dane facing Strife himself; commentary notes Magnus is a former employee of Castor Strife's old production company.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage, Texas Tornado rules
matches.note: No finish is clearly resolved in the text: JJ Deville climbed and dropped over the top of the cage to the floor, tried to signal the timekeeper's bell (which did not ring), then rang it himself, but no official announcement of a winner follows. Troy Windham was left alone in the cage and was subsequently beaten down by Randalls and Hoshi, including a 15-foot moonsault from Hoshi. JJ Deville effectively abandoned his partner Troy Windham to escape the cage himself; whether this counts as an official win-by-escape is left ambiguous by the text, which frames it as a hollow, self-serving act rather than a confirmed result.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: With Mueller hoisted on Malik Anderson's shoulders, Blaine Hollywood dives from the top rope to complete a Doomsday Backcracker on Mueller; referee Scott Speranza counts the pin. Dorchester Stratton dropkicked a fallen Jack Bryant into the steel cage after the bell as a parting shot; a brawl involving all six men and security followed the decision.

matches.stipulation: Triple Crown Championship Qualifier gauntlet: maximum three wrestlers in the ring at once, new entrant every sixty seconds after an elimination, with Stalker, the Fallen, and Windham Clan members serving as outside enforcers/lumberjacks

eliminations.note: Schoolboy rollup, three count by referee Bruce Phillips.
Six Million Dollar Drive to Hell.
Tornado DDT off the top rope.
Implied eliminated via a sunset flip; the text does not show an on-page pin count, only that the field narrows to Legion and Peter Windham immediately after.
Bobby Jack lifts his own ally Peter into a crucifix-lift (Sign of the Cross) and pins him; played as an odd, seemingly deliberate elimination of a teammate.
See No Evil (modified facebuster across the knee).
Altar Call Powerbomb.
See No Evil (modified facebuster across the knee).
Peaceful Slumber submission hold (Walls of Jericho/elevated Boston crab); Seti taps out.
F-5, pinned for the three count to crown Deacon the winner and third entrant into the Triple Crown Championship unification match.

matches.note: Deacon pins Jack Harmen with an F-5 to win the gauntlet and claim the third and final spot in the upcoming Triple Crown Championship unification match alongside Rook Black and Stalker. Doc Curiosity, wielding a sledgehammer and increasingly unstable following recent events, interfered mid-match, attacking the referee and both Harmen and Deacon before officials ejected him from ringside; this interference did not itself register as an elimination since Curiosity was never a bracketed qualifier entrant.

date.source: the document's own dateline (8 Apr 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Alexander locks in his Warsnare Sleeper body vice, rendering Kelly unconscious; referee Bruce Phillips stops the match and calls for the bell. Debut match for Teddy Alexander, a UWA-trained Philadelphia native.

Curiosity refuses to hand over his sledgehammer to officials, then knocks Legion unconscious with it before the match properly starts; the referee awards Legion the win by disqualification. Curiosity, marked with a "?9?"/"Number 9" motif and increasingly unstable, also assaulted four Secret Service members trying to disarm him; Jack Harmen ran in as a distraction and Curiosity chased him off through the curtain.

matches.stipulation: 5-Minute Time Limit
matches.note: Dane stalls for most of the time limit (milking a countout, holding a headlock); Ryan rallies late but the five-minute bell sounds mid-exchange, and ring announcer Sims declares the match a five-minute draw. Billed as a top contender's match for a future shot at Castor Strife's World Championship; Dane, already signed for a title shot, had less to lose from the draw than Ryan.

Malik Anderson pins Saafir Muhammed with a Spinebuster after Shaniqua Carlton's racquet shot (intended for Anderson) inadvertently connects with Muhammed instead. Post-match, Calvin Carlton ordered Bandit to chokeslam Shaniqua Carlton for her role in the loss, but Malik Anderson physically stopped Bandit from doing so.

matches.stipulation: Fatal Four-Way Elimination Tag Team Scramble (four corners, wrestlers may tag only their own partner, anyone legal may enter, elimination rules)

eliminations.who: Bobby Jack Windham & Christian Cruise (The Chosen People)
eliminations.note: Eliminated via double countout, simultaneous with Dark Storm, after Mike Randalls swandives through Bobby Jack Windham and the announce table on the outside.

eliminations.who: "The Wolf" Mike Randalls & "The Dangerman" Akita Hoshi (Dark Storm)
eliminations.note: Eliminated via double countout, simultaneous with the Chosen People.
Fargo pins Nova after Mueller hits a Mississippi Mudslide Jam legdrop off the top rope.

matches.note: With Nova draped over Mueller's legdrop victim, Frankie Fargo makes the cover for the three count, giving the Original Showstoppers the win and the #1 contendership to the new Everette Memorial Tag Team Champions, Malik Anderson and Bandit. A mysterious masked, lab-coated man marked "?9?"/"Number 9" and wielding a sledgehammer repeatedly interfered against Jack Harmen late in the match, strongly evoking Doc Curiosity though his identity is deliberately never confirmed in the text.

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 May 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Point of View (Eric Beachy & Jason Murray) won with a superkick set up into a bridging German suplex. Double debut match for Eric Beachy and Jason Murray. The 'Northern Frontier' wrestlers were never individually named in the broadcast, only billed collectively as a team out of Finland or Norway.

Teddy Alexander hit the Ragekill Driver on Legion for the pin. Four members of The Fallen (Mr. Myers, Krueger the Third, Zombie Shamon, and JV) interfered mid-match but were fought off by both competitors; Stalker then clipped Legion's legs from ringside to set up the finish.

Nova was assaulted backstage before the match by a masked assailant (revealed as 'Nein'/Number 9) and could not compete at the bell; Jack Harmen wrestled the bout essentially alone. Mid-match, Doc Curiosity transformed into the unhinged 'Nein' persona after apparently mistaking Harmen for Nova. Nova recovered and made the save with a steel chair; Nein fled through the crowd with Eegor giving chase. No pinfall, submission, or decision was ever reached.

matches.stipulation: Sudden-Death Triple Threat (Dirty Rotten Scoundrels inserted via a rematch clause)
matches.note: Malik Anderson pinned Saafir Muhammed with a spinebuster after Cal and Shaniqua Carlton both struck Muhammed with their tennis rackets. Shaniqua Carlton turned on The Dirty Rotten Scoundrels -- including her ex, Saafir Muhammed -- mid-match, aligning with Malik Anderson afterward; Anderson appeared to be leaving the Dynasty stable as a result.

date.source: the document's own dateline (10 Jun 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Impulse pinned Doc Curiosity with Sudden Impact. Doc Curiosity repeatedly targeted a masked Nova throughout the match, apparently mistaking him again for the wrestler who once wore the High Flyer mask. Referee Greg Herpin was briefly knocked down by an errant Point of View shoulder block.

matches.stipulation: Grudge Weapons Match (billed for a shot at the EMT Tag Team Championship at Reloaded 12)
matches.note: The scheduled match never took place: the two teams brawled through the arena parking lot, loading dock, and concourse before the show even began, and were pulled apart by arena security. Commentary states outright there was no match; the #1 contendership picture for Reloaded 12 was left unresolved.

Phil Atken rolled up Dan Ryan for the pin after Ryan's surgically-recovering right knee buckled while attempting the Humility Bomb. Billed with major stakes: a win for Atken would earn a NFW World Heavyweight Championship shot; a loss for Ryan would remove him from the World Title picture. Ryan was reported afterward to have suffered only a knee sprain.

Jack Bryant hit the Birmingham Breaker off the top rope for the pin. Bryant and Alexander share a training background under Avery Prosser in the UWA; Alexander took exception to Bryant downplaying it, fueling the match.

date.source: the document's own dateline (21 Jul 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: After Blaine Hollywood publicly humiliated and abandoned his partner Bandit, leaving him to wrestle alone, Mike Randalls felled Bandit with a Cyclone Enziguiri and Akita Hoshi finished him with a top-rope Moonsault for the pin. Pre-match, Bandit choked out his own manager Calvin Carlton; Blaine Hollywood then turned on Bandit, alleging (unconfirmed) an affair with Katherine Windham, spat on him, and quit; Calvin fired Bandit immediately after the loss.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Brandon Mueller pinned Bret Kelly with a top-rope leg drop after Frankie Fargo isolated and softened up Kelly's reluctant partner Mike McGee.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Cameron Cruise made Z.! submit to the Cruise Control STF after thumbing him in the eyes and clipping his leg. JJ DeVille offered Cruise his freedom if he laid down for Impala and Z.!; when Cruise refused, JJ withdrew the offer and had Impala and Z.! jump Deacon before the bell.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Teddy Alexander pinned Chad Fortune with the Ragekill Driver, having carried the entire match himself. The Shadowrunners were managed by Doug Mayfield. Phil Atken avoided tagging in for most of the match.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Troy Windham pinned Eegor with the Slackknife. Doc Curiosity was distracted by his mask and never tagged in to help Eegor.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Eddie Mayfield made Jason Murray submit to the F-P-S Sharpshooter after Cojones Mercado chokeslammed Eric Beachy.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One
matches.note: Malik Anderson pinned Powermaster with the Anderson Spinebuster after he and Jack Bryant isolated and wore down both opponents. The PowerGodz were managed by Neil Riddick. Shaniqua Carlton managed and celebrated with Anderson and Bryant, their first match together as a team.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Round One, No Disqualification (declared by President Eddie Mayfield shortly before the bell)
matches.note: Jack Harmen pinned 187 with the Locomotive running Yakuza kick as Saafir Muhammed failed to break up the count in time. WildStar suggested Mayfield's stipulation change was calculated to wear down both teams ahead of his own upcoming tag match.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Quarterfinal
matches.note: With Deacon held up outside the ring, Teddy Alexander blindsided Cameron Cruise with the Ragekill Driver and dragged the dazed Phil Atken on top for the pin. Bobby Jack Windham, Z.!, and The Mighty Impala surrounded Deacon at ringside and occupied the referee's attention, preventing a save; framed as payback for Deacon and Cruise's earlier defiance of JJ DeVille and Bobby Jack Windham.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Quarterfinal
matches.note: Jack Bryant pinned Brandon Mueller with the Birmingham Breaker after Calvin Carlton, swinging a tennis racquet at Bryant, accidentally struck his own client Mueller instead. Calvin Carlton's continued ringside interference on the Showstoppers' behalf backfired.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Quarterfinal
matches.note: Nova made Cojones Mercado submit to the Caesarian Section (Rear Naked Dragon Sleeper) after earlier being busted open when Mayfield rammed his head into the ring post. Mayfield attempted to bait Nova into a chair-shot disqualification by kneeling and blindfolding himself; Jack Harmen talked Nova out of it.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Championship Tournament — Quarterfinal
matches.note: After Akita Hoshi was stretchered out with a neck injury, Dorchester Stratton repeatedly tagged himself in against Troy Windham's wishes; with Randalls distracted after appearing to force Windham to submit to the Katahajime, Stratton blindsided Randalls with a springboard kick to the temple for the pin. Immediately after the pin, Stratton — egged on by Veronica Abrams-Rumsfeld — chair-attacked the unconscious Randalls and then a battered Windham, betraying his own partner and undercutting the build to the planned Randalls/Windham retirement match; JJ DeVille is shown watching approvingly on a monitor backstage.

date.source: the document's own dateline (22 Jul 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Cup Tag Team Tournament Semifinal
matches.note: Teddy Alexander charged a running Jack Bryant without realizing Bryant had made a blind tag; Malik Anderson intercepted him with the Affirmative Action Spinebuster for the pin. Malik Anderson deliberately had Jack Bryant open the match against Teddy Alexander instead of Phil Atken, a tactical choice praised on commentary. Phil Atken accidentally touched Alexander getting knocked out of the ring, briefly complicating the finish.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Cup Tag Team Tournament Semifinal
matches.note: Jack Harmen pinned Troy Windham with the Slackknife (Jackknife) after a Superfly Splash off the top rope, sealing Superfly Express's advance to the final. Mid-match, Mike Randalls (of the Dark Storm faction, accompanied by Akita Hoshi and Rayne) goaded his way to ringside and was tagged in by Troy Windham in place of JJ Deville, who never re-entered; the bout effectively continued as Windham/Randalls vs. Superfly Express for its remainder while still being billed and called as the Playboys Club match. Treated here as a single, uninterrupted fresh match per the brief's guidance on genuine uncertainty; flagged in lane_notes. After the bell, Akita Hoshi blasted Jack Harmen with red mist as a post-match assault; this did not affect the decision.

With Teddy Alexander having abandoned ringside to join an entrance-ramp brawl, Castor Strife caught a distracted Phil Atken with a vicious kick and the Director's Cut snap swinging neckbreaker for the pin, retaining the title. Lana Dremire (Strife's valet) opened a cut on Atken's forehead with a bladed ring during the match. Eric Dane interrupted mid-match with a title-shot contract for the winner, triggering a brawl among Dane, Rook Black and Legion that spilled to the entrance ramp/gantry with chairshots; Teddy Alexander (Atken's second) left the match area to join that brawl, directly costing Atken the title match.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Cup Tag Team Tournament Final
matches.note: After a lengthy, brutal back-and-forth, Nova press-launched Jack Harmen off the middle rope onto Malik Anderson (billed as a 'Super Rocket Launcher') for the deciding pinfall. Shaniqua Carlton (Anderson & Bryant's valet) struck Nova with her tennis racquet late in the match. Commentary for this match was handled by a separate team, Kerry O'Connor and Lamont Hollywood, distinct from the show's usual Natrone Rice/Wildstar booth. A time-skip graphic ('JOINED IN PROGRESS 18:12') indicates a portion of the match was not shown.

date.source: the document's own dateline (19 Aug 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Tournament, single-elimination triple threat (the man pinned is eliminated; the other two advance)

eliminations.note: Pinned via a Shining Wizard into a Lionsault combo; eliminated from the Grand Prix.

matches.note: Leyenda De Ocho pinned Ikan Jobtooyoo to eliminate him, with both Doom and De Ocho advancing. After the decision, Spooky Doom cheap-shotted the advancing Leyenda De Ocho with a chairshot from behind, drawing the crowd's ire and seeding a rivalry between them.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Tournament, single-elimination triple threat (first man eliminated does not qualify for the Grand Prix)

eliminations.note: Pinned with the Sudden Impact Superkick after Akita Hoshi's Baisaku Knee Kick; eliminated.

matches.note: Impulse pinned P. King Duk Windham with the Sudden Impact Superkick after Akita Hoshi softened him up with a Baisaku Knee Kick; Impulse and Hoshi both advance. Commentary frames Duk Windham's elimination as President Eddie Mayfield indirectly punishing him for joining the Windham Clan.

Jack Harmen hit Nein with the Locomotive (a running big boot) and covered for the pinfall, with Nein's manager Eegor breaking up the count a moment too late. This match was uniquely presented on-air not via standard commentary but as a highly exaggerated, stream-of-consciousness recap narrated by an unnamed fan ('a middle aged long haired hippy') filmed by producers at the event; treated here as a legitimate fresh match despite the unreliable narration. Post-match, Eegor stomped Harmen in frustration, then Nova entered and, with Harmen, beat down Eegor with a splash.

matches.stipulation: NFW Grand Prix Tournament, single-elimination triple threat

eliminations.note: Pinned via a tights-assisted rollup after Atken had removed Jason Murray from the ring with a flying shoulderblock; eliminated. Jason Murray survives as the 'neutral survivor' and also advances.

matches.note: Phil Atken flying-shoulderblocked Jason Murray out of the ring, then pinned Frankie Fargo with an illegal hook of the tights. Bronte Lakes (Jason Murray's valet) interfered with a high-heel stomp on Atken during the match. Teddy Alexander, described as Atken's 'new associate,' chased Atken back into the ring at one point after he tried to walk away.

date.source: the document's own dateline (26 Sep 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: De Ocho dominated throughout and finished Plain Brown Rapper with a Corkscrew Second Rope Quebrada ("The Actulizer") for the pin. Referee Bruce Phillips. Framed as part of De Ocho's role as the 'vs. the World' entrant signed for the NFW vs. the World Grand Prix theme.

Bobby Jack Windham ran in and hit Legion with a chairshot during the match; the interference was ruled against Cameron Cruise, giving Legion (called "the Devil's Reject" by commentary) the win by disqualification. Referee Scott Speranza. After the match, Eddie Mayfield had Cojones Mercado chair Bobby Jack Windham, then personally beat him down before offering him a renegotiated contract; Legion and Cruise looked on from outside.

matches.stipulation: #1 Contender's Match
matches.note: The Hellfire Club (Dorchester Stratton, JJ DeVille, Blaine Hollywood) ran in; Stratton hit Jack Bryant with "The Stepping Stone," and DeVille superkicked Malik Anderson into Blaine Hollywood's backbreaker outside the ring, leaving Phil Atken to pin Bryant. Referee Greg Herpin. Winners (Atken/Alexander) earn a shot at Superfly Express's Everette Memorial Tradition (EMT) Championships at the Gorge. After the pin, the Hellfire Club continued a brutal assault on Bryant's taped ribs until Eddie Mayfield, Cojones Mercado, and Akita Hoshi ran them off.

date.source: the document's own dateline (14 Oct 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Legion pushed De Ocho off a springboard attempt mid-match, then finished Peter Windham with his finishing curbstomp for the pin. Peter Windham, now under a Front Office contract, was told he could qualify for the Grand Prix with a pinfall in this match, but did not get one.

Rook Black retained with a Gauntlet Backhand after a back-and-forth match. Referee not explicitly named in this segment. The Mighty Impala's tag partner, the Mysterious Z, accompanied him to ringside. Afterward Rook told interviewer Devin Millwood he would pitch the NFW Board of Directors about JJ DeVille at the upcoming Washington D.C. show.

After interference from JJ DeVille and a kendo-stick shot from Rayne that accidentally blinded Shaniqua Carlton with Akita Hoshi's own mist, Blaine Hollywood hit a Double-Knee Facecracker (Codebreaker) on Malik Anderson for the pin. Referee Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips. All three men are former tag-team partners/rivals with 'a great deal of bad blood.' Managers/allies at ringside: Shaniqua Carlton (Anderson), JJ DeVille and Rayne (Hollywood/Hoshi).

Jack Harmen hit Phil Atken with the Locomotive Yakuza Kick for the pin, retaining the titles for Superfly Express. Referee Greg Herpin. Superfly Express is managed by Calvin Carlton, who took a tennis-racquet shot from Atken during the match. Won by Anderson/Bryant's opponents (Atken/Alexander) at Brawl 56 to earn this shot.

matches.stipulation: Last Man Standing; Match Two of Best of Five Series
matches.note: After an extended weapons-heavy brawl, Stratton connected with the Stepping Stone, slamming Bryant's head into the ring steps; Bryant could not answer the ten count. Stratton kept valet Veronica Abrams-Rumsfeld away from ringside for her own safety before the match. Bryant is set to face new champion Stratton again (match three of five) at the Halloween show in Salem, Massachusetts.

date.source: the document's own dateline (31 Oct 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Teddy Alexander overwhelmed Mike McGee with strikes and pinned him after driving a forearm across his face. Referee Scott Speranza. McGee is a comedic political-activist jobber character ('Not Just the Wealthy Should Be Healthy' picket sign).

The brawl was ongoing, with Carlton having gained the upper hand, when the Hellfire Club (JJ DeVille, Dorchester Stratton, Blaine Hollywood) stormed the ring and nearly made Carlton their 'sacrifice'; Sons of Liberty members (Malik Anderson, Jack Bryant, Eddie Mayfield, Akita Hoshi, Rayne) ran them off before any finish was reached. Billed as a no-cages, no-weapons attraction sparked by a post-match brawl at Reloaded 13. No winner or formal result is declared in the text; left unresolved per source.

Freddie Sagawa ran in and attacked De Ocho, biting at his mask; the referee called for the bell to stop the match without declaring a winner. Referee Bruce Phillips. The 'Mystery Opponent' billed on the segment title is identified within the broadcast as Lane Cash, a late-arriving newcomer accompanied by two unnamed women ('the Beautiful Blondes') who spent much of the match on the outside. Grand Prix-related bout.

Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld secretly handed Blaine Hollywood a weighted purse; he knocked out Eddie Mayfield with it and pinned him for the win, confirmed by an in-broadcast replay. Referee Scott Speranza. Rayne accompanied the Sons of Liberty with a kendo stick; commentary (Kerry O'Connor and Lamont Hollywood) called the match live at ringside.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere; Match Three of Best of Five Series
matches.note: Blaine Hollywood and JJ DeVille, disguised in cloaks, ran in and hit stereo chairshots on Bryant; Dorchester Stratton then covered him for the pin to retain the title. Referee (Head Official) Greg Herpin. The match was staged through a haunted-house set (hallway, graveyard, house of mirrors, basement). Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld was sent to the back by Stratton before the match began.

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Nov 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Powermaster (of the PowerGodz) hit a big splash on the Mighty Impala (of Z-Impala!) for the pin. Dark match for the live D.C. crowd, relayed as a brief text summary rather than full televised coverage; noted as available in full via the promotion's YouTube channel.

After a hard-fought back-and-forth in which De Ocho nearly scored a big near-fall off a moonsault, Castor Strife caught him with a stiff kick and finished him with the Director's Cut for the pin. Explicitly billed as a non-title match despite Strife being World Heavyweight Champion.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Battle Royal (Open Invitational)

eliminations.note: Tod Destiny clotheslined out; Chad Fortune DDT'd onto their own prop device.
Uppercut over the top rope.
Leaped over the top rope himself to avoid Teddy Alexander, letting tag partner Bret Kelly take the hit.
Thrown over the top rope.
Gauntlet Backhand Face-First Chokeslam over the top rope.
Tossed over the top rope.
Struck in the head with his own chair; eliminated in the same sequence as tag partner Eric Beachy.
Back body drop, enabled by Leyenda De Ocho's distraction with the Triple Crown Championship.
Removed after tag partner Rook Black was eliminated and slammed the title belt into his face.

eliminations.who: Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (Frankie Fargo & Brandon Mueller)

eliminations.note: Eliminated in the same sequence as the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels.
Belly-to-belly suplex over the top rope; final elimination. Cruise entered without his advertised partner Deacon, who did not appear.

matches.note: Teddy Alexander eliminated the last opponent, Cameron Cruise (who had entered without his advertised partner Deacon), via a belly-to-belly suplex over the top rope, giving Alexander and Phil Atken the win. Winners earn a future opportunity at the Everette Memorial Tag Team Championships. Ten teams entered; Cameron Cruise's advertised partner Deacon was recovering from an injury and never appeared.

Rook Black forced Phil Atken to submit to a modified bow-and-arrow stretch ('the Crossbow'). Non-title. Personal issue stemming from the earlier battle royal (each had eliminated the other's team). Teddy Alexander attempted to interfere but was rebuffed; Rook and Alexander brawled after the bell.

With the match mid-brawl (narrowing to a one-on-one Bryant/Stratton segment) and the arena losing power, Freddie Sagawa emerged and attacked Dorchester Stratton with a corkscrew; the referee ruled the match a disqualification win for the Hellfire Club. Referee Greg Herpin. Fan-voted main event (Superfly Express plus Jack Bryant chosen over Rook Black and Castor V. Strife). Prior to the DQ, Malik Anderson and Akita Hoshi ran in to attack Blaine Hollywood and JJ DeVille respectively, and a hooded man allied with Cameron Lee Waubash attacked Jack Harmen at ringside (having also attacked him backstage earlier in the show).

date.source: the document's own dateline (16 Dec 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Orange Dragon II hit his 'Head Kill 13' Frankensteiner for the pin after a fast-paced sequence. Referee Scott Speranza. Debut showcase match for Orange Dragon II, billed from Japan. P. King Duk is a former Windham Clan henchman who dropped 'Windham' from his ring name.

Kid Chameleon, who spent the match mimicking La Estrella 100%'s moveset, finished him with a Diving Guillotine Leg Drop for the pin. Referee Greg Herpin. Debut showcase match; La Estrella 100% returning to NFW after more than two years away.

Ramey worked over Rapper's arm throughout the match, then hit a cross-armed cradle slam (called the 'Darkness Buster' on air) for the pin. Referee Greg Herpin. Debut showcase for Jesse Ramey, introduced as a newcomer who claims to know 'the truth' about NFW.

After a low blow, Baytor applied a Mandible Claw-style hold using a soiled sock, forcing Kelly to tap out while vomiting. Gross-out comedy squash/debut for Fappity Baytor. Mike McGee (Kelly's Can-Am Strike Force partner) at ringside.

Teddy Alexander pinned Ryan Oracle with a roaring elbow (nicknamed 'The Glasgow Smile' on air), set up by a series of tandem maneuvers with Phil Atken. Referee Greg Herpin. Billed as a message to Superfly Express; Teddy Alexander stated he came to Australia looking for Jack Harmen.

matches.stipulation: Barber Shop Window Match (Falls Count Anywhere; win only by throwing the opponent through the shop's front window)
matches.note: Malik Anderson threw Saafir Muhammed through the salon's front window onto the street, landing on a stolen jeep, for the win. Special guest referee Julius Scissor, filmed at his own Sydney salon ('Shear Excellence'). Shaniqua Carlton (Anderson's manager and Muhammed's ex) interfered with a pedicure-tub shot on Muhammed. Julius Scissor later billed Shaniqua Carlton for the property damage.

Rook Black hit a Discus Axe Bomber followed by the Gauntlet Backhand on Akita for the pin, retaining the title. Referee Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips. During the match, JJ DeVille again tried to sway Rook toward the Hellfire Club by attacking valet Rayne; Rook refused to capitalize on the distraction. After the bell, Akita attacked his own valet Rayne, prompting President Eddie Mayfield to have Cojones Mercado knock him unconscious with a chair.

date.source: the document's own dateline (23 Dec 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Kennedy hit a running axe bomber followed by an enziguri-style axe bomber to the back of McGee's head, then rolled him over for the pin. Phillip Kennedy's in-ring debut on NFW television; his finisher is nicknamed "The Nuts," a poker reference.

matches.stipulation: Walkabout Dreamstreet Fight
matches.note: After a brawl using fan-thrown and under-the-ring items (framed portraits, a Vegemite jar, a Fosters can), Voss hit a package piledriver ("vDriver") on McCoy for the pin. Referee was Greg Herpin. The stipulation is also called the "Outback Dreamstreet Fight" later in the same segment; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Six Man Scramble
matches.note: Kid Chameleon caught Leyenda De Ocho in a bridging suplex and referee Pee Wee Troutman counted both men's shoulders down at once; the broadcast explicitly calls this a double-pin draw. Jesse Ramey immediately and angrily disputes the draw result and attacks his opponents post-match. Lord Coyner Pollard then runs in and piledrives ("Boleyn Sisters Driver") Leyenda De Ocho with a tea tray as a weapon before fleeing.

Anderson hit a spinebuster and then locked in the Anderson Armbar until Baytor tapped. Impromptu match after Anderson interrupted Peter Windham's induction ceremony and demanded an opponent; commentary states Anderson broke Baytor's arm (injury angle). Referee was Pee Wee Troutman.

Smallz hit his "99 Problemz" spinning powerbomb on Windham for the pin. Boogie Smallz's surprise in-ring debut, sent out by President Mayfield as a "trial" for Windham's self-declared Commissioner status. Referee was Greg Herpin.

date.source: the document's own dateline (12 Jan 2013), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Sagawa reversed Windham's 'Attention Deficit Disorder' corkscrew tombstone attempt into his own tombstone piledriver for the pin. Billed beforehand only as a 'mystery opponent.' Post-match Sagawa continued attacking Windham with a chair until The Beautiful Blondes distracted him, letting Windham fight back with a DDT and a chair shot.

matches.stipulation: Unification match
matches.note: Lucky Seven knocked Engel out with a leaping roundhouse kick she calls 'The Witch Hunter' and pinned her. A pre-match press conference confrontation, where Seven spat on Engel, nearly caused German officials to cancel the bout. Alex Austin cornered Seven in place of the still-recovering Castor Strife.
Time-limit expired (15 minutes) while Austin had Chameleon trapped in an Anaconda Choke; Chameleon never tapped. Post-match confrontation between the two teases a rematch.

After Venice Coast-to-Coast (Lexx Tarano and Valentino Ferrari) interfered mid-match attacking both teams, Superfly Express hit a combination finish (Inverted Atomic Drop into a Step-Up Kneestrike) on Brandon Mueller for the pin, retaining the EMT titles. Referee Greg Herpin began counting a double count-out during a brawl-out before Venice Coast-to-Coast's interference redirected the match; VCC's ambush foreshadows a future title challenge, following their earlier backstage attack on the Showstoppers in the 'Culture Clash' segment.

date.source: the document's own dateline (19 Jan 2013), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Kennedy hit his 'The Nuts' enziguri-style axe bomber for the pin. Referee was Scott Speranza; Kennedy's second NFW victory.
Smallz hit his 'White Sheet' roaring elbow for the pin after a Superplex/Swanton Bomb exchange. Boogie Smallz's second NFW victory.

Cash and Windham hit a combination finisher (a superkick called 'Cash On Delivery' into a Slacknife, together dubbed 'The Texas Penny') on Banzai Brother #1 for the pin. Team debut for 'Dirty Money' (Cash and Windham), decided via Rock-Paper-Scissors as to who would start. Referee was Greg Herpin. Post-match, The Graverobbers (Bandit and Devastator) ambush Cash and Windham with stereo chokeslams.

matches.stipulation: Bamboo Cage Match (winnable by pin, submission, or escape)
matches.note: While Harmen was climbing over the top of the cage, Alexander shoved him off; Harmen fell twenty feet and crashed through the ringside announce table, and was declared the winner. Referee was Bruce Phillips. A 20+ minute, bloody war stemming from the Alexander/Atken beatdown of Harmen at Brawl 61. Harmen is reported to have no serious injuries but is kept overnight for hospital evaluation. See lane_notes on the finish's exact mechanism.

Teddy Alexander ran in with a chair aiming for Nova; Nova pulled Atken into the shot instead, and referee Pee Wee Troutman awarded Atken the match by disqualification. Not a title match ('the titles aren't up for grabs' per commentary). Post-match Alexander and Atken further beat down Nova with a piledriver, a Figure Four, and an Angerbash Bicycle Kick, strapping a neck brace onto him. See lane_notes on the apparent inconsistency of the DQ result.

matches.stipulation: No Rules Pit Fight
matches.note: Legion goaded Akita (shouting 'DISHONOR!') into striking him with a bamboo/kendo stick; Akita then pinned him for the three count. The Graverobbers (Bandit and Devastator) were at ringside but did not interfere on Legion's signal. Post-match, Legion hands Akita the broken stick and bows, an apparent recruitment overture toward his 'Black Market'/Graverobbers faction.

date.source: the document's own dateline (9 Feb 2013), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Fargo ducked a flying forearm, sending McGee into the turnbuckles for a Side Russian Legsweep, then hit a top-rope splash for the pin. Relayed via commentary recap (the 'Opening Rundown' segment) covering matches held earlier in the RAGNAROCK show, not shown as live action.

Ferrari submitted Kelly with 'The Borgia Cross' Cloverleaf Leglock in about six minutes. Relayed via commentary recap (the 'Opening Rundown' segment), not shown as live action. Both are described as professed submission specialists.

Akita attacked Veroli with a kendo stick roughly three minutes in, drawing a disqualification win for Veroli. Relayed via commentary recap ('Opening Rundown'). Commentary attributes Akita's mental state to Legion 'messing with his brain.' Note: this is a bare 'Akita' as billed — no fuller name given in the text.

Blaine Hollywood hit a Backcracker on IROC, Dorchester Stratton followed with a Stepping Stone, then Blaine locked in the Hellfire Club's 'Secret Handshake' (a bridging STF) for the submission win. Billed collectively as 'The Sicilian Swat Team,' but only 'IROC' is named individually in the text; the team's other member is unnamed. Relayed via commentary recap ('Opening Rundown').

Leyenda De Ocho hit the Actualizer on Orange Dragon II for the pin, secretly aided by Triple Crown Champion Rook Black holding Orange Dragon II's ankle at ringside to stumble him during the closing exchange. Presented as an in-character interview with Rook Black narrating the match to commentator Natrone Rice rather than shown via direct commentary. Result determined the next challenger for Rook Black's Triple Crown Championship (paid off later in the show).

Legion attacked before the bell; the match escalated into a mass locker-room brawl involving the Graverobbers, Hellfire Club, Superfly Express, Shadowrunners, Grand Prix entrants and others. No finish is shown or declared in the text — Impulse is left standing with the title amid the chaos as security separates the combatants. Relayed largely via recap-style cutaways.

Blaine Hollywood ran in and hit a Backcracker off the turnbuckles on Leyenda De Ocho; referee Greg Herpin rang the bell for the disqualification, giving Ocho the win, but Rook Black retained the Triple Crown Championship since the title cannot change hands on a DQ. JJ Deville then retrieved the belt and handed it back to Rook. The Credits-block segment title itself is literally 'ROOK BLACK v...', withholding the opponent's name; the opponent, revealed only once the match starts, is Leyenda De Ocho. This was billed as the payoff of Rook Black's screwjob assist in match #5. Commentary frames the DQ as the newly formed Hellfire Club (JJ Deville, Blaine Hollywood, Dorchester Stratton) 'accruing their first NFW championship' by protecting Rook's title through outside interference.

date.source: the document's own dateline (16 Feb 2013), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After Lane Cash superkicked Ryan Oracle to the floor, Peter Windham hit a second-rope legdrop on Powermaster, then a top-rope Supafly Splash (the 'Sweetwater Sweater Song,' with Cash launching him in) for the pinfall. Billed team names: Dirty Money (Windham & Cash) vs. The PowerGodz (Oracle & Powermaster). The Graverobbers/Black Market (Legion, Bandit, Devastator) then attacked ringside as Dirty Money celebrated, sparking a mass locker-room brawl (Jesse Ramey, Kid Chameleon, Leyenda De Ocho, Akita, Doug Mayfield, Shadowrunners, Blaine Hollywood and others); no separate result is declared from that brawl.

Impulse hit a Sudden Impact superkick on Devastator for the pin while Mayfield cut off Bandit from breaking up the count. Booked mid-show by NFW Commissioner Peter Windham after a backstage confrontation between President Eddie Mayfield and World Champion Impulse over Mayfield's open challenge; Legion was barred from ringside for the match. Team billed as 'Pro-Revolution.'

Nova hit a diving Eaglestar Swandive Headbutt on Phil Atken, and referee Greg Herpin counted the pin amid chaos to give the Superfly Express the win. Manager Calvin Carlton struck Atken with his cane ('Ol Bessie') moments before the finish, and commentary calls the retention 'questionable.' The match ended in a mass run-in brawl immediately after the bell (the Graverobbers and Legion attacking both teams).

date.source: the document's own dateline (4 Jul 2000), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Oblivion Express overwhelmed the Sicilian Swat Team from the opening bell; Jeff Cummins finished Iroc with a piledriver-style 'Doomsday Driver' for the pin. 'Bad Bad' Leroy Brown was billed as accompanying the SST ('their twin brother from another mother') rather than as one of the two official tag members, but he was physically involved in the opening spot and thrown from the ring by Cummins. Wildstar was at ringside managing Oblivion Express, whom he introduced as his 'Five-Star Stable.'

Ares rolled a battered Ryconik into a small-package-style cradle for the pin, propping his own feet on the middle rope for leverage the referee did not see. Commentary explicitly called out the rope-assisted pin live; the decision stood as officially announced. 'Wild Child' Aidan Campbell came to ringside to protest the finish to Commissioner Miles, who dismissed him; Ares then nearly hit Campbell with a Full Nelson Slam until Ryconik made the save with a steel chair.

Aragon sucker-attacked Cancer with a running forearm during Cancer's promo about trust, then hit a reverse chokeslam facefirst into the mat and pinned him. Aragon dropped the mic on the unconscious Cancer and left saying 'Don't trust me.' Commentary noted Cancer had recently bailed Aragon out of jail after a sports-bar incident.

Powell dominated throughout, busted Duk open with Duk's own cane, and finished him with a Dragon Sleeper submission he calls 'the Padlock.' Powell was accompanied to the ring by Ms. Washington, whom he sent to the back before the match started.

Powell again used the Dragon Sleeper submission to make La Estrella 100% tap out. Commissioner Miles forced Powell into this match immediately after his win over Duk, as Powell had tried to leave the arena after the first bout.

Powell suplexed referee Scott Speranza (after KGB shoved the referee into him), knocking Speranza out; KGB retrieved his nightstick and blasted Powell in the back of the head with it, and a second, unnamed referee counted the pin. This was Powell's third consecutive forced match of the night, ordered by Miles as punishment for trying to leave the arena. After the bell, KGB continued the beatdown, including a throat-first 'Final Verdict' drop across the top rope, until officials pulled him off.

Wylde missed a top-rope Wildcard Splash after being distracted by Wildstar's appearance at the entrance; Viper followed with a top-rope Vipersault (moonsault) and pinned him. Wildstar appeared at the entrance mid-match and flashed his 'Five-Star' hand gesture, distracting Wylde.
