Commentary noted bad blood between Wylde and Wildstar, with Wylde having previously claimed he 'used' Wildstar to get ahead in the business.

matches.stipulation: Three-Way Dance
matches.note: After Alex Wylde ran in and chair-shotted Wildstar on the top rope, Aidan Campbell hit Wildstar with a full-nelson fallaway slam (which he calls 'The Overdrive') for the pin. Commissioner Miles put Wildstar's 'Five-Star' nickname on the line for this match on the spot: if pinned, Wildstar would lose the right to use it. Two-legal-men tag rules applied, with the third man tagged in at any time. Wildstar lost, ending his 'Five-Star' persona on the promotion's first show; fans chanted Campbell as the new 'Five Star' afterward. Alex Wylde's chair-shot run-in on Wildstar was the deciding factor.

name: NFW Crash TV 10

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Aug 2003), on the fed's own results archive

city: Lowell, Massachusetts)/North Charleston Colesium (Charleston, South Carolina

matches.note: Poe used his size advantage for much of the match, including backbreakers and a chokeslam, and nearly won after a Powerbomb sequence; but when Poe went up top for the Seventh Seal tombstone, Hornet shoved him off and connected with a Shooting Star Press for the pin. Shown as taped highlights narrated live by Kerry O'Connor and Lamont Hollywood, with the final stretch called in-continuity by Natrone Rice and South Conference Chairman Calvin Carlton. Billed as Hornet's NFW debut match (his second match back from a layoff).

After 23-plus minutes, Stanley's top-rope Guillotine DDT drew what referee Greg Herpin ruled a two-count rather than a clean three, and Southern rallied with a Louisiana Roll into a back bridge for the pin. Stanley and color commentator Lamont Hollywood disputed the call as a screwjob, believing Stanley's hand had hit the mat three times before Southern's shoulder came up; the referee's ruling stood as the staged result.

Priest dominated for long stretches, throwing Aho through a timekeeper's table and later removing the ring padding to drag out another table, but Aho backdropped Priest through that second table instead; Priest barely beat referee Greg Herpin's ten-count outside the ring, and back inside, Aho reversed a Priest attack into a Reverse DDT and finished him with a Jackknife Cradle pinfall. Billed as a double-debut for NFW TV audiences. Post-match, analyst Wildstar's summary states 'Priest had a countout victory... over Evan Aho,' which contradicts the on-screen pinfall finish; flagged as a source inconsistency, with the staged/announced pinfall result treated as controlling.

Payne controlled much of the match and appeared to have Krusher beaten, but Krusher (aware of Payne's tendencies from his day job as a rival commissioner) countered a Full-Nelson setup for the Payne Killer with a Cutter, then finished Payne with a Slingshot Brainbuster pinfall. Referee: Bruce Phillips (named on commentary).

Matthews attacked before the handshake was fully released and worked over Rabesque's injured knee throughout, but when Matthews went for Rabesque's own Figure Four finisher, Rabesque rolled him into a Small Package for the pin. Referee: Scott Speranza. Matthews protested afterward that Rabesque had grabbed his tights; the referee said he saw nothing. Matthews was warned about a points infraction for the pre-bell attack and post-match temper tantrum.

With Flair's knee buckling on the top rope, both men crashed together off the top to the arena floor in a Russian-neckbreaker-style spot; referee Greg Herpin began a ten-count outside the ring, and Flair rolled back under the bottom rope just before ten while Hart did not return in time. Designated the week's 'Five-Star Spot' by guest analyst Wildstar. The document does not use an explicit 'countout' label for the finish; the result is inferred from Flair beating the count with his hand subsequently raised.

After a grueling exchange in which neither man could keep the other down, Montezuma's handler Raul smuggled him a loaded black glove; Montezuma finished Manson with the Fair Shake (Olympic Slam) for the pin, then had referee Scott Speranza raise his other (uninjured, ungloved) arm instead of the loaded hand. DC Stratton attacked Manson before the match with a chain, a wheelchair shove into camera equipment, and a suicide stage dive; Manson wrestled anyway. Commentary called out the glove as loaded after the finish; the staged, announced result stands per the show's own ruling.

McMillan hit Cruise with the Spirit Wolf Driver (an inverted Cradle Piledriver) for the pin as Viper dove back into the ring just late to break it up. Pre-announced stipulation for this and the following triple threat: the winner earns 15 points, and whichever competitor is NOT pinned also earns a bonus 5 points. Cruise was the wrestler pinned, so Viper (not pinned) also scored bonus points despite losing. Referee: Bruce Phillips.

Marx had Strife tapping to the Marxism STF, but Havok broke up the submission and then caught Marx with the O'Reilly Factor (X-Factor) for the pin. Same bonus-points rule as the prior triple threat applied (winner 15, non-pinned competitor 5); Strife was not pinned. Referee: Scott Speranza.

matches.stipulation: Interconference Match
matches.note: After a back-and-forth series of reversed pin attempts (including Melton working over Stevens's knee with a Figure Four using rope leverage), Melton rolled a distracted Stevens into a Small Package for the deciding fall. Billed as NFW's first-ever Interconference Match; ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims stated the winning wrestler's conference would receive 'home field advantage' for the following two weeks. Referee not explicitly named on-page.

name: NFW Crash TV 11

date.source: the document's own dateline (23 Aug 2003), on the fed's own results archive

city: Lowell, Massachusetts)/North Charleston Colesium (Charleston, South Carolina

matches.stipulation: Ironman Match (30-minute time limit, most falls wins)
matches.note: Falls traded throughout: Southern's Top Rope Louisiana Jam scored first, Hornet answered 45 seconds later with a Bridging German Suplex, Southern took a 2-1 lead with a Small Package roughly sixteen minutes later, and in the closing seconds Southern hit the Bourbon Street Plunge for a third fall to win 3 falls to 1. Referee: Scott Speranza. Presented as having happened '30 minutes ago' relative to the studio segment; the two competitors shook hands respectfully after the bell. Southern moves to 20 points.

matches.stipulation: Chain Match
matches.note: After roughly ten minutes of chain-assisted brawling that left both men bleeding, Flair choked Priest with the chain, hit a sitout chokeslam, then finished him with the Fallen One Reverse DDT while the chain was still wrapped around Priest's throat, for the pin. Referee: Bruce Phillips. After the bell, an unresponsive Priest snapped, choking out and chokeslamming Phillips before being subdued by security; NFW subsequently fired Priest over the incident, as announced earlier in the same broadcast's press-conference segment.

Manson worked over Hart's neck with a top-rope sitout powerbomb, then knocked him out with a Sweet Dreams Stunner, afterward tying the unconscious Hart down inside a decorated ringside casket using his own ring-attire streamers. No explicit pinfall or submission call appears on-page; Manson is credited with 10 points for the win. A casket prop was present at ringside throughout, though the document never labels this a formal 'Coffin Match' stipulation, so none is recorded here.

matches.stipulation: Coal Miner's Glove Match
matches.note: Strife attacked before the bell and controlled the match with a Director's Cut neckbreaker and a Hollywood Hazing, then climbed a ladder, retrieved the hanging Coal Miner's Glove, and used it for a Coal Miner's Glove Fistdrop pinfall. Johansson was fired from NFW after this loss, as announced earlier in the same broadcast. Valet Lana Dremire raised Strife's arm in victory.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere Match
matches.note: Stratton put Stevens through a flaming table with an overhead belly-to-belly, busted him open with a fire extinguisher shot, then climbed a ten-foot camera rig and hit a 450 Splash on the concrete floor for the pin. Referee: Scott Speranza. Stratton entered already docked 5 points for his Week One attack on Michael Manson, and wrestled without his manager Neil Riddick, who had been abducted and left in a coffin before the match (Riddick publicly blamed Quentin Sullivan and Michael Manson afterward). Stevens was reported arrested on unspecified charges at an outside fWo event earlier that week. Designated the week's 'Five-Star Spot' by Wildstar.

matches.stipulation: Dog Collar Match
matches.note: Matthews used the connecting collar chain to whip Cruise into a short-arm clothesline and slam him off the top rope, then finished him with a chain-assisted Pisskick (Superkick) landing on Cruise's still-tender broken nose for the pin. Matthews is shown afterward taking a phone call from an unnamed 'coach'-type figure who appears to have fed him scouting tips on Cruise. Matthews and Cruise are noted as becoming tag team partners for Week 3 despite this singles match.

matches.stipulation: Submissions Only Match
matches.note: After a back-and-forth battle, Krusher locked Stanley in a Cobra Clutch-style hold in the center of the ring; referee Bruce Phillips's repeated arm-drop test showed Stanley could not continue, awarding Krusher the submission win. Krusher moves to 20 points; Stanley remains winless through Week 2 of the season.

matches.stipulation: Bunkhouse Match
matches.note: After a brutal weapons brawl through tables, thumbtacks, a shovel, and a Singapore cane, Poe caught Payne with the Seventh Seal (a sitout Tombstone Piledriver) from the top turnbuckle for the pin. Referee: Greg Herpin. Valet Miso accompanied Poe to ringside with a Singapore cane, which Poe later used on Payne mid-match.

matches.stipulation: Amateur Rules Match (three 8-minute periods, only two-counts, no moves above the shoulders; judges score on points if there is no fall or submission)
matches.note: Rabesque built an 11-1 points lead exploiting the amateur ruleset, but Viper repeatedly fouled him with above-the-shoulder strikes (losing points for each one), then trapped him in a Katahajime/Cobra Clutch-style hold, rolled into a bridge, and pinned Rabesque's shoulders down for the fall. Referee: Greg Herpin. Rabesque wrestled the entire match on an already-injured knee that Viper targeted throughout.

matches.stipulation: 2 out of 3 Falls Match
matches.note: Melton won the first fall with a Dangerous Backdrop Driver; McMillan evened it with a Cattle Mutilation submission. In a chaotic decisive third fall of reversed pinning combinations, referee Greg Herpin ruled that both men's shoulders were down simultaneously, declaring the match a draw. Both men were awarded 5 points apiece for the draw. Ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims delivered the official ruling; Joey Melton reacted furiously, believing he had won.

matches.stipulation: Whip Match (the loser was to receive 10 lashes from the winner)
matches.note: In a no-disqualification brawl in which Marx mutilated Havok's fingers and eyes, Marx locked in a whip-aided Marxism (an STF/cross-arm choke combination) in the middle of the ring; referee Scott Speranza's arm-drop test showed Havok could not continue. Marx refused to release the hold even after the bell and had to be physically pulled off by Havok's new bodyguard, Domovoi. Ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims stated the referee ruled the 10-lash stipulation win nullified 'due to Mr. Marx's mental state and post-match actions,' though the pinfall-equivalent win itself (10 points) stood.

matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match
matches.note: After extensive Team Cuba interference and a running ringside brawl among the Lumberjacks, Montezuma's arm was injured when a DC Stratton/Michael Manson skirmish spiked Montezuma (hung upside-down in the ropes) with Manson's boots; Aho capitalized with a Novacaine choke, a clothesline, a knee drop, and a Tiger Driver '91 for the pin. Billed as NFW's first-ever Lumberjack Match, worked by wrestlers from the NFW North roster serving as Lumberjacks, including already-fired Damien Priest and Matt Johansson, plus Michael Manson dressed as a comedic lumberjack with a hatchet. Referee: Scott Speranza. The winner joined Eli Flair, Shane Southern, King Krusher, and Chris McMillan atop the NFW leaderboard at 20 points. Montezuma was left bloodied and required medical attention after the match.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Oct 2003), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The Powell Brothers overwhelmed the Bicep Brothers in a quick squash: Roger Powell planted Bob with a Northern Lights Brainbuster, and Scott Powell battered Bill with combination punches before the team locked him in a Boston Crab/Camel Clutch combination for the win. JT Tyler, presented as the Powells' financier/advisor, brought them to the ring; the Bicep Brothers (Bob and Bill) appear to be enhancement talent.

Melton capitalized after Krusher's knee buckled on a botched back body drop counter, worked the knee with a series of holds, then hooked the leg for the pin. Krusher suffered a real knee injury on the spot; Lindsay Troy accompanied Melton to ringside; referee Bruce Phillips made the count.
Hornet dodged a Firebird Splash and immediately locked in the Scorpion for the submission. Commentary spent much of the match questioning whether Hornet is fully motivated to win this season.

Viper dodged a top-rope clothesline attempt and hit the Viperbomb for the pin. Commentary noted Payne's last NFW win was at 2002's Futureshock against Chris McMillan in a Dog Collar Match; next week's stipulation for Payne was previewed as the same match type, against his tag partner (McMillan).

matches.stipulation: NFW Boiler Room match (both men locked in the arena boiler room until one is pinned)
matches.note: Hart countered a Dragon Suplex attempt into a Jawbreaker, hit a Tombstone Piledriver on the concrete, then finished with a chair-assisted legdrop (El Codo Explosivo) for the pin. Stevens was wrestling against doctor's orders while recovering from a concussion.

Rabesque avoided a top-rope armbar attempt, crotching Poe on the ropes, then rolled him into a La Magistral Cradle for the pin. Rabesque wrestled on an injured knee; Poe was accompanied to ringside by Miso.

Marx clipped Aho's knee from behind, then locked in his submission hold ('Marxism') for the tap-out. Marx's personal security guard Domovoi carried his glove to ringside on a pillow; the win moved Marx to 35 points and into the overall NFW points lead.

Hiroshi hit a top-rope Frog Splash (the Hiroshi-ma Bomb) for the pin at the thirteen-minute mark. Considered a major upset. Flair was moving slower than usual, which commentary attributed to the recent shooting of his manager and best friend Poison Ivy. Flair had been scheduled to face Donald James Havok before Havok's resignation forced the short-notice change to Hiroshi.

matches.stipulation: NFW Boiler Room match
matches.note: After fifteen minutes of brawling through the boiler room, the door was opened with neither man pinned; both were awarded 5 points for the draw.

Ryan absorbed a series of Montezuma strikes and suplexes, then hit a release Dragon Suplex and hooked both legs for the pin. Montezuma arrived late to the arena amid hurricane conditions, sliding into the ring as the count reached six. The text names two different referees for this match: Greg Herpin (early count) and Bruce Phillips (finish) -- likely a continuity slip; flagged in lane_notes.

The back half of the match is narrated through an absurdist guest-commentary bit voiced as 'Leonard Nimoy.' Manson hits his 'Sweet Dreams' Stunner finisher on Strife as the sequence ends, but the text never states a pinfall count or declares a winner, so the outcome is left unresolved per the brief's rule for a match the text never resolves. A coffin gimmick produced a run-in from 'El Bueno Excelente,' who was subdued by Strife's associate Benjamin with a beer bottle. Manson is also described in the text as a 'former NFW Interim Commissioner.'

Matthews struck Southern with a chair, drawing a disqualification, then continued the assault afterward, piledriving Southern twice on the exposed concrete floor. Referee Greg Herpin called for the bell on the chairshot; Southern was left busted open and had to be helped to the back.

matches.stipulation: NFW North Conference Match of the Week (30-minute time limit, worth 10 points)
matches.note: Shizaki hit an Asai Moonsault off the top rope for the pin after both men traded near-falls throughout. Ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims made the introductions; referee Scott Speranza made the count. Stratton's manager Neil Riddick was crescent-kicked out of the ring by Shizaki before the bell even rang. This main event is the only match of the night NOT listed in the show's own Credits block; flagged in lane_notes.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Nov 2003), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Stretcher match (first man carried through the entrance curtains on a stretcher loses)
matches.note: Viper used a submission hold to render Stanley unconscious, then stretchered him through the curtains for the win, finishing with a Viperbomb on the cement after a fan's thrown drink briefly revived Stanley.

matches.stipulation: Freefall to Hell match (first man thrown from the ring loses)
matches.note: Hiroshi flipped out of an attempted Clean Slate and hit a Back Suplex that sent Montezuma over the top rope to the cement floor below. Montezuma's usual ringside associates Raul and Cojones were unexplainedly absent; Montezuma appeared to injure his arm in the fall, though X-rays came back negative.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage
matches.note: Southern climbed to the top of the cage and hit a Shooting Star Press dismount for the pin, after repeatedly grinding Poe's head into the cage mesh. Commentary flagged Southern's unusually brutal, joyless performance as a sign of personal turmoil; he did not celebrate the win.

matches.stipulation: Dog Collar Rematch from Futureshock 2002
matches.note: In a leash-and-collar contest to tap all four turnbuckle corners, Payne fought through a severe neck injury (suffered when McMillan pulled him off the top rope with a Suicide Plancha) to drag himself to the fourth corner just ahead of McMillan. Payne's neck injury was declared season-ending, ruling him out for up to six months; six wrestlers including Hornet came out to help him to the back to a standing ovation.

matches.stipulation: Flaming Table match
matches.note: Rabesque hit a Belly to Belly Suplex that drove Cruise through three flame-engulfed tables for the pin. Called by a guest commentator gimmicked as 'Tsunami,' a Dawn of a New Day member who speaks only in broken exclamations; Shawn Hart accidentally ran naked through the ringside area during the segment.

After Strife's associate Benjamin accidentally threw a tub of glue in Stratton's face, a barely-conscious Stratton stumbled into Strife with a Director's Cut, then rolled onto Strife -- who was stuck to the mat in spilled glue -- for the pin. A hardcore glass-and-glue gimmick match with no formal stipulation name given in the text; referee Bruce Phillips made the count; Neil Riddick and Lana Dremire brawled at ringside during the match.

Melton lifted the small-statured double into a Spinebuster and ordered the referee to make the pin. This is a comedic squash: the document bills the opponent verbatim as 'Shane Matthews,' an explicitly small-statured stand-in/double Melton presents as a mocking makeover of the real Shawn Matthews -- NOT the actual wrestler Shawn Matthews, who faces Melton in the very next segment. Melton was awarded 3 points for the win.

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire Cane Tuxedo Match
matches.note: Melton left the match to attend to Lindsay Troy after a masked man attacked her at ringside with repeated chairshots; referee Scott Speranza counted Melton out. Matthews had nearly been pinned clean with a Piss Kick shortly before the interference; the masked attacker's identity is not revealed in this episode.

matches.stipulation: NFW Interconference Match of the Week -- Japanese Death Match (Texas Death Match rules, 20-minute time limit, ring rigged with mines set to detonate for a draw at the limit)
matches.note: Both men scored pinfalls the other kicked out of before a standing ten-count (Cruise via Cradle Piledriver, Hiroshi via Hiroshi-ma Bomb); time expired and the ring mines detonated, ending the match as a draw with NFW North retaining home-field advantage for two more weeks.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: A chair-wielding fan interfered on Marx from behind in the concession hallway, allowing Hart to hit a leaping elbow drop for the pin. Marx appeared to recognize the interfering fan, addressing him mid-sentence as 'Brandon Jacobs?' before being struck; the fan's identity is not confirmed anywhere in the text, so it is not treated as a resolved name. The crowd chanted 'Overrated!' at Marx throughout the match.

matches.stipulation: Splinter Cell from Hell (unsanctioned, No Holds Barred, no points on the line)
matches.note: Craig Miles goaded Hornet into this unsanctioned cage exhibition after both men had already separately been awarded 10 points via forfeit (tied to Krusher's and Flair's retirements). The Crash TV broadcast explicitly defers the match's outcome to a simultaneous airing on the companion NFW Season Pass channel and does not show or resolve it within this document; per the brief, winner and result are left null.

matches.stipulation: Texas Death Match (main event)
matches.note: After a brawl that spilled to the floor and through a table, Shizaki blinded Ryan with a substance thrown from a hidden turnbuckle stash, hit the Tsume Mahi paralysis strike, followed with a Moonsault through a table and a top-rope Frog Splash; Ryan could not answer referee Scott Speranza's ten-count. An unnamed masked associate accompanied Shizaki to ringside throughout. Shizaki moves into a tie with Michael Manson atop the NFW North standings.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Nov 2003), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Stratton avoided a Tiger Driver 91 attempt, then hit a top-rope Tornado DDT for the pin. Presented via the show's own 'highlight clips' framing rather than live blow-by-blow commentary; treated as fresh content for this broadcast.

Rabesque countered a pump-handle attempt into a DDT, then locked in the Figure Four Leglock on Stanley's already-worked knee for the tap-out. Stanley was reported doubtful for the following week with a knee injury; Rabesque's only loss of the season remains a tainted defeat to Steel Viper in Week 2.
Melton wore down Poe's leg (worked over on the ring steps early) before locking in his own Figure Four Leglock; Poe passed out from the pain.

Sands blocked a Frog Splash attempt with a knee to the stomach and immediately locked in the Sandman's Clutch for the tap-out. Described as Sands's first NFW win; Sands and Hiroshi are announced as tag team partners for the following week despite facing off here.

Neither man could secure his finisher through repeated near-falls; the bell rang at the 30-minute time limit. Garvin's in-ring debut, against the toughest test the announce team felt he could be given; Garvin and Viper are also announced as tag team partners for the following week.

Southern slipped free of a top-rope superplex attempt and finished McMillan with a Louisiana Jam for the pin. Post-match, Southern superkicked (Party's Over) and piledrove (Bourbon Street Plunge) the incapacitated McMillan while Aaron Douglas applauded from the ramp -- an apparent heel turn tied to Douglas's blackmail of Southern earlier in the show.

Both men were still exchanging near-falls when the time limit expired; each was awarded 5 points for the draw. A masked interferer attacked Hornet late in the match and was fought off by Hornet's bodyguard Flash; Lindsay Troy then unmasked the attacker on camera as Aaron Douglas. Shane Southern subsequently arrived and chaired down both Shawn Matthews and Joey Melton, turning on his own NFW South allies. Referee Scott Speranza officiated.

Cruise pulled Promo down into a small package for the pin after Lindsay Troy's ringside stare-down broke Promo's concentration on a top-rope Moonsault attempt. Described as Cruise's first NFW victory. Commentary floats that Promo may have been the masked man who attacked Troy the previous week -- later disproven when Aaron Douglas is unmasked as that attacker later in this same episode.

An unidentified masked man, styled after 'El Puta' and described as bigger than Strife's usual associate Benjamin, threw a grainy substance into Shizaki's eyes to break his Scorpion Deathlock; Strife then rolled him up with a Hollywood Hazing for the pin. Strife wrestled without his usual associate Benjamin at ringside this week. The interferer's identity is not confirmed in the text; commentary explicitly rules out Dan Ryan by height but names no one.

Hart knocked himself out landing awkwardly on a Suicide Twisting Plancha to the floor and could not answer the referee's ten-count. Hart had just fired his spiritual advisor Gary Spivey; post-match he shouted 'Adrian!' toward a cameo appearance by actor Adrien Brody seated at ringside.

Manson raked Marx's eyes to escape Marx's Gory Special submission hold ('Marxism 2.0'), then rolled him into a school-boy pin for the win. Billed as the pupil's first-ever attempt to beat his mentor; Manson mockingly shook the referee's, timekeeper's, ring attendant's, cameramen's, some fans', and the ring announcer's hands at ringside before finally shaking Marx's.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Dec 2003), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Tornado Rules, Bring Your Own Bag of Weapons
matches.note: Shawn Hart shattered a glass dildo over Armando Montemuza's head, busting him open, and pinned him for the win. All four men brought their own bags of weapons under tornado rules. The segment heading spells the Cuban wrestler 'Montezuma' but the running commentary and his own dialogue consistently spell it 'Montemuza' — recorded here as billed in the body of the match text; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules
matches.note: Pariah blindsided Promo with brass knuckles, then drove a cinderblock into the back of Chris McMillan's head, shoved his own partner Cameron Cruise out of the way, and covered McMillan for the pin himself. Pariah effectively turned on his own tag partner Cameron Cruise to steal the win — commentary calls it Pariah's first NFW win. Stipulation inferred from the ring announcer's later statement that BYOB – Bunkhouse Rules were 'in effect for all matches tonight'; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules
matches.note: After Jonathan Marx's thrown salt blinded Kazuo Shizaki rather than its intended target, a still-blind Shizaki nonetheless connected with a Blind Shooting Star Press on Evan Aho for the pin. Billed as the show's 'Five-Star Spot of the Week.' Shizaki wrestled with two bodyguard-like security escorts at ringside following a probation ruling referenced earlier in the show. Stipulation inferred per the ring announcer's blanket statement; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules
matches.note: Jonathan Marx broke free of Jean Rabesque's STF, kicked him in the gut, then knocked him out with Joey Melton's own bat (marked 'PERSONALITY') for the pin. The finishing weapon belonged to Melton, whose own partner Rabesque ended up pinned with it after Marx took it from him. Stipulation inferred per the ring announcer's blanket statement; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules, Tornado Rules, one fall, thirty-minute time limit
matches.note: After extensive weapon use from both benches, Joey Melton rolled up a hairspray-blinded Shawn Matthews (via a Slingshot Brainbuster) while holding a fistful of his tights for the deciding pinfall. Explicitly announced by ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims as under 'standard Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules stipulations in effect for all matches tonight,' one fall, thirty-minute time limit, tornado rules (no tags). Aaron Douglas appeared to be seriously injured after Hornet piledrove him on the concrete floor outside the ring; commentary questioned whether he could continue.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Bag – Bunkhouse Rules
matches.note: After Lindsay Troy's sledgehammer swing at DC Stratton missed and instead shook the ring post, sending Stratton crashing through a table, Christian Sands pulled him from the wreckage and pinned him for the win. A chaotic hardcore brawl: Manson's second, Riddick, set Dan Ryan on fire with an aerosol fireball and dumped hot food on Christian Sands; Troy's errant sledgehammer swing accidentally set up the finish. Stipulation inferred per the ring announcer's blanket statement; see lane_notes.

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Dec 2003), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Chris McMillan reversed a powerbomb attempt into a Tornado DDT, followed it with a top-rope suicide headbutt, and finished Gabriel Poe with the Spirit Wolf Driver for the pin. Billed as a minor upset given Poe's size advantage; commentary suggested Poe's focus may be wavering.

After trading big moves — including Pariah surviving a Viperbomb at two — Steel Viper countered a Tornado DDT attempt into a Northern Lights Suplex for the pin around the 23-minute mark. Pariah had pinned Chris McMillan the prior week; commentary frames this as Viper avenging that loss.

After both men nearly double-count-out off a simultaneous clothesline, Jonathan Marx escaped Montezuma's bulldog attempt with a drop-toe hold and forced a submission with the Marxism (STF). Commentary frames this as another loss in a rough stretch for Montezuma, while Marx continues to lead his division.

Hart ducked a Hiroshi frog-splash attempt, then brawled him into the guard rail and announce desk, mockingly performed a comedic 'revival' routine on him at the desk, and rolled him back in for an easy pin. Played largely for comedy ('jackassery' per commentary) rather than a clean finishing sequence. This was Hart's fourth win in five tries.

Shizaki dominated with a flying lariat, a dropkick, and multiple near-falls he broke himself just to inflict more damage, finishing Stevens with the Tsume-Mahi for the pin. Billed as one of the more one-sided squashes of the year; Shizaki did not need his usual security escort this week.

Melton went for a figure-four but Southern schoolboyed him for a near fall; Melton pulled Southern's tights for a two count, Southern reversed by pulling Melton's tights, let go before the count, and still scored the pin. Manager Lindsay Troy (for Melton) considered interfering on the tights spot but did not. Affected NFW South standings heading into the All-Star break.
Matthews survived a sudden Promo rollup near-fall, then finished with the Pisskick followed by the Showtime Stopper for the pin.

Cameron Cruise wore Jeff Garvin down with a sitout powerbomb and an Impact DDT, then finished with the Shipwreck for the three count. Garvin, a self-proclaimed pure technical wrestler, was outclassed in the opening chain-wrestling sequence.
After Rabesque worked over Hornet's knee for much of the match, Hornet countered a suplex attempt with a reverse Diamond Cutter, speared Rabesque, and finished him with a Dragon Suplex for the pin.

Christian Sands wore down Castor Strife with power and submission offense, ultimately locking in the Sandman's Clutch for the submission win. Improved Sands to 3-0 with 30 points on the season, per commentary.

Dan Ryan overwhelmed Evan Aho with power offense throughout, briefly slowed by an Aho armbar, and finished with the Humility Bomb for the pin. Commentary references a prior real incident where Ryan attacked Aho and 'invaded CSWA' to get at him — bad blood predating NFW.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Feb 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Gas Mask Match
matches.note: Michael Manson ran in unannounced and stunned Poe with the Sweet Dreams Stunner; a groggy Castor Strife covered for the pin. Shown via highlight cutaways from earlier in the day. Manson's run-in doubled as the opening beat of his contract-negotiation storyline with Avery Prosser later in the broadcast.

Manson slipped out of an Aho suplex attempt and reversed it into the Sweet Dreams Stunner for the pin; commentary described the roughly 16-minute match as free of interference. Manson entered riding an army tank driven by a masked man ('Frank'), later revealed as Castor Strife once the post-match negotiation swerve played out.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match (NFW South; objective was a hanging 'Dixie Flag' bandana, with ten points awarded to whoever retrieved it)
matches.note: With both men climbing separate ladders for the flag, ringside heckling from returning rival Steel Viper broke McMillan's concentration; Matthews jawbreakered him off the ladder rungs and grabbed the flag for the win. Match ran over 20 minutes with numerous ladder- and table-based spots. McMillan and Cameron Cruise had been shown plotting strategy against Viper earlier in the broadcast.

matches.stipulation: Singapore Cane match
matches.note: After Viper had punished a bloodied Cruise for most of the match, a run-in by Chris McMillan (wielding a kendo stick) distracted Viper long enough for Cruise to catch him with a Reality Check (reverse Russian legsweep) for the pin. Presented as payback for Viper's interference costing McMillan the earlier Ladder match. New valet Karlena 'Karla' Starr and trainer Mercedes Devon are shown cornering for Cruise.

Hiroshi finished a battered, reportedly concussed Stratton with a leaping piledriver as a rigged ring-mine detonated on the fall; Stratton was left motionless and the segment ended with Hiroshi the only man standing. Contested with barbed-wire ropes and rigged exploding 'ring mines'; no formal pinfall count is shown in the text, only a dramatic five-count and explosion sound effect. Stratton had been found beaten unconscious in his locker room hours earlier by an unidentified attacker and wrestled without medical clearance. Hiroshi's motivation is tied to his anger at former ally Eddy Love's return to NFW.

matches.stipulation: Nickname match (winner earns rights to the name "The Phenom")
matches.note: Douglas absorbed an early Hart comeback, including a crossface submission Hart thumbed his way out of, then finished Hart with an Irish-whip corner boot into a reverse DDT for the pin. Douglas is trained by 'Slade Wilson' per Hollywood's commentary; win takes the 'Phenom' nickname away from Shawn Hart.

As the referee was distracted, Seven Deadly Sins member Jeff Cummins speared Sands on the outside; Shizaki capitalized by bridging a Tiger Suplex '85 for the pin (counted by referee Phillips). Post-match, Avery Prosser publicly offered Shizaki a bribe for his loyalty in destroying the Ultratitle; Shizaki refused and struck Prosser with a briefcase, triggering a brutal multi-man beatdown by the Seven Deadly Sins (chokeslam, spinning spinebuster, double spear, a top-rope frog splash with a briefcase, and a spike piledriver) until Dan Ryan, Jonathan Marx, Lindsay Troy and Domovoi ran in for the save. Prosser was shown ordering Shizaki's mask ripped off before the save arrived.

matches.stipulation: Flag match (changed from the originally planned stipulation)
matches.note: Despite interference from Saafir Muhammed of the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Frankie Fargo scored a flash rollup on Lionel Reese for the three count. Individual Original Showstoppers members beyond Frankie Fargo are not named in this document.

A mystery opponent disguised as an arena mechanic (revealed mid-match, unmasked as returning 'Wild Child' Aidan Campbell) finished Garvin with a top-rope Asai Moonsault DDT for the pin. Garvin had arrived expecting a countout win after his scheduled opponent ('Promo') apparently retired; the mystery man arrived instead claiming his own signed contract.

matches.stipulation: No Figure Four Leglocks Allowed match
matches.note: After Rabesque blew kisses at Lindsay Troy, Troy low-blowed him and knocked his foot off the ropes during a near-fall, allowing Melton to grapevine both legs for the pin. Calvin Carlton was said to be reviewing the match afterward to decide whether to appeal the ten points awarded to Melton given Troy's blatant interference; not resolved in this document.

matches.stipulation: Submissions match
matches.note: DC Stratton (backed by a distraction from Neil Riddick and interference from the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels and Malik Anderson) handcuffed Marx mid-match; Ryan ultimately finished the handcuffed, unconscious Marx with a Torture Rack Backbreaker after a second Humility Bomb. Marx never verbally submitted; he was rendered unconscious rather than tapping. Heavy run-in interference orchestrated by Neil Riddick.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere match
matches.note: With Hornet locking in a Scorpion Deathlock near the concession stands, Calvin Carlton and the Original Showstoppers interfered; Carlton clubbed Hornet twice with his tennis racket and held his legs down while Love pinned him. Post-match, Shane Southern and Deacon ran in to make the save on Hornet. Commentary questioned whether NFW President Quentin Sullivan should overturn the ten points given the underhanded finish; not resolved in this document.

matches.stipulation: Iron Man Match (30-minute time limit; most falls wins)
matches.note: Tied at three falls apiece with seconds left, Southern hit a second Party's Over superkick and covered Deacon, but referee Greg Heprin ruled after a video review that the time-limit buzzer had sounded before his hand completed the third slap, awarding Deacon the match 4 falls to 3. Shawn Matthews interfered repeatedly at ringside on manager Aaron Douglas's orders, directly costing Southern three of Deacon's four falls (grabbing his ankle, taunting, and distracting him during covers). This was Deacon's first match in NFW, following a real-world-framed bout with multiple sclerosis.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Mar 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Marx submitted the slumping Poe with his Marxism STF at the 14:07 mark. Presented as a highlight recap narrated by the studio hosts rather than shown live, due to the broadcast's stated time constraints; treated as fresh same-night content per the brief.

Douglas hit a Reverse DDT (S.D.T.) for the pin after Shizaki, visibly working hurt from a prior attack, kicked out a fraction of a second late on an earlier attempt. Referee Bruce Philips made the count. Also presented via highlight recap narration rather than live action.

Stratton hit a top-rope 450 Corkscrew Splash for the pin after Hart, seemingly unmotivated, missed a flying clothesline. DC Stratton's manager Neil Riddick was at ringside urging him on. Presented via highlight recap narration. Described as Hart's second straight win and first under his own name rather than a prior nickname.

Sands submitted Aho with the Sandman's Clutch. Sands entered with a Riot Squad Officer escort, referencing a prior attack on him by the Seven Deadly Sins. Presented via highlight recap narration; text states Sands earned ten points for the win.

Deacon hit his Crucifix Powerbomb finisher, 'The Alter Call,' for the pin. Deacon's manager Chris Shepard was at ringside coaching him through the match. Presented via highlight recap narration; billed as a meeting of former CSWA and Action! world champions.

With Viper distracted by Matthews' valet Autumn, Matthews rolled him up and used a handful of tights to steal the pinfall. Matthews' valet Autumn was at ringside and factored into the finish; Aaron Douglas came out to confront Matthews and Autumn mid-match. Post-match, Viper hit the Steel Curtain and applied the Viper Clutch on Matthews for several minutes before officials pulled him off.

With the referee down, Steel Viper ran in and hit McMillan with a Viperbomb; Rabesque then applied a Figure Four and the revived referee counted McMillan's shoulders down. Run-in interference by Steel Viper decided the match; staged/announced result stands per the brief. Post-match, Viper also laid Rabesque out with another Viperbomb.

Hornet did not appear for the match, citing legal constraints; the referee awarded Campbell the win by forfeit before any contest occurred. No physical wrestling took place; this was a declared forfeit, included as a match entry because it is the credited segment's official decision. Campbell verbally declined the accompanying Ultratitle points. Hornet then appeared to cut a lengthy promo and confront Campbell face to face; extensive storyline content is captured in storyline_notes rather than here.

Steel Viper ran in with a chair and choked Cruise while the referee was down; Melton then hit a Piledriver for the pin. Steel Viper's interference decided the finish; he then cut a promo declaring he was done respecting NFW's 'Honor Code' after feeling wronged the previous week. Lindsay Troy briefly walked Melton to the aisle beforehand.

Ryan sidestepped a Hiroshi top-rope chop attempt, hit a low blow, and followed with a Dragon Suplex for the pin at the seventeen-minute mark. Lindsay Troy accompanied Ryan to ringside. Commentary frames Ryan and Hiroshi as having a history from prior promotions (GXW/GWE), including a past attack by Ryan on Hiroshi.

During a Party's Over attempt, Southern's boot appeared to explode with smoke and powder on contact, busting Love open; the referee, Greg Herpin, called for the bell and awarded Love the win by disqualification for use of a foreign object ('loaded boot') at the 25-minute mark. Commentary team for this match was Rice and Calvin Carlton (distinct from the studio pairing of O'Connor and Wildstar used elsewhere on the broadcast). Carlton insisted on-air the boot was tampered with and vowed an investigation. An earlier backstage segment this same show ('The Highway to Boot') showed a mysterious 'Highwayman' swapping Southern's boot for an identical one, suggesting the 'loaded boot' may not have been Southern's own doing; the text never resolves this.

date.source: the document's own dateline (24 Jul 2000), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: With referee Herpin distracted by Jade jumping onto the apron, Torch launched a fireball into Aragon's face, then hit a Fisherman's Buster (which he calls 'Spontaneous Combustion') for the pin. Cancer and his valet Jade came to ringside during the match; Aragon appeared to accuse Cancer of setting up the fireball spot. Afterward, Cancer offered Torch a handshake that Torch refused, and Jade tried to blindside Torch with a chair but was tackled by an unnamed fan before she could swing. Dez Aragon was later reported by Calvin Carlton, in a live backstage segment, to have assaulted three EMTs rather than be taken to the hospital for his burns.

Armando Montezuma ran in and swiped Viper's leg; Ryconik capitalized with the 'Polish Hammer' right hand on the stumbling Viper for the pin. Commentary referenced Ryconik's near-upset of Ares at the previous Crash TV. After the loss, Steel Viper attacked Montezuma's entourage backstage, was arrested/removed by security and police, and vowed revenge on Montezuma.

As Radder set up his full-nelson finisher ('Absolute Zero'), Cancer dropped down with a jawbreaker and followed with a cradle piledriver he calls 'The Malignancy' for the pin. Jade was at ringside for Cancer and briefly scuffled with Radder outside the ring. After the match, Dez Aragon ran in with a chair to attack the celebrating Cancer, but Cancer pulled Jade into the chairshot instead, knocking her out; Aragon then left without attacking Cancer further.

Roger Powell's wife, Andrea Powell, arrived at ringside in tears with a videocassette tape and confronted Ms. Washington, distracting Powell; Montezuma capitalized with a bridging rollup for the pin. Montezuma announced before the bell that U.S. Customs would not allow his Cuban World Heavyweight Championship belt into the country, making this a non-title match rather than the advertised title defense. Montezuma also used the ropes for illegal leverage on an earlier nearfall, caught each time by referee Herpin without penalty. Afterward, a confused Powell yelled at Ms. Washington and shoved a cameraman; Andrea Powell left in a cab before Powell could catch her.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Tag Team Texas Tornado (all six men fight at once; a team is eliminated when one member is pinned)

eliminations.note: Pinned via powerbomb; eliminated the A-List as a team.
Pinned via Doomsday Driver piledriver; eliminated the Elite Guard as a team.

matches.note: After eliminating the A-List and then the Elite Guard, Oblivion Express (Cummins & Reese) were left standing as the winners. The Elite Guard (Gomer Pyle & Flint M. Jacobs) had been feuding verbally with Oblivion Express in the weeks prior. Commentary framed the win as further proof Oblivion Express are tag-title contenders.

With Ares blinded after KGB sprayed something into his eyes and accidentally knocked out referee Herpin, KGB retrieved his nightstick and blasted Ares in the back of the head; a recovering Herpin then counted the pin. After the bell, an enraged Ares knocked out referee Herpin with a right hand and hit him with the Full Nelson Slam finisher, then chased KGB backstage to the jobber locker room (where La Estrella 100%, Leroy Brown, and M&M were shown laughing at KGB). There, newcomer Michael Manson chair-shotted Ares from behind, saving KGB and marking Manson's NFW debut.

matches.stipulation: Wildstar (the previous week's deposed 'Five-Star' athlete) served as special guest referee; President Sullivan announced mid-show that the match winner would face Wildstar next for a shot at reclaiming the 'Five-Star' name.
matches.note: The match built to a back-and-forth with both men down repeatedly, but was never resolved: as Campbell set up a submission hold on Wylde, paid mercenaries Bloodhunt, Ms. America, and the Elite Guard (Flint M. Jacobs & Gomer Pyle) ran in. Jacobs snapped Wildstar's neck across the top rope, Wylde chair-shotted Wildstar, and Bloodhunt hit Campbell with a chair-assisted 'Headshot,' leaving both Campbell and Wildstar laid out with no winner declared. Wylde revealed on the mic afterward that he had paid Bloodhunt, Ms. America, and the Elite Guard to attack Campbell and Wildstar. President Sullivan initially wanted to cancel the follow-up match, but Campbell insisted the show continue; Sims announced a five-minute rest period before the next match (Wildstar vs. Aidan Campbell) was held in its place. This match itself was never given an explicit winner, draw, or no-contest call by the broadcast.

matches.stipulation: For the right to be called 'Five Stars'
matches.note: Campbell's injured left knee buckled as he tried to climb the top rope, sending him crashing off the turnbuckles; Wildstar then climbed up himself and hit a moonsault bodypress, hooking the leg for the pin. Campbell had already wrestled the aborted Campbell/Wylde match and taken the paid beatdown from Bloodhunt earlier the same night, plus was nursing a pre-existing car-accident knee injury, and was given only a five-minute rest before this bout. Wildstar reclaimed the 'Five-Star' name he lost to Campbell the previous week. Junior referee Scott Speranza worked this match rather than chief referee Greg Herpin.

Shown as a highlight on the broadcast, a match taken before the cameras came on. The Showstoppers (Lincoln McKinley and Ryan Connors) beat the Sicilian Swat Team (IROC and Cousin Vinny, with Leroy Brown): Connors rolled IROC up after McKinley's Buff Blockbuster and referee Greg Herpin made the count. O'Connor: "A very impressive DEBUT win for THE SHOWSTOPPERS!"

Shown as a highlight on the broadcast, a match taken before the cameras came on. Bloodhunt (with Ms. America, Flint M. Jacobs and Gomer Pyle) beat M&M with the Headshot and a cover for the three-count while Torch distracted Ms. America at ringside.

Shown as a highlight on the broadcast, the last match taken before the cameras came on, a one-fall contest. O'Connor: "CUCHILO finished off Bret Kelly with a devastating succession of martial art manuervers", ending with a superkick to the throat. The card gives no pin or submission.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Apr 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After an interlude involving light-saber props thrown in by fans, Not Jonathan Marx disarmed Beau Michaels and applied the Not Marxism submission for the win. Part of the Star Wars-themed NFW East segment, called by Rayne and the Mad Hatter with ring announcer Cannibal Peters; billed for ten points. Announcer credits Not Jonathan Marx with 65 cumulative points afterward. This 'Not Jonathan Marx' is explicitly a separate, distinct character from the 'Jonathan Marx' who wrestles later on this same broadcast.

Not Hornet cut a promo refusing to wrestle; 'the Panda' then attacked and mauled him. Beau Michaels, not one of the three names originally billed for this segment, entered the ring unannounced on stilts, dropped an elbow on both downed men, and covered them together for a referee's double pin. The segment's own title bills a third participant only as redacted question marks ('???? ???????'), which is never resolved or named in the text -- kept verbatim in 'participants' per the brief's no-guessing rule. Beau Michaels, who wins the fall, is a separate, unbilled interloper rather than a confirmed identity for the mystery name. Announcer credits the win with 'ummmm 30? 30 points' in an explicitly joking, uncertain delivery.

After a brutal brawl including chair shots, a table spot through the announce position, and both men escaping each other's finishing holds, Bloodhunt hit his Headshot finisher for the pin. Bloodhunt entered as defending champion and retained; no title change. Manson attempted to use the title belt as a weapon mid-match. Commentary (Rayne and the Mad Hatter) frames this as a long-running grudge, with Bloodhunt and a former partner having crippled Manson in the past.

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves NFW North
matches.note: Muhammed hit a top-rope double leg drop followed by a leaping Cutter for the pin. North Conference Commissioner Avery Prosser changed Hart's opponent and the stipulation on the eve of the show, declared himself Muhammed's manager, and physically attacked Hart outside the ring (a Pedigree on the floor) during the match. Staged/announced result stands; Hart is written off NFW North per the stipulation.

Stratton missed his StrattonSault, allowing Douglas to hit his Reverse DDT finisher (the SDT) for the pin. DC Stratton's manager Neil Riddick was at ringside. Douglas entered the match at 3-0 on the season, having previously upset division leader Kazuo Shizaki.

After a top-rope brainbuster suplex sequence, Matthews connected with his finishing kick for the pin. Commentary references Matthews having been attacked by Steel Viper after his match the previous week (see Crash TV 19).
Hiroshi backdropped his way free of Aho's Tiger Driver '91 attempt, hit a hurricanrana, and followed with the Hiroshi-Ma Bomb for the pin.

Deacon overcame a hidden low blow from McMillan to hit his Altar Call finisher for the pin. Deacon wrestled this match shortly after his manager Chris Shepherd was ambushed and whipped backstage by the 'Highwayman' in the preceding segment.

Cameron Cruise's ringside presence distracted Viper, allowing Hornet to catch him with a roll-up for the pin. Aidan Campbell appeared on the entrance ramp holding a baseball bat and staring down Hornet after the match.

Marx avoided a Shizaki top-rope Asai Moonsault, grabbed the injured knee, and locked in the Marxism for the submission win. This 'Jonathan Marx' is the genuine NFW North wrestler, distinct from the parody 'Not Jonathan Marx' character who wrestled earlier on this same broadcast in the NFW East segment. Marx is billed as heavily booed; Dan Ryan is referenced as chasing him in the standings.

After a 24-minute match, Ryan raked Sands' eyes and hit the Humility Bomb for the pin. Christian Sands billed as the newly crowned 'EPW Champion' (an outside title, not contested here). Lindsay Troy accompanied Ryan to ringside.

Eddy Love and Joey Melton ran in -- Love attacking Cruise, Rabesque tackling Love -- prompting the referee to call for the bell; Quentin Sullivan overruled an initial attempt by Calvin Carlton to award Cruise a full ten points and instead declared the match a no-contest, with both men receiving five points. Cameron Cruise entered with his wife Mercedes Devon and an unnamed bodyguard figure ('Carter') at ringside.

Blaine Hollywood dropped in from the rafters and attacked Lindsay Troy with the Hollywood Hills Hangover, prompting the referee to call for a disqualification. The text does not name which side the disqualification was awarded to; it states the ruling 'cost Eddy Love a match against a woman,' which is read here as Troy receiving the win -- flagged as an interpretive judgment call. Afterward the Seven Deadly Sins ambushed Love and arena security in the parking lot; Calvin Carlton called a fifteen-minute recess.

The two men worked a deliberately unconvincing match per an off-camera arrangement (Love had bribed referee RM Pitts to fast-count a finish). Deacon then ran in seeking revenge for the earlier attack on Chris Shepherd; Love fled the arena in a stranger's car before any restart or decision was made. The document explicitly states no winner was ever announced ('no announcer would read the winner of the bout'); winner and result left null per the brief. The planned fixed finish and referee bribe are shown in the preceding backstage segment 'Can't Buy Me Love.'

In a brutal, injury-strewn brawl, Vivian Ryconik interfered on Southern's behalf and was then accidentally struck by a Southern Superkick meant for Campbell. Campbell hit his own finisher (Slamdance) on Southern and collapsed on top of him from his own injuries as paramedics arrived at ringside. The document explicitly states no winner was ever announced on air; winner and result left null per the brief. This match and its 'Party's Over' backstage lead-in are NOT listed in the show's own closing Credits block, which stops one segment earlier at 'Eddy Love vs. Joey Melton' -- flagged as a likely production/corpus omission.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 May 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: A second, identical masked Highwayman ran in, delivered a low blow and a Diamond Cutter to Deacon, and pinned him for the win while the original Highwayman fled up the aisle. Special challenge match with a wager: 10 points for Deacon, and Highwayman was to be fined 20 points if unmasked as Eddy Love. A mystery second Highwayman appears mid-match and gets the pinfall; Eddy Love is separately shown walking out of a backstage room the impostor Highwayman had entered, deepening (not resolving) the unmasking mystery. No formal unmasking occurs.

Rabesque fought off a two-on-one attack (including a staple-gun shot to the head from Stratton's manager Neil Riddick), flattened Stratton with a chair shot after Stratton had knocked out the referee, then locked in a figure-four leglock; the revived referee stopped the match with Stratton unconscious. Presented as an announcer recap over full match footage rather than a live call, but depicts fresh in-episode content, not archival replay. Manager Neil Riddick interferes repeatedly and staples Rabesque; the referee is briefly knocked out mid-match.

After a long, evenly-matched contest, Marx played possum and cradled Not Marx for the pinfall. Split decision: Jonathan Marx is the declared official winner by pinfall (10 guaranteed points), but the promotion's separate judges' point-scoring system awarded Not Jonathan Marx the bout 45-40, bringing his NFW East point total to 110. Not Jonathan Marx's identity remains an unresolved in-fiction mystery.

Both costumed 'immortal' monkey characters delivered simultaneous fatal blows in a Highlander parody, ending the bout as an explicit double beheading with a 'Quickening'-style lightning effect. Absurdist comedy sketch presented as an officiated in-ring bout (a bell is rung, a referee is present) and given its own Credits-block segment title, so it is included as a match per the brief; result is stated verbatim in the text as 'No Contest, Double Behead-'. The names used ('Highlander Monkey', 'Katana Monkey') are purely descriptive commentary labels, not proper billed ring names; no other names are given for these characters.

After a lengthy brawl through the crowd using chairs, a camera, a ring bell, and a broken table, Manson hit a diving headbutt off the table using the title belt for extra impact, then pinned Bloodhunt for the three count and the title. Presented within the NFW East segment's in-fiction 'Middle-earth' costume framing; announce team is Rayne and Mad Hatter, with 'Leonard Nimoy' (an in-fiction Star Trek-parody guest character) replacing an ejected Mad Hatter at the announce desk partway through this match. Not a privacy concern per the brief: this is an in-fiction character appearance, however real the name sounds.

Melton escaped an early Sitout Tombstone Piledriver near-fall from Douglas, took control after NFW North owner Avery Prosser crotched Douglas on the top rope, and finished him with a Figure Four leglock submission. Avery Prosser interferes against his own signed wrestler Douglas, flanked by the Hollywood Wrecking Crew (Malik Anderson, Blaine Hollywood).

Cruise battered a downed Viper with chairshots and broke a referee's ten count; Viper rallied with a chloroform-soaked rag and nearly executed Cruise off the ropes before Cruise's allies Carter Cruise and Chris McMillan ran in and beat Viper down, after which a returning Jason Payne chairshotted Viper. Stipulation: No Holds Barred, Last Man Standing. Shown joined-in-progress (JIP) after airing in full only on the NFW Season Pass tape-delay feed. The text never confirms an on-screen ten-count or referee decision after the final run-in, so no winner or result is declared -- left null per the brief. Earlier in the show, Steel Viper attacked Cameron Cruise's brother Carter and wife Mercedes backstage ('Snake in the Grass'), setting up this match.

After trading near-falls, Love blocked Hiroshi's Hiroshima Bomb attempt with a knee lift, then hit the Hurricane Piledriver for the pin. Presented as an announcer recap over full match footage (fresh content, not archival replay). Calvin Carlton is at ringside for Love and briefly distracts the referee with a tennis racket; announcers frame Love's prior three-week win streak as aided by suspect officiating.

Ryan overpowered an injured Campbell throughout the match and finished him with a Dragon Suplex for a clean pin after Campbell's comeback attempts (a Code Red armbar, a suicide dive) fell short. Campbell wrestled hurt after prior-week hip and concussion injuries. Ryan works uncharacteristically clean/sportsmanlike rather than his usual aggression, seemingly out of respect.

After Avery Prosser imposed 'NFL Rules' (four quarters, no disqualification, bench substitutions) and used the format to repeatedly break Team NFW's momentum, the match descended into a brawl with added Seven Deadly Sins reinforcements and weapons (a bowling ball, a turntable, a bucket of fried chicken, a watermelon). Substitute referee Roland Priest counted a fast three after 187 hit Lindsay Troy with a turntable into a Rock Bottom from Blaine Hollywood. Stipulation verbatim: 'NFL RULES' (Prosser's own term), four quarters, No DQ. The real referee Greg Herpin is stunned/knocked out by Prosser mid-match and replaced by Roland Priest, who is shown afterward hugging Prosser -- the fast-count finish is presented in-text as a fix. Two additional Seven Deadly Sins members, Saafir Muhammed and '187', join the SDS side mid-match as a football-style 'special teams' substitution, physically wrest

With Matthews distracted by a ringside dispute between his manager Aaron Douglas and his valet Autumn, Hornet grabbed a fistful of Matthews' tights and rolled him into a schoolboy pin for a clean three count. Matthews' kickout lands after the three count already fell, and he attacks in a rage post-match, chasing Douglas from ringside. Text is somewhat ambiguous on the standings language afterward ('Hornet and Shawn Matthews locked in at 75 points'), but explicitly states the loss dropped Matthews to third place, consistent with a Hornet win.

Southern hit his Hurricane (a Japanese Ocean Cyclone Suplex with a bridge) for what looked like a clean pin, but a slow-motion replay showed his own shoulders were pinned as well during the bridge; the referee ruled a double pinfall draw, and both wrestlers were awarded five points. Main event, one-fall, 30-minute time limit special challenge match, worth 10 points to the winner. Wildstar notes this is the second such double-pinfall-style controversial finish 'twice in a month.' Post-match, the Seven Deadly Sins (Cummins, Reese, Anderson, plus Prosser and Saafir Muhammed) run in and attack both wrestlers; Aidan Campbell, Dan Ryan, and Lindsay Troy run in to help; the brawl is interrupted by the surprise arena-wide return of new champion Michael Manson, who drops from the rafters and hits a plancha to close the show.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Jun 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Melton and Cruise controlled most of the match; Melton finished Lone Wolf with a Brainbuster for the pin while Cruise searched in vain for a hidden Steel Viper at ringside. This Highwayman and Lone Wolf are presented as hired opposition backed by Eddy Love; a Frontiertron shot afterward shows Love and yet another Highwayman playing poker with cheerleaders, further muddying the Highwayman mystery. Steel Viper needles Cameron Cruise via a Frontiertron insert stroking a Mercedes action figure, distracting him mid-match. Presented as a flashback ('TWO HOURS EARLIER') within the episode's riot-framing structure.

Facing a two-on-one handicap after Avery Prosser barred DC Stratton from competing, Shawn Douglas fought hard but was made to submit to Christian Sands's Sandman's Clutch (a Cobra Clutch Crossface). Avery Prosser ordered his own signed wrestler DC Stratton not to show up, punishing Douglas for perceived disloyalty and leaving him to wrestle alone; DC Stratton does not appear on screen at all in this episode.

Shizaki and Marx dominated the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels with clean tag wrestling; Saafir Muhammed grew increasingly unhinged at ringside and Avery Prosser pulled the DRS back before the match reached a fall, and the bout was awarded to Shizaki and Marx. Unusual finish: no pinfall or submission is shown on-screen; the text does not explain the mechanism of the awarded decision, only that Shizaki and Marx 'were awarded ten points for the victory.' Post-match, the DRS are found laid out backstage with a threatening note referencing 'the sins of another' and warning that 'the one at fault will be held responsible' next week.

Viper largely ignored his partner Dubov, leaving her to be worked over alone; late in the match Viper blindsided Magnum Machine with the ring bell to help Dubov score a pin, but Jason Payne ran in with the bell as evidence, and the finish was reversed into a disqualification win for Rabesque and Machine after Viper attacked Rabesque; Cameron Cruise then ran in with a chair to chase Viper off. A threatening note ('Be careful Jean, you're walking on broken glass. -L') and broken glass are left in Rabesque's locker room before the match; the 'L' signature is not identified in the text. The referee also rings the bell prematurely/in apparent confusion earlier in the match after a Rabesque rollup that never reached three.

Shawn Matthews ducked an errant Southern superkick meant for him that instead flattened Southern's own partner Aidan Campbell; Eddy Love then hit Southern with a megaphone shot to take him out, and Matthews covered Campbell for the pin. Match set up by Calvin Carlton and Aaron Douglas pairing Love with Matthews after Campbell superkicked Love earlier on 'The Wild Side'. Post-match, Southern nearly throws Aaron Douglas off the stage before superkicking him instead. Both this match's build ('Showtime Exclusive') and the match itself appear separately in the episode; only the live-called match is counted here.

Beau Michaels appeared to pin Not Jonathan Marx after a Not Craig Miles elbow strike, but instant replay showed Not Marx's own shoulders were down across Michaels in the same fall; the referee ruled a double pin and declared a draw, with all four men awarded ten points. Billed by NFW East officials/Chairman Castor Strife as a match to help decide who gets the next shot at Manson's NFW World Heavyweight Title; the draw leaves that unresolved. Post-match, a furious Not Jonathan Marx attacks both Manson and Not Craig Miles with a chair.

With Dan Ryan holding Not Craig Miles in a headscissors, Manson kicked his own partner Not Miles out of the ring and covered Ryan himself; referee Greg Herpin counted the pin despite Manson not being the legal man, over Lindsay Troy's on-screen protests that it wasn't legal. Main event, three-way six-man tag (NFW East vs. NFW North vs. NFW South). Shane Southern runs in mid-match with a described 'darker' demeanor and brawls with Hornet, contributing to the chaos around the finish. The announced pin is explicitly protested as illegitimate in the text but stands as the result. Post-match, NFW East fans and cast flood ringside to celebrate, sparking a real riot between East and North fans that spills into the parking lot -- this is the riot depicted in the episode's cold open ('Bait'/'Welcome to the Show').

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Jul 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: With the referee distracted checking on Highwayman, a second man also dressed as the Highwayman appeared from the crowd and hit Matthews with a Cutter. The original Highwayman then covered Matthews for the pin. A mysterious second man in Highwayman gear provided the interference; his identity is not revealed in this document. Never guessed at here per the ambiguity rule.

As Douglas went to the top rope for a moonsault, Saafir Muhammed appeared and shoved him off into a Marx small package for the pin. Post-match, Muhammed continued attacking Douglas until a three-way brawl broke out among all three men and security separated them. Commentary states Marx becomes 'the first CENTURY MARK wrestler in New Frontier Wrestling' (see awards_mentioned).

Ryan hit the Humility Bomb, then tried to hogtie Hollywood with rope brought from outside; the Seven Deadly Sins ran in and beat Ryan down before Lindsay Troy and Kazuo Shizaki made the save with chairs. Ryan was awarded the win and 10 points via disqualification. Lindsay Troy's manager/advisor role for Hollywood ('The Ego Buster') is stated at the top of the segment, though she is described as absent at the bell; she appears later making the save. Post-match Troy challenged Hollywood to a Lumberjack Rules match; Avery Prosser later threatened to suspend Ryan from Ultratitle competition.

After a back-and-forth sequence including a Stratton moonsault bodypress, Shizaki connected with the Tsume Mahi strike for the pin. Neil Riddick (Stratton's manager) was at ringside and was needled by Shizaki before the match, comically falling over. Win pushed Shizaki to 85 points.

The 15-minute time limit expired with both competitors still slugging it out; the bell ended the match with no decision. Both were NFW Season I tryout wrestlers being evaluated for the Season II roster; Quentin Sullivan promised both an unsanctioned rematch at Random Rumble.
Hiroshi hit a moonsault bodypress but Sands kicked out right as the bell rang for the time limit; both men gain 5 points and remain tied in the NFW North playoff race.

Deacon set up Melton for the Altar Call, but Melton slipped out, hit a DDT, and rolled Deacon up for the pin. Melton takes a temporary division lead. Commentary frames this as the first move in a chess game ahead of the later Eddy Love vs. Jean Rabesque match.

Viper grabbed manager Vivian Ryconik as a human shield; Southern superkicked her to the floor by mistake, then superkicked Viper for the pin. Vivian Ryconik was taken out on a stretcher after the accidental superkick; a backstage confrontation between Shane Southern and Aidan Campbell followed, with Campbell warning Southern to keep Vivian away from ringside.

With Rabesque holding Love in a Figure Four Leglock, security and Irish police stormed the ring after Calvin Carlton claimed he had been assaulted; Rabesque broke the hold and fled the building. The match was declared a no contest. Earlier the same night, Rabesque revealed himself as the season's mystery attacker of DC Stratton, Neil Riddick, and Jeff Cummins, then bound and caned Calvin Carlton at the top of the ramp before this match. Referee named as Bruce Phillips.

The referee called for the bell to end the match without a decision after a large NFW East contingent (a man impersonating Craig Miles, Benjamin, Bueno Excellente, and hired 'goons') ran in, followed by a Steel Viper run-in and finally a Deacon clothesline run-in that scattered the East group. The document never states an explicit result (no 'no contest' or 'draw' declared), so winner and result are left null per the brief. This match revealed Cameron Cruise had aligned with the NFW East, setting up the trade announced later in the show at the closing 'Special Press Conference' segment (not itself a match: Quentin Sullivan announced Dan Ryan and DC Stratton traded from North to South Conference for Steel Viper and Cameron Cruise; DC Stratton was then released outright, and Lindsay Troy's NFW North managerial license was rendered defunct).

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Aug 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Douglas caught Hiroshi in a Full Nelson, but Hiroshi reversed into a Dragon Suplex for the pin. Shown joined-in-progress (live broadcast content, not a replay). Blaine Hollywood interfered against Douglas mid-match; Lindsay Troy ran down afterward and attacked Hollywood, breaking an announce table with a dropkick.

With Matthews blinded by powder thrown by Beau Michaels, Cruise hooked in the 'Cruise Control' for the submission win. Aaron Douglas (Matthews' manager, in a wheelchair) distracted the referee; Jason Payne then rolled Douglas away against his wishes; Steel Viper caned Payne at ringside. Mercedes Devon was explicitly absent from Cruise's corner this week. Post-match, Eddy Love chair-shotted Matthews and helped Aaron Douglas turn on him, apparently ending the Matthews/Douglas partnership.

After Rabesque bullied Viper's father at ringside, Viper spat red mist in Rabesque's face and hit a double-arm DDT, but the bell had already rung against him; Rabesque is awarded the match via disqualification. Viper's parents were seated at ringside. After the DQ, Viper violently attacked both parents -- kicking his father, ramming his mother into the ringpost, and delivering a Viperbomb to his father -- shocking the announce team. Ringside attendants confiscated Singapore canes both men brought to the ring before the bell.

Marx locked in the Marxism crossface in the center of the ring; Sands could not reach the ropes and tapped out. A different wrestler billed as 'NOT MARX' (the NFW East gimmick) ran in mid-match and chop-blocked Sands, apparently helping the real Jonathan Marx; Sands recovered and continued before eventually submitting. Marx remains the North's overall points leader heading into the Random Rumble.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage (must win by pinfall or submission only; special referee)
matches.note: After a long exchange including a superplex off the cage, Not Jonathan Marx rolled Beau up and special referee Not Craig Miles counted the pin. Special referee for the match was Not Craig Miles, pre-approved by both competitors. Michael Manson climbed the cage to interfere but was crotched on top by Not Miles shaking the structure, then shoved off through the broadcast table by Beau. After the pin, Not Jonathan Marx, Beau, Not Craig Miles, and Brandon Jacobs (joined by Mercedes and Snow White) brutally beat down the incapacitated Manson, eventually handcuffing him to the top of the cage.

matches.stipulation: Interconference Specialty Tag Match, one fall
matches.note: Steel Viper interfered outside the ring, chair-shotting and applying the Viper Clutch to Kazuo Shizaki; with Shizaki incapacitated and Dan Ryan cutting a promo in the ring, referee Greg Herpin counted both Ryan and Shizaki out at ringside. Late in the match Michael Manson blindsided and superkicked his own tag partner Shane Southern with 'Sweet Dreams' after Dan Ryan appeared to be trying to help Southern's team win; security handcuffed Steel Viper to the guardrail for his interference. The finish is unusually chaotic; recorded here as a count-out win for Southern/Manson since the opposing team was counted out, though Manson's assault on his own partner immediately beforehand is a striking anomaly.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Sep 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Ultimate Jeopardy Random Rumble (elimination by pin, submission, or over-the-top-rope; eliminated wrestlers' points transfer to their eliminator; winner takes all and the NFW East playoff position)

eliminations.note: Blinded by Michael Manson's red mist, then back body dropped over the top rope by his own teammate Beau.
Caught in Manson's Tourniquet Crossface, assisted by Not Jonathan Marx pulling back on the neck, until the referee ruled him out.
Manson pulled down the top rope as Marx charged, sending him tumbling to the floor into Brandon Jacobs.

matches.note: Manson entered the match disguised as the ringside cameraman, attacking before revealing himself, then survived a prolonged three-on-one beatdown. He unmasked 'Not Jonathan Marx' as Jonathan Marx by pulling off his panda mask mid-move, then eliminated him last to win. Manson never appeared for his announced entrance; officials believed he had failed to show until he was revealed to have been posing as the cameraman all match. Post-match, color commentator Mad Hatter (a former wrestler) attacked Manson in the ring but was hit with the 'Sweet Dreams' finisher and left lying next to Manson's blood-written 'NFW EAST 2004' message on the mat.

matches.stipulation: Random Rumble, Bunkhouse Style (weapons legal; 8 men, elimination by pinfall or submission worth 5 points each, 20 points and the win to the survivor)

eliminations.note: Matthews was blindsided with a broken camera by Shane Southern and fell awkwardly off the apron, appearing genuinely injured; Rabesque then covered him for the elimination.

A mysterious facepainted man calling himself 'WASP' arrived by car, pulled down the top rope to spill Hornet to the floor, and hit him with a metal briefcase; crowd chanted 'Miles', implying he could be a disguised Craig Miles.
Jackknife pin.
Ryan deliberately lay down and demanded Southern pin him, apparently gifting him the win/division.
Southern voluntarily stepped over the top rope to eliminate himself immediately after pinning Ryan, having already clinched his division.
Rabesque charged Melton on the apron to knock him to the floor; Melton ducked and Rabesque's own momentum carried him over the top, eliminating him.

matches.note: Melton, the last man remaining after Rabesque's own charge sent him to the floor, won the South Conference Random Rumble and the South Regular Season Championship at age 40. Post-match, Lindsay Troy (arm wrapped in barbed wire) ambushed Jean Rabesque with a crossface, continuing their feud. 'WASP' is later interviewed backstage ranting about NFW and hinting at deeper conspiracies; his identity is left unconfirmed in this document, and it is ambiguous whether he was a formally numbered entrant or purely an outside interferer.

matches.stipulation: Two-ring steel cage Random Rumble with the Seven Deadly Sins and Jason Payne as lumberjacks on top of the cage; elimination by pin or submission worth 5 points each, but the match itself can only be won by escaping over the top of the cage to the floor

eliminations.note: Top-rope belly-to-back suplex for the pin, after Jason Payne (a lumberjack) hit Viper with a trash can top. Security immediately removed Viper from the cage.
Marx clipped Hiroshi's knee mid-powerbomb attempt, then locked in the Marxism for the tapout.
Cruise rolled Marx up by the tights for the pin during a chaotic multi-man exchange.

matches.note: In the final two, after a nearly 40-minute war, Kazuo Shizaki fought off a chair shot and interference from the Seven Deadly Sins lumberjacks, hit Cameron Cruise with an elevator drop off the top of the cage, and climbed down to touch the floor for the win in 43 minutes 24 seconds. Despite being eliminated mid-match by Cruise, Jonathan Marx had already clinched the #1 seed and the North Conference Regular Season Championship on points. Shawn Douglas and an unidentified masked man ran in mid-match, tasering and fighting off several Seven Deadly Sins members (Blaine Hollywood, Jason Payne, Malik Anderson) to open a path for Cruise and Shizaki to attempt cage escapes. The masked man closed the show cryptically addressing Avery Prosser and an unnamed 'boss', announcing a Lindsay Troy vs. Blaine Hollywood Lumberjack match for the following week.

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Dec 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: NFW East Conference Rules, Falls Count Anywhere, with a steel cage lowered over the ring during the entrances
matches.note: With the cage door open and the bout spilled to the floor and ramp, Shane Southern ran in and chairshotted Jonathan Marx from behind while Marx had his back turned arguing with him. Michael Manson made the cover for the staged, announced pin. Announced stipulation was Falls Count Anywhere under NFW East rules; a steel cage was also revealed descending from the rafters as a surprise element and both men fought in and out of it. Michael Manson retained the NFW World Heavyweight Championship (Sims: 'AND STILL WORLD CHAMPION') and advanced to the Ultratitle Finals. Finish was via outside interference from Shane Southern (not a competitor in this match), staged and announced as legitimate. Post-match, Jonathan Marx's cornermen Brandon Jacobs and Arthur 'Werewolf' Marx attacked Manson and were both put down (Jacobs flipped to the concrete, both hit with 'Sweet Dreams').

matches.stipulation: Declared mid-segment by Calvin Carlton (as NFW South commissioner) as a 'Wheelchair Match' under 'Tug-of-War rules' with the men's wheelchairs roped together; see note
