matches.note: After a Melton Figure Four Leglock was broken with help from Lindsay Troy, and Melton missed a top-rope move after Troy yanked his leg, Shane Southern hit his 'Party's Over' superkick and pinned Melton for the three count. Calvin Carlton's declared 'Wheelchair Match/Tug-of-War' stipulation was not actually what was contested once the bell rang for the real match — both men wrestled a standard match on their feet with pinfalls and a submission attempt (Figure Four), so the announced stipulation and the bout as called by commentary do not match; flagged rather than resolved. Referee was Greg Herpin. Lindsay Troy (Melton's manager) interfered on both men's behalf during the match, including breaking Melton's Figure Four and costing him the finish. Immediately after the bell, Dan Ryan ran in and chairshotted the winner, Shane Southern, then hit a 'Humility Bomb' on him on the entrance ramp;

date.source: the document's own dateline (4 Jun 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Wong-Fei Hung II hit a Shadowless Kick (bicycle kick) for the three count after Douglas kicked out of an earlier Unfathomable Dream Stance jump kick and avoided a Senton Splash. Framed as a mock nature-documentary bit ('As narrated by Leonard Nimoy to his grandchildren').

After Ryan hit a Humility Bomb (skyscraper powerbomb) sending both to the floor, Ryan beat the referee's ringside count back into the ring while Troy could not, giving Ryan the win by count-out. Text uses a numbered ringside count-up (to twenty) rather than the word 'countout'; inferred as a count-out finish. Commentary frames the match around Troy having previously managed/been close to Ryan.

Southern arrived limping badly after a backstage assault shown in the preceding vignette; Marx attacked him before the bell, targeted the hurt knee, and forced a tapout with the STF ('Marxism'). Southern was attacked by an unidentified assailant backstage minutes earlier ('his unidentifiable enemy'); the text never names the attacker.

Cruise hit a series of fifteen gutbusters followed by a Shipwreck for the pinfall. Cruise continued stomping Michaels-Cruise's midsection after the bell until security intervened; a follow-up medical vignette and commentary confirm this ended Michaels-Cruise's kayfabe pregnancy storyline.

After a back-and-forth brawl, Maggot escaped a full nelson with a low blow and hit his finishing Mutilator for the pin. Billed as Maggot's NFW regular-season debut; commentary references his earlier time-limit draw with Lindsay Troy at WrestleBowl.

After an extended high-spot exchange (including a missed Shattered Horizon swanton and a Tsume Mahi claw counted sequence), Felix Red hit a sit-out Dominator ('Ecstacy of Agony') for the pin. Referee named as Asai Tseng; ring announcer Cannibal Peters awards Red '10 points' with the win. Billed as Felix Red's NFW debut against Season 1 playoff standout Shizaki.

matches.stipulation: No DQ, No Count-Out, No Time Limit ('There MUST be a WINNER!')
matches.note: After an extreme brawl with chairs, thumbtacks and a table, and repeated interference from Manson's 'Goon Squad' (Prizm, Flint M. Jacobs, Matthew Malone) and Manson ally Spectrum -- plus both broadcasters Rayne and Green Machine physically intervening for their preferred man -- Doc Silver pinned a bloodied Manson with an Aces Full using the title belt as a weapon. Extremely violent, weapons-heavy main event; Manson kicked out of numerous prior finishers (Aces Full x2, a chair-assisted stool shot, a con-chair-to on Prizm, a superplex through a table onto thumbtacks) before finally losing.

date.source: the document's own dateline (4 Jul 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Beau Michaels-Cruise disrupted the match by throwing what appeared to be a dead infant into the ring, distracting Cameron Cruise long enough for Doc Silver to superkick him and hit the Widow's Peak (also called 'The River') for the pin. A steel cage is shown suspended above the ring before this match but is not used or referenced as a stipulation here; it factors into the night's main event instead.

Payne ducked Wong's Shadowless Kick and hit the Payne-Killer for the pin. Shown as a highlight recap of a match that happened earlier the same evening on this broadcast; treated as this document's own match record.

With Stone in control, Yakamo hit a low blow the referee missed, then threw powder in Stone's eyes ('Yori=Awesome') to get the pinfall. Both wrestlers' NFW debuts. Shown as a highlight recap of an earlier match on this same broadcast. Damian Stone's wife/valet Echo got involved at ringside, distracting the referee.

Shizaki hit the Tsume Mahi (Claw of Paralysis) and rolled Marx into a pin; Marx's arm was trapped under the bottom rope, out of the referee's sight, when the three-count was made. Head referee Tenshi Tseng. Marx's seconds Brandon Jacobs and Domovoi were sent to the back mid-match at his insistence. After a post-match handshake, Marx sucker-punched Shizaki, protesting the finish.

Beau Michaels hit a standing headscissors facebuster called 'Love Lost' for the pin. Referee given as 'Tenchi Tseng' here (likely the same person as 'Tenshi Tseng' elsewhere in the document; not resolved). Both men used repeated low blows during the match without being disqualified.

After a long, violent match including a table spot and dueling near-falls, Felix Red collapsed on top of an already-down Troy while attempting to finish her with a baseball bat, and the referee made a three-count credited to Troy. Shown as a highlight recap of a match earlier in this same broadcast. The exact mechanics of the final pin are unclear from the text (Red physically falls on top of Troy, yet the count and the reactions of Ryoko/Doc/Mikoto all read as a Troy win); flagged as ambiguous. Post-match, Red attacked again with the bat, striking Troy's manager/fiance Joey Melton (who took the shot for her) before Dan Ryan ran in for the save.

Powers hit a Slingshot Powerbomb and, though he could not properly hook the leg, collapsed on top of Hiroshi for the three-count. Kevin Powers' first match back after roughly a year away from wrestling. Commentary's closing line ('HE'S BACK AND HE'S WON') was read as crediting Powers with the win, consistent with the finishing sequence; flagged as a slightly ambiguous call.

After an extended, bloody brawl in which both men fell from and were thrown against a steel cage suspended above the ring, Ryan hit the Humility Bomb and, though barely conscious himself, draped an arm over Manson for the three-count. Commentary and the referee explicitly state this remained a standard one-fall match despite the suspended cage ('This match remains winner by a single fall in the ring...despite the cage'), so no stipulation is recorded. Referee Asai Tseng (twin brother of Tenshi Tseng, per commentary). Both men were stretchered out afterward.

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 Aug 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: After a sprawling brawl through the arena, a parking lot, a rival dojo, a hijacked airplane, and a hospital, Dan Ryan finally pinned Felix Red with a Humility Bomb in a hospital corridor. Broadcast in five separate installments across the show, with referee Asai Tseng trailing throughout. Felix's ally the Mad Hatter repeatedly assisted him (getaway driving, mace spray, was used as a weapon by Ryan); a masked 'Panda Mask IV,' teased to debut the following week, sprayed black mist in Ryan's face and hit a Panda-Suplex on him at the dojo. Treated here as a single match ordered at its first appearance; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Two out of Three Falls
matches.note: Manson won two falls to one: Marx took the first with a jumping piledriver, lost the second when the referee rang the bell on him for refusing to release his own submission hold, and lost the third when he tapped out to Manson's Tourniquet Crossface. Billed as a rivalry between former mentor (Manson) and student (Marx). Post-match, Domovoi and Brandon Jackobs attacked Manson while Marx got in cheap shots, until Maggot ran in with a chair to make the save. Commentary frames this segment as being shown 'from earlier in the evening,' though unlike other clip segments it is called in full continuous detail; see lane_notes.

Cameron Cruise dominated much of the match and even knocked Maggot out cold with the ring bell, but Maggot no-sold it, fought back, and finished Cruise with the Trash Compactor (Electric Chair Face Bomb) for the pin. Referee Asai Tseng let several borderline tactics (a low blow, an extended choke) go uncalled. Cruise was accompanied by Mercedes Devon.

Lindsay Troy won her first NFW match, pinning Kin Hiroshi with a top-rope Blockbuster Bulldog after a back-and-forth battle that included a Bronco Buster and dueling near-falls. Joey Melton was at ringside for Troy; the referee watched him closely throughout.

After Ryoko Takanohana twice saved Doc Silver from a pinfall and Silver landed a low blow behind the referee's back, Silver finished Powers with his finisher 'The River' for the pin to retain the title. Silver exposed a turnbuckle pad mid-match and used it against Powers. Powers kicked out of a Chokeslam, an Aces Full attempt, and other near-finishes before ultimately losing.

Shown as a highlight earlier in the broadcast, a match taken earlier that day. Fei-Hung controlled the opening with the Seven Cat Nerve Pinch, then Michaels hit a clothesline and his finisher Love Lost: "After the three seconds it was all academic."

Shown as a highlight, a match taken earlier that night. Shizaki took control until Yakamo Jr. kicked him low behind the referee's back and hit the YORI=AWESOME (a reverse sitout tombstone): "three taps of the canvas later it was Yakamo Jr. celebrating", for ten points.

Shown as a highlight of an earlier match, in the Ultratitle points race. Damian Stone (with his manager Echo), Jason Payne and Troy Douglas fought in a three-way; Payne took out Douglas with his finisher The Payne Killer and collected the ten points. Troy Douglas is not registered and is left off the sides.

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Oct 2000), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: 30-Man Random Rumble (elimination by pinfall, submission, or being thrown over the top rope to the floor)

eliminations.note: First man eliminated; thrown over the top rope.
Commentary declares 'Price gone' as Torch slings him to the floor with one move; no explicit referee-signal phrase is shown for this one, unlike most other eliminations.
Made to submit to a leg-and-arm lock, then tossed over the top rope.

Bloodhunt's ringside allies Flint M. Grand Elder Susano-O-No-Mikoto was shown giving a cutthroat signal just before Panda Mask's interference, implying he ordered it. Document explicitly calls this a 'DOUBLE KNOCKOUT'; mapped to result "no-contest" per lane convention (see lane_notes).

After a back-and-forth interconference flyer showcase with numerous near-falls and reversals, Almasy reversed a Hurricanrana into a Sitout Powerbomb, then hit a top-rope Ultima (Shooting Star Press) for the pin. The document itself spells this wrestler's name two ways: 'Lindsay Troy' in the segment title/Credits and header narration, and 'LINDSEY TROY' when introduced by the ring announcer; sides here use the ring-announced spelling, discrepancy flagged for the coordinator.

Payne hit the Payne Killer (Full Nelson Slam) and pinned Beau Michaels clean after Michaels was left dazed by the shocking ringside appearance of a diapered, purple-skinned giant man later suggested to be his and 'Cammy's' son. Commentary handled partly by a special guest 'Monkey With Stick' and his translator Sergei the Organ Grinder. The mysterious 'son' storyline is followed up backstage with Beau confirming the claim to Snow White.

After Yori chair-shotted referee Shin Takayuma, both men played possum; when Hiroshi checked on him, Yori rolled him up for the pin. Yori used repeated illegal tactics throughout (low blow, eye poke, back rake, throat shot) with referee Takayuma described as inexperienced/lenient.

After extended brawling and a Craig Miles chair shot that knocked out Doc Silver at ringside (sandwiching his head on the steel steps), Mike Manson crawled over to pin Kazuo Shizaki for the win. Doc Silver nearly made Shizaki submit to the Liontamer while the referee was distracted by a Miles/Silver brawl outside. Post-match, Beau Michaels ran in to check on the fallen Doc Silver and was assaulted by Dan Dority (wrestling as 'Spectrum,' filling in for an injured 'Prizm') with two Sit-Out Powerbombs and then Silver's own finisher, 'The River,' while Silver held his NFW World Heavyweight Title aloft — the title was not at stake in the tag match itself.

Both men brawled to ringside where Panda Mask blindsided them with a top-rope 'Space Flying Panda Attack'; the referee counted both out to twenty for a double countout, with no points awarded to either. Panda Mask's interference again appeared to follow a cutthroat gesture from Grand Elder Mikoto.

After a lengthy exchange, Felix Red hit a top-rope tornado DDT followed by the Shattered Horizon senton bomb for the pin. Commentary is heavily interspliced with surreal 'astral plane' dream-sequence cutaways narrated by guest commentator the Mad Hatter, who correctly predicts the finish via a pre-written letter; treated as narrative color around a real in-ring contest, not archival replay.

Windham stalled outside the ring and avoided contact for the opening minutes while Maggot dominated once the match began. After August De La Rossi ran in from the crowd and hit a Slackknife on the eye-poke-blinded Maggot, Windham followed with his own Slackknife for the pin. Referee Asai Tseng. Grand Elder Mikoto had bribed Maggot before the match to cripple Windham permanently. After the loss-via-interference, Mikoto had security surround Windham and De La Rossi and ordered Maggot to finish them; Maggot reluctantly complied, chair-shotting and 'Trash Compactor'-ing both men on the bare floor after the bell.

matches.note: Kooter Michaels-Cruise ran in and struck Lindsay Troy with a surfboard; disoriented, she stumbled into her opponent Michael Manson, who accidentally connected with his own finisher and fell on top of her for the pin. Troy's announced tag partner Dan Ryan never appeared -- a later backstage segment reveals he was drunk, disoriented, and effectively stranded on his flight to the show -- leaving Troy to face Manson and Felix Red essentially alone. Felix Red also accidentally kicked his own partner Manson during the interference chaos.

After Maggot cornered Yori outside the ring, referee Shin Takayuma confiscated a chair from Maggot; Yori then blindsided Maggot with a hidden steel-plated copy of his own book and finished him with a reverse sitout tombstone piledriver for the pin. The referee's name is spelled both 'Shin Takayuma' and 'Takayama' within the source text (preserved verbatim). Yori also used a concealed low blow and an eye poke earlier in the match.

Kin Hiroshi pinned Jonathan Marx with a bridging German suplex, but the referee ruled it a simultaneous double pin because Marx had earlier pinned Hiroshi in a fall the rest of the field broke up; ring announcer Cannibal Peters declared both Marx and Hiroshi winners. This six-man tag carried individual stipulations for each of Doc Silver's three challengers: a win would earn Kevin Powers and Kin Hiroshi future NFW World Title shots and Beau Michaels the right to name a man-servant from the NFW East, all under a threat of unspecified 'consequences' from Susano-o-no-Mikoto if his handpicked champions weren't sufficiently tested. Doc Silver spent much of the match avoiding direct engagement and tagging teammates in instead. Kooter Michaels-Cruise interfered mid-match, knocking out Cameron Cruise with a surfboard shot. After the decision, Mikoto's enforcers Panda Mask and Dan Dority ran in a

Beau Michaels pinned Panda Mask with a top-rope moonsault after Kevin Powers ran in and hit Panda Mask with a chair shot that the referee saw but did not penalize. This extra match was ordered on the spot by Susano-o-no-Mikoto at his granddaughter Ryoko's request, specifically so Beau Michaels could be formally pinned as humiliation; the win still carried the earlier stipulation letting Beau name a man-servant from the NFW East, though Mikoto stripped it of any standings points. Beau used the win to name Mikoto himself as his 'man-servant,' and Mikoto was then forcibly carried off and driven away by Beau's escort at the close of the show.

Manson entered with a Santa Claus-costumed companion, 'Hoteiosho,' who interfered on his behalf; Hiroshi choke-slammed and hit a Burning Hammer ('Hiroshi-ma Bomb') on Hoteiosho, prompting Manson to abandon the match. Manson briefly 'Hulked out' mid-match, hitting two Hornet Splashes before Hiroshi warded off a third with a mock-crucifix gesture. Kin Hiroshi is separately established (in the cold open) as holding a standing, anytime First Blood title shot against NFW World Champion Doc Silver, unused this show.

eliminations.note: Counted out after leaving the match to attend a special movie screening backstage with cameo guest Heath Ledger.

matches.note: After Beau Michaels was eliminated by count-out, Maggot hit the Mutilator on Kevin Powers for the pin. Post-match, Maggot went to the backstage movie screening and attacked Beau Michaels, throwing him through the projection screen in front of guest star Heath Ledger.

matches.stipulation: Number One Contendership Match for the NFW World Heavyweight Championship, one fall, 10 points
matches.note: Yori Yakamo Jr. shattered a novelty sex-toy item over Dan Ryan's face, then hit his reverse sit-out tombstone ('Yori=Awesome') for the pin to become the number-one contender for the NFW World Heavyweight Championship. Extensive weapon (novelty item) use played for comedy; the referee confiscated and later returned pieces of the item without checking Yori's tights, allowing a smuggled second piece to factor into the finish. Commentary calls the finish a cheat, but the staged result stands.

Marx wrestled with two unnamed masked men stationed atop the cage as backup, apparently linked to a mysterious 'Panda Mask IV'; the original Panda Mask (Marx's trainer) watched from a VIP skybox. Doc Silver was busted open early and bled heavily through the match. This match/segment is missing its own writer-credit line in the show's printed Credits block despite being the advertised featured bout.

Both men entered off recent results: Maggot won a triple threat the prior week, Ryan lost to Yori Yakamo Jr. the prior week.

Marx was visibly disgusted with himself afterward.

After Payne reversed Manson's Sweet Dreams attempt into a second Full Nelson (Payne Killer), Manson caught him with a sudden Small Package for the pin. Manson is billed as the 2005 Ultratitle winner; the match was framed as significant with both men tied at 30 points apiece heading in. Manson's valet Rayne provided a ringside distraction that helped him counter an earlier Piledriver attempt.

After a long exchange of finishers (Kin's Burning Hammer, Felix's Ecstasy of the Agony sit-out dominator and Shattered Horizon senton), Kin reversed a Felix backdrop attempt into a sunset flip for the pin. Post-match, Felix Red attacked the celebrating Kin Hiroshi, and NFW World Champion Doc Silver's enforcers Dan Dority and Panda Mask then assaulted Kin further, delivering a verbal warning from Doc that Kin must publicly name his eventual title-shot stipulations a week in advance or face continued beatings; Felix finished the beatdown himself with an Ecstasy of the Agony off a chair onto the guardrail, leaving Kin bleeding.

After extensive interference from both corners (Dan Dority chokeslamming Yori and taking an 'Aces Full' meant for the blinded referee; Yori nearly winning with his own weapon), Doc turned Yori's own weapon against him with an eye-poke and finished him with his signature move, The River, for the pin. Main event, for the NFW World Heavyweight Championship (Doc Silver retains); this segment has no writer-credit line in the document's own Credits block, unlike every other segment on the show — flagged as a likely source defect/omission.

Billed as the first half of the show's double main event. Commentary frames this as the biggest win of Monsieur Fantastic's career, done in part to avenge his fired former student Maggot. Fantastic injures his left shoulder early via a ringside fall and wrestles through it for the rest of the match.

Weapons (a table, a chair) are allowed without disqualification, per commentary, because it is a title match. matches.stipulation: I Quit

Commentary itself questions whether Payne actually spoke the words 'I Quit.' Per the brief's rule, the staged, announced result (Manson wins by submission) stands.

Felix Red lands the Swanton Bomb for the pin after Kooter Michaels-Cruise is incapacitated by a second, GHB-laced bottle of Mountain Dew that Ryoko slips him mid-match. Kooter's father Cameron Cruise tries to warn him off the drink; the referee does not react to the drugging. This is billed pre-match as a title defense for Felix Red.

The real, current Monsieur Fantastic hits the Trash Compactor on Doc Silver for the deciding pin, then unmasks as Maggot. Staged as Monsieur Fantastic wagering his mask to win back his student Maggot's NFW contract/career from Doc Silver; no single named stipulation type is given. Before the finish, the Fantastic mask/identity is worn in sequence by five different people, each producing its own mini-finish: Jericoholic Anonymous (pinned by Doc's Aces Full), retired legend Bobby R (pinned by Doc's Aces Full), Ryoko as 'Mademoiselle Fantastic' (low-blows Doc, unmasks, fires broadcaster Greenie on air, does not wrestle a fall), Michael Manson (hits two Stunners on Doc and Ryoko but does not go for a cover), and the retired original Monsieur Fantastic Jean-Pierre Gauthard (loses to Doc's River after a rope-break controversy and an eye rake). Recorded here as one match matching the show's sin

matches.stipulation: Strap Match (NFW Round One Playoff Elimination); each man strapped not to the other, but individually to Kooter Cruise
matches.note: After Kooter Cruise repeatedly disrupted both men (including double-chokeslamming the referee), Felix Red used a chair slipped to him by the Mad Hatter, hit a tombstone piledriver onto the chair, then landed the Ecstasy of the Agony (angle slam sitout dominator) on Cameron Cruise and touched the fourth and final corner to win. matches.stipulation: NFW East Wild Card Round Playoff Match
matches.note: After a one-sided beating of Yori Yakamo Jr. (including a leaping piledriver) and late interference from the mysterious Powermaster, who nearly strangled Yori, the referee stopped the match at the 21-minute mark and disqualified Jason Payne for allowing his opponent to be attacked. The man introduced in the ring as Jason Payne is revealed mid-entrance, before the bell, to be an impostor (unmasked on camera as 'NOT Craig Miles') who ambushes Yori with a chair; the broadcast nonetheless continues billing this figure as Jason Payne for the remainder of the segment, the in-ring action, and the official result. Recorded as staged-announced per the binding rule; the identity swerve is flagged rather than resolved. Powermaster's late interference (choking Yori) directly precipitates the stoppage and DQ.

matches.stipulation: NFW Playoff Match (Eastern Conference)
matches.note: Maggot survived a prolonged beating -- including a corner press slam and a missed Dan Ryan moonsault that instead drove Ryan into the barricade -- then hit a cradle piledriver for the pin and the upset win. A mid-match stretch is marked within the broadcast itself as censored ('THIS PORTION OF THE TELECAST HAS BEEN DELETED BY REQUEST OF MANY LAWYERS AND THE STATE OF TEXAS'), with commentary picking back up at the 15-minute mark.

matches.stipulation: NFW Playoff Match (Eastern Conference)
matches.note: Doc Silver finished a mentally unraveled Kin Hiroshi (who spends the match believing himself dead) with the White Trash Wipeout for the pin, advancing to face Felix Red next round. Felix Red interferes at ringside partway through, stabbing Hiroshi with a syringe (referred to on commentary as 'Captain Morphine'), which visibly affects Hiroshi before the finish. Hiroshi realizes mid-match that he is not actually dead after seeing his own blood, prompting him to attack Felix Red at ringside before Doc Silver regains control.

After an extended brawl through the crowd and backstage areas, the two men returned to the ring where Felix Red hit a top-rope dragon-rana (360 hurricanrana) and held Manson's legs down for the pin to retain the title. The match begins with a pre-bell brawl after Manson's disciple Rayne canes Ryoko (the NFW East chairperson and Felix's wife) from behind as she attempts to announce a match stipulation ('Stipulation 670'). Commentary describes that stipulation as a handicap match adding a masked 'Panda Mask' on Felix's side against Manson, but it is never actually enacted -- the match proceeds and concludes as a standard one-on-one bout. The announced-but-unused stipulation is flagged in lane_notes rather than recorded as this match's stipulation.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match

Felix's camp planted a disguised interferer ('Sack Thing,' unmasked mid-match as Lindsay Lohan) to attack Doc Silver; Ryoko Mikoto also interfered directly (low blow) on Felix's behalf. Doc took an ugly unplanned-looking fall off the ladder to the floor that commentary treated as a legitimate, serious neck/head injury he continued through. Post-match, Doc offers Felix a handshake, then sucker-punches him with a White Trash Wipeout, spits on the title, and walks off holding his neck.
