A masked figure (identity never revealed on-air) climbed out of Manson's own robot prop mid-match and assaulted Manson with it; commentary never resolves who it was. This eliminates the reigning/former Ultratitle Champion Michael Manson from Ultratitle contention; a comedic hallucination sequence has Yori temporarily 'possessed' by the spirit of Hulk Hogan, which is played as an in-story event affecting the match rather than a break from the broadcast.

Kin Hiroshi hits the Hiroshima Bomb (Argentine backbreaker rack drop) for the pin after a back-and-forth main event with multiple near-falls on both sides. Main event of the Eastern Conference playoffs; the winner earns a championship match against Felix Red, which is the driving stake of the bout. Post-match, Felix Red runs in and attacks the injured Kin Hiroshi with a chair and a Brainbuster; Maggot returns to superplex Felix off the top rope in a save; Dan Ryan then runs in on Maggot, and Yori Yakamo Junior runs in for the save on Ryan, ending the show mid-brawl with next week's matches (Felix Red vs. Dan Ryan, Yori Yakamo Jr. vs. Maggot) teased.

date.source: the document's own dateline (29 Nov 2000), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Aragon hit a chokeslam followed by a reverse chokeslam off the turnbuckles for the pin at the 4:36 mark. Shown only as edited studio highlights, not as a full match. Studio commentary implies Cancer previously bailed Aragon out of jail.

Andersen Scott pinned Leroy Brown at the 3:56 mark after R.J. Quiksilver hit a Diamond Cutter. Shown only as edited studio highlights. The segment heading/Credits spell the names 'R.J. Quicksilver' and 'Anderson Scott,' while the in-text commentary spells them 'Quiksilver' and 'Andersen Scott'; the in-text spellings are used for the verbatim sides field. The SST member named here as 'Vito' is billed under a different name ('Cousin Vinny') for the same tag team in the prior lane document; both are kept verbatim without assuming identity.

Sean Toombs hit a sit-down powerbomb on White Tiger while Calamity simultaneously landed a moonsault (the combination called 'The Toolbox') for the pin. Debut of the tag team Hellmachine, managed by 'Doc' Martina Martens. Shown only as edited studio highlights.
Bondage hit a sit-down piledriver he calls 'Original Sin' for the pin. Golden Hawk is billed as a local Baltimore favorite; shown only as edited studio highlights.

Montezuma hit a rolling triple German suplex, bridging on the third, for the pin after Powell was too stunned to kick out. Powell attacked Montezuma's entourage before the bell; one of Montezuma's aides grabbed Powell's leg mid-match to help Montezuma regain control. Shown only as edited studio highlights. Commentary references ongoing off-screen financial/personal troubles for Powell.

After Manson DDT'd the referee, he set a rag on fire inside a steel chair and smashed it over Cancer's head; the broadcast cuts away to medics attending Cancer with no bell rung and no winner declared. Left unresolved on-screen; recorded as no winner/no result per the brief since the document never stages a decision. Jade (Cancer's valet) posted 666 off the apron mid-match; 666 and 4-PAC/'Demonic X' (bandaged after an earlier Torch attack) watch from ringside.

The match broke down into a mass brawl — Alex Wylde attacked guest commentator Aidan Campbell, Wildstar attacked Wylde, and Hellmachine's Sean Toombs and Calamity ran in swinging chairs — until referee Greg Herpin raised his arms and called for the bell without declaring a winner. Shown 'joined in progress' at the twelve-minute mark rather than in full. Ryan Connors hit a swinging DDT off the top rope and later a Diamond Cutter on Jeff Cummins, but no fall was ever completed before the stoppage. Nixon then appeared, restored order via security, and booked a follow-up tag match (Wildstar & Rick Ryconik vs. Alex Wylde & Steel Viper) later in the show as a consequence.

Ricky Zane rolled up Ares with his knees on Ares' shoulders and one hand on the second rope for illegal leverage; the referee did not see the rope-grab and counted the pin. Zane was coerced into this match by Nixon under threat of contract/financial exposure. Post-match, Ares choked out referee Greg Herpin with a Full Nelson Slam in anger over the finish.

Alex Wylde knocked out Rick Ryconik with an uppercut thrown using a concealed roll of quarters, then pinned him for the win. Booked by Nixon as a bonus match following the Oblivion Express/Showstoppers no-contest. Commentary explicitly calls the finish a 'tainted'/stolen win via a foreign object. References an earlier, otherwise-undocumented loss by Steel Viper to Rick Ryconik ('a few shows ago').

After a long back-and-forth defense, Bloodhunt hit the Cop Killer (Burning Hammer) on Torch for the deciding pinfall, retaining the title. Billed as the first-ever defense of the NFW World Heavyweight Championship, and Bloodhunt is noted as wrestling without his usual 'Elite Guard' after reports compared him unfavorably to another wrestler ('Doc II'). Ms. America placed Bloodhunt's foot on the ropes to break an early Torch pin attempt. During the match, Mike Manson ran in with a chair but was intercepted by Cancer and Jade; a mysterious returning figure called Rayne then ran in and attacked both Ms. America and Jade. After the pinfall, a recovering Torch threw a fireball that hit Bloodhunt in the chest as the broadcast closed, an angle left unresolved going into the next show. This segment has no corresponding entry in the document's own Credits block.

date.source: the document's own dateline (12 Aug 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The match broke down into a four-way brawl after run-ins from Jacob McKail and Maggot (the special referee), with security separating everyone; no finish is narrated. Not given its own Credits heading -- recapped in-show via highlight-reel narration during the 'Not Your Average Sportscenter Recap' studio segment as having happened earlier that evening. Maggot, drenched in whiskey, was the special referee.
Listed in the Credits and given a card position, but the document shows only a stillshot captioned 'Still in Progress' -- no actual match content is narrated for this bout.

Both men brawled to the outside through the crowd and a broadcast table; Kin Hiroshi and The New VD (Johnny Rage & Johnny Styles) repeatedly interfered, at one point physically holding Ryan back from re-entering the ring. With both men down and unable to beat the count, referee Scott Speranza rang the bell without a winner. Stipulation: Special Challenge Match. Billed with the implication that the winner earns a future World Title opportunity against Kin Hiroshi. Explicit double count-out per the brief's mapping rule. Heavy crowd 'BULLSHIT' chants followed the no-decision.

After a ladder-and-trashcan-strewn brawl, Joe the Plumber hit a 'Sh(*)t River Plunge' onto a ladder for the pin. Stipulation: Hardkorr Gravy Match, No Holds Barred, No Disqualifications, No Countouts -- the first match of its kind, contested in a ring filled with gravy, thumbtacks, and trash. Joe the Plumber is billed as co-champion alongside his plunger, personified as 'Shawn Hart'; both are announced as retaining. Referee: Tseng Tsi.

date.source: the document's own dateline (30 Sep 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Stevens hooked Cruise for his 'X-Terminator' (Osaka Street Cutter) and pinned him. Stipulation: National Title Elimination match (National Championship Tournament).

After manager Dirk Dickwood, in disguise, attacked Dusk and was fought off, Atken chop-blocked the weakened Dusk and locked in his 'Humiliation' Figure Four for the win as Dusk was rendered unable to continue. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- Second Round. A ringside carton labeled 'Yori Yakamo Junior's Industrial Strength Roofie Colada' is shown to have incapacitated both Dickwood and a cameraman during the match, implying tampering. Atken remains undefeated in the tournament.

With Rook Black caught in Teresa Q's Cross Armbreaker, the debuting/returning Legion led the crowd in 'TAP' chants; Rook, seemingly affected, tapped out. Stipulation: National Championship Tournament -- Round Two. Called by Paul Shiro and The Mad Hatter. After the bell, Rook Black clotheslined Teresa Q and appeared not to understand why he could no longer wrestle. Legion then cut a promo threatening Rook and referencing a 'first test' in Vancouver, promising a 'final test' at the next Crash TV.

Maggot pinned Jason Payne and Felix Red pinned Yori Yakamo Jr. at the same moment; special referee Kin Hiroshi ruled the simultaneous pinfalls a no-decision, declaring there was no winner. Kin Hiroshi entered as special referee with an absurd rulebook, then Craig Miles publicly overrode him mid-match, declaring Texas Tornado rules with no disqualifications and no countouts. Miles subsequently announced that Hiroshi must defend the World Title against an unnamed opponent next Crash TV, and set the next Crash TV main event as Felix Red & Maggot vs. Dan Ryan & Nova, with a future SuperCrash World Title opportunity on the line for the winners.

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Nov 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Kin Hiroshi hit the H.L.B. for the pinfall to retain the title, in what was billed as the first defense of his championship reign. The broadcast repeatedly lost its feed to static throughout the match due to the riot inside and outside the arena; commentary resumed mid-action each time. After the pin a rioter got into the ring and was leveled by Hiroshi's Japanese Thunder, and Cameron Cruise hit a superkick on another rioter; neither affected the decision.

matches.stipulation: Non-tournament exhibition bout (both wrestlers were undefeated in the National Championship Tournament, but this specific match was explicitly agreed as a non-sanctioned bout)
matches.note: Mike Randalls ran in swinging a Singapore cane apparently meant for Sean Stevens but struck Mittens T. Cat in the mask instead; the referee rang for the bell and Mittens was announced the winner. Shown to viewers only via narrated highlight-reel recap because the live broadcast had cut away to deal with the riot; the match itself is described as having occurred earlier in this same show, not on a prior broadcast. See lane_notes on how this lane treated recapped-but-same-show matches.

Dusk had Randalls reeling with strikes and slams, but Randalls turned the tide with a series of illegal low blows and an Iron Claw to the groin; the referee disqualified Randalls and awarded Dusk the win. Also shown only via recap narration rather than live, immediately following the Stevens/Mittens recap in the same segment. Afterward Sean Stevens ran in and hit Randalls with a chair, sparking a brawl among Stevens, Dusk, and Randalls; that brawl is not itself a match.

matches.stipulation: National Championship Tournament match (winner advances to the semifinals with a bye)
matches.note: Teresa Q hit a Crossarm Diamond Cutter (called "The Process of Illumination") for the pinfall win. Phil Atken's manager Dirk Dickwood interfered twice (tossing a coin into the ring as a distraction, then hooking Atken's leg onto the bottom rope to break a pin) without changing the outcome. Immediately after the decision, Rook Black ran in and chair-shotted Teresa Q, leading directly into the next segment.

The match's in-ring action is never shown; the broadcast cuts instead to a comedic writers'-room exchange and an unrelated sketch. A later line elsewhere in the show confirms only that Kooter Michaels-Cruise "failed to win the TV title," implying Joe the Plumber retained. The 'recap' immediately following this match is a self-aware, joking, out-of-fiction exchange between two named screen-handle scriptwriters arguing about how to cover the match, followed by an absurdist unrelated skit; it is not treated as a literal blow-by-blow (see privacy_flags and lane_notes). Joe the Plumber is elsewhere in this same show referred to as "CO-TELEVISION CHAMPION," suggesting an unexplained split/shared title arrangement not otherwise documented here.

matches.stipulation: Texas Tornado rules, with conditional pre-match stipulations: if Maggot was not at ringside, the match's No Disqualification/No Countout provision would be lifted and enforced instead as a standard match; and any wrestler who failed to reach ringside before the match was decided would be fired from
matches.note: With Maggot never arriving and Dan Ryan absent for most of the bout, Nova and Felix Red wrestled one-on-one; late in the match Dan Ryan finally fought his way to the ring, knocked out the referee, and attacked both Nova and Felix Red, after which Craig Miles declared the match a no-contest. Originally announced as a tag match, Dan Ryan & Nova vs. Felix Red & Maggot, with the winning team earning the right to wrestle at a Hulk-A-Thon qualifier for a World Championship shot at Wrestlestock (Hulk-A-Thon was itself cancelled later in the show). Maggot never arrived at all; Dan Ryan arrived only in the closing moments as an attacker rather than as a fighting tag partner, so he is recorded here as interference (and in non_match_appearances) rather than as a formal side.

date.source: the document's own dateline (29 Dec 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Title Tournament Semifinal; joined in progress, framed as having started earlier in the evening
matches.note: Mike Gordey locked Tsunami in a double underhook and hit a Tiger Driver for the pin, after Neil Riddick's Suicide Kings had spent the match on the back foot against Duncan and Gordey. Shown joined-in-progress at the '9:00 minute mark' as a recap of action that occurred before the broadcast's official start; treated as fresh content per the brief since it is presented as this show's own footage, not an archival replay. Neil Riddick (manager) and a woman named Rayne, dressed as a gothic dominatrix/elf, were both at ringside for the Suicide Kings; Rayne's exact role is never stated. Winners advance to the Everette Memorial Title tournament final.

After a back-and-forth match including several near-falls, Pollard raked Tremendous's eyes, applied a cobra clutch, and rolled it into a bridging suplex for the pin. Billed as Lord Coyner Pollard's first live NFW match. Referee: Greg Herpin. A backstage vignette later in the show reveals Professor Tremendous already possesses a burned 'Unified Championship' belt, given to him by Mike Randalls — that title was not contested in this match.

matches.stipulation: National Championship Series Semifinal; joined in progress. Structured so that a wrestler already carrying one fall against him is eliminated if pinned, disqualified, or counted out again.

eliminations.note: Commentary frames this as a deliberate, unexplained gesture by Randalls rather than a clean loss; it draws heavy crowd boos.

matches.note: After Mittens T. Cat attacked referee Chris Fusco with his guitar (costing him a fall) and Randalls eliminated himself, Rook Black finished Mittens with a Desecrator DDT for the pin. Commentary states Rook Black already led both opponents by a pinfall entering the shown portion, implying earlier action occurred off-screen before this broadcast joined the match. Winner advances to the National Championship Series final. A locker-room vignette immediately after shows Legion confronting Mike Randalls about the burned championship belt Randalls gave to Professor Tremendous.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Tag Team Title Tournament Semifinal; champions defending
matches.note: After a brawl-heavy match that included Malik Anderson injuring Brandon Mueller's arm before the bell and Mueller returning to fight one-armed, Blaine Hollywood pinned Frankie Fargo while grabbing a handful of tights. The Original Showstoppers were the reigning tag champions, managed/accompanied by Calvin (Jay Chalmers) Carlton III; referee Chris Fusco. Winners advance to face The Dream Team in the tournament final.

matches.stipulation: Secret stipulation announced before the bell by ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims on President Eddie Mayfield's orders: if champion Kin Hiroshi is disqualified or counted out, he loses the title outright, not just the match.
matches.note: Late in the match, champion Kin Hiroshi appeared to suffer a breakdown, seemingly forgetting his own identity, and fled through the crowd and out of the building, leaving Dan Ryan and Felix Red to continue alone. Ryan eventually hit a bridging Dragon Suplex on Red, and referee Roland Priest counted three and called for the bell. Commentary and the crowd immediately disputed the count, saying Felix Red appeared to get a shoulder up before three and that Priest missed it. Before any champion was announced or the belt presented, new President Eddie Mayfield and his enforcer Cojones Mercado ran in, attacked Dan Ryan, blindfolded and then knocked out referee Roland Priest with a chair, and Mayfield left the arena carrying the physical title belt without any on-air confirmation of a winner. The broadcast ends with commentary explicitly asking, unanswered, whether Dan Ryan is champion. Per the

matches.stipulation: National Championship Series four-way elimination (Teresa Q enters only after the first man is eliminated)
matches.note: Dusk was eliminated first, tapping out to Phil Atken's "Humiliation" Figure Four (commentary: Atken "stole that pinfall from Sean Stevens"). Stevens then pinned Atken once, and later had him covered after the X-Terminator with referee Bruce Phillips knocked from the ring, when a masked figure in razor wire (unmasked as Legion) attacked him. Teresa Q pinned Atken with a 450 splash and had her hand raised by Phillips; Craig Miles then let Stevens wrestle for the title as well.

date.source: the document's own dateline (31 Mar 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Alyas hits a Vertical Drop Exploder and picks up the three-count after a one-sided beating that leaves O'Keefe barely responsive. Referee Scott Speranza allows the match to continue despite O'Keefe appearing to be knocked out mid-match; O'Keefe requires medical attention afterward and Alyas shoves the referee away rather than let his hand be raised cleanly. Ring announcer bills the opponent as 'Shaun O'Keefe,' while the segment header spells it 'O'Keeke' — kept the ring-announced spelling in sides.

Pollard reverses a Torture Rack attempt into a piledriver (the "B.S.D. — Boleyn Sisters Driver") for the pinfall. Phil Atken's manager Dirk Dickwood interferes once (tripping Pollard) but it isn't enough. A loud, unexplained horn sound disorients Dickwood three separate times during the match per commentary ('the THIRD time in a row that's happened to him') — the source never explains its origin.

After a hard-fought back-and-forth (including a suicide dive through the timekeeper's table), Rook Black connects with the Gauntlet Throwdown for the pin. Black shows unusual sportsmanship afterward, helping the dazed Impulse to his feet before leaving; Impulse remains winless in NFW.

During a tug-of-war over Tremendous's briefcase, Brock Alyas runs in and clotheslines both men; Tremendous capitalizes with a Spinning Fisherman's Buster (the "Tremendousplex") for the pin, then Alyas blindsides Tremendous with the briefcase and steals it. Referee Greg Herpin. The match itself included Tremendous's taunting 'Spunk Face' crotch-to-face maneuver. Backstage afterward, Alyas is shown prying the stolen briefcase open — it turns out to be empty, a storyline swerve on the rumored $40,000 inside.

matches.stipulation: Fatal Fourway (Everette Memorial Titles explicitly NOT on the line; winner earns a title shot at Wrestlestock 2)

eliminations.note: Team counted out for being off the ring apron together for ten seconds, after the returning Dream Team (Brian Duncan, Mike Gordey) ambushed and knocked both men unconscious at ringside earlier in the segment.

eliminations.who: Blaine Hollywood & Malik Anderson (Hollywood Wrecking Crew)
eliminations.note: Team walks out of the match/leaves ringside voluntarily rather than being formally eliminated by pinfall or countout, after roughly thirty minutes of punishment (including fire and table spots); Blaine is later ordered back for the main event as punishment by Eddie Mayfield.

matches.note: Felix Red hits a top-rope Swanton Bomb ("Shattered Horizon") on DC Stratton for the pinfall at 38 minutes, 43 seconds, winning for himself and his reluctant, probation-assigned partner Steve Torchowski ("Torch"). Extremely chaotic multi-team brawl with extensive weapons/fire spots (tables, lighter fluid, a burning chair); manager Calvin Carlton is blinded by Tsunami's green mist at ringside early on; a costumed interferer billed as 'Madonna Wayne Grossard' also factors in. Eddie Mayfield subsequently overrules the stipulated reward and grants the Everette Memorial Tag Title shot to the Suicide Kings (Tsunami & DC Stratton) instead of the match's actual winners.

A masked interferer ('Mister Magnificent II') superkicks Blaine Hollywood and clotheslines Dan Ryan out of the ring; Joe the Plumber then connects with a top-rope frog splash on the prone Blaine Hollywood for the pinfall at 20 minutes, 57 seconds — Blaine Hollywood's first-ever pinfall loss in NFW. The segment header bills Nova's partner as 'Mystery,' but the broadcast itself introduces and uses Blaine Hollywood as Nova's partner throughout the actual match — the 'mystery' element instead belonged to the outside interferer, Mister Magnificent II, who was never one of the four announced competitors. Post-match, Dan Ryan grabs the mic and challenges Nova to a World Heavyweight Championship match at the next show, in Las Vegas, before Wrestlestock 2; Eddie Mayfield confirms it.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Jun 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier
matches.note: Felix Red hit the Shining Wizard on James von Doom for the pin to earn an automatic Grand Prix berth, after Legion and Luci4's ringside interference on von Doom's behalf backfired. One of two 'dark matches' taped earlier the same evening and aired on tape during the broadcast (under the Credits heading 'Grand Prix Qualifiers,' shared with the Legion/Pollard match and the 'Diplomatic Immunity' aftermath segment).

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier
matches.note: Referee Scott Speranza awarded Legion the win by disqualification after James von Doom ran in with a chair and attacked Legion, who then continued beating von Doom down until security intervened. The second of two 'dark matches' taped earlier and shown 'joined in progress' from the 8:15 mark. Craig Miles subsequently overruled the tournament stakes in the following 'Diplomatic Immunity' segment: he disqualified both Legion and von Doom from Grand Prix eligibility over the interference and instead advanced Lord Coyner Pollard (the in-ring loser) to the tournament, later granting him a mock 'Diplomatic Immunity' knighting alongside Eddie Mayfield. The in-ring DQ win for Legion is recorded here as the announced match result; the Grand Prix advancement outcome is a separate authority ruling captured in storyline_notes.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Qualifier
matches.note: Impulse used a modified drop toe hold/ankle wrench to injure Almasy's knee, then finished him with a top-rope Shooting Star Press for the pin. Almasy attacked Impulse with a chair before the bell and focused on hurting him rather than winning; the referee never removed the chair from ringside or disqualified Almasy for repeated weapon use.

Mike Gordey pinned Sean Stevens with a Tiger Driver after Brock Alyas blindsided Stevens with his handcuffs, giving the outnumbered Dream Team the win over 'The Old School' trio of Jason Payne, Sean Stevens, and Cameron Cruise. Billed as 'The Old School' (Payne, Stevens, Cruise) vs. the Dream Team plus Brock Alyas, but Alyas — shown arrested earlier in the broadcast — never officially entered as a tagged competitor, instead interfering from ringside in shackles; sides reflect only the wrestlers who actually competed in the ring. After the bell, Jason Payne chairshotted Gordey, Duncan, and Alyas, and Cameron Cruise finished by hitting a still-shackled Alyas with a Shipwreck.

After a masked '5th Uber Judge' hit a frog splash on a three-man pile, referee Scott Speranza counted a fall with both Steve Knox and the Uber Judge on top of Rook Black simultaneously; the decision was announced as a double pinfall win for both men. The winners were awarded a joint National Championship title shot at Crash 46. A squadron of decoy 'Uber Judges' (including one wielding a Kendo stick) interfered mid-match; referee Speranza was knocked out by a clothesline and missed much of the finish sequence.

matches.stipulation: Title vs. Title
matches.note: Nova made Teresa Quaranta submit to the Caesarian Section (a rear naked dragon sleeper) to retain the NFW World Heavyweight Championship, handing Quaranta the first loss of her NFW career. Billed as the first-ever Title vs. Title match in NFW history, but per its own announced stakes the winner keeps the World Heavyweight Championship while the loser is 'consoled with' (retains) the National Championship, so no title actually changed hands; Quaranta remained NFW National Champion despite losing.

The match reached its full 30-minute time limit with both teams down; it was ruled a time-limit draw, and the Hollywood Wrecking Crew retained the Everette Memorial Tag Team Titles. Extensive interference from Calvin Carlton (revealed mid-match to have faked his injury, attacking both teams with a tennis racket) and manager Rayne (accompanying despite a kayfabe broken neck). DC Stratton bit Blaine Hollywood open and was nearly disqualified for it. After the bell, Blaine Hollywood dragged the injured Rayne into the ring and hit her with a Backcracker, shocking the announce team; this segment's Credits-block writer line is missing entirely (see lane_notes).

date.source: the document's own dateline (23 Aug 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage, with Blaine's Hollywood Wrecking Crew partner Malik Anderson and manager Calvin Carlton suspended above the ring in a shark cage
matches.note: DC Stratton climbed to the top of the steel cage and then onto the suspended shark cage roughly twenty feet up, hitting a Corkscrew Senton Bomb across Blaine Hollywood's sternum after Rayne dove clear of the impact zone; Stratton and Rayne then covered Blaine together for the pin. Rayne (Stratton's love interest) interfered repeatedly on his behalf, including using a needle Calvin Carlton had intended for Malik Anderson on Blaine. DC Stratton's previously injured shoulder was targeted throughout by Blaine. The win earned Stratton a tag team title shot.

James von Doom and an ally called 'The Florida Gator' ran in and hit a Double DDT on Koopa while the referee was down; Chester Cheeseburger then hit a frog splash, popping Koopa's shell again, and scored the pin. Reported via an in-fiction written recap ('As reported by DoomUnderground.com') rather than shown as live action. Von Doom was chased off by Insurgent Security afterward; ties into the ongoing 'Kill the Koopa' storyline. The exact sequence involving 'The Florida Gator' being caught in a hold outside the ring is garbled in the source and not fully clear.

matches.stipulation: Handicap match (1 vs. 2), with barbed wire weapons in play
matches.note: After Felix Red's attempted interference on Kooter's behalf was neutralized by a surprise appearance from the Uber Judge (a gavel shot to Felix), Legion hit a curbstomp on a barbed wire chair for the pin. Recapped verbally by commentary as a match that took place before the broadcast went live, rather than shown as live action.

The Uber Judge pulled Teresa Quaranta off the top rope and struck her with his gavel, then walked away up the ramp instead of making the cover; Steve Knox capitalized with the pin to win the National Championship, becoming a double champion alongside his Elite Championship. Immediately after the finish, Felix Red revealed a bound and gagged Rook Black, rigged with explosives, on the Startron and detonated him backstage. Craig Miles then announced a two-out-of-three-falls elimination match at SuperCrash 2 between Knox, Quaranta, and Rook Black (if he survives) for the National title, with Knox also defending the Elite Championship there.

Joe the Plumber hit his Ace Crusher variation, 'The Great Flood,' for the pin after Hiroshi accidentally punched the turnbuckle post chasing a low blow. Also contested for the status of #1 contender to the World Heavyweight Championship; Joe's win earns him a rematch with Nova at SuperCrash 2. Afterward, Kin Hiroshi cryptically threatened Nova ('Next time, I won't be stealing your gold…I'll be stealing your soul') while handing back the actual World Heavyweight Championship belt he had been carrying.

matches.stipulation: Six-man tag: if Alyas, Payne, or Atken pins Nova, that man earns a Nova title shot at Crash 47; if Cruise or Noble scores the winning pin, they face each other later for a Nova shot; if Nova's team wins clean, none of the three earn a shot
matches.note: The finish was two simultaneous pinfalls: Phil Atken rolled up a dazed David Noble (staggered into the cover by a Helga headbutt) at the same moment Cameron Cruise covered Jason Payne after hitting his 'Reality Check' finisher; the referee could not resolve which count landed first before the broadcast cut to commercial. Craig Miles later ruled it an official 'double pin' with no immediate title-shot outcome awarded, promising a special announcement for Crash 47. Helga and Dirk Dickwood interfered repeatedly on Phil Atken's behalf throughout.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix 500 Elimination Match, with an in-match 'Curious Rulebook' controlled by Doctor Curiosity's corner (enforced by his second, Eegor) in effect for most of the bout; Lord Coyner Pollard's Diplomatic Immunity nullifies the Curious Rules whenever he is the legal man

eliminations.note: Standing Moonsault pinfall.
Submitted to High Flyer's Boston-Crab-style 'Peaceful Slumber' after his own teammate SARS bit his hand off the ropes, preventing the rope break.
Small package reversal pinfall, set up by Lord Coyner Pollard raking Flyer's eyes moments earlier.
Boleyn Driver pinfall.
Shining Wizard / 'Schrodinger's Smack' pinfall.

Failed to beat a standing ten-count at ringside, along with SARS, after Felix Red's 'Shattered Horizon' Swanton Bomb wiped out Impulse, SARS, and Doctor Curiosity in a pile atop a broken table; eliminated together, credited to Felix Red.
Failed to beat the same standing ten-count as Impulse, eliminated together in the same pile; credited to Felix Red.

matches.note: Felix Red was the sole survivor for his group, pinning Doctor Curiosity after the masked Uber Judge (revealed moments later to be Rook Black) ran in and struck Curiosity with a flail fashioned from a severed robotic head and spine. An elaborate 'Curious Rules' gimmick governed much of the match, including forcing High Flyer to start with his hands tied and Impulse to start blindfolded; Craig Miles personally took over enforcement mid-match after burning the physical rulebook and substituting a single handwritten rule on a sheet of paper. Felix Red's win advances him in the Grand Prix standings toward the SuperCrash 2 Final Four. Immediately after the pin, the Uber Judge unmasked as Rook Black and attacked both Curiosity and Felix Red with the flail, cutting a cryptic promo. This entire match is not listed in the show's own Credits block, despite being the show's de facto main event — lik

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Mar 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Castor V. Strife hit a Sickle-Cell Neckbreaker on Leroy Brown for the pin. Bold New Disaster's in-ring NFW debut. Manager Jimmy Mylde installed a blind guest color commentator, Blink Rogers, alongside Kerry O'Connor for the match; Calvin Carlton filled in on commentary in Lamont Hollywood's absence (Hollywood was recovering after being powerbombed by Joe the Plumber earlier in the show).

matches.stipulation: Looking Glass match (glass cage weapons match)
matches.note: Teresa Quaranta slipped off a broken table and caught Luci4 with the Process of Illumination on the way down for the pin, after earlier hurricanrana'ing Legion off the top rope and through the glass cage wall. Called in-progress by guest commentators Madonna Wayne Grossard and Kooter Michaels-Cruise (an in-story broadcast-team audition). A 2-on-1 handicap match inside a soundproof glass cage packed with weapons; joined in progress (9:30 already elapsed).

Eegor covered the incapacitated Cary Turkington for the pin after Doctor Curiosity's interference took Rook Black out of the equation. Doctor Curiosity refused to wrestle (citing Grand Prix injuries) and sent his assistant Eegor in as his substitute, then interfered twice from ringside as Eegor's manager -- hitting Rook Black with a trick exploding book and pulling down the ropes to spill him to the floor. Joined in progress (11:52 already elapsed).

Felix Red hit a bridging Dragon Suplex for the pin. Vic Tarano's NFW television debut; he used illegal brass knuckles mid-match to bust Felix Red open. After the loss, Tarano attacked Felix Red with a post-match Bull Rush Shining Wizard. Joined in progress (14:13 already elapsed).

matches.stipulation: Sears Tower (no-ladders, tables-and-chairs title retrieval match)
matches.note: Impulse grabbed the championship belt off its hook, aided by the force of Brock Alyas' failed powerbomb attempt on him, to become the new champion. Six-man scramble for the vacant title with no fixed teams, hence 'participants' rather than 'sides.' High Flyer, absent earlier in the show after a staged 'attack,' secretly entered as the masked 'Fakepulse' impersonator and was unmasked mid-match by the real Impulse.

matches.stipulation: 30 Minute Ironman match
matches.note: With the match tied 3 falls apiece and seconds remaining, New Day Rising's own ringside ally DC Stratton took the title belt -- apparently to hand to WildStar's corner -- and instead struck WildStar himself with it; Blaine Hollywood covered the stunned WildStar for the match- and title-winning pinfall as time expired. Fall-by-fall: Fall 1 to NDR (WildStar pinned Blaine via a cradle, 22:43 remaining); Fall 2 to HWC (Malik's sitout powerbomb on Tsunami, 20:18 remaining); Fall 3 to HWC by DQ (NDR's DC Stratton struck Calvin Carlton and Blaine Hollywood with a tennis racket, 17:12 remaining); Fall 4 to HWC (Malik's Michinikou Driver on Tsunami, 13:31 remaining, HWC led 3-1); Fall 5 to NDR (WildStar's spinning Tiger Driver on Blaine, 5:12 remaining); Fall 6 to NDR (WildStar's Five Star Frog Splash on Blaine after a Tsunami assist, 1:07 remaining, tying it 3-3); Fall 7/deciding fall as describ

date.source: the document's own dateline (26 Apr 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Conga overwhelmed Kelly with a long string of high spots and finished him with a corkscrew leg drop (called the 'Dios Mi') after a tornado DDT, extending Kelly's long losing streak. Presented as one of two 'debut matches' that 'took place' earlier in the evening, shown via flash-cut/highlight narration rather than full live play-by-play (including an explicit 'SPORT SCIENCE REPLAY' label). Treated as fresh show content per the brief's default rule since it carries its own Credits-block segment title; see lane_notes for the archival-vs-fresh ambiguity.

Unicorn Mask dominated with power offense and finished La Estrella 100% with a move billed as the 'Skullf*cka Bustah' for the pin. Also billed as a debut and shown via flash-cut narration (same archival-vs-fresh ambiguity as the prior match). Immediately after the bell, High Flyer ran in with an Impulse-mask-adorned baseball bat, attacked both men and tore off La Estrella 100%'s mask before Unicorn Mask fought him off.

Castor V. Strife set David Jericho on fire with a flamethrower and pinned him while referee Greg Herpin, visibly intimidated, made the count. Bold New Disaster (Castor V. Strife & Problem Child) were managed by Jimmy Mylde, who instigated the fight by having Biff Busey superkicked with a wrapped 'gift' (a sports almanac). The Normal Human Beings (David Jericho & Shawn Coppola, spelled 'Coppolla' elsewhere in the source) were accompanied by Biff Busey and Michael 'The Mind' Heenan. A separate real-time crowd riot (Biff Busey's entourage vs. fan characters, plus a costumed Doc Brown/Marty McFly run-in) bled into the match; Castor's flamethrower also caught several riot participants (Biff Busey, and members of his 'Saved By the Bell'-styled entourage) on fire. Bold New Disaster's valet Lana Dremire, visibly drugged, was thrown bodily by Biff Busey to break up an earlier pin attempt. No disq

An uninvited Kooter Michaels-Cruise ran in, super-chokeslammed challenger Felix Red, then positioned champion Rook Black's arm over Felix for the cover; referee Greg Herpin counted the three despite the outside interference. Felix Red's manager Gotho interfered repeatedly throughout (placing Felix's foot on the ropes to break a pin, throwing the timekeeper's bell at Rook, dropping a chair onto Rook's back, and tripping Rook) without ever drawing a disqualification. NFW Head of Security Cojones Mercado also came to ringside with a chair and was clotheslined out by Kooter's run-in. Immediately after the bout, Kooter Michaels-Cruise unmasked and renounced his gimmick under a new name, denouncing the promotion before walking off to a hostile crowd reaction (recorded separately under non_match_appearances).

matches.stipulation: Steel Curtain Cage Match
matches.note: Vic Tarano, not advertised for the match, ran in and struck Alyas with bolt cutters and a running knee strike ('Shining Wizard'); Cameron Cruise then pinned the incapacitated Alyas for the three count, announced at 20 minutes 33 seconds. Extremely violent hardcore-style main event with chairs, a ladder, a hammer, a staple gun, a charcoal chimney, a screwdriver, handcuffs and stretched barbed wire from the cage itself used as weapons; no disqualification was called for any of it, and both men bled heavily. Match rules allowed victory by pinfall, submission, or climbing out of the cage; a 60-minute time limit was announced but not reached. Unicorn Mask and High Flyer (wearing a stolen Impulse mask) also ran in mid-match and briefly fought each other before security intervened; Vic Tarano's run-in first helped free a handcuffed Cameron Cruise before turning the match's finish in his favor.

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 Jun 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After the Sicilian Swat Team nearly stole the titles, Blaine Hollywood forced a hesitant referee into the count and hit a Doomsday Device off the top rope on Cousin Vinny for the pin. Debut match for the newly formed Carlton Dynasty stable. Blaine Hollywood interfered as a spectator-turned-participant, knocking IROC out with a stolen house microphone before the finish; Cousin Vinny was stretchered out afterward, seemingly seriously hurt.

Dorchester Stratton hit a Package Piledriver (dubbed "The Kiss of Death") for the pin. Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld low-blowed Scissors from behind before he could enter the ring, and the referee did not act on it. Segment title in the Credits block spells the loser's name "Scissors"; the body text alternates between "Julius Scissor" and "Julius Scissors" throughout — recorded verbatim per the Credits heading.

With referee Bruce Phillips distracted after Felix's manager Gotho Lamont accidentally shook the ring, guest commentator High Flyer cracked Unicorn Mask in the face with a baseball bat, shattering his mask. Felix Red then hit "Ecstasy of Agony" for the pin. High Flyer worked as a guest color commentator for this match (alongside his ongoing feud with masked wrestlers) before delivering the interference bat shot himself. Result stands as announced despite the hidden interference, per the staged-result rule.

After BatPulse (High Flyer's baseball-bat tag partner) was destroyed via a Dos Equis Shooting Star Press through a table, Dos Equis used half of the broken bat in a Cobra Clutch and hit the "Negro Modelo Legsweep" on High Flyer for the pin. Announced as a handicap match, then corrected on-air to a tag match with BatPulse — a baseball bat wearing a mask/helmet — booked as High Flyer's literal tag team partner. BatPulse's destruction is later referenced by High Flyer at Brawl 26 as the death of his "fallen comrade."

WildStar dominated with a Wild Driver, but referee Greg Herpin rang the bell and disqualified WildStar for continuing the assault on McGee outside the ring after the move. President Mayfield forced accountant Mike McGee (representing Dynasty client Calvin Carlton) into this impromptu match as punishment/leverage. Despite losing by DQ, WildStar kept attacking McGee and then called out Dorchester Stratton, leading Calvin Carlton and the Dynasty to accept a Pinfalls-Count-Anywhere match at Crash 50 with WildStar's career against Blaine Hollywood and Malik Anderson's tag titles.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: After the brawl spilled backstage and Tarano's foe Dirk Dickwood was slam-dunked into a basketball hoop by the Timberwolves mascot Crunch, Tarano revealed he had swapped places with Crunch in the mascot suit, ambushed Helga and Atken, and hit a Bull Rush Shining Wizard for the pin. Match text spells the loser's surname both "Atken" (segment title and ring announcement) and "Atkin" (some body text) — recorded per the segment title/ring announcement.

Pollard raked the eyes, then hit the "Boleyn Sisters Driver" while holding a handful of tights for extra leverage, and pinned Cruise. Pollard also used the ring ropes for extra leverage during a chinlock earlier, caught by the referee once.

Castor Strife locked Impulse in a modified sleeper/camel-clutch submission he calls the "Euthanasian Torture Hug." Impulse passed out without tapping; the referee waved it off and the bout was awarded to Bold New Disaster. Heavy interference throughout: Jimmy Mylde and Blanche Barnett interfered on Bold New Disaster's behalf; a fan dressed as a special-needs child was revealed to be Castor's associate Starshooter, who handcuffed Rook Black to the guardrail and hit Impulse in the hamstring with a bat during the climax. After the bout, Castor forced the old Impulse mask onto the unconscious Impulse and spat on him.

matches.stipulation: World Championship Gauntlet, Round 1 of 3 — 30-minute time limit
matches.note: Joe the Plumber hit a top-rope Volcano Splash, covering both Banzai Brothers at once for the pin. First of three consecutive gauntlet defenses staged back-to-back under one "The World Championship Gauntlet" segment/Credits heading; recorded here as a separate match entry because it has its own discrete finish. The Banzai Brothers were managed by John Bryan III.

matches.stipulation: World Championship Gauntlet, Round 2 of 3
matches.note: With Joe covering Alyas after a Sh*t River Plunge (Tiger Driver) for a two count, President Mayfield's bodyguard Cojones Mercado ran in and repeatedly chair-shotted Joe. The bell rang and Joe was announced as the winner and still champion despite no clean fall being shown. Second of three gauntlet rounds under the shared "The World Championship Gauntlet" heading. Alyas had been ordered backstage by Mayfield to soften Joe up ahead of a planned angle; the finish is murky (no pin or submission is depicted) but the announced result is recorded per the staged-result rule.

matches.stipulation: World Championship Gauntlet, Round 3 of 3 — "Curious Rules" (Doctor Curiosity's own ad-hoc rules from his cashed-in 2008 NFW Grand Prix title shot: his assistant Eegor permitted at ringside, foreign objects, tables, and other amendments allowed as announced by Eegor)
matches.note: Joe reapplied an ankle lock using a barbed-wire 2x4 against Curiosity's bare foot and bit through the wire until Curiosity tapped out. Third and final gauntlet round under the shared "The World Championship Gauntlet" heading. Doctor Curiosity had been feigning a wheelchair-bound injury and revealed it was a ruse to spring this title shot. Eegor interfered repeatedly (mallet, low blow, a second barbed-wire 2x4 shot); National Champion Rook Black intervened on Joe's behalf, removing Eegor from ringside at one point.

Shown as a highlight of a match taken before the broadcast. Luci4 pulled Captain Conga's leg on the apron and struck him while the referee was distracted by Legion, who then piledrove him for the three-count after Conga's superkick had earned only a two.

matches.stipulation: Dark match
matches.note: A dark match shown as a highlight. Kelly attacked Johnson from behind during his anti-Socialist rant; Johnson answered with a running powerslam and a chokeslam, and referee Bruce Phillips raised his arm. The card gives no pin.

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Dec 2000), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Handicap Match
matches.note: Zane's Mr. T-impersonator manager blasted Pyle with a fistful of gold chains while the referee argued with Zane, allowing Zane to score the pinfall. Shown as taped highlights of a match that took place earlier the same night rather than live; treated as a fresh match belonging to this broadcast per brief guidance for uncertain cases.

Aragon reversed a Bondage attack into a reverse chokeslam ('No Way Out') for the pin, after Bondage had earlier staggered him with a DDT. Referee Greg Herpin. Post-match, guest color commentator 'Iceman' Steve Radder (in a Santa suit) offered Aragon a handshake and was clotheslined, sparking a brawl between the two at ringside.

Wildstar hit his Wild Driver finisher on Wylde, but the match was ruled a disqualification against Wildstar after Aidan Campbell, seated at ringside in a chair, struck Wylde with that chair during the closing sequence. Wildstar was accompanied by manager Calvin Carlton and a drag-disguised stand-in presented as Wylde's sister; Wylde attacked the impostor to start the brawl before the bell. Referee Scott Speranza. Both Aidan Campbell (with a chair) and Carlton (with a croquet mallet) interfered during the match.

matches.stipulation: Intergender Tag Team Match
matches.note: Cancer hit his Malignancy (Cradle Piledriver) on Rayne for the pin after guest referee Mike Manson had incapacitated Torch with his own finisher. Guest referee Mike Manson officiated with open bias and violence throughout, at one point piledriving Torch himself; after the bell he attacked both Cancer and Jade with a steel ladder.

After a big clothesline collision left both men down, Ryconik crawled over for a cover; the referee ruled Ryconik's shoulder had been up in time while Montezuma's shoulders stayed down for the full count, awarding Ryconik the pinfall. Referee Greg Herpin. Post-match, Montezuma attacked Ryconik with the Cuban flag on its pole, breaking it over him and choking him with the broken half; Ryconik's daughter Vivian brought out a returning Shane Southern, who superkicked Montezuma to make the save.

matches.stipulation: Three-Way Dance (all tags legal; first pinfall or submission wins)
matches.note: Ryan Connors switched places with a beaten-down Lincoln McKinley without the referee noticing, then rolled up Calamity with a small package for the pin. Doc Martina Martens managed Hellmachine (Calamity & Sean Toombs); referee Scott Speranza. Post-match, Hellmachine's Calamity ambushed the new champions with repeated chair shots during their celebration.

matches.stipulation: Sixty-Minute Time Limit
matches.note: Not listed in this show's own Credits block despite being a full contested segment in the body (source defect). Ricky Zane repeatedly interfered, attacking referee Greg Herpin and briefly impersonating him at ringside; with no legitimate official able to make a count, the broadcast cuts to Ares chokeslamming Zane and the sign-off without a declared winner or stoppage call, so winner and result are left null per brief.

date.source: the document's own dateline (29 Aug 2009), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere, No Disqualification
matches.note: After a brutal brawl through the crowd, concourse, and men's room, Dorchester connected with the Wild Driver on the ring ramp for the pin; when WildStar recovered enough to embrace his family, Dorchester blindsided him with a chair shot in front of them. Stakes were billed as WildStar's career against the NFW Tag Team Championship held by Dorchester's new stablemates, the Hollywood Wrecking Crew, though the text never clarifies what WildStar stood to gain had he won. WildStar's wife is named 'Vanessa' at her introduction but 'Veronica' (once as the full name 'Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld') later in the same segment -- see lane_notes. Referee's name appears once as 'Heprin' and thereafter as 'Herpin.'

matches.stipulation: War Games
matches.note: High Flyer trapped Unicorn Mask in a submission hold (shown as the 'Cold Snow Liontamer') while his team fended off the rest of Cuatro-X and Legion; Unicorn Mask tapped out, ending the match for his team. Presented in heavily condensed flash-cut form; a voiceover states footage from this match (and one other) was trimmed for time. After the bell, an enraged Futurequis turned on his own beaten teammate, ripping off Unicorn Mask's mask to reveal an unidentifiable, face-painted man underneath, then piledriving him. Exactly which hold produced the tap-out is genuinely ambiguous in the text -- see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Street Fight
matches.note: Amid a four-way brawl after the returning Original Showstoppers (Brandon Mueller and Frankie Fargo) rode in on a truck and fought off the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Blaine Hollywood blindsided Saafir Muhammed with the That's Entertainment Backcracker and pinned him to retain the titles for the Hollywood Wrecking Crew. President Mayfield announced the match as the Hollywood Wrecking Crew defending against a mystery opponent 'and possibly some mystery guests as well'; the Original Showstoppers' run-in reads as a planned second surprise rather than an accident, but they were never credited as an official side in the pinfall.

Von Doom single-handedly destroyed all three Normal Human Beings with a steel chair, a barbed-wire bat, and a ladder-assisted top-rope Arabian Facebuster before security and referees pulled him off; all three were stretchered out. No bell, referee decision, or pinfall appears in the text -- this reads more like an unsanctioned squash/angle than an officiated contest. Included per the brief's fresh-content default, with winner and result left null as instructed for an unresolved outcome; see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: National Guard Rules
matches.note: Rook Black struck ringside National Guardsman Eegor with the Gauntlet Backhand; referee Greg Herpin disqualified Rook Black, awarding the match to Doc Curiosity, but under the match's National Guard rules the champion retained the title and was left free to punish Eegor with a belt shot. Match winner (Doc Curiosity, by DQ) and title-holder (Rook Black retains) diverge here -- recorded separately. Alias (Christopher Sheffield) then made a surprise, non-violent confrontational appearance with Rook Black, exchanging cryptic lines implying unresolved shared history; no violence follows and Rook leaves with his Guardsmen.

matches.stipulation: Bunkhouse Stampede, final three contested inside a lowered War Games cage

eliminations.note: Juggular Chomp double chokeslam, with an Irish whip assist from Jonathan Marx.
Death Valley Driver, after Teresa Quaranta hit him with a meteor-hammer dart.
Mahogany stole the pin with a top-rope leg drop after Ultrajira had already hit Kelly with the Stanley Cup.
DDT, after La Estrella accidentally walked into a chain swing meant for Dawn McGill.
Double-knee facebreaker; Terence was a surprise fan-turned-wrestler debut entrant who joined mid-match.
Pinned after Teresa Quaranta hit him with Captain Justice's American flag.
Backstabber into a clothesline.
Headshot (brass-knuckle-assisted strike).
German suplex.

Led away from ringside by his manager, Miss America, after a heckling fan; never explicitly ruled an elimination on-air, but the announcers' running competitor count only reconciles if this counts as one -- see lane_notes.
Countered a superplex attempt into a front suplex on the rope, then clotheslined her to the outside.
Spinning capoeira kick followed by a dropkick over the top rope; Panda re-entered afterward for an unofficial sneak-attack neckbreaker on Quaranta before leaving for good.
Elevator Drop / guillotine leg drop combination with Captain Justice, inside the lowered War Games cage sealing in the final three.

matches.note: With the War Games cage lowered around the final three, Captain Justice powerslammed Teresa Quaranta (the 'Holy Justice Slam') for the pin immediately after the two of them had together eliminated Kelly Masters, crowning Justice the winner. The opening narration states 'fourteen wrestlers in-all,' but the in-match countdown ('Down to 10 competitors from 15') implies a 15-man field once surprise entrant Terence is added -- the totals don't reconcile; treat the elimination order above as a best-effort reconstruction rather than an exactly source-verified sequence.

matches.stipulation: All-Star Legacy Challenge (one fall, non-title exhibition)
matches.note: After a loaded elbow pad knockout was overturned when Alias exposed it, and a chaotic restart involving brass knuckles, a headbutt from Bradley Duncan, and repeated interference, Max Danger scored the pin with a small package while Alias prevented Hart from grabbing Danger's tights. Extremely interference-heavy finish involving both men's entourages (Felicia Hart, Tiny, Leigh Landers, Bradley Duncan) and a run-in from Alias (Christopher Sheffield); Bradley Duncan and Tiny brawled at ringside during the match.

The match ran through three stages: Castor first won by count-out after Starshooter chaired Impulse, but demanded (and got) a restart; Impulse then won by submission when Castor appeared to tap in an inverted version of The Message, a call Castor disputed; after Impulse walked away with the belt, Castor goaded him into an unsanctioned continuation that ended with both men's shoulders down for a simultaneous pin, which referee Greg Herpin ruled a draw -- leaving Impulse champion. The fed's own final, controlling announcement is the draw ruling, so that is recorded as the match result here; a lane reading only part of this long segment could reasonably record the earlier count-out or submission outcome instead -- see lane_notes.

matches.stipulation: Pentagram Match (No Disqualification, No Countout, No Time Limit, Falls Count Anywhere, first fall wins)
matches.note: After roughly 101 minutes fighting through the ring, the crowd, a production truck, and the Presidential Skybox, Joe the Plumber reversed Hornet's Scorpion Deathlock into his own Lockjaw ankle lock; Hornet's raised arm dropped three times and emergency guest referee Eddie Mayfield called for the bell, awarding Joe the Plumber the win and the title. Both assigned referees -- Greg Herpin, knocked out by a Steve Knox punch that cost him a tooth, and Bruce Phillips, knocked out after Joe's dive from the Presidential Skybox -- were incapacitated mid-match, forcing President Eddie Mayfield to don a referee's shirt and personally officiate the remainder, including at least one visibly fast three-count favoring Sean Stevens that the match continued past anyway. Joe the Plumber spent much of the match in an altered, hallucinatory 'John Trojan' persona referencing his father's death. Immediately a

date.source: the document's own dateline (9 Mar 2001), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Handicap Match
matches.note: Powermaster no-sold both opponents, hitting a clothesline, a powerslam, and back-to-back top-rope splashes on P. King Duk and Julius Scissor in succession for the pin. Powermaster's in-ring NFW debut; officiated by guest official Ricardo Esteban Fernandez.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket One
matches.note: Ares caught Carter with his FNS finisher after Carter had briefly turned the tide with an Implant DDT and a Diamond Cutter. Shown via still-photo recap narration rather than full live footage; the broadcast picked up live for the post-match, where Ares shoved through Nakita Dubov and her manager Kevin LeBrock on his way out, and Dubov ran in to attack Ares with an STF before security separated them.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket One
matches.note: Ares ran in and blindsided Dubov with his FNS finisher; Montezuma then covered the incapacitated Dubov for the pin, with guest referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez making the count. Dubov opened the match by spearing Montezuma mid-promo. Montezuma stole the win via Ares' interference, itself prompted by Dubov's earlier attack on Ares.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket One
matches.note: Comelightly appeared to genuinely injure his knee slipping off the top turnbuckle; while Wildstar had him locked in an STF, Comelightly's valet Samantha threw in the towel to stop the match against his wishes. Ruled a win for Wildstar via forfeit/towel-in.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket One
matches.note: Manson choked Radder through a ringside table with a moonsault and locked in his secondary finisher, the 'Tourniquet' Crippler Crossface, but refused to release the hold after Radder reached the ropes, drawing a disqualification. Radder wrestled while still selling an earlier spearing by Nakita Dubov backstage. Shown via recap narration with cut-in stills before returning to live coverage of the finish.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket Two
matches.note: Wylde knocked Neuromancer out with a concealed foreign object (a roll of coins) and hit the Wildcard Splash for the pin; guest referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez did not call for a disqualification despite the object visibly flying out.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket Two
matches.note: Southern hit his Party's Over superkick for the pin after Torch had missed a moonsault attempt off the ring apron. Torch's manager/valet Rayne was at ringside throughout.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One, Bracket Two
matches.note: Ryconik hit the Polish Hammer clothesline for the pin after a ringside brawl between Torch and Mike Manson (Torch also chair-shotting Cancer's valet Jade) disrupted Cancer's momentum; guest referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez was slow to make the count until Ryconik demanded it. Cancer's valet Jade was at ringside. This match's aftermath spills into a brutal backstage assault by Torch and Rayne on Cancer and Jade (see storyline notes).

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round One
matches.note: Aragon speared a distracted Zane as the bell rang, then finished him with a reverse chokeslam ('No Way Out') for the pin. Commissioner Craig Miles ambushed Zane with this surprise pairing after Zane wrongly announced himself in the ring as the tournament's 'mystery man.'

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round Two, Bracket One
matches.note: Radder rolled Wildstar up with a schoolboy for the pin after Wildstar, shoved from behind by Radder, accidentally knocked his own manager Calvin Carlton off the apron. Guest referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez officiated with apparent bias toward Radder throughout, missing a chairshot from Radder and disputing a clean Wildstar pin attempt.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round Two, Bracket Two
matches.note: With referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez still dazed, Wylde locked Southern in a figure-four leglock (using rope leverage) and forced the submission. NFW World Champion Bloodhunt ran in beforehand and attacked Southern's knee with a golf club and a cinderblock, and knocked out senior official Greg Herpin, directly enabling Wylde's finish.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round Two, Bracket One
matches.note: Guest referee Ricardo Esteban Fernandez called for the bell and awarded Montezuma the win by submission despite no submission having occurred, over the timekeeper's objection. Staged/crooked-official result stands per brief. Post-match, an enraged Ares brutalized Fernandez with two FNS finishers after Montezuma's handlers dragged him to safety; Fernandez was stretchered out.

matches.stipulation: Mid-Atlantic Title Tournament - Round Two, Bracket Two, Final Four Qualifier
matches.note: Ryconik capitalized on a distraction from Steve Radder (who waved an old newspaper clipping at Aragon) to hit the Polish Hammer for the pin; referee Scott Speranza. Sets the Final Four for NFW's first Pay-Per-View: Armando Montezuma, Steve Radder, Alex Wylde, and Rick Ryconik. Post-match, Aragon knocked out Radder and the two brawled to the back.

Ryan Connors accidentally struck referee Scott Speranza with a steel chair meant for Calamity, and McKinley forced Speranza to call for the bell, giving Hellmachine the match by disqualification. Titles do not change hands on a DQ finish; the Showstoppers retain despite losing the match. Hellmachine managed by 'Doc' Martina Martens.

Powell attacked Bloodhunt with a baseball bat before a real match could develop; Ares and Ricky Zane both ran in, and Commissioner Craig Miles declared the contest officially over once the referee was taken out amid the brawl. This was the reveal of the tournament's advertised 'mystery man' as a returning Roger Powell. The 'This is the end...' segment that follows in the body (Miles announcing a Bloodhunt/Ares/Zane Three-Way Dance for the Pay-Per-View, then real-world authorities shutting the broadcast down) is not listed in this show's own Credits block, a source defect.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Nov 2001), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Montezuma dropped Devotion with a brainbuster and the referee's three-count landed at the announced time of 9:15, just before the ten-minute limit. Stipulation: "10 Minute Challenge" - Devotion wins by lasting ten minutes; Montezuma wins by pinfall before time expires. The crowd chanted "Time Ran Out," disputing whether the pin actually beat the clock; the announced result (Montezuma wins) is recorded as staged/stands per the brief.

After Torch missed a top-rope Superfly Splash, Strife hit the Director's Cut and pinned him. Officially announced/started as Torch vs. Benjamin (wrestling disguised as masked luchador "El Puta"); Strife ran in mid-match and took over in Benjamin's place without a formal tag, then scored the pin himself. Recorded under the document's own segment title (Strife vs. Torch).

With Neuromancer seconds from a submission win, Torch's valet Rayne ran in and tripped him; Black rolled him up while holding the tights for the pin. Billed as a 'rubber match.' Rayne's interference on Black's behalf is notable given Black had previously attacked her; Black's own valet Jade reacted with visible jealousy/suspicion toward Rayne.

Bloodhunt caught Manson, fighting from a wheelchair taped to the top turnbuckle, with a Headshot for the pin. Manson had just been revealed minutes earlier as the new NFW Interim Commissioner; referee Scott Speranza called for the bell once Manson entered the ring. After the pin, Bloodhunt also Headshotted the referee. Includes a spot where Bloodhunt shoves Manson (in his wheelchair) off the top rope through a table.

A recurring masked man pulled special referee Roger Powell outside to brawl; Bloodhunt hit the Headshot on Montezuma with no referee to count, then Shane Southern ran in and superkicked Bloodhunt, letting Montezuma hit the Clean Slate for the pin. Special guest referee: Roger Powell (booked by Interim Commissioner Manson). Bloodhunt and Montezuma were shown hugging and stalling beforehand, visibly reluctant to fight each other.

Toombs planted Mueller with a modified Dominator and pinned him after Calamity cut off a Rocket Launcher attempt. Managers Doc Martina Martens (Hellmachine) and Calvin Carlton (Original Showstoppers) both interfered repeatedly; Martens low-blowed Carlton. Champions retain.

Ryconik hit the Polish Hammer on a dazed Zane and pinned him for the three-count, with referee Pee Wee Troutman recovering from an earlier collision just in time to make the count. Zane is shown pre-match conspiring by phone to have Powell 'taken out.' The recurring masked man interfered with a bat but was fought off by Powell before it could be used against Ryconik.

Unresolved on-page. Ryconik hit two rolling Polish Suplexes and referee Greg Herpin appeared to count a legitimate three and signal for the bell, but ATC members (Cojones Mercado, Raul, Gladiator) immediately ran in, chair-shooting Ryconik unconscious and strangling Herpin with piano wire; a second, apparently unlicensed 'referee' (Ricardo Esteban Fernandez) then declared Montezuma the winner and handed him the title belt as ATC members fled with it. Requested by Ryconik moments after winning the title, five minutes after the previous match. Commentator Kerry O'Connor explicitly disputes the Fernandez decision as illegitimate on air ("This isn't LEGAL... He's not even licensed!"), and the broadcast signs off saying the matter will hopefully be 'straightened out' on the next Impact. Because the document itself never settles who legitimately holds the title, winner/result/title_change are

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Dec 2001), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Scott Powell pinned Iroc following a Running Liger Bomb off a Belly-to-Back Superplex, while Roger Powell simultaneously had Cousin Vinny locked in 'The Contract' Dragon Sleeper submission at ringside. The Powell Brothers attacked the SST with baseball bats before the bell, effectively squashing them from the start. Manager 'Bad Bad' Leroy Brown fled early and was not otherwise involved.

Nakita DuBov hit a top-rope Shooting Star Press ('My Time') on Vanni Ru for the pin. Manager Kevin LeBrock was at ringside for DuBov. Immediately after, Powermaster ran in demanding a test of strength with DuBov, then press-slammed and threw LeBrock over the top rope in a beatdown.

Castor Strife hit his 'Director's Cut' (a modified Scorpion Death Drop) on a dazed Mr. Dread for the pin, after manager Lana Dremire's ringside interference (tripping Dread, then blasting him with a stolen fan's camera) turned the match around. Strife's associate Benjamin briefly entered the ring uninvited and was hit with a Dread Driver by Mr. Dread before the referee ejected him.

Pat Black hit a 450 Splash on Wildstar for the pin to retain the title. Wildstar wrestled while banged up from a pre-show ambush by Calvin Carlton and the Original Showstoppers, aired earlier as a video package in 'Hollywood's on Fire.' Jade was at ringside for Black. Immediately after the bell, Calvin Carlton and debuting wrestler Shawn Matthews attacked the injured Wildstar (chair shot, then a Razor's Edge through the ring); Matthews then turned and attacked Carlton with an Ura-nage before leaving.

Sean Toombs hit 'The Toolbox' (a top-rope powerbomb combination) on Tornado for the pin, after manager Doc Martena Martens shoved Hurricane off the top rope to break up a Storm double-team attempt. Post-match, Storm's manager Windy attacked Martens at ringside until security separated them.

Shane Southern hit a second superkick ('Party's Over') on Armando Montezuma and pinned him for the win and the vacant championship. Bloodhunt attacked Southern before the bell/before all four men had formally entered. Commissioner Manson personally ordered ATC seconds Raul, Cojones Mercado, and Miss Cuba away from ringside mid-match to even the odds. Montezuma used a coin flip to settle a dispute with ally Bloodhunt over pinfall order, then revealed the coin was double-sided, double-crossing Bloodhunt. Referee Greg Herpin was knocked out via an accidental collision and replaced by Bruce Phillips for the finish.

date.source: the document's own dateline (25 Apr 2002), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Puroresu-San controlled the match with kicks, a triple Asai moonsault, and a half-nelson suplex he calls the Rising Sun, then pinned Plain Brown Rapper for the three count. This was Puroresu-San's NFW debut. After the bell he blinded Rapper with a green mist, hit a Michinoku Driver II, and finished with a shooting star press through a ringside table — all after the decision, as an unprotected post-match beatdown rather than part of the match itself.

Stratton overwhelmed Duk with a string of aerial strikes -- a springboard senton, a corkscrew legdrop, a twisting 450 splash, and a tornado moonsault -- before pinning him. Billed and introduced only as a mystery 'Man with No Name'; he was revealed by name only when manager Neil Riddick introduced him to the crowd as DC Stratton during his entrance.

The match dissolved into a mass brawl when the Original Showstoppers (Fargo and Mueller) attacked referee Greg Herpin and ran in, followed by Storm (Hurricane and Tornado); the bell rang amid the chaos with no fall ever recorded. Manager Shaniqua Carlton speared Doc Silver and fought off Calvin Carlton and the Original Showstoppers with her tennis racket. Text never resolves a winner, so winner and result are left null per brief.

Tempesta bridged a back suplex on Viper for what looked like a clean three count, but guest referee Adrenaline ruled both men's shoulders were down simultaneously and announced that both competitors had scored the pinfall. Adrenaline was accused on commentary of alternating fast and slow counts favoring each man in turn. His final ruling -- a mutual/double pinfall -- does not fit a single winner or the brief's draw/no-contest definitions, so winner_side and result are left null; the fed's own staged ruling instead set up a three-way match with all three men (Viper, Tempesta, Adrenaline) at Futureshock. Flagged in lane_notes for coordinator review.

After a large, unnamed enforcer ambushed guest commentator Wildstar with a coin-filled sock, Matthews finished a battered Edmunds with a top-rope Jackhammer he calls the 'Showtime Shocker' for the pin. Guest color commentator Wildstar worked the match accompanied by his family (wife Miss Karen, son 'Little Ninja' Kyle) at ringside. Matthews cursed at and threatened the family during the match, and after the bell used his unnamed enforcer to hold Karen and Kyle while beating down Wildstar and vowing to take his wife and son. Sims's winner call is cut off by a bleep in the text ('SHOWTIME SH-OH SH[BLEEP!]'), but the surrounding action and post-match promo confirm Matthews as the winner.

With the referee distracted, manager Calvin Carlton tossed his tennis racket into the ring; Mueller struck Chris Reed with it and pinned him for the win. Manager Calvin Carlton interfered repeatedly at ringside (including a low blow on Sean Xavier) before Xavier picked him up and threw him bodily into the crowd. After the bell, the returning Showstoppers (McKinley, Connors) and manager Shaniqua Carlton chased the Original Showstoppers to the back.

Power Master caught Dread's shooting star press attempt and set him up for a powerbomb, but Dread slipped free, faceplanted him, and rolled him up for the three count. Manager Vanni Ru interfered repeatedly on Power Master's behalf during the match, including breaking up an early Dread pin attempt.

After a brutal brawl that included a table spot and Miles inadvertently DDT-ing referee Greg Herpin, Bloodhunt caught Miles with his Headshot finisher for the pin. Billed as the 'Grudge Match From Hell'; per pre-match stakes, a Bloodhunt loss would have kept him out of Futureshock's main event. The win confirms Bloodhunt as Shane Southern's challenger for the World Heavyweight Championship at Futureshock. Post-match, Bloodhunt continued the assault on Miles (driving him through a second table) until NFW security, led by JJ Boulevard and Quentin Sullivan, pulled the two apart.

The match broke down when Storm (Hurricane and Tornado) ran in during a Powell double press slam on Calamity; the referee (Roland Priest) called for the bell amid the ensuing multi-team brawl, and no fall was ever recorded. Doc Silver and Gladiator (wielding piano wire) also entered the fray attacking Storm, and an unnamed hired heavy brought out Storm's kidnapped manager Windy and choke-slammed her on the floor to close the segment. Text never resolves a winner, so winner and result are left null per brief; titles do not change hands.

After interference from manager Armando Montezuma (including a staged arena blackout and a near title-belt shot on Ryconik) and a save by a run-in Mister Dread against Montezuma, Southern ducked Ryconik's Polish Hammer and hit his 'Party's Over' superkick for the pin. Southern retains. Post-match, Ryconik announced this had been a pre-arranged, contractually 'immutable' final World Title challenge, and that his previously-announced Futureshock match against Bloodhunt (also on this show) will be the last match of his career; he and Southern shook hands to close the show.
