name: NFW Hall of Fame

date.source: The document carries no date of its own; the surviving capture is dated 2013-08-30.

no_appearances_reason: Served mechanically from the fed's own archive; no per-show extraction has been done for this document.
notes: A standing document from the fed's own site, not a show.

date.source: the document's own dateline (2 Aug 2001), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After both men traded near-falls off a botched tree-of-woe spot, Morrison smashed Adrenaline's head into the mat repeatedly and fell across him for the pin. Adrenaline's debut in-ring TV match; commentary recaps his prior save of Shane Southern at Crash via a flashback clip.

After Windy (Storm's valet) low-blowed Koltrane at ringside, Tornado powerbombed Erickson and Hurricane finished him with a top-rope legdrop for the pin. Tag match, 20-minute time limit stated. Raul interfered briefly, and Koltrane held Windy hostage at one point to keep Tornado from making a save.

Powell hit an Impaler DDT on Radder for the three-count. Radder wrestled visibly bruised, referencing an off-page kidnapping/captivity angle. Post-match, an unidentified masked man ambushed Powell with a baseball bat as he retreated up the aisle; Powell ducked the shot and fled.

With Gladiator applying a Mandible Claw, Cojones Mercado ran in and chair-shotted Gladiator unconscious (then chair-shotted the celebrating Devotion too); Devotion's arm was still draped over Gladiator, and the referee counted the pin. Devotion's in-ring NFW debut; the document frames it as a feel-good upset over the veteran Gladiator. Immediately after the decision, Gladiator recovered and choked Devotion with piano wire until officials broke it up; the pinfall result itself was not reversed.

Never resolved on-page. Jade and Pat Black ran in and attacked Neuromancer's students Lao and Chen at ringside; the referee began ringing the bell repeatedly amid the chaos, but no winner is ever declared before Torch appears and accidentally fireballs Strife's associate Benjamin. Treated as unresolved per the brief: a bell is rung (apparently a stoppage call, not a finish signal) but Lee-Baby Sims never announces a result and commentary never states one. Left winner and result null rather than guess.

Ares caught Dones in a full nelson, slingshotted him off the ropes into a Full Nelson Slam ("F-N-S"), and pinned him. Post-match, in an unscripted-feeling backstage/parking-lot segment (not a formal match), Ares attacked Nakita Dubov before Alex Wylde ran in with a chair and beat Ares down through a table; not logged as a match since there was no bell, referee, or announced stipulation.

After Raul pushed Dubov off the top rope and Jade sprayed mist in her eyes, Black hit a Fade to Black (top-rope spot) and pinned her. Raul repeatedly interfered against Dubov despite claiming to love her; manager Kevin LeBrock was decked with a chair by Raul post-match, and Dubov chased Raul from the arena. In a following backstage segment, a doctor says Raul's cologne spray has left Dubov with permanent discoloration and light sensitivity in one eye.

Brandon Mueller hit a Mississippi Mudslide legdrop off the truck's hood through a table onto Lincoln McKinley, and Frankie Fargo covered for the pin. Stipulation announced as "Memphis Bar Brawl/Chicago Street Fight" - pinfalls count anywhere, no holds barred. Winner earns a future NFW World Tag Team Title shot against Hellmachine (not itself a title match). Calvin Carlton (managing the Original Showstoppers) interfered repeatedly and was knocked unconscious by a mid-air spear off the truck cab and a follow-up dive from the truck's roof.

eliminations.note: tapped out after being bent backward toward Ryconik by Southern; his team with Michael Manson was eliminated with him
beaten unconscious with a jabbed piece of broken wood, left bleeding heavily; eliminated together with Ricky Zane's tap-out
verbally submitted ("I quit") to stop further punishment on his handcuffed/beaten partner Rick Ryconik
left battered when Southern quit on his behalf; freed from cuffs late in the match by Tully Devotion with wire cutters

matches.note: With Southern's verbal submission ending the match, Bloodhunt and Montezuma were declared the winners. Stipulation: two rings, one cage, submission rules only (a team is eliminated when one member taps or quits). Originally billed with Gladiator as Bloodhunt's partner, but officials barred Gladiator from entering; Armando Montezuma (previously shown 'attacked' backstage and on crutches with a knee injury) later walked in unassisted and revealed the injury and the earlier attack were staged with Bloodhunt. Post-match, Bloodhunt aligns publicly with Team Cuba and debuts a new valet introduced as "Miss Cuba" (see lane_notes on a naming inconsistency).

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Nov 2001), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Adrenaline superkicked a distracted Vanni Ru and covered him for a very quick three count. Carlton objected the count was fast, but the announced result stands. Immediately after the bell, a masked man came from the crowd and beat down Adrenaline; he was later shown to be an ally of Vanni Ru (revealed as Power Master).

Nakita DuBov (LeBrock's client) speared Cojones Mercado at ringside, then low-blowed Raul; LeBrock crawled over and made the cover for the pin. Presented on the broadcast as a post-taped highlight package ('what our live audience saw here earlier tonight') rather than full live commentary, though it occurred at this same taping. Treated here as fresh match content per the lane's default rule; coordinator should double check. Cojones Mercado hit LeBrock with an unseen chairshot mid-match. The specific 'special stipulation' named in the segment title is never spelled out in the text.

Joey Morrison reversed a series of holds and dropped Steve Radder with a knee smash to the chin for the pin. Same highlight-package presentation caveat as the Raul/LeBrock match; treated as fresh content.

A masked assailant emerged from the crowd and attacked Roger Powell, dragging the fight away from the ring; with Powell unable to return, the referee awarded the match to Wildstar. Ring announcer worded the decision as 'winner, by disqualification owing to count out.' The masked attacker was revealed backstage afterward as Roger Powell's own brother Scott Powell, who had been hired by Ricky Zane and then double-crossed him.

After a piano-wire attack on Southern was stopped by the referee, Gladiator retrieved the wire again from ringside ally Miss Cuba, but Southern reversed momentum with a superkick and pinned him for the three count. Southern no-showed his first two ring introductions before entering through the crowd. Gladiator assaulted the original referee (thrown from the ring) and was replaced mid-match by Scott Speranza. ATC allies Bloodhunt and Miss Cuba were at ringside for Gladiator; Bloodhunt gave a thumbs-down signal during a submission hold Southern escaped.

Calvin Carlton interfered with a tennis racquet, hitting Lincoln McKinley in the ankle; Hurricane then nearly pinned Ryan Connors before Tornado speared Connors for the finish. Post-match, Carlton celebrated in the ring and was nearly caught by the recovering Showstoppers before the returning Original Showstoppers (Fargo & Mueller) ran in; McKinley and Connors then dropkicked the OSS out of the ring, leaving Carlton and the OSS laid out.

Alex Wylde hit a springboard dropkick and a Wildcard Frogsplash onto a steel chair placed on Bret Kelly for the pin. Kelly was a late replacement opponent after champion Ares no-showed the event, per Commissioner Manson's ruling that Wylde still had to defend. Earlier backstage, Wylde had already attacked Kelly in the locker room. Weapons (a steel chair) were used without a named stipulation.

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification
matches.note: After a hardcore brawl using a trash can, thumbtacks, and other weapons, Pat Black reversed a Wylde powerbomb attempt into a Boston Crab and forced the submission. Manson stipulated that Wylde would be fired if he lost; the broadcast confirms afterward that 'Alex Wylde is outta work.' Jade accompanied Pat Black at ringside.

date.source: the document's own dateline (17 Mar 2002), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Roger Powell rolled up Andersen Scott for the pin after an extended beatdown by both Powells. Billed together as 'Yin and Yang,' Andersen Scott and RJ Quicksilver worked as a mismatched, bickering team. Immediately after the bell the Powell Brothers turned on their own beaten opponents, locking in a double ankle lock and camel clutch until security intervened, then collected a briefcase payment from an unnamed businessman at ringside, revealing themselves as hired mercenaries rather than genuine allies.

With referee Greg Herpin distracted by manager Armando Montezuma, Raul's chair swing meant for Mueller instead struck Cojones Mercado, letting Mueller roll him up for the pin. A hair-themed grudge match: Mueller's tag partner Frankie Fargo carried clippers throughout, and after the bell Mueller hit Raul with a Mafia Kick while Fargo again brandished the clippers on Mercado, but officials broke it up before any hair was actually cut. Interference throughout from Raul (a hand mirror thrown at Fargo's head, busting him open) and manager Armando Montezuma.

The bell sounded for the fifteen-minute time limit moments after Tempesta Del Fuerte pinned Adrenaline with the Depth Charge piledriver; ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims ruled the match a time-limit draw. Earlier in the match referee Greg Herpin briefly began a count on a Tempesta Del Fuerte pin before waving it off, ruling Tempesta's foot had been on the ropes. After the draw was announced, Tempesta continued attacking Adrenaline, and the brawl spilled to the floor before extra security separated them.

matches.stipulation: Three-Way Boston Street Fight
matches.note: Mister Dread rolled up a dazed Nakita Dubov for the pin as referee Roland Duncan counted three, moments after Dubov and Billy Gray had each kicked out of near-falls on the other. Fought entirely backstage and in a loading dock rather than the ring, using a broomstick, a fluorescent light tube, cabling, a cardboard box, a mesh trashcan, a shovel, an A/V cart and the hood of the ATC's limousine as weapons. Referee Roland Duncan arrived a few minutes after the brawl had already started.

Hellmachine dominated the masked, comedic challengers billed as 'Extra Extra Extra Terrestrial'; Sean Toombs sat down with a powerbomb on Dirty Sanchez while Calamity hit a second moonsault, then covered for the pin as Toombs held down Donkey Punch. Challengers were billed from 'the planet Arcturus' as Donkey Punch (armed with a Kendo stick) and Dirty Sanchez, played as a comedy jobber act; Hellmachine's manager 'Doc' Martena Martens was at ringside. Immediately after the bell the Powell Brothers ran in with a toolbox of weapons (hammer, pliers, saw blade, drill, soldering iron, nails) and destroyed both Hellmachine members, handcuffing Martens to the ropes and finishing with a double-team 'Spike Tiger Driver' through two tables on Sean Toombs; this was an unsanctioned post-match assault, not part of the contest itself.

matches.stipulation: Number One Contender's Match for the NFW World Heavyweight Title
matches.note: After a chaotic finishing stretch featuring a referee bump and run-ins from both Shane Southern and returning 'Cocky' Craig Miles, Rick Ryconick hit the Kielbasa Krunch on Bloodhunt for the pin. Managers Armando Montezuma and Miss Cuba were at ringside for Bloodhunt throughout. Montezuma tried to drug Bloodhunt with a blowdart twice; both attempts failed, the second going off accidentally when Craig Miles slapped Montezuma on the back. Referee Greg Herpin was briefly knocked loopy by an accidental Bloodhunt elbow and later shoved out of the ring by Montezuma, delaying multiple counts. Shane Southern ran in and attacked Montezuma with a lariat and choked him with his own hat.

After Benjamin's interference backfired, Shane Southern press-slammed Benjamin onto Castor Strife, clotheslined Lana Dremire off the apron, then hit a second Party's Over superkick on Strife for the pin. Thirty-minute time-limit main event for the NFW World Heavyweight Championship. Strife's manager Lana Dremire and enforcer Benjamin were at ringside; Dremire distracted referee Greg Herpin during a false finish. Southern appeared to spit up blood and favored his ribs by the finish, an injury angle left unresolved on this broadcast.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Jul 2002), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Presented as a recap of an earlier-in-the-night bout. Matthews' unnamed 'monster' associate distracted the referee so Peterson could be crotched on the ropes and thrown into the post; the shot to his arm let Matthews later win an exchange of reversed pin attempts with an inside cradle for the three count. Round 1 of the 16-man NFW Television Championship tournament. Relayed via highlight-clip narration over B-roll rather than full live commentary, describing action that took place before the broadcast went live ('the doors opened a little over two hours ago'); treated as fresh content since this document is the only record of the bout, not a rerun of previously-aired footage.

Tempesta wore Johnson down with kicks and a judo throw into an elbow to the throat, then finished with a kick to the head and a grapevined-leg pinfall. He then pulled Johnson up and threw him over the top rope before allowing the referee to raise his hand. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, recap-narration format (see order 1 note). Header spells the wrestler 'Tempuesta Del Fuerte'; ring announcer and most commentary use 'Tempesta Del Fuerte' — used the latter as the billed name.

After a back-and-forth in which Raze injured Dread's shoulder and Dread was crotched off the top rope, Dread nipped up, hit a dropkick, and finished Raze with a La Magistral cradle. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, recap-narration format (see order 1 note). Segment header and prior seed table bill this man 'Chris McMillan'; body commentary calls him 'Mister Dread' throughout and the tournament final's ring introduction bills him as 'Mister Dread Chris McMillan' — both names verbatim, used the combined form. Commentary calls this Raze's debut.

Adrenaline won by pinfall (spinebuster into a lateral press) seconds after the opening bell. Raul goaded him into a second bell-to-bell segment and lost again by pinfall (German suplex). After Raul insulted Adrenaline's mother, a third segment was called; Adrenaline won decisively with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker and a powerbomb, with referee Greg Herpin punching a protesting Raul down after Raul shoved him, then counting the pin himself. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, presented live. Structurally one tournament bracket slot restarted twice at Raul's own insistence, each restart ending in a clean bell-to-bell pinfall for Adrenaline; recorded here as a single match entry. The referee striking Raul is an irregularity, but per the staged-announced-result rule the pinfall stands.

An impostor wrestled most of the match under a commissioner's decree forcing the broadcast to address him as 'Michael Manson.' The real Manson secretly swapped in while the impostor was hidden under the ring; the man now in the match hit his Sweet Dreams finisher on Ru for the pin. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, presented live. Immediately after the pin, the real Manson powerbombed the impostor (referred to once the swerve is revealed as 'Triple 6'/'Triple 666') through the Spanish-broadcast table, then DC Stratton ran in and chair-shotted Manson from behind — a post-match angle, not part of the match result. The official record is Michael Manson defeating Vanni Ru; see non_match_appearances for the impostor.

Distracted by worry over a rival's threat against his family, Wildstar missed a dive and was busted open against the barricade; Bondage capitalized with a Leaping DDT for the pin. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, recap-narration format (see order 1 note). Commentary calls this an upset elimination of the tournament favorite 'Five-Star Athlete' Wildstar.

matches.stipulation: New York Back Alley Brawl
matches.note: A brawl through the arena concourse (a refreshment stand, a hot dog stand). Powermaster no-sold a piledriver through a table to rally, but Gray ultimately powerbombed him through two ice blocks set up ringside by Vanni Ru, and Powermaster failed to answer referee Nile Simmons' standing ten count. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, recap-narration format (see order 1 note). Document defines the 'New York Back Alley Brawl' stipulation in-text as a No Countout, No DQ, Last Man Standing match.

A back-and-forth brawl including a 450 splash off the ring post by Stratton that also took out Michael Manson, who had inserted himself at ringside. Manson later sprayed a fire extinguisher into Stratton's face; Viper shoved the blinded Stratton off the top rope through two stacked tables outside the ring, and Stratton failed to beat referee Nile Simmons' ten count. Round 1 of the TV title tournament, presented live. Stratton's manager Neil Riddick was at ringside throughout. Result is a count-out win for Viper, not a draw (only one man was counted out).

Shown joined in progress. After a series of reversed pinfall attempts, Tempesta reversed an inside cradle attempt by Matthews for the three count. Quarterfinal of the TV title tournament, presented live but joined in progress after a commercial break.

Shown joined in progress. Gray nearly finished Manson with a series of strikes and pushed away a Sweet Dreams attempt, but Manson ducked a follow-up clothesline and hit his own boot-and-stunner Sweet Dreams combination for the pin. Quarterfinal of the TV title tournament, presented live but joined in progress after a commercial break.

Shown joined in progress. Bondage nearly stole the match with a small package and reversed a Tornado DDT attempt, but Viper caught him with a suplex on the floor outside the ring and finished with a leg-hook pinfall back in the ring. Quarterfinal of the TV title tournament, presented live but joined in progress after a commercial break.

Shown joined in progress. A competitive technical exchange turned brutal as Dread chopped Adrenaline down and covered off a moonsault, but Adrenaline kicked out and reversed a powerbomb attempt into an elbow drop of his own; Dread ultimately reversed a suplex attempt into a Northern Lights Driver and bridged for the pin. Quarterfinal of the TV title tournament, presented live but joined in progress after a commercial break.

matches.stipulation: Locked, Stocked, Box (a fully enclosed steel cage, no disqualification, no countout, with an under-ring arsenal of weapons pre-approved by both competitors)
matches.note: A hardcore brawl using a golf club, a shovel, a car battery, bolt cutters, a portable TV, an odd assortment of items from a bowling-ball bag, and a ladder Manson used to cut an escape hole in the cage roof. Tempesta ejected his own cornermen Mr. Redd and Dieter Haas when they tried to cut the cage open to help him; Manson then used those same bolt cutters to bust Tempesta's face open. DC Stratton climbed the outside of the cage and fought Manson on its roof, faceplanting him through the hole Manson had cut; Tempesta covered the unconscious Manson for the pin. Semifinal of the TV title tournament, presented live. Referee Greg Herpin, in a pre-match interview, described this specific match as being contested 'for the brand-spanking new NFW Television Title,' but the tournament's own bracket logic (confirmed by the final's ring introduction, which recaps each finalist's full run) shows this

matches.stipulation: Ultimate Japanese Death Match
matches.note: A weapons brawl using a glass-covered bat, a fluorescent light tube, barbed wire, and a table set on fire with lighter fluid. Dread went through the flaming table off a dive but recovered, spilled a bag of thumbtacks so Viper's own diving Vipersault landed in them, then finished Viper with a barbed-wire frog splash for the pin. Semifinal of the TV title tournament, presented live. Billed in the pre-match build as Steel Viper's specialty stipulation.

matches.stipulation: Hell's Kitchen (a 30-foot steel cage wrapped in barbed wire enclosing the ring; the title belt hangs from a hook 30 feet up and must be retrieved via ladder to win)
matches.note: Both men traded near-falls and dives, including a corner-post dive by Dread that missed and a moonsault off a ladder that Tempesta rolled away from. Both were counted to the brink of a standing ten before recovering; both then climbed separate ladders toward the hanging title, fought at the top, and Dread was knocked off, allowing Tempesta Del Fuerte to reach the belt and unhook it for the win. Final of the TV title tournament, presented live. Ring introductions state Tempesta defeated Chris Johnson, Shawn Matthews, and Michael Manson to reach the final, and Dread defeated Raze, Adrenaline, and Steel Viper — confirming the bracket order used for orders 1-14 above.

date.source: the document's own dateline (18 Jun 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After Uriel dominated early with power moves including a Sinner Stampede running powerslam, Prosser turned the match with a low blow, then hit an Implant DDT and a Blaxploitation Shining Wizard for the pin. Presented as a taped highlight recap for viewers newly tuned in to Midnight Madness, but the segment gives a full account of the match; treated as this show's own record of it since no other document covers it. Post-match, backstage personality 'Just' Mark reports that Prosser rushed to the trainer's room.

After Garvin's Axe Bomber (The Encore) was ducked, Deacon countered with a Standing Headscissors into the Altar Call for the pin. Referee Greg Herpin (spelled 'Heprin' elsewhere in the document; treated as the same referee). Deacon's manager Chris Shepherd was at ringside. Garvin was livid at the finish and shoved the referee. Presented as a taped recap of an earlier match on the same broadcast.

After a back-and-forth war of near-falls, Black caught Almasy's top-rope Ultima attempt with a Gauntlet Backhand off the top rope (a face-first chokeslam) and pinned him. Billed by the show as the true opening match of the season, shown here as the 'full version' replay after being teased with highlights earlier in the broadcast. Time of the match given as 16:12. Ring announcer Lee Baby Sims.

Gabriel escaped Heimdal's Cranial Smoke attempt, hit a reverse hurricanrana, then finished with a Full-Rotation Single-Arm DDT for the three-count. Presented in prose form as a 'Season Pass Ticker' recap rather than a live commentary call, but it is this show's only record of the match.

Troy Windham ran in and attacked Winters while he had Adler in a full nelson; Adler pulled Windham off, but the referee stopped the match and awarded the win to Winters due to the interference. Not a clean, in-ring finish; the match was stopped by referee decision after outside interference from Troy Windham. Aftermath: Windham, August De La Rossi, and The Mysterious Zoltan ambushed and beat down Winters backstage, with Windham urinating on Winters' face on camera.

After a chair shot busted Christ open, Christ voluntarily walked to the back rather than continue fighting, and was counted out at ten. Angelo Deville's NFW debut, preceded by a lengthy hostile promo trashing Steve Christ and the defunct 'Asylum' promotion. Referee not named.

Alias hit a top-rope belly-to-belly suplex he calls the '(Bigger Fatter) Kill' for the pin, though the impact dislocated his own shoulder, which he then popped back into place himself at ringside. Alias's NFW debut. Referee Bruce Phillips. Includes a spot where Cameron powerbombed Alias through the announce table.

Flair reversed a suplex attempt into a small package for the pin. Lennox Love's NFW debut. Text picks up the match 'joined in progress' at 11:24, so the opening is not shown. Managers Poison Ivy (with Flair) and MaryJane Fields (with Love) briefly confronted each other at ringside.

After a long, brutal live main-event brawl, Randalls countered Miles into a Crucifix and hit the Tommyhawk for the pin. Mike Randalls' NFW debut, billed as the first-ever in-ring meeting between two 13-year real-life friends and allies. Referee Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips.

No finish is shown. The match opened as a staged, friendly exchange of near-falls (Mayfield rolled Windham up for a two-count using the ropes for leverage) before Mayfield 'shoot' attacked Windham and the brawl spilled out of the ring, through the crowd, and into the concourse. August De La Rossi and The Mysterious Zoltan interfered on Windham's behalf; Donaven Winters ran in, speared De La Rossi (aiming for Windham) through a glass popcorn machine, badly busting him open, then fought Zoltan (hitting a Burning Hammer on the concrete) while Windham fled the arena in a cab. The segment ends with the match unresolved. Referee Greg Heprin (see note on match 2 re: spelling).

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Aug 2006), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Gravy Wrestling Match (Mittens T. Cat Celebrity Bash)
matches.note: After trading near-falls in a tub of gravy, Mittens T. Cat won with a small package while grabbing a handful of Trebek's tights. Post-match, the San Diego Chicken runs in with a chair and attacks both Mittens and a returning Trebek before security and a crowd brawl break it up.

matches.stipulation: Western Conference Wild Card Round Playoff Match
matches.note: After absorbing a near-squash beating (including a Pump Handle Slam into the ring post that appeared to end the match early), Guy Boudreaux caught Scott Riktor with a sunset flip, using the ropes for leverage without the referee seeing, for the pinfall upset. Commentary explicitly notes the referee did not see Guy's illegal use of the ropes on the finish; the staged-announced result stands per the binding rule.

matches.stipulation: Western Conference Wild Card Round Playoff Match
matches.note: Lindsay Troy forced Manpower to submit to a Figure Four Leglock. Commentary notes Troy's finishing hold is normally Joey Melton's signature move; Manpower is barred by prior ruling from having his manager Calvin Carlton at ringside for this match.

matches.stipulation: Wildcard Round Playoff Match
matches.note: Both men's shoulders were down simultaneously off a reversal sequence; the referee's on-screen signal is ambiguous, and NFW Commissioner Craig Miles later personally rules Joey Melton's fall invalid for an illegal tights pull, awarding the match to Nova. Immediately after ruling for Nova, Miles announces a blanket second-chance policy that lets every Wild Card Round loser -- Melton included -- back into Ultratitle contention regardless of this match's outcome.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere; spontaneously announced by Craig Miles with the two survivors advancing

eliminations.note: Pinned after a chair shot to the back of the head.
Pinned following a Van Daminator (spinning leg clothesline into a chair).
Pinned after a top-rope splash, with manager Calvin Carlton piling on for the cover.

matches.note: Joey Melton and Scott Riktor were the two men left standing after successive eliminations and were both declared winners, advancing per Craig Miles's own stipulation. Manager Calvin Carlton reinvigorates a struggling Joey Melton mid-match with a football jacket tied to an unseen, referenced subplot involving "Eddy Love" and Mike Randalls. Scott Riktor separately assaults Craig Miles both during and after the match; Miles responds by announcing a future "Demolition Derby Match" for the West's second-chance round, in which he says he will personally compete.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat (first round)
matches.note: Shown only as a spoken summary: Craig Miles introduces the highlights package of the first-round triple threat of Kodiak Vic Creed (billed KVC), Rook Black and Sean Stevens, says Creed outwrestled both, then skips the footage for the Mittens T. Cat match. The closing recap credits "resounding victories by Kodiak Vic Creed and Lindsay Troy". No finish is given.

date.source: the document's own dateline (20 Jan 2007), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Scaffold Grudge Match, ten-minute time limit
matches.note: The match is never resolved on-screen. Scotty J. Bowman runs in, takes a bribe from the Chicken, then double-crosses him by dropkicking him off the scaffold through a concession stand; he then fakes helping a handcuffed Mittens T. Cat before stomping his hand. The segment cuts away to commentary with no bell, pinfall, or declared winner; the Chicken is taken to a hospital and Mittens is led backstage by security.

matches.stipulation: Second Chances Match (a hardcore, weapons/minefield/scaffold gauntlet billed as the 'Divisional Demolition Derby,' run across the whole arena floor in installments interspersed through the rest of the card)

eliminations.note: eliminated via the pinfall loss in his separate seeded singles match against Creed (recorded below), which doubles as his elimination here; he continues taking punishment in the background brawl afterward despite being out
rolled up with a handful of tights after Guy hits him with a loaded punch using Maxwell Diamond's stolen diamond rings
pinned via a Shooting Star Press Nova hits after leaping off a moving ATV

matches.note: This match/stipulation opens the show and runs continuously in the background of every other match via cutaways (junkyard brawling, a C-4 mine-laden dune field, a broken-glass-and-thumbtack pit, a scaffold/slide). Its own rules require Craig Miles (also a combatant and the Western Conference's authority figure) to be knocked out or to call a stop to it. The broadcast ends with the stipulation unresolved: remaining/still-active figures (Craig Miles, Joey Melton, Calvin Carlton, Nova, Guy Boudreaux) are still fighting or fleeing when the show cuts off, disrupted by a surprise sledgehammer attack on Miles from returning wrestler High Flyer and a countdown ('Project: X-TERMINATE') that goes off before any final resolution airs; per the binding rule on unresolved matches, no winner or result is recorded.

Kodiak Vic Creed hits a Hangman's DDT for the pin after a bloody brawl (a burned foam finger, a low blow, chair shots) that spilled through the crowd and ringside area. Fought in an extremely hardcore style consistent with the show's environment, though no formal stipulation is named for this bout specifically. Alias remains a combatant in the broader Second Chances Match afterward despite the loss (see above).

Lindsay Troy hits the Ultima IX (Almasy's own finisher) for the pin. Billed as a rematch of a prior 'Week 4' encounter Almasy won. Almasy, who had pre-announced his retirement, wrestles with deliberate apathy and repeatedly bails from the ring, drawing heavy crowd heat; Troy deliberately breaks up her own pin attempts partway through to punish him further before finishing him. Post-match, in a segment titled 'Fated Fantasy,' Troy ambushes Almasy with a chair as he tries to leave and delivers a chair-assisted superplex-type move ('Supafishamanbusta'), then cuts a promo calling out Kodiak Vic Creed, who responds live with a menacing promo of his own.

Eli Flair hits a low blow followed by the Fallen One (reverse headlock neckbreaker) for the pin. An extremely chaotic 'Round Two playoffs' brawl that spills into the ongoing Second Chances Match's environment, including both men being dragged behind a moving monster truck through the landmine-laden dune area. Flair wins via a low blow after the match had been built up around mutual pre-match respect, then leaves without celebrating as the crowd boos the finish.

Tom Adler hits the Adlerplex for the pin after a back-and-forth match with multiple false finishes. Guy Boudreaux steals Maxwell Diamond's diamond rings mid-match and uses a loaded punch with them; Craig Miles also interferes, blasting Seymour Almasy (not a participant in this match) with a shotgun beanbag round nearby. Post-match, Guy Boudreaux keeps the stolen rings and is folded into the ongoing Second Chances Match as the finale's barbed-wire cage descends.

date.source: the document's own dateline (30 Jul 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wired Match
matches.note: No finish was declared. Avery Prosser interfered on Deville's behalf, chairshots flew on both sides, and a bloodied Zameer eventually walked off toward the back without being pinned while Deville did not pursue him. Ring announcer stated the stakes as 10 points to the winner, 5 points each on a double pin/double knockout draw, but no such result occurred. See lane_notes for why this is left unresolved rather than guessed.

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire Bat Match
matches.note: Love's own manager MaryJane grabbed the barbed wire bat to help him but accidentally struck her own man in the face; Almasy rolled Love up for the pin. Shown joined-in-progress; both men entered the match 0-1 on the season.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Barbed-wire, HON-er Role
matches.note: After a sitout powerbomb through a barbed-wire table left both men down for a long count, Garvin nearly finished Alias, but Alias fought back and hit an 'A-Bomb' for the pin. Commentary calls Alias 'Chris Sheffield' throughout the in-ring action even though he is billed as 'Alias.'

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire Match
matches.note: After Windham's ally August De La Rossi fed him blinding powder and a flaming barbed-wire table spot, Winters countered with a top-rope Burning Hammer Redemption through the flaming table for the pin. Presented as 'a live replay of an earlier match tonight' rather than live action (see lane_notes). Immediately after the pin, Eli Flair ran in from the crowd, attacked the EMTs, and beat down both Windham and a still-recovering Winters, cutting a promo about their shared history.

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire and Bullrope Match
matches.note: After Christ dominated much of the bout, Black turned the tide with a barrage of headbutts and a Spike Michinoku Driver, then ground him down with strikes until the referee counted Christ's shoulders down. Told partly through an intercut framing device (Black showering afterward, haunted by the violence).

matches.stipulation: Barbed-Wired Steel Cage
matches.note: Cameron pinned Randalls with a Running Razor's Edge into the turnbuckle. A mysterious unnamed 'doctor' interfered repeatedly on both sides (drugging Randalls' eyes, later trying to inject him with a syringe), addressing Randalls as 'Michael' and claiming a court would let him take Randalls back into custody. Randalls fought the doctor off post-match and fled up the ramp, still blinded.

Adler wrapped his UWA World Title belt in barbed wire and suplexed Deacon onto it with a Double Chicken Wing Death Lake Driver for the pin. A barbed wire steel cage is lowered around the ring per the stage directions, but no formal 'Stipulation:' line is given for this match unlike others on the card (see lane_notes); the UWA World Title itself was not defended, only used as a weapon. Commentary states this was the first-ever singles meeting between these two World Champions.

Heimdal reversed a Uriel powerbomb attempt into a Tornado DDT, then rolled him into a bridging cradle for the pin. Ring ropes are described as replaced with barbed wire for this match, though no formal stipulation name is given (see lane_notes). Uriel falls to 0-2 on the season.

Donaven Winters ran in through the crowd and blasted Flair with a chair from behind; Flair collapsed on top of Brown for the pin. Text explicitly notes barbed wire replaced the ring ropes for this match, one of only a few contested that way this show (see lane_notes for why stipulation is left blank). Brown was visibly reluctant to accept a win handed to him by outside interference.

matches.stipulation: Jacobs Ladder Match
matches.note: After an extended brawl involving razor wire, fire, a nailed-down table spot, and interference from both Anne Mystic and Miles' estranged wife Nixon, Mayfield locked Miles in the Sharpshooter and Miles tapped out. Co-owners and former best friends/tag partners; extremely bloody main event with numerous weapon spots (hammer, hatchet, pliers, fireball, ring bell, boot spur).

date.source: the document's own dateline (28 Aug 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Played almost entirely for comedy (rock-paper-scissors, a noogie contest, an overselling contest); Black won by escaping Heimdal's Cranial Smoke submission and hitting the Gauntlet Backhand. Entire match staged as a comedic exchange between the two friends.

Shown via highlights on the arena screen: Zameer nearly won with a huge elbowdrop, but Almasy hit a Frog Splash; Zameer kicked out and pressed Almasy out of the ring. Zameer's cornerman Avery Prosser tried to chair Almasy but hit Zameer instead when Almasy dodged; Almasy dropkicked Prosser out and finished Zameer with a springboard Shooting Star Press ("Ultima"). Commentary states this match itself took place before the broadcast went on air; only highlights were shown due to time constraints. Avery Prosser was at ringside for Zameer (manager role). Commentary notes this was Almasy's second straight week improving to 2-1 in NFW.

Garvin absorbed a prolonged beating, hit a German Suplex, and after Calvin Carlton's ringside chair shot turned the tide against Cameron, finished with the Memphis Death Certificate (leaping piledriver) for the pin. Shown largely via replayed/announced audio-video segments from earlier NFW Season Pass coverage of the same broadcast, not a fresh live call. Calvin Carlton interfered with a steel chair, striking Cameron and enabling Garvin's comeback; referee Greg Herpin worked the match. Commentary states Garvin earned 10 points for the win.

After Mayfield threw powder in Deacon's eyes and nearly finished him with a piledriver, a pretaped Craig Miles segment destroying Mayfield's apartment played on the arena screen as a distraction; Deacon recovered with a headbutt/reversal sequence and hit the Altar Call for the pin. Referee Scott Speranza. Anne Mystic (Mayfield's manager/wife) interfered at ringside, accusing Deacon of choking Mayfield to cover for Mayfield's foreign-object (powder) use. Craig Miles aired a pretaped segment destroying Mayfield's home electronics with a chainsaw and blowtorch during the match as a receipt for a prior angle.

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves Town
matches.note: Deville dominated, working Uriel's leg and nearly finishing with the Soprano, but stopped to taunt ringside manager Avery Prosser; Prosser tripped Deville, after which Uriel suddenly no-sold his injuries, hit a lariat, then Break Upon The Altar (gorilla-press backbreaker) and the Fire of God (double underhook kneeling piledriver) for the pin. Uriel appeared to enter a trance-like state (eyes closed) after the lariat, moving with unnatural speed; commentary suggested something supernatural ('like Uriel was someone else'). Avery Prosser engineered the stipulation and interfered. Deville is written out of NFW West per the loser-leaves stipulation.

Both men brawled to a lengthy stalemate; after Windham missed a moonsault and both men later crashed into the ringside barricade, Eddie Mayfield ran in and chair-shotted Miles then clotheslined Windham, felling both. Referee Greg Herpin declared a double knockout and NFW ruled neither man would receive points. Document explicitly calls the finish a 'DOUBLE KNOCKOUT' rather than a double count-out or double disqualification; mapped to result "no-contest" as the closest fit per lane convention (see lane_notes). Eddie Mayfield and Anne Mystic interfered. After the bell, Miles tore off Windham's novelty ring pants (which bore an image of Miles' wife Nixon) as a receipt for Windham's earlier promo about her.

matches.stipulation: Ten-Minute Time Limit Exhibition
matches.note: The ten-minute time limit expired with the match still in progress; no fall was recorded. Manager William Taggert (wheelchair-bound) at ringside for Brown. This was Riktor's first in-ring appearance in NFW West (an exhibition, distinct from his 'official' debut match at the next Midnight Madness).

matches.stipulation: Sudden Death overtime following a 30-minute time-limit draw
matches.note: The original 30-minute time limit expired with the match ruled a draw. Craig Miles then ordered a sudden-death restart. During a Randalls crossface submission attempt on Adler, a ringside physician (Dr. White) ruled that Randalls could not confirm awareness due to blood in his eyes and stopped the match; the decision was awarded to Adler by official's decision. A hooded figure teased as returning legend Stumanchoo turned out to be Troy Windham in disguise, who announced a signed rematch with Adler for the UWA World Championship (not contested in this match). Dr. White, previously reported fired the prior week, was revealed to have been reinstated by Anne Mystic; his stoppage cited re-injury to Randalls' eyes from the previous week's match with Marcus Cameron. Randalls never verbally submitted; this was an official's stoppage, not a submission loss.

date.source: the document's own dateline (11 Oct 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves Town (per NFW President Quentin Sullivan's announcement: a 90-day ban from NFW competition, with the right to re-apply afterward)
matches.note: Joined in progress at an on-screen 17:47 time-code; after a back-and-forth big-man exchange, Cameron reversed Deacon's Altar Call attempt into a Reverse Neckbreaker, then hit a Jackknife Powerbomb for the pin. Referee Greg Herpin. Deacon was initially feared to have a broken neck but was confirmed afterward to have suffered only a neck stinger. Deacon is eliminated from Ultratitle competition under Sullivan's new stipulation, jointly submitted by Craig Miles and Anne Mystic.

Riktor hit a top-rope move called 'The Riktor Scale' for the pin after a technical/submission-heavy contest. Billed in narration as Riktor's official NFW debut match, distinct from his earlier non-title exhibition against Gabriel Brown at the previous Midnight Madness.
After a long, evenly-matched technical contest, Adler locked in the Adlerlock (Crossface Chicken Wing) and Alias tapped out.

After Mayfield used a hidden chain (supplied by manager Anne Mystic) for a piledriver, chokes and strikes throughout, Ryan intercepted a final chain hand-off attempt, reversed a leapfrog into the Humility Bomb, big-booted Mystic off the apron when she climbed in to interfere again, then covered Mayfield for the pin. Billed as a thirty-minute time-limit interconference match worth ten points to the winner; referee Scott Speranza; ring announcer Lee-Baby Sims. Keeps Dan Ryan the only undefeated wrestler in NFW this season.

date.source: the document's own dateline (18 Nov 2005), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After interference from both men's ringside seconds (Anne Mystic for Mayfield, Calvin Carlton for Garvin) and a shot from Calvin Carlton's tennis racket, Mayfield reversed a sunset flip attempt into a roll-through pin for the win. Managers Anne Mystic (Mayfield) and Calvin Carlton (Garvin) were both active at ringside throughout, including Carlton piledriving Mystic through the announce table. Immediately after the bell, Troy Windham ran in and, joined by Garvin, Carlton, and Windham's New South Enterprises entourage (August De La Rossi, Lord Zoltan, The Mysterious Z), beat down Mayfield until Tom Adler made the save.

Uriel missed a second Big Splash attempt, and Seymour Almasy capitalized immediately with an Oklahoma roll for the pin. Billed as an inter-divisional (NFW West vs NFW East) matchup; Almasy's fourth straight NFW win.

Gabriel Brown announced he was quitting the match and the promotion outright before the bell rang and walked to the back; Ghost was left standing in the ring with the referee as the implied but never formally announced winner. No bell ever rang and no official winner was declared by referee or ring announcer; this is a borderline non-match/forfeit case, flagged for the coordinator's judgment on whether it should register as a match at all.

Guy Boudreaux hit a hidden low blow followed by a superkick for the pin, after a match built around Guy repeatedly feigning injury (playing possum and faking a bladed cut) to create openings. Guy Boudreaux's in-ring NFW debut, refereed by Chris Fusco.

Norman Quiry made Marcus Cameron submit to an inverted Texas-cloverleaf-style hold he calls the 'Black Jigsaw,' set up by a low blow the referee did not see. Norman Quiry's in-ring NFW debut; he was accompanied to ringside by his secretary, Elissa Quinzell.

Scott Riktor hit his fireman's-carry finisher, 'The Finishing Touch,' for the pin after Rook Black had controlled much of the match with a Dragon Sleeper and repeated near-falls. Both men billed as top contenders for the Ultratitle; no title was directly at stake.

Following interference from Melton's horse, which kicked Eli Flair, Melton reversed a rollup attempt and finished Flair with a low blow immediately before the referee's three-count. A returning Joey Melton's NFW West debut of Season Two, refereed by Roland Priest. Post-match, Flair retaliated by lassoing Melton to his own horse and having it drag him up the entrance ramp.

Mike Randalls hit a bridging Cobra Clutch Suplex for the pinfall after a lengthy back-and-forth exchange of near-falls, refereed by Greg Herpin. The match was interrupted mid-way by the surprise ringside arrival of Brandon Youngblood, previously reported to have quit his Season Two contract before it began; he did not physically interfere, but visibly unsettled both competitors before departing.

matches.stipulation: Count-out and disqualification rules waived (a winner must be determined)
matches.note: Referee Greg Herpin called for the bell and awarded Adler the win and the vacant title by disqualification after Windham sprayed him in the face with a liquid, having already used Zoltan's interference (a steel chair shot) earlier in the match. Windham's entourage (Lord Zoltan, August De La Rossi) interfered repeatedly at ringside throughout. Immediately after the match, a returning Eddie Mayfield presented a contract signed by Anne Mystic forcing Adler to defend the title again on the spot.

matches.stipulation: I Quit Rules
matches.note: Adler picked up a microphone and said 'I Quit' without further physical contest, immediately surrendering the UWA World Heavyweight Championship to Eddie Mayfield. Before conceding, Adler delivered an on-air monologue revealing a long secret history in which Anne Mystic had for years protected him from confronting Mayfield directly; his forfeit followed that revelation rather than any move by Mayfield. Refereed by Greg Herpin.

Kodiak Vic Creed hit his 'Powertrip' powerbomb-style finisher for the pin, moments after new UWA World Champion Eddie Mayfield ran in and broke a champagne bottle over Craig Miles' head. The Credits/segment title conceals the opponent's identity as a swerve; Kodiak Vic Creed (KVC) is revealed as Miles' opponent only when he appears on camera. Booked by Anne Mystic as payback against Miles for earlier burning down Eddie Mayfield's apartment and pitting him against Dan Ryan. Refereed by Greg Herpin.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 Jan 2006), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Nova, subbing in off the waiting list for a no-showed opponent, defeated Frank Heimdal at the 23-minute mark with a Corkscrew Cradle Suplex he calls the In-NOVA-vator. Shown only via in-show recap/highlights covering action from 'the early going tonight,' not full live commentary. This match and the following Almasy/N. Quiry match are both recapped under the single Credits-block segment title above, which names only the Almasy match. Treated as fresh matches from this broadcast (not archival replay of a prior show) per brief guidance.

A thirty-minute time-limit expired with both wrestlers down after Quiry survived Almasy's springboard shooting star press ('Ultima'). Shown only via in-show recap/highlights, not full live commentary; see note on the preceding match sharing this segment title.

Adler capitalized on Black's mid-match breakdown and forced a tapout with a combination Indian deathlock/crossface Adler calls the Masterlock. Black suffered an inexplicable vomiting/'possession' episode mid-match (commentary jokes it was a bad taco, but frames it as Black being 'haunted'/'stalked by a dead woman'), which let Adler take over. This was the show's first live match, following recap packages of earlier action.

After Boudreaux bladed himself and framed Riktor for a chair shot to the referee's back to steal a near-fall, Riktor kicked out and finished Boudreaux with the Finishing Touch for the pin. Boudreaux's entrance music was botched (wrong song played) before the match, prompting an in-storyline complaint from him afterward. The referee was deceived by Boudreaux's staged chair-shot frame job and never learned the truth on-screen.

Calvin Carlton flashed a distracting 'money sign' at Cameron from the apron; Windham capitalized and pinned Cameron with the Slackknife. Shown via in-show recap/highlights of action from 'earlier tonight,' not full live commentary. Calvin Carlton (Windham's New South Enterprises associate) was at ringside; commentary speculates this is part of a pattern of Carlton buying decisions for wrestlers outside his own stable, since Cameron is not himself a New South member.

Manpower survived Miles's full arsenal (flaming tennis racket, fire extinguisher, chair shots, Torture Rack, missed top-rope splash through a table) and won with a Power Plant (spinebuster) through a table. Manpower's NFW debut; a major upset win over the former fWo Internet Champion Craig Miles.

After Alias nearly finished Uriel with a Dragon Sleeper, KVC speared Alias out to the floor, then pinned the incapacitated Uriel with the Creedzillinator. Billed in the segment title/commentary as 'KVC'; introduced by full name 'Kodiak Vic Creed' elsewhere in the show. Single-fall three-way, not an elimination match.

After Youngblood's Gridlock (Seated Katahajime) submission held to the time-limit warning without forcing a tapout, and a missed post-kickout chair shot from Youngblood, Randalls knocked him out cold with an enziguiri he later dubbed 'Bad Moon Rising.' The text never shows an explicit pinfall count or a referee 'ring the bell' line declaring a winner — the finish reads as a knockout/medical stoppage (EMTs are shown arriving for Youngblood). Randalls is treated throughout the aftermath as having won; flagged for coordinator confirmation given the missing explicit decision line. Billed as the rubber match of a long-running rivalry (their third encounter).

matches.stipulation: Chicken Wire Cage 'Mexican Cock Fight' (climb a ladder to grab a kendo stick off a wire, then use it to break open a hanging piñata to win)
matches.note: Text never resolves the match: Melton appeared to strike the win-condition piñata, but it was booby-trapped with a pyrotechnic explosion, and the broadcast immediately cut to Troy Windham bungee-cording into the ring for a run-in. Windham and Calvin Carlton (who had been locked in the cage as Garvin's second, and became an active participant) then brutally beat down and humiliated Melton (forcing his face into Windham's crotch) to close the show; no bell, pin, or decision is ever shown. Left winner and result null per the brief's rule for a match the text never resolves.

date.source: the document's own dateline (18 Feb 2006), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Caldwell used a tennis racket smuggled in by manager Calvin Carlton to blindside Cameron and pin him. Calvin Carlton accompanied Caldwell to ringside as manager and slipped him the racket while distracting the referee; the referee never saw the weapon.

Alias won by disqualification after Manpower ignored the referee's five-count while beating him down with forearm shots in the ropes. Presented in the document as a written fan recap rather than live commentary, but produced fresh for this broadcast (has its own Credits-block writer attribution), so treated as a match. Calvin Carlton managed Manpower at ringside; Manpower speared Carlton mid-match after Alias baited him into the ropes, and turned on Carlton afterward over a broken promise (an MP3 player).

Boudreaux won by count-out after N. Quiry failed to beat the referee's ten count back into the ring. Calvin Carlton (Boudreaux's manager, ringside) illegally held N. Quiry's leg outside the ring, unseen by the referee, preventing his return. Elisa "Quiz" Quiznell, Quiry's valet, was at ringside and was thrown into the steel steps by Boudreaux after the bell.

No finish was ever declared. Marcus Cameron chair-shot the referee before any decision could be reached; the bout dissolved into a multi-man brawl involving Nova, Cameron, and Brandon Youngblood that spilled through the crowd, across the boardwalk amusement park, and off a pier, ending in police intervention and arrests rather than a wrestling finish.

Almasy reversed Windham's Autograph finisher attempt into a backslide pin for the three count. The Mysterious Zoltan (part of Windham's Entourage) hit Almasy with a stool while the referee was distracted checking on Windham; later, manager Calvin Carlton summoned Manpower to run in and chokeslam Almasy while the referee was down (referee bumped by Windham). Joey Melton then ran in and chased Manpower off with repeated chairshots before Almasy secured the win. Almasy is noted as the reigning ACW World Champion, but that title (from another promotion) was not contested here.

Miles hit a diving elbow drop off a camera tower through a table set up over Melton for the pinfall. An extended brawl left the ring for the crowd, the beach, a sand sculpture, and the ocean. Referee Chris Fusco was knocked out mid-match by a Miles neckbreaker and later distracted repeatedly. Rival duo "The Original Showstoppers" (Frankie Fargo and Brandon Mueller) attacked both men on jet skis in the ocean, and Calvin Carlton buzzed the beach on his yacht taunting Melton; none of this altered the eventual finish.

Flair caught Creed's top-rope Creedzillinator attempt with raised knees, then hit the Fallen One (a reverse DDT-style finisher) for the pin. Billed as the main event, a rematch of a prior fWo World Championship feud. The broadcast cut off shortly after this match when commentators announced a real fire had broken out nearby and the area needed to be cleared.

date.source: the document's own dateline (18 Mar 2006), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Hulk-A-Thon Tournament First Round

eliminations.note: Pinned after a Backdrop Suplex on the floor and a rolled-up cover in the ring.

matches.note: Payne pinned Alias, but before it was signaled, the man billed as Yori Yakamo Jr. hit a top-rope legdrop on Payne and covered him for the win. The wrestler billed as 'Yori Yakamo Jr.' here and elsewhere on this card is explicitly identified in the prose as Riki Yakamo, Yori's twin brother, made up to resemble Yori (eyepatch, pirate motif); narration alternately calls him 'NOT Yori' and '"YYJ"'. The real Yori Yakamo Jr. does not appear in this match; see the main event note for his in-fiction return.

matches.stipulation: Hulk-A-Thon Tournament First Round

eliminations.note: Pinned with a German Suplex.

matches.note: After Anatoly nearly finished Marx with a top-rope sitdown powerbomb and both men beat a double ten-count, Marx recovered and hit a Canadian Backbreaker into a Gory Special (called 'Gory 2000') for the pin. Norman Quiry's manager Quiz was at ringside for him. A Quiry near-fall on Anatoly via schoolboy used a handful of tights that the referee caught and disallowed.

matches.stipulation: Hulk-A-Thon Tournament First Round

eliminations.note: Disqualified for repeatedly hitting Brandon Youngblood with a fan's novelty baseball bat.

matches.note: After Nova was disqualified for the weapon shots on Youngblood, Troy finished Youngblood alone with a top-rope shooting-star frog splash. Billed as the final first-round Hulk-a-Thon qualifier. Commentary states Dan Ryan, Jonathan Marx, Kin Hiroshi and 'Yori Yakamo Junior' had already advanced to the War Games final before this match began.

Creed kicked out of Manpower's finishing sequence, then hit a spear and a Hangman's DDT for the pin, after Manpower had already survived Creed's Power Trip DDT. Billed as a Hulk Hogan tribute 'giant vs. giant' attraction match. Calvin Carlton was at ringside managing Manpower, who wrestled soaked in orange body paint as a Hulk Hogan homage.

Riktor speared Roland into the ring steps outside the ring, then finished him in the ring with his signature move ('The Finishing Touch') for the pin. Andy Johnson is introduced as a debuting rookie ('The 13th Warrior'). Malik Roland is billed as the LoC Team Champion and a member of a stable called the Faction, sent by 'Black Tom Williams' to physically attack Riktor, who was said to be an authority figure in a separate promotion (LoC) and thus unreachable by the Faction there.

matches.stipulation: Hulk-A-Thon Tournament Final — modified two-ring War Games cage match; no escape (only pinfall/submission/knockout), scoring 5/5/10/20 points to the 1st/2nd/3rd/4th eliminations

eliminations.note: Never answered the bell after being assaulted before the match by Dan Dority, a wrestler called 'Green Machine,' and a masked man called 'Panda Mask' near the entrance ramp's Hulk Hogan sculpture. Counted out; the ring announcer stated no points were awarded for this removal.
Eliminated together with Dan Ryan when Troy dropkicked both men off the top of the cage through the Spanish announce tables.
Eliminated together with Jonathan Marx; see above.

matches.note: With only Troy and 'Yori Yakamo Jr.' (Riki) left, Kodiak Vic Creed — not a billed participant — entered the cage, chair-shotted all three assigned referees, powerbombed Troy through a table, and brawled with her for several minutes. A costumed figure billed as 'Powermaster,' framed in the prose as the returning genuine Yori Yakamo Jr., then dropped in with a legdrop onto both Troy and Creed; Powermaster and Riki both covered Troy, and the referee counted the pin for 'Yori Yakamo Jr.' Extensive unsanctioned interference in the closing minutes: Kodiak Vic Creed entered unbilled and incapacitated all three assigned referees (Bruce 'Powerslide' Phillips, Greg Herpin, S.B. Wong) before the finish. A second, previously unseen man billed as 'Powermaster' also entered unbilled and is framed in the narration as the genuine Yori Yakamo Jr. (distinct from the Riki Yakamo impersonator who wrestled t

date.source: the document's own dateline (20 Jun 2006), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Guy Boudreaux hits the Bourbon Street Hangover (a Sunset Leg Drop) for the pin after a low blow, capping a match in which he repeatedly used smuggled brass knuckles and Mardi Gras beads as weapons. Guy Boudreaux is confiscated brass knuckles and a lead pipe before the bell but still cheats to win; the win moves him 'fifteen points closer to the playoffs' and to a 3-3 record.

In the segment's own heavily fantastical framing, Nova defeats a monstrous, dragon-transformed Manpower and pins him for the win. This segment is written as an intentionally over-the-top, self-parodying 'overselling' comedy sketch (Manpower literally transforms into a dragon; commentary shouts in all caps); the in-fiction result is nonetheless a clean pinfall win for Nova as announced.

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification
matches.note: Tom Adler turns on his own partner Eddie Mayfield mid-match, low-blowing him and hitting him with a chair; the returning tag team the Cutters (Nathan Storm and J. Bishop) interfere on Adler's behalf, and Adler drops an unconscious Craig Miles onto Mayfield for the deciding pin. Craig Miles' partner is revealed as Sean Stevens ('Triple X'). Stakes: the winning side chose who received a Western Conference Ultratitle wildcard slot and who received a UWA World Championship title shot against Mayfield; Triple X takes the wildcard slot and Miles earns the title shot. Afterward, Maxwell Diamond of the rival 'Diamond Exchange'/CSWA cuts a promo revealing the match was engineered as part of a long-running grudge against the UWA and NFW.

The segment itself contains no play-by-play, only a brief three-line stub. The winner recorded here (Eli Flair) is inferred from a later in-show Craig Miles promo line stating that Eli Flair 'strung up Rook Black' that night; no finish detail is otherwise given. Flagged as a source defect in lane_notes.

After Scott Riktor's Sharpshooter forces the referee to begin a three-count on Alias's dropped arm, Riktor prematurely celebrates; Alias rolls him up with a handful of tights for a schoolboy pin before the bell is called for Riktor. Billed as deciding which man gets a bye through the first round of the Western Conference playoffs; the two competitors are close friends and trade real blows after the match out of anger.

Joey Melton strikes Vic Creed with the timekeeper's bell and covers him; suspended wrestler Lindsay Troy runs in, shoves down referee Greg Herpin, and physically forces the three-count herself before Herpin recovers. Billed as worth ten Ultratitle qualifying points, which Melton is awarded despite briefly conceding the match by having initially thrown in the towel against Creed.

name: NFW Playoffs

date.source: The document carries no date of its own; the surviving capture is dated unknown.
