notes: A standing document from the fed's own site, not a show.

date.source: the document's own dateline (1 May 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: When Mercado tries to flee up the ramp, two masked agents sent by President Mayfield spear/elbow him down; Joe the Plumber then hits a Tiger Driver on the ramp itself for the pin. Mercado was ordered into this match under threat of being fired if he lost; per a later show's recap he was fired anyway after losing. The pin occurred on the entrance ramp, not in the ring.

Impulse lands the Sudden Impact Superkick for a clean pin after a competitive showing from the NFW newcomer. Post-match, Orlando Grant is ambushed and repeatedly Director's-Cut neckbreakered by Castor V. Strife, Blanche Barnett, and The Triumvirate in a segment titled 'Settle the Score,' setting up the next match.

Freak accident (broken top rope) leaves Impulse unresponsive; Castor Strife finishes with a Director's Cut for the pin. Impromptu rematch of the Crash 50 draw, called for on the spot after Castor demanded a title shot post-beatdown. Referee Speranza does not stop the match despite Impulse appearing unresponsive; Blanche Barnett and Rosie (Impulse's second) brawl at ringside during the match; Impulse needs help to the back afterward.

American Panda's neck-biting run-in interference against High Flyer causes the bell to ring; the match is awarded to High Flyer via disqualification. President Mayfield had decreed the 'clean' winner of this match would qualify for the National Championship 'Around the USA in 80 Days' tour; since it ended in a DQ mess (referee Speranza was earlier knocked unconscious by an accidental Shoryuken, and Felicia Hart tried to hairspray Flyer), Mayfield's subsequent proclamation admitted all three men involved -- Hart, Flyer, and American Panda -- into the tour field. Post-match Hart Shoryukens both Flyer and Panda and stands alone.

date.source: the document's own dateline (24 Jun 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Bryant locks in his Southern Cross sharpshooter variant and Crowe taps out. Bryant's second NFW television match.

Ryan hits the Ego Buster for a suspiciously quick three-count win. A #1 contender's match for the PURE World Heavyweight Championship held by Sean Stevens; commentary questions whether Bloodhunt intentionally underperformed given his alignment with Stevens.

matches.stipulation: Roofed Steel Cage (National Championship, opening the 'Around the USA in 80 Days' tour)
matches.note: After a mutinous National Guard infiltrator disrupts the match by attacking both men, Rook Black traps Curiosity in a head-and-arm triangle; the referee's three-arm-drop consciousness test rules Curiosity unable to continue, and Rook Black is declared the winner. Both men are searched with a metal detector before the match, confiscating numerous smuggled weapons. An unidentified National Guardsman ('#13') infiltrates the raised cage, speaks cryptically to Curiosity calling him 'Chris' and referencing a buried shared identity/history, attacks both competitors, and delivers a Frog Splash and a Release Dragon Suplex to Curiosity. Curiosity's manager Eegor also breaches the cage roof, starts a small fire, and is subdued; he passes a lighter, cigarettes, and a flask down into the ring for Curiosity to use as improvised weapons.

date.source: the document's own dateline (4 Sep 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Reel-to-Reel Strap Match
matches.note: Both men triggered their fourth corner monitor at almost the same moment, with Brock falling forward across the line as he passed out from High Flyer's choke. Guest referee Blanche Barnett, after conferring with Castor Strife, ruled that Brock fell intentionally rather than from being knocked out, and awarded him the win. Guest referee Blanche Barnett was aligned with Castor Strife's interests throughout (Castor is the reigning TV Champion and stood to pick his own next challenger); the staged/announced decision favoring Brock stands per the fed's own ruling despite the ambiguous evidence. Winner becomes new #1 contender to Castor Strife's Television Championship.

The match dissolved into a mass brawl after a disguised National Guardsman 'Thirteen' ran in with a chair and attacked multiple wrestlers. Referee Rook Black rang the bell; the NFW executive office subsequently ruled the match a win for Doc Curiosity/Legion/Lord Coyner Pollard by disqualification. Rook Black (NFW National Champion) served as guest referee for this match, not a competitor. 'Thirteen' -- previously established as having sabotaged a Rook Black vs. Doc Curiosity match -- infiltrated disguised as a cameraman wearing a National Guardsman armband, chair-shotting American Panda, Legion, Lord Coyner Pollard and Jeeves, then attacked Doc Curiosity directly. FutureQuis then also grabbed the chair and attacked Rook, Curiosity and Legion before being tackled by the National Guard.

date.source: the document's own dateline (5 Sep 2010), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: PURE Championship Open Challenge
matches.note: After Bryant nearly hit an X-Factor counter, President Mayfield's security dragged him from the ring roughly two minutes in, per the strict time limit Stevens later says he unilaterally imposed on the open challenge. No pinfall or submission occurred; Stevens retains by default. Stevens mockingly tells Bryant he 'deserved about two minutes of PURE wrestling.'

matches.stipulation: PURE Championship Open Challenge
matches.note: Mid-match (after an atomic drop sent Stevens through the ropes), Mayfield's security entered and physically removed Rook Black from ringside; Rook shrugged them off and left under his own power. Stevens states Rook 'deserved about five minutes of purity.' No pinfall or submission occurred. Rook Black used the confrontation to deliver a chess-themed verbal challenge to Stevens, referencing Stevens' past loss to 'the Queen of the Disillusioned'.

matches.stipulation: PURE Championship Open Challenge
matches.note: A hard-fought, competitive match with several near-falls both ways ended when several of President Mayfield's Secret Service agents stormed the ring and the bell was rung before either man could secure a decision. This marked Impulse's full in-ring return to NFW after a neck injury suffered against Castor Strife and Blanche. Stevens and Impulse shared a brief, reluctant handshake afterward.
After a back-and-forth brawl, Bryant locked in the Southern Cross Sharpshooter for the submission win.

matches.stipulation: Blindfold Match
matches.note: Mid-match, Dorchester secretly removed his own blindfold (which had been tied on 'in good faith') and the Hollywood Wrecking Crew (Malik Anderson, Blaine Hollywood) ran in, targeting Joe's already-injured knee with repeated chair shots as Calvin Carlton egged them on. The broadcast ends on the assault with no fall recorded and no decision announced. Joe wrestled partially sighted after being blinded by lye thrown by Dorchester/Veronica at an earlier, off-screen event in Oklahoma City. No title change; Joe's championship status is not resolved on-air.

date.source: the document's own dateline (15 Jan 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: With Lord Coyner Pollard having abandoned the match by riding off on a snowmobile with Jeeves out of disdain for his partner's performance, Legion pinned a struggling Mighty Impala with the Six Million Dollar Drive to Hell. Legion and Rook Black, reluctant/uneasy partners who nearly came to blows with each other early on, still won the match. Commentary notes the actual NFW National Championship belt remained unaccounted for (reportedly lost in North Korea) and the Executive Branch had not clarified the title's status, so Rook Black's champion status here is nominal only.

After a long back-and-forth with several near-falls, Impulse caught Bryant in a Crucifix Cradle for the pinfall win. Impulse worked around a recurring bad knee, dislocating and popping it back into place mid-match on at least two occasions.

Referee Greg Herpin was mid-count on Ryan's Ego Buster pin of Dorchester (reaching two) when Troy Windham ran in and SlackKnifed both men; the Windham Clan then ambushed the ringside area entirely, leaving the match's outcome undetermined. This was billed as a #1 contender's match for Joe the Plumber's World Heavyweight Championship. Dan Ryan wrestled the entire match on a leg/ankle injury inflicted in a pre-match backstage ambush by Calvin Carlton, Blaine Hollywood, and Malik Anderson. The Windham Clan invasion that ended the match also brutalized the ringside commentary team and several other roster/staff members.

date.source: the document's own dateline (22 Jan 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Atken and Cruise traded control, culminating in a simultaneous clothesline that put both men down; the referee began a double count that both men beat, but the match was overrun before any finish could be reached. The Windham Clan (Troy, Mark, Bobby Jack Windham and JJ DeVille) ran in and beat down both men; the referee was said to have signaled for the bell as he fled, but no winner or stoppage type is stated in the text, so this is left unresolved.

After a series of near-falls (including Brock's middle-rope DDT) and a belt-shot exchange, Castor blocked a punch, hit a knee to the midsection and pinned Brock with the Director's Cut to retain. Referee Scott Speranza nearly disqualified Castor for grabbing the title belt but let the match continue to a clean-ish pinfall; described as the closest Brock has come to the title.

The Dynasty (Calvin Carlton, Dorchester Stratton, Blaine Hollywood) repeatedly interfered; Dorchester Stratton piledrove Joe the Plumber through a steel chair on the outside, and Joe could not beat the referee's ten count, giving Malik Anderson the win by count-out. Commentary continued to refer to Joe the Plumber as 'our champion' immediately after the count-out, indicating the title did not change hands on the count-out even though Malik won the match. The Windham Clan then ran in and beat down the fallen champion, prompting President Mayfield's video appearance.

date.source: the document's own dateline (26 Feb 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Malik Anderson hit a Tiger Driver on Brock Alyas, then tagged Blaine Hollywood, who delivered the Doomsday Backcracker for an easy three-count; Alyas and Atken showed little cohesion as a team. Billed and recapped as a pre-show 'DARK MATCH' rather than covered with full live commentary. The title at stake is not explicitly named in the text beyond the '(c)' designation in the segment heading; commentary elsewhere refers to Malik Anderson and Blaine Hollywood ('the Hollywood Wrecking Crew') as tag champions.

After Jack Bryant powerbombed an interfering Problem Child off the apron, Bandit climbed the apron and chokeslammed Bryant into the corner; JJ DeVille rolled over for the pin to win. Bobby Jack Windham and August De La Rossi accompanied JJ DeVille to ringside. After the bell, Bryant attacked the Windham Clan members present; on the arena's video replay, JJ DeVille was shown visibly angry at Bandit for interfering on his behalf, seemingly unhappy the win wasn't clean.

matches.stipulation: Troy Windham as Special Guest Referee, under a Presidential order fining any wrestler $100,000 (and the rest of the roster $25,000) for attacking Windham unless he or the Windham Clan broke the rules first
matches.note: The match broke down when Dorchester Stratton accidentally knocked out guest referee Troy Windham with a springboard move; Impulse and Dan Ryan began beating Windham down, at which point Dan Ryan revealed himself as the newest Windham Clan member and turned on his tag partner Impulse. The assembled Windham Clan then ran in with chairs to brutalize Impulse, and the match ended with no formal decision. No pinfall or official result occurred; commentary and both broadcasters (Kerry O'Connor, Lamont Hollywood) ultimately abandoned the desk out of fear of the Windham Clan. Mark Windham (injured earlier in the show) was not part of the beatdown.

date.source: the document's own dateline (13 Jun 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Dane drove a loaded titanium knee brace (the 'Starmaker') into Duk's temple simultaneously with the opening bell and pinned him in seconds. Billed as 'The Only Star' Eric Dane. Commentary notes this is Dane's third win in three NFW appearances; Dane has been publicly lobbying President Mayfield and the Windham Clan for tougher opponents.

With Bryant having Deville trapped in the Southern Cross Sharpshooter submission, hand-picked 'supervising referee' Pee Wee Troutman rang the bell and ring announcer Lee Baby-Sims declared Deville the winner and new champion. Shown only as a highlight package, not in full, per broadcast note ('due to a number of situations'). Troutman was installed pre-match by Deville as a friendly official; the stoppage functioned as a screwjob. Per lane rules the staged-announced result stands. Post-match, Bryant knocked out referee Greg Herpin and trashed the ringside area in a rage; Deville was confronted and rebuked by Troy Windham backstage for celebrating alone instead of tending to the injured Dan Ryan.

After a chaotic brawl involving both teams' seconds (Calvin Carlton for the Hollywood Wrecking Crew, Shaniqua Carlton for the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels), Saafir Muhammed hit a frog splash through a table onto Blaine Hollywood for the pinfall. Calvin Carlton (manager of the Hollywood Wrecking Crew) and his half-sister Shaniqua Carlton (manager of the DRS, also introduced as former manager of 'The New Showstoppers') both interfered throughout, including a tennis-racket spot between them. Immediately after the pin, Bobby Jack Windham and Christian Cruise of the Windham Clan ran in and attacked the new champions -- Bobby Jack hit 187 with the Pure Championship belt, Christian Cruise chairshotted Saafir Muhammed -- but this was a post-match assault, not a match-result change; the DRS's title win stands.

matches.stipulation: NFW World Heavyweight Championship Semi-Final
matches.note: Strife locked in the Anderson Armbar submission hold and Stratton tapped out; referee Greg Herpin called for the bell. Dorchester Stratton wrestled with an arm injured minutes earlier in a backstage attack by an unidentified hooded man (later revealed, at the end of the show, to be Joe the Plumber). Castor Strife's stable 'The Guild' (Lana Dremire, Alex Austin, Magnus) interfered repeatedly at ringside: Lana Dremire bladed Stratton's forehead with a bladed glove and later placed Strife's foot on the rope to save a pin, Magnus attacked Stratton in the crowd after he fled over the guardrail, and Alex Austin was knocked out by a Stratton kick. A Stratton small-package pin attempt was ruled a two-count by referee Herpin despite H'Wood's on-air protest that it was a clean three.

matches.stipulation: NFW World Heavyweight Championship Semi-Final
matches.note: Impulse reversed a Dan Ryan superkick attempt and rolled him into a jackknife pin for the three count. Dan Ryan wrestled with a leg injured in a backstage attack by the same hooded assailant earlier in the show; Impulse offered pre-match to let Ryan take a walkout countout so Ryan could recover, which Ryan refused. Impulse's shoulder was separated and popped back into place at ringside (by Lamont Hollywood, per H'Wood's own on-air account) partway through the match. Commentary and Ryan himself repeatedly refer to Impulse by the name 'Randall Knox' during and after this match, paralleling the earlier reveal that High Flyer's legal name is Jack Harmen -- the document does not clarify whether this is a formal real-name reveal or simply an alternate in-fiction alias, so it is reported here without resolving it. No factions were at ringside for this match, a deliberate departure from the two

date.source: the document's own dateline (29 Jul 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Deacon planted Christian Cruise with the Altar Call (crucifix powerbomb) for the pinfall win. Immediately after the bell, Bobby Jack Windham and Troy Windham ran in and attacked Deacon; Eric Dane then turned on Deacon, hitting him with a chair and calling him 'choir boy,' and helped dump Christian Cruise from the ring, loosely aligning himself with the Windham Clan for the moment.

The NCSU mascot 'Mrs. Wulf' ran in and coldcocked JJ Deville; referee Greg Herpin called for the bell, ruling it interference against Deville's title defense, and Deville retained. The match itself was largely a chase around and through the crowd/parking area rather than sustained in-ring action. Post-match, Jack Bryant unmasked 'Mrs. Wulf' as Peter Windham and beat him down with a spinebuster and punches. JJ Deville then fled the arena in a stolen NFW-branded pickup truck; Jack Bryant destroyed a limousine belonging to Troy Windham with a sledgehammer in retaliation for not catching Deville.

matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match
matches.note: After Dorchester Stratton shoved referee Greg Herpin into a charging Dan Ryan, Joe the Plumber (working as special guest referee per pre-match stipulation) took over officiating; JJ Deville ran in and low-blowed Stratton, allowing Ryan to hit the Humility Bomb, and Joe the Plumber made what commentary called a quick three-count. Winner earned the right to face the winner of the Impulse/Castor Strife NFW World Heavyweight Championship final later on this same show, not a title itself. The match dissolved into a mass brawl among the assembled lumberjacks (Windham Clan, Dynasty, and 'Team NFW'), during which Mike Randalls was revealed/unveiled as the mystery attacker from the cold-open recap and chopped Joe the Plumber with a barbed-wire-wrapped arm; Troy Windham was subsequently caught in the same wire by Randalls and then dropkicked by Nova. Commentator H'Wood called the finish a 'fix.'

matches.stipulation: No Interference Permitted (NFW Board of Directors decree for this match only)
matches.note: After a 37-minute back-and-forth war with multiple near-falls and reversed finishers, Castor Strife caught Impulse with the Director's Cut for the pinfall at 37:42. Commentary states the NFW Board of Directors barred all outside personnel from ringside for this match; no interference occurred. This segment/match heading does not appear in the show's own Credits block at the end of the document, unlike every other segment -- likely a document/production omission rather than evidence the match didn't happen (it is clearly the live main event).

date.source: the document's own dateline (20 Apr 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: Bloodhunt tapped out to Castor Strife's camel-clutch-style sleeper hold (the 'Golden Dream') after a long, hard-fought surprise challenge. Bloodhunt, a two-time former World Champion and Hall of Famer, made a surprise return to challenge for the title. After the finish Castor showed him a rare moment of respect and the crowd gave him a standing ovation.

Billed as a title match in the show's own Credits block, but no in-ring contest occurred: Stratton did not come out for introductions, and the two instead brawled uncontrollably through the backstage corridors, a supply closet, and a banquet area until arena security separated them. No bell, no referee, no decision; Bryant retained the belt by default since no match took place.

JJ Deville pinned Impulse using a handful of tights for leverage. Referee Greg Herpin was knocked unconscious mid-match in an accidental collision; while he was out, JJ Deville slapped his own hand on the mat for an uncounted, non-standing 'three' before recovering enough to later win legitimately (if illegally) off the tights. After the bell, Calico Rose -- returning to television after a months-long injury absence -- superkicked JJ Deville, and she and Impulse embraced in the ring.

matches.stipulation: Sudden Death Triple Threat
matches.note: Rook Black pinned Deacon with a double-knee facebreaker onto a steel chair. Deacon's manager Chris Shepherd performed a card-trick bit before the bell that made three members of Stalker's Fallen entourage 'vanish.' Senior referee Greg Herpin was taken out by a Stalker DDT mid-match, bringing in backup official Scott Speranza. Legion ran in to break up a Stalker pin on Deacon with a 450 splash. Deacon was busted open badly from repeated chair shots; the match was chaotic with multiple near-falls and referee bumps.

date.source: the document's own dateline (16 Jun 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: No formal contest ever began. Calvin Carlton, attempting to announce new number-one contenders for the tag titles, was interrupted in succession by the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, the Original Showstoppers, Point of View, and the Superfly Express, and all parties dissolved into a mass ringside brawl. Akita Hoshi then ran in swinging a burning kendo stick and spraying green mist before vanishing, and referee Greg Herpin put the fire out with an extinguisher as security broke up the fight. Segment is titled as a championship match in the show's Credits block, so it is recorded here per the brief's rule, but it never resolves into an actual pairing or contest; no #1 contender was named and the EMT tag title situation is left unresolved.

matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match (guest lumberjacks: The Windham Clan), thirty-second time limit
matches.note: JJ DeVille had the bell rung and rung again before either man could engage, then declared the match a draw under a previously unannounced thirty-second time limit, keeping Cruise under the Windham Clan's control and denying Deacon the number-one contendership. Immediately after the draw was declared, the Windham Clan lumberjacks (Peter Windham, August De La Rossi, The Mighty Impala, Z.!) beat down Deacon's second Chris Shepherd and then Deacon and Cruise themselves; Bobby Jack Windham finished by throwing Cruise through a table with a running Razor's Edge he calls the 'Crucifixion,' then delivered an unhinged religious promo to Cruise about hearing the voice of God.

After a berserk early rally from Legion followed by a back-and-forth battle, Rook Black kipped up to counter Legion's top-rope 'Legion's Air Disease' senton with a single-knee facebuster, then pinned him for the three count to retain. During the match, the Frontiertron aired a fresh (not archival) segment of Stalker and Luci4 taunting Legion and announcing they were leaving NFW indefinitely, which sent Legion into an early berserker rage.

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification
matches.note: After a brutal brawl through the arena (bathroom, food court, crowd) involving brass knuckles, a chain, a chair, and a near-shoulder separation via Kimura, Castor Strife countered a chain-choke attempt and reversed a turnbuckle escape into the Director's Cut for the pinfall to retain. Angus Skaaland and Alex Austin worked the match on Dane's behalf; Austin turned on Dane late, laying him and Angus out with chair shots before storming off, evening the numbers for Strife. Lana Dremire (Strife's valet) brawled with Kelly (Dane's valet) at ringside.

date.source: the document's own dateline (9 Sep 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: With Peter Windham trapped in Mayfield's FPS submission and attempting a cradle counter, Mayfield's cornerman Cojones Mercado chairshotted Windham from behind, allowing Mayfield the pinfall. Recapped in highlight form as having already taken place in the show's first hour, as part of President Mayfield's ongoing campaign against Windham Clan-affiliated wrestlers.

After ducking a double chairshot from outside interferers Mysterious Z and Mighty Impala (who instead knocked each other down), Cruise pinned Bobby Jack Windham while gripping referee Pee Wee Troutman's lapels for extra leverage. Cruise substituted for Deacon, who was attacked backstage before the show and unable to compete. The referee, Pee Wee Troutman, is described as 'the Windham Clan representative official' and was repeatedly complicit in the interference against Cruise; per the binding rules, the staged/announced pinfall result stands regardless. The document itself is inconsistent about this wrestler's first name, alternating between 'Christian Cruise' (segment title) and 'Cameron Cruise' (body text); both are preserved verbatim rather than resolved. Framed by commentary as the conclusion of 'the Christian Cruise Saga.'

matches.stipulation: Stairway to Hell ladder match (razor wire suspended above a center ladder) for the Number One Contendership to the NFW World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Impulse rolled up a distracted Eric Dane for the pinfall to become the new Number One Contender to the NFW World Heavyweight Championship. Originally a five-man match, reduced to four after Blaine Hollywood was attacked backstage before the show and could not compete. Referee: Scott Speranza. Immediately beforehand, Rook Black blocked what looked like an Impulse superkick meant for Eric Dane with his own arm and fell through the ropes, seemingly a deliberate act to let Impulse win (Black later mouths 'YOU'RE WELCOME' to Impulse); this is inferred from the text rather than stated outright. NFW World Heavyweight Champion Castor Strife, fresh off his 2012 Ultratitle tournament win, guest-commentated the match.

matches.stipulation: Strap Match; opener of a Best of Five Series for the Television Championship (first to touch all four turnbuckles wins)
matches.note: Jack Bryant touched all four corners, the last coming right after Dorchester Stratton's valet Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld was knocked down trying to interfere, giving Bryant the series-opening win and retaining the Television Championship. After the bell, Dorchester Stratton ambushed Bryant with a chair, targeting his taped ribs, until Malik Anderson crotched Stratton on the top rope and gorilla-press-slammed him out of the ring while Shaniqua Carlton threw Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld from the ring. Referee: Bruce Phillips.

matches.stipulation: Two Out of Three Falls, No Holds Barred, No Time Limit, Retirement match (loser must retire from professional wrestling)
matches.note: Fall one went to Mike Randalls via a bridging Crossface Chickenwing submission at 22:33; fall two went to Troy Windham via the Slackknife onto a steel chair at 34:37; in the decisive fall, with Randalls choking Windham out in a Katahajime/Kashmir Clutch, JJ Deville (Windham's own manager) blindsided Randalls with a chairshot, then placed Randalls on top of the unconscious Windham and forced referee Greg Herpin to make the count, awarding the match and the retirement stipulation to Randalls. An extraordinarily bloody, brutal match including two ring-step piledrivers/backdrop drivers, a chair-assisted DDT, a suplex through a table, and multiple near-falls. Immediately after the bizarre finish, Dorchester Stratton and Blaine Hollywood ran in, chairshotted Randalls and referee Herpin, and hit Randalls with a Doomsday-Device-style combination ('Doomsday That's Entertainment'); JJ Deville then

matches.stipulation: Australian Rules Tuxedo Match (fans may supply weapons; match 4 of a Best of Five series)
matches.note: Using fan-supplied weapons (a coconut, a surfboard, an oil can, a road sign, and a didgeridoo), Bryant hit a Birmingham Breaker (uranage backbreaker) on Stratton for the pin. Referee was Bruce Phillips. Steel Viper's surprise return and interference on Bryant's behalf is a major angle; see storyline_notes.

matches.stipulation: Cutting Room Floor match (no countouts, no disqualifications, no time limit; the loser is whoever is sent through the pane of glass above the ring)
matches.note: Impulse escaped Strife's Cult Classic (GTS) attempt in mid-air atop the scaffold and hit a hurricanrana that sent Strife off the platform through a stack of tables and the pane of glass below. Castor Strife accompanied by Lucky Seven; Impulse accompanied by Calico Rose. Ring announcer/official was Lee-Baby Sims. Strife injures his arm/shoulder mid-match via his own headbutt counter. Post-match, Strife is stretchered out and hospitalized; a mysterious shadowed figure is later shown at his bedside holding his gas mask.

eliminations.note: Eliminated simultaneously with Freddie Sagawa; Ocho himself stayed in the match.
Eliminated simultaneously with Akita Hoshi.
Pollard press-slammed a distracted Peter Windham on top of Fappity.

matches.note: Jack Harmen hit a top-rope Flying Moon Shot that eliminated both Leyenda De Ocho and Jesse Ramey together, winning the 2013 Grand Prix and a shot at the NFW World Heavyweight Championship. See lane_notes: this segment's own running elimination counts ('down to nine,' 'final five') do not arithmetically match the named eliminations in the text, and several wrestlers are described as eliminated and then shown active again later. A commentary call of 'Jack Harmen eliminated' mid-match was also retracted on-air by guest commentator Impulse ('Not yet! Jack dove out of the way!') and is excluded from the eliminations list as a false call.

matches.stipulation: I Quit / Steel Cage (fifth and deciding match of a Best of Five series)
matches.note: After an extended, bloody brawl in and around the steel cage -- including a roughly fifteen-foot fall by Bryant off the top of the cage through the broadcast table -- Stratton dropped Bryant head/neck-first onto the ring steps and locked in a submission hold; Bryant's second Shaniqua Carlton threw in the towel rather than let him continue, and Dorchester Stratton was declared the winner and new NFW Television Champion. The Hellfire Club (JJ Deville, Blaine Hollywood) tried to run in three-on-one but were driven off by Malik Anderson. Both men bled heavily; Bryant bit a chunk out of Stratton's ear (and was bitten in turn earlier), and Stratton appeared to dislocate/injure a finger on his own hand. matches.note: August De La Rossi stalled and refused to enter the ring until threatened with a forfeit and expulsion; once the bout started, Impulse quickly had him tapping in a half nelson, but JJ Deville interrupted before any decision was rendered, announcing that Impulse was suspended (for an incident at the prior NFW Brawl) and could not continue. No formal winner was ever announced; JJ Deville halted proceedings, fined Impulse by confiscating his and Calico Rose's cash/belongings, and confiscated/tore up personal items belonging to Rose. After JJ left, Calico Rose knocked out the still-recovering August De La Rossi with a punch.

matches.stipulation: Bounty Match (Calvin Carlton placed a $50,000 bounty on Nova; Troy Windham separately placed a bounty on Bandit)
matches.note: No bell rang and no contest was ever formally staged: Eric Dane ambushed Nova with a chair before the match began, then Bandit choked the downed Nova. Dane collected Calvin Carlton's $50,000 bounty for taking out Nova, then immediately double-crossed the Windham Clan by also crowning Bandit and hitting Troy Windham with a Stardriver, stealing a second $50,000 briefcase off Peter Windham and walking off with $100,000 total. Functionally an angle rather than a contested match; included because it was billed and announced as a match in the show's own presentation and Credits block. Eric Dane's double-cross of both the Windham Clan and Dynasty (via Calvin Carlton) is the key outcome of the segment. Troy Windham was reportedly injured (neck) on the resulting Stardriver.

matches.stipulation: National Championship Contenders Match, Timed Lumberjack Rules (National Guard permitted to enter for 30 seconds after every 5 minutes)
matches.note: National Guard member #13 (Emilio Ruiz) turned on Jack Harmen during a Guard interference window, hitting a facebuster and a double-underhook brainbuster ('Hypothermia'); Lowell then covered the incapacitated Harmen for the pinfall. Shown only as a highlights package during the broadcast because it happened earlier the same night, off-camera, due to time constraints; treated as fresh content of this same show, not archival replay. National Champion Rook Black tore #13's patch off in the aftermath; the entire National Guard stable was subsequently fired by the Windham-Clan-controlled front office via a JJ Deville memo.

matches.stipulation: Pentecostal Four Corners Match (two turnbuckles rigged with breakable stone tablets, two rigged with flame jets; entry via a pre-match battle royal to determine first legal men; each wrestler allotted two time-outs; Peter Windham suspended in a cage 45 feet above the ring with a chained Luci4 as an
matches.note: After Stalker hit Deacon with an Evenflow DDT into a fiery corner, Legion fell onto and covered the separately-unconscious champion Bobby Jack Windham; the referee counted the legal men down for the three-count, crowning Legion the new Pure Champion. Christian Cruise (Bobby Jack's ringside ally) was physically drawn into the action multiple times (clotheslined by Deacon, thrown outside). Mr. Myers and Frederick Krueger III (Stalker's entourage) also entered the ring during the match to help unmask/attack Peter Windham, who was forced to play 'Moses' pre-match and was thrown from the ring and caged with Luci4 for the stipulation; Luci4 later DDT'd Peter Windham inside the suspended cage.

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification, Pinfalls Count Anywhere
matches.note: After fighting through a gauntlet of Windham Clan interference across the arena, Jack Bryant cornered JJ Deville in the Clan's suite; JJ used Fiona Love as a human shield, but Fiona elbowed JJ, allowing Bryant to beat him down and pin him for the title (referee Greg Herpin, having replaced a knocked-out Pee Wee Troutman, made the count). Extensive scripted interference against Bryant en route: P. King Duk (newly aligned with the Windham Clan) and August De La Rossi ambushed him with a kendo stick; corrupt referee Pee Wee Troutman colluded with JJ before being knocked out; Bobby Jack Windham threw coffee in Bryant's face and powerbombed him through a concession stand's glass pretzel-warmer case; Christian Cruise suplexed him through a rack of chairs. Immediately after the title change, in the following segment ('Windhams Gone Wild'), Troy Windham returned and chair-shotted the newly-crown

matches.stipulation: 30-minute time limit (shortened from a scheduled 60 minutes by an announcement attributed to President Eddie Mayfield)
matches.note: Time expired at 30 minutes with Castor backdropping Dan Ryan to the outside; the match was declared a time-limit draw and Castor Strife retained the title. The two continued brawling after the bell until officials separated them. Castor Strife's dialogue once refers to himself as 'Castor V Stryfe' (alternate spelling of the surname used only in that line); the show and Credits otherwise consistently use 'Strife.'

matches.note: An incoherent, drugged Felix Red was lifted and dropped with an Elevator Drop, then finished with a full-nelson slam (the 'Humility Bomb') for the pin in what the announcers called the quickest title match in NFW history. Referee Greg Herpin. Felix Red was visibly incapacitated (staged storyline drugging) for the entire match; Eddie Mayfield and 'Just' Mark are shown administering the pre-match drug test backstage. Felix Red was taken out on a stretcher after the match.

Joe the Plumber hit a top-rope splash ('Volcano') on a dazed Nova for the three-count, retaining the title. Referee sided with Joe after Joe tearfully claimed Nova had sexually assaulted him; Nova hallucinated/spouted physics-textbook quotes mid-match and was dunked head-first into Joe's slop bucket before the finish. The Hyperspace Kid (Nova's Cosmonauts partner) seconded Nova at ringside and broke up a wrench shot with his skateboard but did not wrestle.

matches.stipulation: National Championship Tournament Final
matches.note: After Rook nearly finished Teresa with a choke-out chokeslam attempt, she reversed into her Crossarm Diamond Cutter (Process of Illumination) for the pinfall. Teresa opened the match by claiming to have hypnotized Rook via a trigger phrase from an old video message and briefly put him into a mock trance; this had no lasting effect once the bell rang. Craig Miles ('El Presidente'/'Generalissimo') sat at the announce table and personally presented Teresa with the title afterward under a strict no-outside-interference edict.

matches.stipulation: Everette Memorial Title Tournament Final
matches.note: Ringside interference from Calvin Carlton, using a tennis racket concealing a pillow, took out both Dream Team members, letting Blaine Hollywood pin Mike Gordey. Referee Bruce Phillips. Carlton was revealed post-match to be Blaine Hollywood's newly-signed, licensed ringside representative via 'Calvin Carlton Enterprises,' retroactively legitimizing his presence at ringside despite appearing to back the Dream Team beforehand.

After a long weapons-filled brawl, Ryan escaped an attempted Tombstone Piledriver and rolled Eddie Mayfield into a tight cradle for the deciding pinfall. This was billed as Dan Ryan's mystery first title challenger, revealed to be Eddie Mayfield himself. Referee Greg Herpin failed to catch Mayfield using a salad fork twice, brass knuckles, and a chain-wrapped fist during the match; Mayfield also waved off an interference attempt by Cojones Mercado. Despite the earlier screwjob buildup, Mayfield handed the title belt back to Ryan cleanly after the bout. This segment/match is NOT listed in the show's own Credits block.

name: NFW SUPERCRASH II: DAWN OF A REVOLUTION

date.source: the document's own dateline (19 Oct 2008), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match
matches.note: Both men brawled through chairs and 1,000 thumbtacks dumped from the rafters, then crashed through a table together outside the ring; surrounding lumberjacks piled on and the referee called for the bell on a double countout. Pre-match stakes (the loser must manage the winner for 30 days) go unresolved due to the double countout. Ringside 'lumberjacks' included Buff Manley (guest 'host'), Luci4, Teresa Quaranta, Kin Hiroshi, Cameron Cruise, Rook Black, Koopa, several costumed 'von Doom' wrestlers (Ninja von Doom/P. King Duk, Afro-von Doom/Leroy Brown, Emo Anakin von Doom/Beef, Lando von Doom/El Janito), and Cojones Mercado's Insurgent Patrol. It took roughly 15 minutes to break up the brawl; Legion and von Doom were both forced to leave the building.

matches.stipulation: Grand Prix Semifinal
matches.note: Impulse superkicked Sars flush on the side of the head off a shoulder-flip counter and hooked both legs for the pin. Advances Impulse to the Grand Prix Final against the winner of Felix Red vs. Doc Curiosity.

matches.stipulation: Cage Match; Grand Prix Semifinal
matches.note: Neither man could answer referee Bruce Phillips' twenty-count after a double clothesline left both down inside the cage; rather than let it end in a no-decision, NFW official Craig Miles ordered the cage raised and gave the two men five minutes to produce a winner, or Impulse would be added to create a three-way Grand Prix decider. This segment does not resolve on its own — it flows directly, without a bell reset, into the separately Credits-listed 'Grand Prix 500 Championship Final' segment when Impulse is added. Doc Curiosity used hidden brass knuckles mid-match. Both men were bloodied; Curiosity was cut open diving into the cage.

matches.stipulation: Three-way, direct continuation of the Felix Red/Doc Curiosity Cage Match after Craig Miles added Impulse under a five-minute ultimatum
matches.note: After chaos involving an unsanctioned imposter billed as 'Impulse' (eventually speared off the apron by the real Impulse), Doc Curiosity pinned a dazed Impulse following a jawbreaker/chairshot distraction from the imposter to become the first-ever NFW Grand Prix winner. Commentator Kerry O'Connor voices on-air skepticism about the legitimacy of the finish afterward, given the imposter's involvement.

matches.stipulation: Two Out of Three Pinfalls Elimination Match

eliminations.note: Disqualified by the referee for attacking him with a chair, after Rook Black had pulled the ropes down on her during a handspring rebound spot, sending her crashing to the floor and apparently injuring her.

matches.note: After Quaranta was disqualified, Rook Black capitalized on a groggy Steve Knox with the Gauntlet Backhand for the deciding fall and the National Championship. Dangerous mid-match spot: Rook pulled the top rope down on Quaranta mid-handspring, sending her hard to the floor; she was checked by paramedics/security, briefly kicked free of a stretcher, and returned to ringside before her DQ.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match (challenger's choice of stipulation, per a title-contract clause); title belts hung above the ring
matches.note: After a chaotic ladder match with repeated interference from manager Calvin Carlton (including handcuffing Tsunami to the ropes and whipping him with a belt), Tsunami blinded a climbing Malik Anderson with a mist attack, causing a double fall from the ladder, then climbed and grabbed both belts to win. DC Stratton, ruled unfit to wrestle pre-match, interfered early and was formally banned from ringside by referee Greg Herpin. Wildstar's surprise legal substitution reunited him with Tsunami as 'Dawn of a New Day' for the first time in years.

matches.stipulation: One Fall, Sixty-Minute Time Limit
matches.note: After a brutal brawl through the crowd and a Falcon Arrow off the ring apron, Joe caught a diving Nova with a modified inverted piledriver-style finisher for the pin. Post-match, President Eddie Mayfield has enforcer Cojones Mercado chairshot the beaten Nova, blindfolds him with toilet paper, publicly declares him 'fired,' and refuses to let Joe hold the physical championship belt. Mayfield then publicly pressures Craig Miles to step back from NFW authority; Miles agrees and leaves through the crowd, and Mayfield shuts down NFW programming for the remainder of 2008.

name: NFW SUPERCRASH III: REMEMBER THE ALAMO

date.source: the document's own dateline (30 Apr 2011), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: The Hollywood Wrecking Crew (Blaine Hollywood and Malik Anderson) jumped Peter Windham and Bandit before the bell and controlled most of the brawl, but the champions were left outside the ring when the referee's twenty-count ran out while Windham scrambled back inside, giving the challengers the match by count-out. Because titles cannot change hands on a count-out, the Hollywood Wrecking Crew retained the Everette Memorial Tag Team Titles despite losing the match itself; the announcer explicitly clarified this. Hollywood and Anderson then beat down both challengers after the bell, including a spinebuster through a table on Bandit.

Legion, as special guest referee, knocked out both Rook Black and Thirteen and then counted his own pinfall to declare Thirteen the winner and new National Champion. Legion warns Thirteen afterward that he now owes him and threatens to expose Thirteen's hidden identity.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match
matches.note: Bryant and Shawn Hart both hung from the belt hook after a ladder tip; Bryant landed a low blow and pulled the title free as both men fell. Lord Coyner Pollard was denied 'diplomatic immunity' by presidential decree and pulled from the match at the last second, replaced by Shawn Hart. A newly arrived Stalker and his ringside crew, including a masked enforcer referred to as Mr. Myers, interfered repeatedly throughout; Myers even entered the ring uninvited and briefly grabbed for the title before being knocked off the ladder. After Bryant won, Stalker double-arm DDT'd him through the ladder and fled with his group before security could act.

Blinded by the powder, Thirteen was kicked down and hit with a Shining Wizard (called 'Schrodinger's Smack') for the pin. Legion attempted to enter the ring mid-match but backed off after Thirteen and the referee objected.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat, First Fall Wins
matches.note: Thirteen unmasked himself mid-match, revealing himself as High Flyer, then deliberately struck Doctor Curiosity with a Yakuza kick, allowing a recovering Rook Black to fall on Curiosity for the pin. President Mayfield granted both Doctor Curiosity and Thirteen same-night rematch clauses after the prior match, and Rook Black turned the double rematch into this triple threat. Referee Greg Herpin threw Doctor Curiosity's 'Curious Rulebook' into the crowd rather than honor it. High Flyer/Thirteen cut an extended, disjointed promo afterward explaining he sabotaged Curiosity to spite Legion's blackmail over his identity and to make a point about loss and identity; he referenced Curiosity's kayfabe name 'Chris Goodman' during the promo.

matches.stipulation: Elimination Tag Match (50% ownership of New Frontier Wrestling at stake)

eliminations.note: Caught a moonsault attempt and pinned him with a spinning Tombstone.
Thrown over the top rope to the concrete floor and counted out at ringside during Bobby Jack's in-match sermon.
Pinned with a top-rope soccer-style kick Stratton calls the Stepping Stone, after playing possum.
Pinned with the Humility Bomb after Dorchester Stratton sucker-punched Mayfield from the apron, betraying his own team.
Disqualified immediately after for shoving referee Greg Herpin to the mat.
Pinned with the Director's Cut.
Pinned moments later by a Director's Cut of his own, ending the match.

matches.note: JJ Deville copied Castor Strife's own finishing move to pin Castor immediately after Castor had eliminated Troy Windham, clinching the match and 50% ownership of NFW for the Windham Clan. Eddie Mayfield revealed himself as the mystery 'fifth man' for Team NFW at the bell. Dorchester Stratton, placed on the team against his stated wishes, first eliminated Bobby Jack Windham single-handedly, then betrayed his own team to cost Mayfield the match before getting himself disqualified. Impulse was never shown being pinned or eliminated, yet the match was declared over for the Windham Clan immediately after Castor Strife's fall -- flagged as an apparent story inconsistency in lane_notes.

date.source: the document's own dateline (9 Jan 2012), on the fed's own results archive

matches.note: After a chaotic match featuring repeated ringside interference, manager Shaniqua Carlton was struck attacking Malik Anderson, then Blaine Hollywood hit her with a Backcracker off the top rope while she sat on Calvin Carlton's shoulders; the match was ruled a disqualification. The show's own announcement declares the Hollywood Wrecking Crew the winners by disqualification while explicitly stating the titles do NOT change hands, so the champions (Dirty Rotten Scoundrels) retain despite the loss. The text is muddled on exactly whose interference caused the DQ (Shaniqua Carlton is presented as aligned with the challengers' camp, yet appears to attack her own side's Malik Anderson); the staged-announced result is recorded as-is per the binding rule that announced results stand. Saafir Muhammed and 187 attacked the Wrecking Crew before the bell; Blaine Hollywood briefly fled the arena mid-matc

matches.stipulation: Chain Match
matches.note: Stalker hit an Evenflow DDT on a chain-bound Legion for the pinfall, after his valet Luci4 twice pulled the referee from the ring to break up Legion's pin attempts and repeatedly struck Legion with a steel chair. Referee pulled from the ring twice by Luci4 during the match. After the finish, Legion's own valet Luci4 sided with the new champion Stalker, who handed her the belt.

After Akita Hoshi hit Dorchester Stratton with a Shining Wizard and green mist, and Dorchester choked valet Rayne (who was in turn attacked by Stratton's own valet Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld for interfering), Nova pulled Hoshi off the top rope, then finished Stratton with a Bourbon For Breakfast for the pin. Rayne (accompanying Hoshi) attacked Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld with a kendo stick at ringside; Rumsfeld made a save on a Stratton pin attempt by shoving Rayne into the guardrail; Stratton later choked Rayne before Hoshi hit him with green mist.

matches.stipulation: Submissions Match
matches.note: Eric Dane used a smuggled golden spike, gouging and fish-hooking Austin's face until Austin tapped out from the pain. Pre-match, a sealed stipulation contract was wagered: had Austin won, Dane would have retired, owed The Guild $100,000, and served as its manservant for a year. Because Dane won instead, a hidden reverse clause -- smuggled into the paperwork by Lana Dremire without Castor Strife reading it -- forced Castor to cede ownership of Castor Strife Productions to Dane (revealed later in the show).

matches.stipulation: Two out of Three Falls (special conditions dictated by JJ DeVille, who had referee Pee Wee Troutman ordered to count Impulse's side out at nine and disqualify them at four)
matches.note: Impulse's team won the first fall when Bobby Jack Windham submitted to an armbar/wristlock. They won the deciding fall when Jack Bryant locked JJ DeVille in the Southern Cross and DeVille, unable to escape, tapped out. Referee Pee Wee Troutman, nominally the Windham Clan's own senior referee, repeatedly made calls against his own side's interests. Post-match, JJ DeVille attacked Impulse with a chair but Deacon took the blow instead; Impulse got JJ in a chair-assisted position but stopped just short of hitting him, warning 'You're next.'

matches.stipulation: No Holds Barred
matches.note: After a brawl involving spurs, a sledgehammer, and a broken snow shovel, Rook Black hit a sledgehammer-assisted Gauntlet Throwdown (STO) for the pin. A man called Emilio interfered trying to steal cash bags at ringside, tried to grab Harmen's sledgehammer, was paint-bombed by a rigged bag, and was arrested by NFW Security. Both men bled heavily; the match is explicitly tied to the looming Triple Crown Championship consolidation announced earlier in the show.

matches.stipulation: 60-minute time-limit, rematch of a prior 30-minute draw
matches.note: Both men were down as the 60-minute time limit expired; the match was declared a time-limit draw and Castor Strife retained the title as champion. This was a rematch of a 30-minute draw between the same two men at 'Reloaded X' (Oct 30, 2011, Norfolk, Virginia), shown in a recap at the top of the broadcast. Lana Dremire kicked Dan Ryan at ringside during the match and was ejected by officials. After the match, Castor attacked his own Guild ally Magnus with a Director's Cut out of frustration over the Eric Dane contract swindle revealed moments later.

matches.note: After a back-and-forth grudge match, Viper kicked out of a Garvin DDT and survived a top-rope superplex counter (Vipersault near-fall), then finished Garvin with the Steel Curtain for the pin. Billed as a 'dark match' held earlier the same night and shown via highlight-style cutaways rather than live; treated as fresh content produced for this broadcast.

Cruise nearly won with the Shipwreck for a 2.9 count, but McMillan backdropped out of a second Shipwreck attempt and hit the Dread Driver Beta for the pin. Billed as another match held 'off the air' and shown via highlight-style cutaways rather than live; treated as fresh content produced for this broadcast.

Sands booted Hart in the gut immediately after the bell and rolled him up for a quick three count. Presented as a 'highlight clip of a dark match'; treated as fresh content produced for this broadcast. Post-match, Hart's protest of the finish drew out Avery Prosser and the Seven Deadly Sins, who threatened him until he fled the ring.

matches.stipulation: War Games (double-ring, steel-cage-enclosed; Submit or Surrender; Code of Honor suspended; the ten points normally awarded were waived by wrestler vote; winning conference secures homefield advantage for the entire playoffs)
matches.note: After DC Stratton (nominally on the NFW North team) rigged the cage with explosives that detonated and collapsed half the structure, Calvin Carlton's allies interfered on NFW South's behalf, focusing a weapons beatdown on Dan Ryan's already-injured knee until Ryan submitted to Joey Melton's Figure-Four Leglock. DC Stratton was revealed as an ally of Avery Prosser and Neil Riddick; his sabotage caused an in-ring explosion that collapsed part of the cage onto several competitors and referee Greg Herpon. The match continued afterward per the stipulation. Calvin Carlton's allies (unnamed Original Showstoppers members and the masked 'Highwayman') ran in heavily on the South's behalf. Immediately post-match, the Highwayman unmasked as returning veteran Hurricane Eddy Love.

name: Season 1 Ultratitle All-Star Week Legends Night

date.source: the document's own dateline (17 Jan 2004), on the fed's own results archive

matches.stipulation: No DQ, Falls Count Anywhere (billed as the 'NFW Legends Match')
matches.note: After a brawl that spilled into the parking area involving Bloodhunt's limo and his wife Emily, Bloodhunt fought off a low blow and a chair shot, then finished Ricky Zane with a headshot driving him face-first into the trunk of the limo for the pin. Zane attacked limo driver Gomer Pyle and briefly grabbed Bloodhunt's wife/valet Emily during the brawl. Billed as an exhibition 'Legends Match,' not a title bout, despite both men being introduced as former NFW World Champions.

Frankie Fargo used manager Calvin Carlton's tennis racquet to knock out Beretta behind the referee's back and pinned him for a first announced win; two men identified only as 'the Powell brothers' then alerted the referee to the racquet shot, the match was restarted, and Beretta finished Fargo with the Peacemaker for the actual, standing win. Billed as the final match for the SWAT Team duo (Colt & Beretta) — 'the end of an era' per commentary. Miles then also knocked Mayfield out cold with the same chair. The referee called for the bell amid the interference, but no winner or title decision is ever announced in the text. Anne Mystic (Mayfield's manager) was struck in the back of the head with a chair by Adler mid-match while trying to plead with him; her neck-brace injury from a prior incident ('Judas Carlton') is referenced repeatedly. The on-duty referee is never named. Craig Miles' motive for interfering (attacking both men rather than favoring either) is left deliberately unclear by the broadcast team.

After a back-and-forth match (interrupted by a comedic on-air board game break and some fan-thrown marijuana business), Nova caught Rook Black in a rear-naked-choke variation called the Caesarian Section, forcing the tap. Match included a roughly ten-minute in-ring comedic interlude where both men played a board game (Axis & Allies) before the bell actually rang. An author's note after the match states this finish is 'ironic' because Black had made 'Doc Silver' tap out in a prior show ('Week 8').

After a brutal, mud-soaked brawl, Craig Miles sprayed pepper spray/mace directly into Alias's face, blinding him. Referee Roland Priest caught the canister as evidence and immediately called for the bell, ending the match via disqualification in Alias's favor. Miles continued to assault the blinded Alias after the bell (choking him out with his 'Stun Gun'/Coldcock finisher), which is presented as a post-match beatdown rather than part of the decision. Commentary refers to Alias interchangeably as 'Alias' and 'Chris Sheffield' throughout; he wrestles with an eyepatch over a previously lost eye, which Miles repeatedly targets and mocks.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat
matches.note: After putting Guy Boudreaux through an announce table with a top-rope throw and no-selling most offense, Manpower hit Gaige Caldwell with a sitout powerbomb and pinned him for the three-count. The winner earned a spot in Calvin Carlton's 'New South' stable; Carlton was at ringside overseeing the match. Manpower knocked out the referee with a boot to the head after the pin had already been counted (no bearing on the result).

Melton reversed a top-rope powerbomb attempt into a DDT off the turnbuckle. Guy Boudreaux then ran in posing as a substitute referee, gave a fake fast count, and turned on Melton instead of counting the pin. After more back-and-forth (including Boudreaux getting knocked out by accident), Melton locked in a Figure Four Leglock; the actual referee, Roland Priest, then counted the pin while the hold was applied for the official win. Scott Riktor's wife/manager Christina Riktor was heavily involved physically (a top-rope German suplex on Melton, interference, getting whipped into the ring post and knocked out). Guy Boudreaux's fake-referee interference was orchestrated by Calvin Carlton, who hates Melton; this spills into the following segment where Riktor attacks Carlton in retaliation.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: No play-by-play of this match exists in the document. The segment consists entirely of an in-story, fourth-wall-breaking narrator aside claiming the write-up was lost (described as a computer crash 'eating fourteen pages of work'), and cuts directly to the next segment without ever showing the match. A winner is only inferable from a single later commentary line, during the Marcus Cameron vs. Mike Randalls match, that references 'Kodiak Vic Creed's methodology for winning his falls count anywhere match against Seymour Almasy.' Flagged prominently in lane_notes: this is the one advertised match on the card with no narrated content whatsoever. THE FED'S OWN RECORD SETTLES IT: its backstage database (lot 0159) grades this match a Loss for almasyDEATH and a Win for Vic Creed, so the result no longer rests on the later commentary line alone. The aside also breaks frame to speak to a memorial name directly — "But alas, Sean Williams fear not, Jesus' sibling is incubating in your hard drive as we speak" — which stands as written.

matches.stipulation: Ambulance Match
matches.note: Billed as NFW's first-ever Ambulance match (win by locking your opponent in the vehicle's cargo hold for five seconds). Both men brutalized each other in and around the ambulance (table spot, broken bottle, a 20-foot scaffolding dive, a car-hood/windshield double powerbomb) while the sinister Dr. White injected Randalls with an unknown drug mid-match and later defibrillated him. Randalls was sealed in the ambulance and a five-count began, but he burst back out before it completed. The bell is described as ringing once Cameron was left motionless after Randalls slammed his head in a door repeatedly, but no winner or stipulation completion is ever formally announced; the segment instead dissolves into Randalls' berserker rampage. Extremely chaotic, ambiguous finish — see lane_notes. Randalls, apparently under the drug's effect, attacked Dr. White (breaking his neck with a Backdrop Driver),

After a long back-and-forth main event (each kicking out of the other's finisher, the Fallen One and the Slackknife), Eli Flair transitioned an escaped body-scissors attempt into the Total Elimination submission hold (full nelson plus leg lock). Troy Windham tapped out, giving Flair the win. Billed/treated in commentary as Troy Windham's final/retirement match; his associate August De La Rossi pleaded with him beforehand not to wrestle. Windham was the reigning 'UNIFIED Championship' holder, but commentary explicitly states that title 'doesn't hold water' in the NFW West and it was not defended in this match. Eli Flair's manager/wife Poison Ivy was at ringside; Valerian's Garden (the live house band) performed Windham's introduction and Angel of the band cut a hostile promo on him beforehand.

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire Posts (one fall, thirty-minute time limit)
matches.note: A mysterious masked interloper called the Uber Judge ran in and hit Legion and Luci4 with gavel shots, including Rook Black's own finisher (the Gauntlet Throwdown) on Legion. Rook Black then pinned Luci4. The Uber Judge was not a listed participant; he fled before security could grab him and was later shown unmasking privately to Felix Red backstage, with the reveal hidden from the camera. Madonna Wayne Grossard (Felix Red's self-appointed lawyer/manager) was at ringside for this match and was banned from NFW later in the show for a flame-shooting prop ('Fire Porn'). The winners earn a National Championship shot at SuperCrash 2.

matches.stipulation: Ladder Match (briefcase reportedly containing $40,000)
matches.note: Brock Alyas knocked Professor Tremendous off the ladder with a briefcase shot to the head and pinned him to claim the briefcase. The briefcase, opened backstage afterward, was revealed to contain only Monopoly money rather than real cash.

Thrown over the top rope after Knox shoved him into a swerve on Payne. The fed's own call credits both men: "PAYNE THROWS ALMASY OUT OF THE RING! (LOUD EXPLOSION!) STEVE KNOX AND JASON PAYNE ELIMINATED ALMASY!" — sixth from last, leaving the final five.

matches.note: In the climax, Steve Knox attempted the Gold Rush; Impulse and Sars the Clown 2 held on to him and all three crashed through ringside tables to the floor together, leaving an unconscious Joe the Plumber, slumped over a ladder in the ring, as the last man standing after 122 minutes. A large, unnamed woman calling herself the Viking Queen 'Helga' invaded the ring mid-match without being a listed entrant; she was revealed to be both Dirk Dickwood's ex-wife and Phil Atken's mother. Her interference (chokeslams, a bear hug on Atken) is not counted in the eliminations list above since she was never an official participant. THE FED'S OWN TITLE TABLE FILES THIS AS A CHAMPIONSHIP DEFENCE: its backstage database (lot 0159) ties this match to the NFW Television Championship, with Joe the Plumber the champion both before and after — "Joe the Plumber retained the Television Championship in the 25-man Television Royale, left lying on a ladder in the ring when Steve Knox's Gold Rush took Knox, Impulse and Sars through the tables to the floor."

matches.stipulation: Two out of Three Falls, No Holds Barred, No Time Limit
matches.note: Nova won the first fall via pinfall (the Funkichronic Comet, an Arabian facebuster off the top rope onto a steel chair) at 22:07. Dan Ryan won the second fall via pinfall (the Humility Bomb powerbomb onto a steel chair) at 28:47. Nova won the third fall and the match by submission, forcing Ryan to tap out to a rear naked/dragon sleeper hold, at 46:47. The Credits block for this show breaks off before crediting a writer for this main event; see lane_notes.

The Battle for Mordor, a nine-man three-way tag, the Broken Fellowship (Teddy Alexander and the Chromatic Dragons, with Ancalagon) against Dirty Deeds against the Black Market, the potential shotgun load for an Everette Memorial Titles shot, Chris Fusco refereeing: Omega Zero pinned Windham with Absolute Zero, knocking Dirty Deeds out; Teddy's Angerbash missed Legion and flattened Fusco, Windham hit Teddy with a chair and brought in Marcus Robinson, but Greg Herpin stunned Robinson, and when Legion, shoving Windham, walked into Teddy's Angerbash kick, Windham counted the pinfall himself with no official left: Teddy pinned Legion.

matches.note: The number-one contenders' Four Corners match for Leyenda De Ocho's Triple Crown Championship (one fall, all tags legal, two men in at a time): Calvin Carlton hit Xavier Langston with his tennis racket off the top rope, Teddy Alexander powerbombed him from the top and pinned him before Kerry Kuroyama and Commissioner Windham could break it up, with Marcus Robinson refereeing and Greg Herpin at ringside.

Malik Anderson against Mike Randalls, Chris Fusco refereeing and Shaniqua Carlton at ringside: Malik won by disqualification after Blaine Hollywood ran in and hit him with That's Entertainment while he held a submission on Randalls; Dorchester Stratton then cleared the ring with a TV-title shot.

Everette Memorial Titles in a steel cage, sixty-minute limit, no disqualification: the Chromatic Dragons beat the Graverobbers (c) for the titles when Zack Dragon pinned Devastator with the Fall of Darkness shooting star press, Bandit held off by Omega Zero.

date.source: Argyle's booking date 2014-07-12 for this show (booking 2895, status 5, published); the write-up carries no dateline of its own.

matches.note: The debut of Los Olvidados against the Meatwrappers, Plain Brown Rapper and Mystery Meat (no record here): Rey Amarillo and El Cabron won with the Carcosa Driver.
Windham's 'The Legend of Bagger Vance': Kerry Kuroyama beat Lane Cash with the Kuroyama Driver as Peter Windham shattered his golf club on the ringpost.
Xavier Langston beat Cancer by disqualification when Calvin Carlton hit him with a tennis racket during the Koji Clutch; Cancer and Carlton then attacked him until Castor Strife appeared.
Legion beat Blaine Hollywood with the Legionaires Disease splash after Malik Anderson ran out and Falcon Punched Blaine; Lamont Hollywood had interfered earlier.

An intergender tag: Shaniqua Carlton pinned Dorchester Stratton after Blaine Hollywood ran in and hit him with That's Entertainment, and the Hollywoods left Malik Anderson and Veronica Abrams Rumsfeld looking for answers.
Leyenda De Ocho beat Cojones Mercado with the Actualizer corkscrew quebrada, then told Greg Herpin to give Teddy Alexander a message.

date.source: Argyle's booking date 2014-07-27 for this show (booking 2896, status 5, published); the write-up carries no dateline of its own.

matches.note: JJ DeVille's return, seconded by Mike Randalls: he beat Ryan Oracle with the Coup de Ville spinning pedigree.
Los Olvidados won over the Shadowrunners, Rey Amarillo pinning Chad Fortune with a Spider Northern Lights suplex, with Doug Mayfield and 'Just' Mark interfering.
Kerry Kuroyama beat Legion with a flying bodypress turned powerslam when Legion, perched on the top rope, called him to his feet instead of leaping.

Malik Anderson beat Blaine Hollywood: Malik held the ropes as Blaine went for the Backstabber, Shaniqua Carlton hit Lamont Hollywood, Mike Randalls ran in and kicked Blaine in the head, and Malik covered him.
Castor Strife beat Xavier Langston with the Director's Cut snap swinging neckbreaker after a near fall off a Hart Attack clothesline.
Ill Fortune beat Dirty Deeds: Lucky Seven's Witch Hunter shining wizard set up Alex Austin's Anaconda, and Royce Ramsey tapped; Peter Windham was caught in the crossfire.
Omega Zero beat Bandit with Absolute Zero; Devastator then attacked the Chromatic Dragons, who double-misted him.
NFW World Heavyweight Championship, Jack Harmen (c) against a blinded Devastator: Harmen attacked before the bell and won in about four minutes with the Locomotive kick.
